verses.Neh.13.2: because they met not the children of Israel with bread and with water, but hired Balaam against them, to curse them: howbeit our God turned the curse into a blessing.
verses.Neh.13.3: And it came to pass, when they had heard the law, that they separated from Israel all the mixed multitude.
verses.Neh.13.4: Now before this, Eliashib the priest, who was appointed over the chambers of the house of our God, being allied unto Tobiah,
verses.Neh.13.5: had prepared for him a great chamber, where aforetime they laid the meal-offerings, the frankincense, and the vessels, and the tithes of the grain, the new wine, and the oil, which were given by commandment to the Levites, and the singers, and the porters; and the heave-offerings for the priests.
verses.Neh.13.6: But in all this time I was not at Jerusalem; for in the two and thirtieth year of Artaxerxes king of Babylon I went unto the king: and after certain days asked I leave of the king,
verses.Neh.13.7: and I came to Jerusalem, and understood the evil that Eliashib had done for Tobiah, in preparing him a chamber in the courts of the house of God.
verses.Neh.13.8: And it grieved me sore: therefore I cast forth all the household stuff of Tobiah out of the chamber.
verses.Neh.13.9: Then I commanded, and they cleansed the chambers: and thither brought I again the vessels of the house of God, with the meal-offerings and the frankincense.
verses.Neh.13.10: And I perceived that the portions of the Levites had not been given them; so that the Levites and the singers, that did the work, were fled every one to his field.
verses.Neh.13.11: Then contended I with the rulers, and said, Why is the house of God forsaken? And I gathered them together, and set them in their place.
verses.Neh.13.12: Then brought all Judah the tithe of the grain and the new wine and the oil unto the treasuries.
verses.Neh.13.13: And I made treasurers over the treasuries, Shelemiah the priest, and Zadok the scribe, and of the Levites, Pedaiah: and next to them was Hanan the son of Zaccur, the son of Mattaniah; for they were counted faithful, and their business was to distribute unto their brethren.
verses.Neh.13.14: Remember me, O my God, concerning this, and wipe not out my good deeds that I have done for the house of my God, and for the observances thereof.
verses.Neh.13.15: In those days saw I in Judah some men treading winepresses on the sabbath, and bringing in sheaves, and lading asses therewith; as also wine, grapes, and figs, and all manner of burdens, which they brought into Jerusalem on the sabbath day: and I testified against them in the day wherein they sold victuals.
verses.Neh.13.16: There dwelt men of Tyre also therein, who brought in fish, and all manner of wares, and sold on the sabbath unto the children of Judah, and in Jerusalem.
verses.Neh.13.17: Then I contended with the nobles of Judah, and said unto them, What evil thing is this that ye do, and profane the sabbath day?
verses.Neh.13.18: Did not your fathers thus, and did not our God bring all this evil upon us, and upon this city? yet ye bring more wrath upon Israel by profaning the sabbath.
verses.Neh.13.19: And it came to pass that, when the gates of Jerusalem began to be dark before the sabbath, I commanded that the doors should be shut, and commanded that they should not be opened till after the sabbath: and some of my servants set I over the gates, that there should no burden be brought in on the sabbath day.
verses.Neh.13.20: So the merchants and sellers of all kind of wares lodged without Jerusalem once or twice.
verses.Neh.13.21: Then I testified against them, and said unto them, Why lodge ye about the wall? if ye do so again, I will lay hands on you. From that time forth came they no more on the sabbath.
verses.Neh.13.22: And I commanded the Levites that they should purify themselves, and that they should come and keep the gates, to sanctify the sabbath day. Remember unto me, O my God, this also, and spare me according to the greatness of thy lovingkindness.
verses.Neh.13.23: In those days also saw I the Jews that had married women of Ashdod, of Ammon, and of Moab:
verses.Neh.13.24: and their children spake half in the speech of Ashdod, and could not speak in the Jews’ language, but according to the language of each people.
verses.Neh.13.25: And I contended with them, and cursed them, and smote certain of them, and plucked off their hair, and made them swear by God, saying, Ye shall not give your daughters unto their sons, nor take their daughters for your sons, or for yourselves.
verses.Neh.13.26: Did not Solomon king of Israel sin by these things? yet among many nations was there no king like him, and he was beloved of his God, and God made him king over all Israel: nevertheless even him did foreign women cause to sin.
verses.Neh.13.27: Shall we then hearken unto you to do all this great evil, to trespass against our God in marrying foreign women?
verses.Neh.13.28: And one of the sons of Joiada, the son of Eliashib the high priest, was son-in-law to Sanballat the Horonite: therefore I chased him from me.
verses.Neh.13.29: Remember them, O my God, because they have defiled the priesthood, and the covenant of the priesthood, and of the Levites.
verses.Neh.13.30: Thus cleansed I them from all foreigners, and appointed charges for the priests and for the Levites, every one in his work;
verses.Neh.13.31: and for the wood-offering, at times appointed, and for the first-fruits. Remember me, O my God, for good.
verses.Esth.1.1: Now it came to pass in the days of Ahasuerus (this is Ahasuerus who reigned from India even unto Ethiopia, over a hundred and seven and twenty provinces),
verses.Esth.1.2: that in those days, when the king Ahasuerus sat on the throne of his kingdom, which was in Shushan the palace,
verses.Esth.1.3: in the third year of his reign, he made a feast unto all his princes and his servants; the power of Persia and Media, the nobles and princes of the provinces, being before him;
verses.Esth.1.4: when he showed the riches of his glorious kingdom and the honor of his excellent majesty many days, even a hundred and fourscore days.
verses.Esth.1.5: And when these days were fulfilled, the king made a feast unto all the people that were present in Shushan the palace, both great and small, seven days, in the court of the garden of the king’s palace.
verses.Esth.1.6: There were hangings of white cloth, of green, and of blue, fastened with cords of fine linen and purple to silver rings and pillars of marble: the couches were of gold and silver, upon a pavement of red, and white, and yellow, and black marble.
verses.Esth.1.7: And they gave them drink in vessels of gold (the vessels being diverse one from another), and royal wine in abundance, according to the bounty of the king.
verses.Esth.1.8: And the drinking was according to the law; none could compel: for so the king had appointed to all the officers of his house, that they should do according to every man’s pleasure.
verses.Esth.1.9: Also Vashti the queen made a feast for the women in the royal house which belonged to king Ahasuerus.
verses.Esth.1.10: On the seventh day, when the heart of the king was merry with wine, he commanded Mehuman, Biztha, Harbona, Bigtha, and Abagtha, Zethar, and Carcas, the seven chamberlains that ministered in the presence of Ahasuerus the king,
verses.Esth.1.11: to bring Vashti the queen before the king with the crown royal, to show the peoples and the princes her beauty; for she was fair to look on.
verses.Esth.1.12: But the queen Vashti refused to come at the king’s commandment by the chamberlains: therefore was the king very wroth, and his anger burned in him.
verses.Esth.1.13: Then the king said to the wise men, who knew the times (for so was the king’s manner toward all that knew law and judgment;
verses.Esth.1.14: and the next unto him were Carshena, Shethar, Admatha, Tarshish, Meres, Marsena, and Memucan, the seven princes of Persia and Media, who saw the king’s face, and sat first in the kingdom),
verses.Esth.1.15: What shall we do unto the queen Vashti according to law, because she hath not done the bidding of the king Ahasuerus by the chamberlains?
verses.Esth.1.16: And Memucan answered before the king and the princes, Vashti the queen hath not done wrong to the king only, but also to all the princes, and to all the peoples that are in all the provinces of the king Ahasuerus.
verses.Esth.1.17: For this deed of the queen will come abroad unto all women, to make their husbands contemptible in their eyes, when it shall be reported, The king Ahasuerus commanded Vashti the queen to be brought in before him, but she came not.
verses.Esth.1.18: And this day will the princesses of Persia and Media who have heard of the deed of the queen say the like unto all the king’s princes. So will there arise much contempt and wrath.
verses.Esth.1.19: If it please the king, let there go forth a royal commandment from him, and let it be written among the laws of the Persians and the Medes, that it be not altered, that Vashti come no more before king Ahasuerus; and let the king give her royal estate unto another that is better than she.
verses.Esth.1.20: And when the king’s decree which he shall make shall be published throughout all his kingdom (for it is great), all the wives will give to their husbands honor, both to great and small.
verses.Esth.1.21: And the saying pleased the king and the princes; and the king did according to the word of Memucan:
verses.Esth.1.22: for he sent letters into all the king’s provinces, into every province according to the writing thereof, and to every people after their language, that every man should bear rule in his own house, and should speak according to the language of his people.
verses.Esth.2.1: After these things, when the wrath of king Ahasuerus was pacified, he remembered Vashti, and what she had done, and what was decreed against her.
verses.Esth.2.2: Then said the king’s servants that ministered unto him, Let there be fair young virgins sought for the king:
verses.Esth.2.3: and let the king appoint officers in all the provinces of his kingdom, that they may gather together all the fair young virgins unto Shushan the palace, to the house of the women, unto the custody of Hegai the king’s chamberlain, keeper of the women; and let their things for purification be given them;
verses.Esth.2.4: and let the maiden that pleaseth the king be queen instead of Vashti. And the thing pleased the king; and he did so.
verses.Esth.2.5: There was a certain Jew in Shushan the palace, whose name was Mordecai, the son of Jair, the son of Shimei, the son of Kish, a Benjamite,
verses.Esth.2.6: who had been carried away from Jerusalem with the captives that had been carried away with Jeconiah king of Judah, whom Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon had carried away.
verses.Esth.2.7: And he brought up Hadassah, that is, Esther, his uncle’s daughter: for she had neither father nor mother, and the maiden was fair and beautiful; and when her father and mother were dead, Mordecai took her for his own daughter.
verses.Esth.2.8: So it came to pass, when the king’s commandment and his decree was heard, and when many maidens were gathered together unto Shushan the palace, to the custody of Hegai, that Esther was taken into the king’s house, to the custody of Hegai, keeper of the women.
verses.Esth.2.9: And the maiden pleased him, and she obtained kindness of him; and he speedily gave her her things for purification, with her portions, and the seven maidens who were meet to be given her out of the king’s house: and he removed her and her maidens to the best place of the house of the women.
verses.Esth.2.10: Esther had not made known her people nor her kindred; for Mordecai had charged her that she should not make it known.
verses.Esth.2.11: And Mordecai walked every day before the court of the women’s house, to know how Esther did, and what would become of her.
verses.Esth.2.12: Now when the turn of every maiden was come to go in to king Ahasuerus, after that it had been done to her according to the law for the women twelve months (for so were the days of their purifications accomplished, to wit, six months with oil of myrrh, and six months with sweet odors and with the things for the purifying of the women),
verses.Esth.2.13: then in this wise came the maiden unto the king: Whatsoever she desired was given her to go with her out of the house of the women unto the king’s house.
verses.Esth.2.14: In the evening she went, and on the morrow she returned into the second house of the women, to the custody of Shaashgaz, the king’s chamberlain, who kept the concubines: she came in unto the king no more, except the king delighted in her, and she were called by name.
verses.Esth.2.15: Now when the turn of Esther, the daughter of Abihail the uncle of Mordecai, who had taken her for his daughter, was come to go in unto the king, she required nothing but what Hegai the king’s chamberlain, the keeper of the women, appointed. And Esther obtained favor in the sight of all them that looked upon her.
verses.Esth.2.16: So Esther was taken unto king Ahasuerus into his house royal in the tenth month, which is the month Tebeth, in the seventh year of his reign.
verses.Esth.2.17: And the king loved Esther above all the women, and she obtained favor and kindness in his sight more than all the virgins; so that he set the royal crown upon her head, and made her queen instead of Vashti.
verses.Esth.2.18: Then the king made a great feast unto all his princes and his servants, even Esther’s feast; and he made a release to the provinces, and gave gifts, according to the bounty of the king.
verses.Esth.2.19: And when the virgins were gathered together the second time, then Mordecai was sitting in the king’s gate.
verses.Esth.2.20: Esther had not yet made known her kindred nor her people; as Mordecai had charged her: for Esther did the commandment of Mordecai, like as when she was brought up with him.
verses.Esth.2.21: In those days, while Mordecai was sitting in the king’s gate, two of the king’s chamberlains, Bigthan and Teresh, of those that kept the threshold, were wroth, and sought to lay hands on the king Ahasuerus.
verses.Esth.2.22: And the thing became known to Mordecai, who showed it unto Esther the queen; and Esther told the king thereof in Mordecai’s name.
verses.Esth.2.23: And when inquisition was made of the matter, and it was found to be so, they were both hanged on a tree: and it was written in the book of the chronicles before the king.
verses.Esth.3.1: After these things did king Ahasuerus promote Haman the son of Hammedatha the Agagite, and advanced him, and set his seat above all the princes that were with him.
verses.Esth.3.2: And all the king’s servants, that were in the king’s gate, bowed down, and did reverence to Haman; for the king had so commanded concerning him. But Mordecai bowed not down, nor did him reverence.
verses.Esth.3.3: Then the king’s servants, that were in the king’s gate, said unto Mordecai, Why transgressest thou the king’s commandment?
verses.Esth.3.4: Now it came to pass, when they spake daily unto him, and he hearkened not unto them, that they told Haman, to see whether Mordecai’s matters would stand: for he had told them that he was a Jew.
verses.Esth.3.5: And when Haman saw that Mordecai bowed not down, nor did him reverence, then was Haman full of wrath.
verses.Esth.3.6: But he thought scorn to lay hands on Mordecai alone; for they had made known to him the people of Mordecai: wherefore Haman sought to destroy all the Jews that were throughout the whole kingdom of Ahasuerus, even the people of Mordecai.
verses.Esth.3.7: In the first month, which is the month Nisan, in the twelfth year of king Ahasuerus, they cast Pur, that is, the lot, before Haman from day to day, and from month to month, to the twelfth month, which is the month Adar.
verses.Esth.3.8: And Haman said unto king Ahasuerus, There is a certain people scattered abroad and dispersed among the peoples in all the provinces of thy kingdom; and their laws are diverse from those of every people; neither keep they the king’s laws: therefore it is not for the king’s profit to suffer them.
verses.Esth.3.9: If it please the king, let it be written that they be destroyed: and I will pay ten thousand talents of silver into the hands of those that have the charge of the king’s business, to bring it into the king’s treasuries.
verses.Esth.3.10: And the king took his ring from his hand, and gave it unto Haman the son of Hammedatha the Agagite, the Jews’ enemy.
verses.Esth.3.11: And the king said unto Haman, The silver is given to thee, the people also, to do with them as it seemeth good to thee.
verses.Esth.3.12: Then were the king’s scribes called in the first month, on the thirteenth day thereof; and there was written according to all that Haman commanded unto the king’s satraps, and to the governors that were over every province, and to the princes of every people, to every province according to the writing thereof, and to every people after their language; in the name of king Ahasuerus was it written, and it was sealed with the king’s ring.
verses.Esth.3.13: And letters were sent by posts into all the king’s provinces, to destroy, to slay, and to cause to perish, all Jews, both young and old, little children and women, in one day, even upon the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, which is the month Adar, and to take the spoil of them for a prey.
verses.Esth.3.14: A copy of the writing, that the decree should be given out in every province, was published unto all the peoples, that they should be ready against that day.
verses.Esth.3.15: The posts went forth in haste by the king’s commandment, and the decree was given out in Shushan the palace. And the king and Haman sat down to drink; but the city of Shushan was perplexed.
verses.Esth.4.1: Now when Mordecai knew all that was done, Mordecai rent his clothes, and put on sackcloth with ashes, and went out into the midst of the city, and cried with a loud and a bitter cry;
verses.Esth.4.2: and he came even before the king’s gate: for none might enter within the king’s gate clothed with sackcloth.
verses.Esth.4.3: And in every province, whithersoever the king’s commandment and his decree came, there was great mourning among the Jews, and fasting, and weeping, and wailing; and many lay in sackcloth and ashes.
verses.Esth.4.4: And Esther’s maidens and her chamberlains came and told it her; and the queen was exceedingly grieved: and she sent raiment to clothe Mordecai, and to take his sackcloth from off him; but he received it not.
verses.Esth.4.5: Then called Esther for Hathach, one of the king’s chamberlains, whom he had appointed to attend upon her, and charged him to go to Mordecai, to know what this was, and why it was.
verses.Esth.4.6: So Hathach went forth to Mordecai unto the broad place of the city, which was before the king’s gate.
verses.Esth.4.7: And Mordecai told him of all that had happened unto him, and the exact sum of the money that Haman had promised to pay to the king’s treasuries for the Jews, to destroy them.
verses.Esth.4.8: Also he gave him the copy of the writing of the decree that was given out in Shushan to destroy them, to show it unto Esther, and to declare it unto her, and to charge her that she should go in unto the king, to make supplication unto him, and to make request before him, for her people.
verses.Esth.4.9: And Hathach came and told Esther the words of Mordecai.
verses.Esth.4.10: Then Esther spake unto Hathach, and gave him a message unto Mordecai, saying:
verses.Esth.4.11: All the king’s servants, and the people of the king’s provinces, do know, that whosoever, whether man or woman, shall come unto the king into the inner court, who is not called, there is one law for him, that he be put to death, except those to whom the king shall hold out the golden sceptre, that he may live: but I have not been called to come in unto the king these thirty days.
verses.Esth.4.12: And they told to Mordecai Esther’s words.
verses.Esth.4.13: Then Mordecai bade them return answer unto Esther, Think not with thyself that thou shalt escape in the king’s house, more than all the Jews.
verses.Esth.4.14: For if thou altogether holdest thy peace at this time, then will relief and deliverance arise to the Jews from another place, but thou and thy father’s house will perish: and who knoweth whether thou art not come to the kingdom for such a time as this?
verses.Esth.4.15: Then Esther bade them return answer unto Mordecai,
verses.Esth.4.16: Go, gather together all the Jews that are present in Shushan, and fast ye for me, and neither eat nor drink three days, night or day: I also and my maidens will fast in like manner; and so will I go in unto the king, which is not according to the law: and if I perish, I perish.
verses.Esth.4.17: So Mordecai went his way, and did according to all that Esther had commanded him.
verses.Esth.5.1: Now it came to pass on the third day, that Esther put on her royal apparel, and stood in the inner court of the king’s house, over against the king’s house: and the king sat upon his royal throne in the royal house, over against the entrance of the house.
verses.Esth.5.2: And it was so, when the king saw Esther the queen standing in the court, that she obtained favor in his sight; and the king held out to Esther the golden sceptre that was in his hand. So Esther drew near, and touched the top of the sceptre.
verses.Esth.5.3: Then said the king unto her, What wilt thou, queen Esther? and what is thy request? it shall be given thee even to the half of the kingdom.
verses.Esth.5.4: And Esther said, If it seem good unto the king, let the king and Haman come this day unto the banquet that I have prepared for him.
verses.Esth.5.5: Then the king said, Cause Haman to make haste, that it may be done as Esther hath said. So the king and Haman came to the banquet that Esther had prepared.
verses.Esth.5.6: And the king said unto Esther at the banquet of wine, What is thy petition? and it shall be granted thee: and what is thy request? even to the half of the kingdom it shall be performed.
verses.Esth.5.7: Then answered Esther, and said, My petition and my request is:
verses.Esth.5.8: If I have found favor in the sight of the king, and if it please the king to grant my petition, and to perform my request, let the king and Haman come to the banquet that I shall prepare for them, and I will do to-morrow as the king hath said.
verses.Esth.5.9: Then went Haman forth that day joyful and glad of heart: but when Haman saw Mordecai in the king’s gate, that he stood not up nor moved for him, he was filled with wrath against Mordecai.
verses.Esth.5.10: Nevertheless Haman refrained himself, and went home; and he sent and fetched his friends and Zeresh his wife.
verses.Esth.5.11: And Haman recounted unto them the glory of his riches, and the multitude of his children, and all the things wherein the king had promoted him, and how he had advanced him above the princes and servants of the king.
verses.Esth.5.12: Haman said moreover, Yea, Esther the queen did let no man come in with the king unto the banquet that she had prepared but myself; and to-morrow also am I invited by her together with the king.
verses.Esth.5.13: Yet all this availeth me nothing, so long as I see Mordecai the Jew sitting at the king’s gate.
verses.Esth.5.14: Then said Zeresh his wife and all his friends unto him, Let a gallows be made fifty cubits high, and in the morning speak thou unto the king that Mordecai may be hanged thereon: then go thou in merrily with the king unto the banquet. And the thing pleased Haman; and he caused the gallows to be made.
verses.Esth.6.1: On that night could not the king sleep; and he commanded to bring the book of records of the chronicles, and they were read before the king.
verses.Esth.6.2: And it was found written, that Mordecai had told of Bigthana and Teresh, two of the king’s chamberlains, of those that kept the threshold, who had sought to lay hands on the king Ahasuerus.
verses.Esth.6.3: And the king said, What honor and dignity hath been bestowed on Mordecai for this? Then said the king’s servants that ministered unto him, There is nothing done for him.
verses.Esth.6.4: And the king said, Who is in the court? Now Haman was come into the outward court of the king’s house, to speak unto the king to hang Mordecai on the gallows that he had prepared for him.
verses.Esth.6.5: And the king’s servants said unto him, Behold, Haman standeth in the court. And the king said, Let him come in.
verses.Esth.6.6: So Haman came in. And the king said unto him, What shall be done unto the man whom the king delighteth to honor? Now Haman said in his heart, To whom would the king delight to do honor more than to myself?
verses.Esth.6.7: And Haman said unto the king, For the man whom the king delighteth to honor,
verses.Esth.6.8: let royal apparel be brought which the king useth to wear, and the horse that the king rideth upon, and on the head of which a crown royal is set:
verses.Esth.6.9: and let the apparel and the horse be delivered to the hand of one of the king’s most noble princes, that they may array the man therewith whom the king delighteth to honor, and cause him to ride on horseback through the street of the city, and proclaim before him, Thus shall it be done to the man whom the king delighteth to honor.
verses.Esth.6.10: Then the king said to Haman, Make haste, and take the apparel and the horse, as thou hast said, and do even so to Mordecai the Jew, that sitteth at the king’s gate: let nothing fail of all that thou hast spoken.
verses.Esth.6.11: Then took Haman the apparel and the horse, and arrayed Mordecai, and caused him to ride through the street of the city, and proclaimed before him, Thus shall it be done unto the man whom the king delighteth to honor.
verses.Esth.6.12: And Mordecai came again to the king’s gate. But Haman hasted to his house, mourning and having his head covered.
verses.Esth.6.13: And Haman recounted unto Zeresh his wife and all his friends everything that had befallen him. Then said his wise men and Zeresh his wife unto him, If Mordecai, before whom thou hast begun to fall, be of the seed of the Jews, thou shalt not prevail against him, but shalt surely fall before him.
verses.Esth.6.14: While they were yet talking with him, came the king’s chamberlains, and hasted to bring Haman unto the banquet that Esther had prepared.
verses.Esth.7.1: So the king and Haman came to banquet with Esther the queen.
verses.Esth.7.2: And the king said again unto Esther on the second day at the banquet of wine, What is thy petition, queen Esther? and it shall be granted thee: and what is thy request? even to the half of the kingdom it shall be performed.
verses.Esth.7.3: Then Esther the queen answered and said, If I have found favor in thy sight, O king, and if it please the king, let my life be given me at my petition, and my people at my request:
verses.Esth.7.4: for we are sold, I and my people, to be destroyed, to be slain, and to perish. But if we had been sold for bondmen and bondwomen, I had held my peace, although the adversary could not have compensated for the king’s damage.
verses.Esth.7.5: Then spake the king Ahasuerus and said unto Esther the queen, Who is he, and where is he, that durst presume in his heart to do so?
verses.Esth.7.6: And Esther said, An adversary and an enemy, even this wicked Haman. Then Haman was afraid before the king and the queen.
verses.Esth.7.7: And the king arose in his wrath from the banquet of wine and went into the palace garden: and Haman stood up to make request for his life to Esther the queen; for he saw that there was evil determined against him by the king.
verses.Esth.7.8: Then the king returned out of the palace garden into the place of the banquet of wine; and Haman was fallen upon the couch whereon Esther was. Then said the king, Will he even force the queen before me in the house? As the word went out of the king’s mouth, they covered Haman’s face.
verses.Esth.7.9: Then said Harbonah, one of the chamberlains that were before the king, Behold also, the gallows fifty cubits high, which Haman hath made for Mordecai, who spake good for the king, standeth in the house of Haman. And the king said, Hang him thereon.
verses.Esth.7.10: So they hanged Haman on the gallows that he had prepared for Mordecai. Then was the king’s wrath pacified.
verses.Esth.8.1: On that day did the king Ahasuerus give the house of Haman the Jews’ enemy unto Esther the queen. And Mordecai came before the king; for Esther had told what he was unto her.
verses.Esth.8.2: And the king took off his ring, which he had taken from Haman, and gave it unto Mordecai. And Esther set Mordecai over the house of Haman.
verses.Esth.8.3: And Esther spake yet again before the king, and fell down at his feet, and besought him with tears to put away the mischief of Haman the Agagite, and his device that he had devised against the Jews.
verses.Esth.8.4: Then the king held out to Esther the golden sceptre. So Esther arose, and stood before the king.
verses.Esth.8.5: And she said, If it please the king, and if I have found favor in his sight, and the thing seem right before the king, and I be pleasing in his eyes, let it be written to reverse the letters devised by Haman, the son of Hammedatha the Agagite, which he wrote to destroy the Jews that are in all the king’s provinces:
verses.Esth.8.6: for how can I endure to see the evil that shall come unto my people? or how can I endure to see the destruction of my kindred?
verses.Esth.8.7: Then the king Ahasuerus said unto Esther the queen and to Mordecai the Jew, Behold, I have given Esther the house of Haman, and him they have hanged upon the gallows, because he laid his hand upon the Jews.
verses.Esth.8.8: Write ye also to the Jews, as it pleaseth you, in the king’s name, and seal it with the king’s ring; for the writing which is written in the king’s name, and sealed with the king’s ring, may no man reverse.
verses.Esth.8.9: Then were the king’s scribes called at that time, in the third month, which is the month Sivan, on the three and twentieth day thereof; and it was written according to all that Mordecai commanded unto the Jews, and to the satraps, and the governors and princes of the provinces which are from India unto Ethiopia, a hundred twenty and seven provinces, unto every province according to the writing thereof, and unto every people after their language, and to the Jews according to their writing, and according to their language.
verses.Esth.8.10: And he wrote in the name of king Ahasuerus, and sealed it with the king’s ring, and sent letters by posts on horseback, riding on swift steeds that were used in the king’s service, bred of the stud:
verses.Esth.8.11: wherein the king granted the Jews that were in every city to gather themselves together, and to stand for their life, to destroy, to slay, and to cause to perish, all the power of the people and province that would assault them, their little ones and women, and to take the spoil of them for a prey,
verses.Esth.8.12: upon one day in all the provinces of king Ahasuerus, namely, upon the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, which is the month Adar.
verses.Esth.8.13: A copy of the writing, that the decree should be given out in every province, was published unto all the peoples, and that the Jews should be ready against that day to avenge themselves on their enemies.
verses.Esth.8.14: So the posts that rode upon swift steeds that were used in the king’s service went out, being hastened and pressed on by the king’s commandment; and the decree was given out in Shushan the palace.
verses.Esth.8.15: And Mordecai went forth from the presence of the king in royal apparel of blue and white, and with a great crown of gold, and with a robe of fine linen and purple: and the city of Shushan shouted and was glad.
verses.Esth.8.16: The Jews had light and gladness, and joy and honor.
verses.Esth.8.17: And in every province, and in every city, whithersoever the king’s commandment and his decree came, the Jews had gladness and joy, a feast and a good day. And many from among the peoples of the land became Jews; for the fear of the Jews was fallen upon them.
verses.Esth.9.1: Now in the twelfth month, which is the month Adar, on the thirteenth day of the same, when the king’s commandment and his decree drew near to be put in execution, on the day that the enemies of the Jews hoped to have rule over them (whereas it was turned to the contrary, that the Jews had rule over them that hated them),
verses.Esth.9.2: the Jews gathered themselves together in their cities throughout all the provinces of the king Ahasuerus, to lay hand on such as sought their hurt: and no man could withstand them; for the fear of them was fallen upon all the peoples.
verses.Esth.9.3: And all the princes of the provinces, and the satraps, and the governors, and they that did the king’s business, helped the Jews; because the fear of Mordecai was fallen upon them.
verses.Esth.9.4: For Mordecai was great in the king’s house, and his fame went forth throughout all the provinces; for the man Mordecai waxed greater and greater.
verses.Esth.9.5: And the Jews smote all their enemies with the stroke of the sword, and with slaughter and destruction, and did what they would unto them that hated them.
verses.Esth.9.6: And in Shushan the palace the Jews slew and destroyed five hundred men.
verses.Esth.9.7: And Parshandatha, and Dalphon, and Aspatha,
verses.Esth.9.8: and Poratha, and Adalia, and Aridatha,
verses.Esth.9.9: and Parmashta, and Arisai, and Aridai, and Vaizatha,
verses.Esth.9.10: the ten sons of Haman the son of Hammedatha, the Jews’ enemy, slew they; but on the spoil they laid not their hand.
verses.Esth.9.11: On that day the number of those that were slain in Shushan the palace was brought before the king.
verses.Esth.9.12: And the king said unto Esther the queen, The Jews have slain and destroyed five hundred men in Shushan the palace, and the ten sons of Haman; what then have they done in the rest of the king’s provinces! Now what is thy petition? and it shall be granted thee: or what is thy request further? and it shall be done.
verses.Esth.9.13: Then said Esther, If it please the king, let it be granted to the Jews that are in Shushan to do to-morrow also according unto this day’s decree, and let Haman’s ten sons be hanged upon the gallows.
verses.Esth.9.14: And the king commanded it so to be done: and a decree was given out in Shushan; and they hanged Haman’s ten sons.
verses.Esth.9.15: And the Jews that were in Shushan gathered themselves together on the fourteenth day also of the month Adar, and slew three hundred men in Shushan; but on the spoil they laid not their hand.
verses.Esth.9.16: And the other Jews that were in the king’s provinces gathered themselves together, and stood for their lives, and had rest from their enemies, and slew of them that hated them seventy and five thousand; but on the spoil they laid not their hand.
verses.Esth.9.17: This was done on the thirteenth day of the month Adar; and on the fourteenth day of the same they rested, and made it a day of feasting and gladness.
verses.Esth.9.18: But the Jews that were in Shushan assembled together on the thirteenth day thereof, and on the fourteenth thereof; and on the fifteenth day of the same they rested, and made it a day of feasting and gladness.
verses.Esth.9.19: Therefore do the Jews of the villages, that dwell in the unwalled towns, make the fourteenth day of the month Adar a day of gladness and feasting, and a good day, and of sending portions one to another.
verses.Esth.9.20: And Mordecai wrote these things, and sent letters unto all the Jews that were in all the provinces of the king Ahasuerus, both nigh and far,
verses.Esth.9.21: to enjoin them that they should keep the fourteenth day of the month Adar, and the fifteenth day of the same, yearly,
verses.Esth.9.22: as the days wherein the Jews had rest from their enemies, and the month which was turned unto them from sorrow to gladness, and from mourning into a good day; that they should make them days of feasting and gladness, and of sending portions one to another, and gifts to the poor.
verses.Esth.9.23: And the Jews undertook to do as they had begun, and as Mordecai had written unto them;
verses.Esth.9.24: because Haman the son of Hammedatha, the Agagite, the enemy of all the Jews, had plotted against the Jews to destroy them, and had cast Pur, that is the lot, to consume them, and to destroy them;
verses.Esth.9.25: but when the matter came before the king, he commanded by letters that his wicked device, which he had devised against the Jews, should return upon his own head, and that he and his sons should be hanged on the gallows.
verses.Esth.9.26: Wherefore they called these days Purim, after the name of Pur. Therefore because of all the words of this letter, and of that which they had seen concerning this matter, and that which had come unto them,
verses.Esth.9.27: the Jews ordained, and took upon them, and upon their seed, and upon all such as joined themselves unto them, so that it should not fail, that they would keep these two days according to the writing thereof, and according to the appointed time thereof, every year;
verses.Esth.9.28: and that these days should be remembered and kept throughout every generation, every family, every province, and every city; and that these days of Purim should not fail from among the Jews, nor the remembrance of them perish from their seed.
verses.Esth.9.29: Then Esther the queen, the daughter of Abihail, and Mordecai the Jew, wrote with all authority to confirm this second letter of Purim.
verses.Esth.9.30: And he sent letters unto all the Jews, to the hundred twenty and seven provinces of the kingdom of Ahasuerus, with words of peace and truth,
verses.Esth.9.31: to confirm these days of Purim in their appointed times, according as Mordecai the Jew and Esther the queen had enjoined them, and as they had ordained for themselves and for their seed, in the matter of the fastings and their cry.
verses.Esth.9.32: And the commandment of Esther confirmed these matters of Purim; and it was written in the book.
verses.Esth.10.1: And the king Ahasuerus laid a tribute upon the land, and upon the isles of the sea.
verses.Esth.10.2: And all the acts of his power and of his might, and the full account of the greatness of Mordecai, whereunto the king advanced him, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Media and Persia?
verses.Esth.10.3: For Mordecai the Jew was next unto king Ahasuerus, and great among the Jews, and accepted of the multitude of his brethren, seeking the good of his people, and speaking peace to all his seed.
verses.Job.1.1: There was a man in the land of Uz, whose name was Job; and that man was perfect and upright, and one that feared God, and turned away from evil.
verses.Job.1.2: And there were born unto him seven sons and three daughters.
verses.Job.1.3: His substance also was seven thousand sheep, and three thousand camels, and five hundred yoke of oxen, and five hundred she-asses, and a very great household; so that this man was the greatest of all the children of the east.
verses.Job.1.4: And his sons went and held a feast in the house of each one upon his day; and they sent and called for their three sisters to eat and to drink with them.
verses.Job.1.5: And it was so, when the days of their feasting were gone about, that Job sent and sanctified them, and rose up early in the morning, and offered burnt-offerings according to the number of them all: for Job said, It may be that my sons have sinned, and renounced God in their hearts. Thus did Job continually.
verses.Job.1.6: Now it came to pass on the day when the sons of God came to present themselves before Jehovah, that Satan also came among them.
verses.Job.1.7: And Jehovah said unto Satan, Whence comest thou? Then Satan answered Jehovah, and said, From going to and fro in the earth, and from walking up and down in it.
verses.Job.1.8: And Jehovah said unto Satan, Hast thou considered my servant Job? for there is none like him in the earth, a perfect and an upright man, one that feareth God, and turneth away from evil.
verses.Job.1.9: Then Satan answered Jehovah, and said, Doth Job fear God for nought?
verses.Job.1.10: Hast not thou made a hedge about him, and about his house, and about all that he hath, on every side? thou hast blessed the work of his hands, and his substance is increased in the land.
verses.Job.1.11: But put forth thy hand now, and touch all that he hath, and he will renounce thee to thy face.
verses.Job.1.12: And Jehovah said unto Satan, Behold, all that he hath is in thy power; only upon himself put not forth thy hand. So Satan went forth from the presence of Jehovah.
verses.Job.1.13: And it fell on a day when his sons and his daughters were eating and drinking wine in their eldest brother’s house,
verses.Job.1.14: that there came a messenger unto Job, and said, The oxen were plowing, and the asses feeding beside them;
verses.Job.1.15: and the Sabeans fell upon them, and took them away: yea, they have slain the servants with the edge of the sword; and I only am escaped alone to tell thee.
verses.Job.1.16: While he was yet speaking, there came also another, and said, The fire of God is fallen from heaven, and hath burned up the sheep and the servants, and consumed them; and I only am escaped alone to tell thee.
verses.Job.1.17: While he was yet speaking, there came also another, and said, The Chaldeans made three bands, and fell upon the camels, and have taken them away, yea, and slain the servants with the edge of the sword; and I only am escaped alone to tell thee.
verses.Job.1.18: While he was yet speaking, there came also another, and said, Thy sons and thy daughters were eating and drinking wine in their eldest brother’s house;
verses.Job.1.19: and, behold, there came a great wind from the wilderness, and smote the four corners of the house, and it fell upon the young men, and they are dead; and I only am escaped alone to tell thee.
verses.Job.1.20: Then Job arose, and rent his robe, and shaved his head, and fell down upon the ground, and worshipped;
verses.Job.1.21: and he said, Naked came I out of my mother’s womb, and naked shall I return thither: Jehovah gave, and Jehovah hath taken away; blessed be the name of Jehovah.
verses.Job.1.22: In all this Job sinned not, nor charged God foolishly.
verses.Job.2.1: Again it came to pass on the day when the sons of God came to present themselves before Jehovah, that Satan came also among them to present himself before Jehovah.
verses.Job.2.2: And Jehovah said unto Satan, From whence comest thou? And Satan answered Jehovah, and said, From going to and fro in the earth, and from walking up and down in it.
verses.Job.2.3: And Jehovah said unto Satan, Hast thou considered my servant Job? for there is none like him in the earth, a perfect and an upright man, one that feareth God, and turneth away from evil: and he still holdeth fast his integrity, although thou movedst me against him, to destroy him without cause.
verses.Job.2.4: And Satan answered Jehovah, and said, Skin for skin, yea, all that a man hath will he give for his life.
verses.Job.2.5: But put forth thy hand now, and touch his bone and his flesh, and he will renounce thee to thy face.
verses.Job.2.6: And Jehovah said unto Satan, Behold, he is in thy hand; only spare his life.
verses.Job.2.7: So Satan went forth from the presence of Jehovah, and smote Job with sore boils from the sole of his foot unto his crown.
verses.Job.2.8: And he took him a potsherd to scrape himself therewith; and he sat among the ashes.
verses.Job.2.9: Then said his wife unto him, Dost thou still hold fast thine integrity? renounce God, and die.
verses.Job.2.10: But he said unto her, Thou speakest as one of the foolish women speaketh. What? shall we receive good at the hand of God, and shall we not receive evil? In all this did not Job sin with his lips.
verses.Job.2.11: Now when Job’s three friends heard of all this evil that was come upon him, they came every one from his own place: Eliphaz the Temanite, and Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite; and they made an appointment together to come to bemoan him and to comfort him.
verses.Job.2.12: And when they lifted up their eyes afar off, and knew him not, they lifted up their voice, and wept; and they rent every one his robe, and sprinkled dust upon their heads toward heaven.
verses.Job.2.13: So they sat down with him upon the ground seven days and seven nights, and none spake a word unto him: for they saw that his grief was very great.
verses.Job.3.1: After this opened Job his mouth, and cursed his day.
verses.Job.3.3: Let the day perish wherein I was born, And the night which said, There is a man-child conceived.
verses.Job.3.4: Let that day be darkness; Let not God from above seek for it, Neither let the light shine upon it.
verses.Job.3.5: Let darkness and the shadow of death claim it for their own; Let a cloud dwell upon it; Let all that maketh black the day terrify it.
verses.Job.3.6: As for that night, let thick darkness seize upon it: Let it not rejoice among the days of the year; Let it not come into the number of the months.
verses.Job.3.7: Lo, let that night be barren; Let no joyful voice come therein.
verses.Job.3.8: Let them curse it that curse the day, Who are ready to rouse up leviathan.
verses.Job.3.9: Let the stars of the twilight thereof be dark: Let it look for light, but have none; Neither let it behold the eyelids of the morning:
verses.Job.3.10: Because it shut not up the doors of my mother’s womb, Nor hid trouble from mine eyes.
verses.Job.3.11: Why died I not from the womb? Why did I not give up the ghost when my mother bare me?
verses.Job.3.12: Why did the knees receive me? Or why the breasts, that I should suck?
verses.Job.3.13: For now should I have lain down and been quiet; I should have slept; then had I been at rest,
verses.Job.3.14: With kings and counsellors of the earth, Who built up waste places for themselves;
verses.Job.3.15: Or with princes that had gold, Who filled their houses with silver:
verses.Job.3.16: Or as a hidden untimely birth I had not been, As infants that never saw light.
verses.Job.3.17: There the wicked cease from troubling; And there the weary are at rest.
verses.Job.3.18: There the prisoners are at ease together; They hear not the voice of the taskmaster.
verses.Job.3.19: The small and the great are there: And the servant is free from his master.
verses.Job.3.20: Wherefore is light given to him that is in misery, And life unto the bitter in soul;
verses.Job.3.21: Who long for death, but it cometh not, And dig for it more than for hid treasures;
verses.Job.3.22: Who rejoice exceedingly, And are glad, when they can find the grave?
verses.Job.3.23: Why is light given to a man whose way is hid, And whom God hath hedged in?
verses.Job.3.24: For my sighing cometh before I eat, And my groanings are poured out like water.
verses.Job.3.25: For the thing which I fear cometh upon me, And that which I am afraid of cometh unto me.
verses.Job.3.26: I am not at ease, neither am I quiet, neither have I rest; But trouble cometh.
verses.Job.4.1: Then answered Eliphaz the Temanite, and said,
verses.Job.4.2: If one assay to commune with thee, wilt thou be grieved? But who can withhold himself from speaking?
verses.Job.4.3: Behold, thou hast instructed many, And thou hast strengthened the weak hands.
verses.Job.4.4: Thy words have upholden him that was falling, And thou hast made firm the feeble knees.
verses.Job.4.5: But now it is come unto thee, and thou faintest; It toucheth thee, and thou art troubled.
verses.Job.4.6: Is not thy fear of God thy confidence, And the integrity of thy ways thy hope?
verses.Job.4.7: Remember, I pray thee, who ever perished, being innocent? Or where were the upright cut off?
verses.Job.4.8: According as I have seen, they that plow iniquity, And sow trouble, reap the same.
verses.Job.4.9: By the breath of God they perish, And by the blast of his anger are they consumed.
verses.Job.4.10: The roaring of the lion, and the voice of the fierce lion, And the teeth of the young lions, are broken.
verses.Job.4.11: The old lion perisheth for lack of prey, And the whelps of the lioness are scattered abroad.
verses.Job.4.12: Now a thing was secretly brought to me, And mine ear received a whisper thereof.
verses.Job.4.13: In thoughts from the visions of the night, When deep sleep falleth on men,
verses.Job.4.14: Fear came upon me, and trembling, Which made all my bones to shake.
verses.Job.4.15: Then a spirit passed before my face; The hair of my flesh stood up.
verses.Job.4.16: It stood still, but I could not discern the appearance thereof; A form was before mine eyes: There was silence, and I heard a voice, saying,
verses.Job.4.17: Shall mortal man be more just than God? Shall a man be more pure than his Maker?
verses.Job.4.18: Behold, he putteth no trust in his servants; And his angels he chargeth with folly:
verses.Job.4.19: How much more them that dwell in houses of clay, Whose foundation is in the dust, Who are crushed before the moth!
verses.Job.4.20: Betwixt morning and evening they are destroyed: They perish for ever without any regarding it.
verses.Job.4.21: Is not their tent-cord plucked up within them? They die, and that without wisdom.
verses.Job.5.1: Call now; is there any that will answer thee? And to which of the holy ones wilt thou turn?
verses.Job.5.2: For vexation killeth the foolish man, And jealousy slayeth the silly one.
verses.Job.5.3: I have seen the foolish taking root: But suddenly I cursed his habitation.
verses.Job.5.4: His children are far from safety, And they are crushed in the gate, Neither is there any to deliver them:
verses.Job.5.5: Whose harvest the hungry eateth up, And taketh it even out of the thorns; And the snare gapeth for their substance.
verses.Job.5.6: For affliction cometh not forth from the dust, Neither doth trouble spring out of the ground;
verses.Job.5.7: But man is born unto trouble, As the sparks fly upward.
verses.Job.5.8: But as for me, I would seek unto God, And unto God would I commit my cause;
verses.Job.5.9: Who doeth great things and unsearchable, Marvellous things without number:
verses.Job.5.10: Who giveth rain upon the earth, And sendeth waters upon the fields;
verses.Job.5.11: So that he setteth up on high those that are low, And those that mourn are exalted to safety.
verses.Job.5.12: He frustrateth the devices of the crafty, So that their hands cannot perform their enterprise.
verses.Job.5.13: He taketh the wise in their own craftiness; And the counsel of the cunning is carried headlong.
verses.Job.5.14: They meet with darkness in the day-time, And grope at noonday as in the night.
verses.Job.5.15: But he saveth from the sword of their mouth, Even the needy from the hand of the mighty.
verses.Job.5.16: So the poor hath hope, And iniquity stoppeth her mouth.
verses.Job.5.17: Behold, happy is the man whom God correcteth: Therefore despise not thou the chastening of the Almighty.
verses.Job.5.18: For he maketh sore, and bindeth up; He woundeth, and his hands make whole.
verses.Job.5.19: He will deliver thee in six troubles; Yea, in seven there shall no evil touch thee.
verses.Job.5.20: In famine he will redeem thee from death; And in war from the power of the sword.
verses.Job.5.21: Thou shalt be hid from the scourge of the tongue; Neither shalt thou be afraid of destruction when it cometh.
verses.Job.5.22: At destruction and dearth thou shalt laugh; Neither shalt thou be afraid of the beasts of the earth.
verses.Job.5.23: For thou shalt be in league with the stones of the field; And the beasts of the field shall be at peace with thee.
verses.Job.5.24: And thou shalt know that thy tent is in peace; And thou shalt visit thy fold, and shalt miss nothing.
verses.Job.5.25: Thou shalt know also that thy seed shall be great, And thine offspring as the grass of the earth.
verses.Job.5.26: Thou shalt come to thy grave in a full age, Like as a shock of grain cometh in in its season.
verses.Job.5.27: Lo this, we have searched it, so it is; Hear it, and know thou it for thy good.
verses.Job.6.2: Oh that my vexation were but weighed, And all my calamity laid in the balances!
verses.Job.6.3: For now it would be heavier than the sand of the seas: Therefore have my words been rash.
verses.Job.6.4: For the arrows of the Almighty are within me, The poison whereof my spirit drinketh up: The terrors of God do set themselves in array against me.
verses.Job.6.5: Doth the wild ass bray when he hath grass? Or loweth the ox over his fodder?
verses.Job.6.6: Can that which hath no savor be eaten without salt? Or is there any taste in the white of an egg?
verses.Job.6.7: My soul refuseth to touch them; They are as loathsome food to me.
verses.Job.6.8: Oh that I might have my request; And that God would grant me the thing that I long for!
verses.Job.6.9: Even that it would please God to crush me; That he would let loose his hand, and cut me off!
verses.Job.6.10: And be it still my consolation, Yea, let me exult in pain that spareth not, That I have not denied the words of the Holy One.
verses.Job.6.11: What is my strength, that I should wait? And what is mine end, that I should be patient?
verses.Job.6.12: Is my strength the strength of stones? Or is my flesh of brass?
verses.Job.6.13: Is it not that I have no help in me, And that wisdom is driven quite from me?
verses.Job.6.14: To him that is ready to faint kindness should be showed from his friend; Even to him that forsaketh the fear of the Almighty.
verses.Job.6.15: My brethren have dealt deceitfully as a brook, As the channel of brooks that pass away;
verses.Job.6.16: Which are black by reason of the ice, And wherein the snow hideth itself:
verses.Job.6.17: What time they wax warm, they vanish; When it is hot, they are consumed out of their place.
verses.Job.6.18: The caravans that travel by the way of them turn aside; They go up into the waste, and perish.
verses.Job.6.19: The caravans of Tema looked, The companies of Sheba waited for them.
verses.Job.6.20: They were put to shame because they had hoped; They came thither, and were confounded.
verses.Job.6.21: For now ye are nothing; Ye see a terror, and are afraid.
verses.Job.6.22: Did I say, Give unto me? Or, Offer a present for me of your substance?
verses.Job.6.23: Or, Deliver me from the adversary’s hand? Or, Redeem me from the hand of the oppressors?
verses.Job.6.24: Teach me, and I will hold my peace; And cause me to understand wherein I have erred.
verses.Job.6.25: How forcible are words of uprightness! But your reproof, what doth it reprove?
verses.Job.6.26: Do ye think to reprove words, Seeing that the speeches of one that is desperate are as wind?
verses.Job.6.27: Yea, ye would cast lots upon the fatherless, And make merchandise of your friend.
verses.Job.6.28: Now therefore be pleased to look upon me; For surely I shall not lie to your face.
verses.Job.6.29: Return, I pray you, let there be no injustice; Yea, return again, my cause is righteous.
verses.Job.6.30: Is there injustice on my tongue? Cannot my taste discern mischievous things?
verses.Job.7.1: Is there not a warfare to man upon earth? And are not his days like the days of a hireling?
verses.Job.7.2: As a servant that earnestly desireth the shadow, And as a hireling that looketh for his wages:
verses.Job.7.3: So am I made to possess months of misery, And wearisome nights are appointed to me.
verses.Job.7.4: When I lie down, I say, When shall I arise, and the night be gone? And I am full of tossings to and fro unto the dawning of the day.
verses.Job.7.5: My flesh is clothed with worms and clods of dust; My skin closeth up, and breaketh out afresh.
verses.Job.7.6: My days are swifter than a weaver’s shuttle, And are spent without hope.
verses.Job.7.7: Oh remember that my life is a breath: Mine eye shall no more see good.
verses.Job.7.8: The eye of him that seeth me shall behold me no more; Thine eyes shall be upon me, but I shall not be.
verses.Job.7.9: As the cloud is consumed and vanisheth away, So he that goeth down to Sheol shall come up no more.
verses.Job.7.10: He shall return no more to his house, Neither shall his place know him any more.
verses.Job.7.11: Therefore I will not refrain my mouth; I will speak in the anguish of my spirit; I will complain in the bitterness of my soul.
verses.Job.7.12: Am I a sea, or a sea-monster, That thou settest a watch over me?
verses.Job.7.13: When I say, My bed shall comfort me, My couch shall ease my complaint;
verses.Job.7.14: Then thou scarest me with dreams, And terrifiest me through visions:
verses.Job.7.15: So that my soul chooseth strangling, And death rather than these my bones.
verses.Job.7.16: I loathe my life; I would not live alway: Let me alone; for my days are vanity.
verses.Job.7.17: What is man, that thou shouldest magnify him, And that thou shouldest set thy mind upon him,
verses.Job.7.18: And that thou shouldest visit him every morning, And try him every moment?
verses.Job.7.19: How long wilt thou not look away from me, Nor let me alone till I swallow down my spittle?
verses.Job.7.20: If I have sinned, what do I unto thee, O thou watcher of men? Why hast thou set me as a mark for thee, So that I am a burden to myself?
verses.Job.7.21: And why dost thou not pardon my transgression, and take away mine iniquity? For now shall I lie down in the dust; And thou wilt seek me diligently, but I shall not be.
verses.Job.8.1: Then answered Bildad the Shuhite, and said,
verses.Job.8.2: How long wilt thou speak these things? And how long shall the words of thy mouth be like a mighty wind?
verses.Job.8.3: Doth God pervert justice? Or doth the Almighty pervert righteousness?
verses.Job.8.4: If thy children have sinned against him, And he hath delivered them into the hand of their transgression;
verses.Job.8.5: If thou wouldest seek diligently unto God, And make thy supplication to the Almighty;
verses.Job.8.6: If thou wert pure and upright: Surely now he would awake for thee, And make the habitation of thy righteousness prosperous.
verses.Job.8.7: And though thy beginning was small, Yet thy latter end would greatly increase.
verses.Job.8.8: For inquire, I pray thee, of the former age, And apply thyself to that which their fathers have searched out
verses.Job.8.9: (For we are but of yesterday, and know nothing, Because our days upon earth are a shadow);
verses.Job.8.10: Shall not they teach thee, and tell thee, And utter words out of their heart?
verses.Job.8.11: Can the rush grow up without mire? Can the flag grow without water?
verses.Job.8.12: Whilst it is yet in its greenness, and not cut down, It withereth before any other herb.
verses.Job.8.13: So are the paths of all that forget God; And the hope of the godless man shall perish:
verses.Job.8.14: Whose confidence shall break in sunder, And whose trust is a spider’s web.
verses.Job.8.15: He shall lean upon his house, but it shall not stand: He shall hold fast thereby, but it shall not endure.
verses.Job.8.16: He is green before the sun, And his shoots go forth over his garden.
verses.Job.8.17: His roots are wrapped about the stone -heap, He beholdeth the place of stones.
verses.Job.8.18: If he be destroyed from his place, Then it shall deny him, saying, I have not seen thee.
verses.Job.8.19: Behold, this is the joy of his way; And out of the earth shall others spring.
verses.Job.8.20: Behold, God will not cast away a perfect man, Neither will he uphold the evil-doers.
verses.Job.8.21: He will yet fill thy mouth with laughter, And thy lips with shouting.
verses.Job.8.22: They that hate thee shall be clothed with shame; And the tent of the wicked shall be no more.
verses.Job.9.2: Of a truth I know that it is so: But how can man be just with God?
verses.Job.9.3: If he be pleased to contend with him, He cannot answer him one of a thousand.
verses.Job.9.4: He is wise in heart, and mighty in strength: Who hath hardened himself against him, and prospered?—
verses.Job.9.5: Him that removeth the mountains, and they know it not, When he overturneth them in his anger;
verses.Job.9.6: That shaketh the earth out of its place, And the pillars thereof tremble;
verses.Job.9.7: That commandeth the sun, and it riseth not, And sealeth up the stars;
verses.Job.9.8: That alone stretcheth out the heavens, And treadeth upon the waves of the sea;
verses.Job.9.9: That maketh the Bear, Orion, and the Pleiades, And the chambers of the south;
verses.Job.9.10: That doeth great things past finding out, Yea, marvellous things without number.
verses.Job.9.11: Lo, he goeth by me, and I see him not: He passeth on also, but I perceive him not.
verses.Job.9.12: Behold, he seizeth the prey, who can hinder him? Who will say unto him, What doest thou?
verses.Job.9.13: God will not withdraw his anger; The helpers of Rahab do stoop under him.
verses.Job.9.14: How much less shall I answer him, And choose out my words to reason with him?
verses.Job.9.15: Whom, though I were righteous, yet would I not answer; I would make supplication to my judge.
verses.Job.9.16: If I had called, and he had answered me, Yet would I not believe that he hearkened unto my voice.
verses.Job.9.17: For he breaketh me with a tempest, And multiplieth my wounds without cause.
verses.Job.9.18: He will not suffer me to take my breath, But filleth me with bitterness.
verses.Job.9.19: If we speak of strength, lo, he is mighty! And if of justice, Who, saith he, will summon me?
verses.Job.9.20: Though I be righteous, mine own mouth shall condemn me: Though I be perfect, it shall prove me perverse.
verses.Job.9.21: I am perfect; I regard not myself; I despise my life.
verses.Job.9.22: It is all one; therefore I say, He destroyeth the perfect and the wicked.
verses.Job.9.23: If the scourge slay suddenly, He will mock at the trial of the innocent.
verses.Job.9.24: The earth is given into the hand of the wicked; He covereth the faces of the judges thereof: If it be not he, who then is it?
verses.Job.9.25: Now my days are swifter than a post: They flee away, they see no good.
verses.Job.9.26: They are passed away as the swift ships; As the eagle that swoopeth on the prey.
verses.Job.9.27: If I say, I will forget my complaint, I will put off my sad countenance, and be of good cheer;
verses.Job.9.28: I am afraid of all my sorrows, I know that thou wilt not hold me innocent.
verses.Job.9.29: I shall be condemned; Why then do I labor in vain?
verses.Job.9.30: If I wash myself with snow water, And make my hands never so clean;
verses.Job.9.31: Yet wilt thou plunge me in the ditch, And mine own clothes shall abhor me.
verses.Job.9.32: For he is not a man, as I am, that I should answer him, That we should come together in judgment.
verses.Job.9.33: There is no umpire betwixt us, That might lay his hand upon us both.
verses.Job.9.34: Let him take his rod away from me, And let not his terror make me afraid:
verses.Job.9.35: Then would I speak, and not fear him; For I am not so in myself.
verses.Job.10.1: My soul is weary of my life; I will give free course to my complaint; I will speak in the bitterness of my soul.
verses.Job.10.2: I will say unto God, Do not condemn me; Show me wherefore thou contendest with me.
verses.Job.10.3: Is it good unto thee that thou shouldest oppress, That thou shouldest despise the work of thy hands, And shine upon the counsel of the wicked?
verses.Job.10.4: Hast thou eyes of flesh? Or seest thou as man seeth?
verses.Job.10.5: Are thy days as the days of man, Or thy years as man’s days,
verses.Job.10.6: That thou inquirest after mine iniquity, And searchest after my sin,
verses.Job.10.7: Although thou knowest that I am not wicked, And there is none that can deliver out of thy hand?
verses.Job.10.8: Thy hands have framed me and fashioned me Together round about; yet thou dost destroy me.
verses.Job.10.9: Remember, I beseech thee, that thou hast fashioned me as clay; And wilt thou bring me into dust again?
verses.Job.10.10: Hast thou not poured me out as milk, And curdled me like cheese?
verses.Job.10.11: Thou hast clothed me with skin and flesh, And knit me together with bones and sinews.
verses.Job.10.12: Thou hast granted me life and lovingkindness; And thy visitation hath preserved my spirit.
verses.Job.10.13: Yet these things thou didst hide in thy heart; I know that this is with thee:
verses.Job.10.14: If I sin, then thou markest me, And thou wilt not acquit me from mine iniquity.
verses.Job.10.15: If I be wicked, woe unto me; And if I be righteous, yet shall I not lift up my head; Being filled with ignominy, And looking upon mine affliction.
verses.Job.10.16: And if my head exalt itself, thou huntest me as a lion; And again thou showest thyself marvellous upon me.
verses.Job.10.17: Thou renewest thy witnesses against me, And increasest thine indignation upon me: Changes and warfare are with me.
verses.Job.10.18: Wherefore then hast thou brought me forth out of the womb? I had given up the ghost, and no eye had seen me.
verses.Job.10.19: I should have been as though I had not been; I should have been carried from the womb to the grave.
verses.Job.10.20: Are not my days few? cease then, And let me alone, that I may take comfort a little,
verses.Job.10.21: Before I go whence I shall not return, Even to the land of darkness and of the shadow of death;
verses.Job.10.22: The land dark as midnight, The land of the shadow of death, without any order, And where the light is as midnight.
verses.Job.11.1: Then answered Zophar the Naamathite, and said,
verses.Job.11.2: Should not the multitude of words be answered? And should a man full of talk be justified?
verses.Job.11.3: Should thy boastings make men hold their peace? And when thou mockest, shall no man make thee ashamed?
verses.Job.11.4: For thou sayest, My doctrine is pure, And I am clean in thine eyes.
verses.Job.11.5: But oh that God would speak, And open his lips against thee,
verses.Job.11.6: And that he would show thee the secrets of wisdom! For he is manifold in understanding. Know therefore that God exacteth of thee less than thine iniquity deserveth.
verses.Job.11.7: Canst thou by searching find out God? Canst thou find out the Almighty unto perfection?
verses.Job.11.8: It is high as heaven; what canst thou do? Deeper than Sheol; what canst thou know?
verses.Job.11.9: The measure thereof is longer than the earth, And broader than the sea.
verses.Job.11.10: If he pass through, and shut up, And call unto judgment, then who can hinder him?
verses.Job.11.11: For he knoweth false men: He seeth iniquity also, even though he consider it not.
verses.Job.11.12: But vain man is void of understanding, Yea, man is born as a wild ass’s colt.
verses.Job.11.13: If thou set thy heart aright, And stretch out thy hands toward him;
verses.Job.11.14: If iniquity be in thy hand, put it far away, And let not unrighteousness dwell in thy tents.
verses.Job.11.15: Surely then shalt thou lift up thy face without spot; Yea, thou shalt be stedfast, and shalt not fear:
verses.Job.11.16: For thou shalt forget thy misery; Thou shalt remember it as waters that are passed away,
verses.Job.11.17: And thy life shall be clearer than the noonday; Though there be darkness, it shall be as the morning.
verses.Job.11.18: And thou shalt be secure, because there is hope; Yea, thou shalt search about thee, and shalt take thy rest in safety.
verses.Job.11.19: Also thou shalt lie down, and none shall make thee afraid; Yea, many shall make suit unto thee.
verses.Job.11.20: But the eyes of the wicked shall fail, And they shall have no way to flee; And their hope shall be the giving up of the ghost.
verses.Job.12.2: No doubt but ye are the people, And wisdom shall die with you.
verses.Job.12.3: But I have understanding as well as you; I am not inferior to you: Yea, who knoweth not such things as these?
verses.Job.12.4: I am as one that is a laughing-stock to his neighbor, I who called upon God, and he answered: The just, the perfect man is a laughing-stock.
verses.Job.12.5: In the thought of him that is at ease there is contempt for misfortune; It is ready for them whose foot slippeth.
verses.Job.12.6: The tents of robbers prosper, And they that provoke God are secure; Into whose hand God bringeth abundantly.
verses.Job.12.7: But ask now the beasts, and they shall teach thee; And the birds of the heavens, and they shall tell thee:
verses.Job.12.8: Or speak to the earth, and it shall teach thee; And the fishes of the sea shall declare unto thee.
verses.Job.12.9: Who knoweth not in all these, That the hand of Jehovah hath wrought this,
verses.Job.12.10: In whose hand is the soul of every living thing, And the breath of all mankind?
verses.Job.12.11: Doth not the ear try words, Even as the palate tasteth its food?
verses.Job.12.12: With aged men is wisdom, And in length of days understanding.
verses.Job.12.13: With God is wisdom and might; He hath counsel and understanding.
verses.Job.12.14: Behold, he breaketh down, and it cannot be built again; He shutteth up a man, and there can be no opening.
verses.Job.12.15: Behold, he withholdeth the waters, and they dry up; Again, he sendeth them out, and they overturn the earth.
verses.Job.12.16: With him is strength and wisdom; The deceived and the deceiver are his.
verses.Job.12.17: He leadeth counsellors away stripped, And judges maketh he fools.
verses.Job.12.18: He looseth the bond of kings, And he bindeth their loins with a girdle.
verses.Job.12.19: He leadeth priests away stripped, And overthroweth the mighty.
verses.Job.12.20: He removeth the speech of the trusty, And taketh away the understanding of the elders.
verses.Job.12.21: He poureth contempt upon princes, And looseth the belt of the strong.
verses.Job.12.22: He uncovereth deep things out of darkness, And bringeth out to light the shadow of death.
verses.Job.12.23: He increaseth the nations, and he destroyeth them: He enlargeth the nations, and he leadeth them captive.
verses.Job.12.24: He taketh away understanding from the chiefs of the people of the earth, And causeth them to wander in a wilderness where there is no way.
verses.Job.12.25: They grope in the dark without light; And he maketh them to stagger like a drunken man.
verses.Job.13.1: Lo, mine eye hath seen all this, Mine ear hath heard and understood it.
verses.Job.13.2: What ye know, the same do I know also: I am not inferior unto you.
verses.Job.13.3: Surely I would speak to the Almighty, And I desire to reason with God.
verses.Job.13.4: But ye are forgers of lies; Ye are all physicians of no value.
verses.Job.13.5: Oh that ye would altogether hold your peace! And it would be your wisdom.
verses.Job.13.6: Hear now my reasoning, And hearken to the pleadings of my lips.
verses.Job.13.7: Will ye speak unrighteously for God, And talk deceitfully for him?
verses.Job.13.8: Will ye show partiality to him? Will ye contend for God?
verses.Job.13.9: Is it good that he should search you out? Or as one deceiveth a man, will ye deceive him?
verses.Job.13.10: He will surely reprove you, If ye do secretly show partiality.
verses.Job.13.11: Shall not his majesty make you afraid, And his dread fall upon you?
verses.Job.13.12: Your memorable sayings are proverbs of ashes, Your defences are defences of clay.
verses.Job.13.13: Hold your peace, let me alone, that I may speak; And let come on me what will.
verses.Job.13.14: Wherefore should I take my flesh in my teeth, And put my life in my hand?
verses.Job.13.15: Behold, he will slay me; I have no hope: Nevertheless I will maintain my ways before him.
verses.Job.13.16: This also shall be my salvation, That a godless man shall not come before him.
verses.Job.13.17: Hear diligently my speech, And let my declaration be in your ears.
verses.Job.13.18: Behold now, I have set my cause in order; I know that I am righteous.
verses.Job.13.19: Who is he that will contend with me? For then would I hold my peace and give up the ghost.
verses.Job.13.20: Only do not two things unto me; Then will I not hide myself from thy face:
verses.Job.13.21: Withdraw thy hand far from me; And let not thy terror make me afraid.
verses.Job.13.22: Then call thou, and I will answer; Or let me speak, and answer thou me.
verses.Job.13.23: How many are mine iniquities and sins? Make me to know my transgression and my sin.
verses.Job.13.24: Wherefore hidest thou thy face, And holdest me for thine enemy?
verses.Job.13.25: Wilt thou harass a driven leaf? And wilt thou pursue the dry stubble?
verses.Job.13.26: For thou writest bitter things against me, And makest me to inherit the iniquities of my youth:
verses.Job.13.27: Thou puttest my feet also in the stocks, And markest all my paths; Thou settest a bound to the soles of my feet:
verses.Job.13.28: Though I am like a rotten thing that consumeth, Like a garment that is moth-eaten.
verses.Job.14.1: Man, that is born of a woman, Is of few days, and full of trouble.
verses.Job.14.2: He cometh forth like a flower, and is cut down: He fleeth also as a shadow, and continueth not.
verses.Job.14.3: And dost thou open thine eyes upon such a one, And bringest me into judgment with thee?
verses.Job.14.4: Who can bring a clean thing out of an unclean? not one.
verses.Job.14.5: Seeing his days are determined, The number of his months is with thee, And thou hast appointed his bounds that he cannot pass;
verses.Job.14.6: Look away from him, that he may rest, Till he shall accomplish, as a hireling, his day.
verses.Job.14.7: For there is hope of a tree, If it be cut down, that it will sprout again, And that the tender branch thereof will not cease.
verses.Job.14.8: Though the root thereof wax old in the earth, And the stock thereof die in the ground;
verses.Job.14.9: Yet through the scent of water it will bud, And put forth boughs like a plant.
verses.Job.14.10: But man dieth, and is laid low: Yea, man giveth up the ghost, and where is he?
verses.Job.14.11: As the waters fail from the sea, And the river wasteth and drieth up;
verses.Job.14.12: So man lieth down and riseth not: Till the heavens be no more, they shall not awake, Nor be roused out of their sleep.
verses.Job.14.13: Oh that thou wouldest hide me in Sheol, That thou wouldest keep me secret, until thy wrath be past, That thou wouldest appoint me a set time, and remember me!
verses.Job.14.14: If a man die, shall he live again? All the days of my warfare would I wait, Till my release should come.
verses.Job.14.15: Thou wouldest call, and I would answer thee: Thou wouldest have a desire to the work of thy hands.
verses.Job.14.16: But now thou numberest my steps: Dost thou not watch over my sin?
verses.Job.14.17: My transgression is sealed up in a bag, And thou fastenest up mine iniquity.
verses.Job.14.18: But the mountain falling cometh to nought; And the rock is removed out of its place;
verses.Job.14.19: The waters wear the stones; The overflowings thereof wash away the dust of the earth: So thou destroyest the hope of man.
verses.Job.14.20: Thou prevailest for ever against him, and he passeth; Thou changest his countenance, and sendest him away.
verses.Job.14.21: His sons come to honor, and he knoweth it not; And they are brought low, but he perceiveth it not of them.
verses.Job.14.22: But his flesh upon him hath pain, And his soul within him mourneth.
verses.Job.15.1: Then answered Eliphaz the Temanite, and said,
verses.Job.15.2: Should a wise man make answer with vain knowledge, And fill himself with the east wind?
verses.Job.15.3: Should he reason with unprofitable talk, Or with speeches wherewith he can do no good?
verses.Job.15.4: Yea, thou doest away with fear, And hinderest devotion before God.
verses.Job.15.5: For thine iniquity teacheth thy mouth, And thou choosest the tongue of the crafty.
verses.Job.15.6: Thine own mouth condemneth thee, and not I; Yea, thine own lips testify against thee.
verses.Job.15.7: Art thou the first man that was born? Or wast thou brought forth before the hills?
verses.Job.15.8: Hast thou heard the secret counsel of God? And dost thou limit wisdom to thyself?
verses.Job.15.9: What knowest thou, that we know not? What understandest thou, which is not in us?
verses.Job.15.10: With us are both the gray-headed and the very aged men, Much elder than thy father.
verses.Job.15.11: Are the consolations of God too small for thee, Even the word that is gentle toward thee?
verses.Job.15.12: Why doth thy heart carry thee away? And why do thine eyes flash,
verses.Job.15.13: That against God thou turnest thy spirit, And lettest words go out of thy mouth?
verses.Job.15.14: What is man, that he should be clean? And he that is born of a woman, that he should be righteous?
verses.Job.15.15: Behold, he putteth no trust in his holy ones; Yea, the heavens are not clean in his sight:
verses.Job.15.16: How much less one that is abominable and corrupt, A man that drinketh iniquity like water!
verses.Job.15.17: I will show thee, hear thou me; And that which I have seen I will declare
verses.Job.15.18: (Which wise men have told From their fathers, and have not hid it;
verses.Job.15.19: Unto whom alone the land was given, And no stranger passed among them):
verses.Job.15.20: The wicked man travaileth with pain all his days, Even the number of years that are laid up for the oppressor.
verses.Job.15.21: A sound of terrors is in his ears; In prosperity the destroyer shall come upon him.
verses.Job.15.22: He believeth not that he shall return out of darkness, And he is waited for of the sword.
verses.Job.15.23: He wandereth abroad for bread, saying, Where is it? He knoweth that the day of darkness is ready at his hand.
verses.Job.15.24: Distress and anguish make him afraid; They prevail against him, as a king ready to the battle.
verses.Job.15.25: Because he hath stretched out his hand against God, And behaveth himself proudly against the Almighty;
verses.Job.15.26: He runneth upon him with a stiff neck, With the thick bosses of his bucklers;
verses.Job.15.27: Because he hath covered his face with his fatness, And gathered fat upon his loins;
verses.Job.15.28: And he hath dwelt in desolate cities, In houses which no man inhabited, Which were ready to become heaps;
verses.Job.15.29: He shall not be rich, neither shall his substance continue, Neither shall their possessions be extended on the earth.
verses.Job.15.30: He shall not depart out of darkness; The flame shall dry up his branches, And by the breath of God’s mouth shall he go away.
verses.Job.15.31: Let him not trust in vanity, deceiving himself; For vanity shall be his recompense.
verses.Job.15.32: It shall be accomplished before his time, And his branch shall not be green.
verses.Job.15.33: He shall shake off his unripe grape as the vine, And shall cast off his flower as the olive-tree.
verses.Job.15.34: For the company of the godless shall be barren, And fire shall consume the tents of bribery.
verses.Job.15.35: They conceive mischief, and bring forth iniquity, And their heart prepareth deceit.
verses.Job.16.2: I have heard many such things: Miserable comforters are ye all.
verses.Job.16.3: Shall vain words have an end? Or what provoketh thee that thou answerest?
verses.Job.16.4: I also could speak as ye do; If your soul were in my soul’s stead, I could join words together against you, And shake my head at you.
verses.Job.16.5: But I would strengthen you with my mouth, And the solace of my lips would assuage your grief.
verses.Job.16.6: Though I speak, my grief is not assuaged; And though I forbear, what am I eased?
