verses.Ps.50.20: Thou sittest and speakest against thy brother; Thou slanderest thine own mother’s son.
verses.Ps.50.21: These things hast thou done, and I kept silence; Thou thoughtest that I was altogether such a one as thyself: But I will reprove thee, and set them in order before thine eyes.
verses.Ps.50.22: Now consider this, ye that forget God, Lest I tear you in pieces, and there be none to deliver:
verses.Ps.50.23: Whoso offereth the sacrifice of thanksgiving glorifieth me; And to him that ordereth his way aright Will I show the salvation of God.
verses.Ps.51.1: For the Chief Musician. A Psalm of David; when Nathan the prophet came unto him, after he had gone in to Bath-sheba. Have mercy upon me, O God, according to thy lovingkindness: According to the multitude of thy tender mercies blot out my transgressions.
verses.Ps.51.2: Wash me thoroughly from mine iniquity, And cleanse me from my sin.
verses.Ps.51.3: For I know my transgressions; And my sin is ever before me.
verses.Ps.51.4: Against thee, thee only, have I sinned, And done that which is evil in thy sight; That thou mayest be justified when thou speakest, And be clear when thou judgest.
verses.Ps.51.5: Behold, I was brought forth in iniquity; And in sin did my mother conceive me.
verses.Ps.51.6: Behold, thou desirest truth in the inward parts; And in the hidden part thou wilt make me to know wisdom.
verses.Ps.51.7: Purify me with hyssop, and I shall be clean: Wash me, and I shall be whiter than snow.
verses.Ps.51.8: Make me to hear joy and gladness, That the bones which thou hast broken may rejoice.
verses.Ps.51.9: Hide thy face from my sins, And blot out all mine iniquities.
verses.Ps.51.10: Create in me a clean heart, O God; And renew a right spirit within me.
verses.Ps.51.11: Cast me not away from thy presence; And take not thy holy Spirit from me.
verses.Ps.51.12: Restore unto me the joy of thy salvation; And uphold me with a willing spirit.
verses.Ps.51.13: Then will I teach transgressors thy ways; And sinners shall be converted unto thee.
verses.Ps.51.14: Deliver me from bloodguiltiness, O God, thou God of my salvation; And my tongue shall sing aloud of thy righteousness.
verses.Ps.51.15: O Lord, open thou my lips; And my mouth shall show forth thy praise.
verses.Ps.51.16: For thou delightest not in sacrifice; else would I give it: Thou hast no pleasure in burnt-offering.
verses.Ps.51.17: The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit: A broken and a contrite heart, O God, thou wilt not despise.
verses.Ps.51.18: Do good in thy good pleasure unto Zion: Build thou the walls of Jerusalem.
verses.Ps.51.19: Then wilt thou delight in the sacrifices of righteousness, In burnt-offering and whole burnt-offering: Then will they offer bullocks upon thine altar.
verses.Ps.52.1: For the Chief Musician. Maschil of David; when Doeg the Edomite came and told Saul, and said unto him, David is come to the house of Ahimelech. Why boastest thou thyself in mischief, O mighty man? The lovingkindness of God endureth continually.
verses.Ps.52.2: Thy tongue deviseth very wickedness, Like a sharp razor, working deceitfully.
verses.Ps.52.3: Thou lovest evil more than good, And lying rather than to speak righteousness. [Selah
verses.Ps.52.4: Thou lovest all devouring words, O thou deceitful tongue.
verses.Ps.52.5: God will likewise destroy thee for ever; He will take thee up, and pluck thee out of thy tent, And root thee out of the land of the living. [Selah
verses.Ps.52.6: The righteous also shall see it, and fear, And shall laugh at him, saying,
verses.Ps.52.7: Lo, this is the man that made not God his strength, But trusted in the abundance of his riches, And strengthened himself in his wickedness.
verses.Ps.52.8: But as for me, I am like a green olive-tree in the house of God: I trust in the lovingkindness of God for ever and ever.
verses.Ps.52.9: I will give thee thanks for ever, because thou hast done it; And I will hope in thy name, for it is good, in the presence of thy saints.
verses.Ps.53.1: For the Chief Musician; set to Mahalath. Maschil of David. The fool hath said in his heart, There is no God. Corrupt are they, and have done abominable iniquity; There is none that doeth good.
verses.Ps.53.2: God looked down from heaven upon the children of men, To see if there were any that did understand, That did seek after God.
verses.Ps.53.3: Every one of them is gone back; they are together become filthy; There is none that doeth good, no, not one.
verses.Ps.53.4: Have the workers of iniquity no knowledge, Who eat up my people as they eat bread, And call not upon God?
verses.Ps.53.5: There were they in great fear, where no fear was; For God hath scattered the bones of him that encampeth against thee: Thou hast put them to shame, because God hath rejected them.
verses.Ps.53.6: Oh that the salvation of Israel were come out of Zion! When God bringeth back the captivity of his people, Then shall Jacob rejoice, and Israel shall be glad.
verses.Ps.54.1: For the Chief Musician; on stringed instruments. Maschil of David; when the Ziphites came and said to Saul, Doth not David hide himself with us? Save me, O God, by thy name, And judge me in thy might.
verses.Ps.54.2: Hear my prayer, O God; Give ear to the words of my mouth.
verses.Ps.54.3: For strangers are risen up against me, And violent men have sought after my soul: They have not set God before them. [Selah
verses.Ps.54.4: Behold, God is my helper: The Lord is of them that uphold my soul.
verses.Ps.54.5: He will requite the evil unto mine enemies: Destroy thou them in thy truth.
verses.Ps.54.6: With a freewill-offering will I sacrifice unto thee: I will give thanks unto thy name, O Jehovah, for it is good.
verses.Ps.54.7: For he hath delivered me out of all trouble; And mine eye hath seen my desire upon mine enemies.
verses.Ps.55.1: For the Chief Musician; on stringed instruments. Maschil of David. Give ear to my prayer, O God; And hide not thyself from my supplication.
verses.Ps.55.2: Attend unto me, and answer me: I am restless in my complaint, and moan,
verses.Ps.55.3: Because of the voice of the enemy, Because of the oppression of the wicked; For they cast iniquity upon me, And in anger they persecute me.
verses.Ps.55.4: My heart is sore pained within me: And the terrors of death are fallen upon me.
verses.Ps.55.5: Fearfulness and trembling are come upon me, And horror hath overwhelmed me.
verses.Ps.55.6: And I said, Oh that I had wings like a dove! Then would I fly away, and be at rest.
verses.Ps.55.7: Lo, then would I wander far off, I would lodge in the wilderness. [Selah
verses.Ps.55.8: I would haste me to a shelter From the stormy wind and tempest.
verses.Ps.55.9: Destroy, O Lord, and divide their tongue; For I have seen violence and strife in the city.
verses.Ps.55.10: Day and night they go about it upon the walls thereof: Iniquity also and mischief are in the midst of it.
verses.Ps.55.11: Wickedness is in the midst thereof: Oppression and guile depart not from its streets.
verses.Ps.55.12: For it was not an enemy that reproached me; Then I could have borne it: Neither was it he that hated me that did magnify himself against me; Then I would have hid myself from him:
verses.Ps.55.13: But it was thou, a man mine equal, My companion, and my familiar friend.
verses.Ps.55.14: We took sweet counsel together; We walked in the house of God with the throng.
verses.Ps.55.15: Let death come suddenly upon them, Let them go down alive into Sheol; For wickedness is in their dwelling, in the midst of them.
verses.Ps.55.16: As for me, I will call upon God; And Jehovah will save me.
verses.Ps.55.17: Evening, and morning, and at noonday, will I complain, and moan; And he will hear my voice.
verses.Ps.55.18: He hath redeemed my soul in peace from the battle that was against me; For they were many that strove with me.
verses.Ps.55.19: God will hear, and answer them, Even he that abideth of old, [Selah The men who have no changes, And who fear not God.
verses.Ps.55.20: He hath put forth his hands against such as were at peace with him: He hath profaned his covenant.
verses.Ps.55.21: His mouth was smooth as butter, But his heart was war: His words were softer than oil, Yet were they drawn swords.
verses.Ps.55.22: Cast thy burden upon Jehovah, and he will sustain thee: He will never suffer the righteous to be moved.
verses.Ps.55.23: But thou, O God, wilt bring them down into the pit of destruction: Bloodthirsty and deceitful men shall not live out half their days; But I will trust in thee.
verses.Ps.56.1: For the Chief Musician; set to Jonath elem rehokim. A Psalm of David. Michtam; when the Philistines took him in Gath. Be merciful unto me, O God; for man would swallow me up: All the day long he fighting oppresseth me.
verses.Ps.56.2: Mine enemies would swallow me up all the day long; For they are many that fight proudly against me.
verses.Ps.56.3: What time I am afraid, I will put my trust in thee.
verses.Ps.56.4: In God (I will praise his word), In God have I put my trust, I will not be afraid; What can flesh do unto me?
verses.Ps.56.5: All the day long they wrest my words: All their thoughts are against me for evil.
verses.Ps.56.6: They gather themselves together, they hide themselves, They mark my steps, Even as they have waited for my soul.
verses.Ps.56.7: Shall they escape by iniquity? In anger cast down the peoples, O God.
verses.Ps.56.8: Thou numberest my wanderings: Put thou my tears into thy bottle; Are they not in thy book?
verses.Ps.56.9: Then shall mine enemies turn back in the day that I call: This I know, that God is for me.
verses.Ps.56.10: In God (I will praise his word), In Jehovah (I will praise his word),
verses.Ps.56.11: In God have I put my trust, I will not be afraid; What can man do unto me?
verses.Ps.56.12: Thy vows are upon me, O God: I will render thank-offerings unto thee.
verses.Ps.56.13: For thou hast delivered my soul from death: Hast thou not delivered my feet from falling, That I may walk before God In the light of the living?
verses.Ps.57.1: For the Chief Musician; set to Al-tashheth. A Psalm of David. Michtam; when he fled from Saul, in the cave. Be merciful unto me, O God, be merciful unto me; For my soul taketh refuge in thee: Yea, in the shadow of thy wings will I take refuge, Until these calamities be overpast.
verses.Ps.57.2: I will cry unto God Most High, Unto God that performeth all things for me.
verses.Ps.57.3: He will send from heaven, and save me, When he that would swallow me up reproacheth; [Selah God will send forth his lovingkindness and his truth.
verses.Ps.57.4: My soul is among lions; I lie among them that are set on fire, Even the sons of men, whose teeth are spears and arrows, And their tongue a sharp sword.
verses.Ps.57.5: Be thou exalted, O God, above the heavens; Let thy glory be above all the earth.
verses.Ps.57.6: They have prepared a net for my steps; My soul is bowed down: They have digged a pit before me; They are fallen into the midst thereof themselves. [Selah
verses.Ps.57.7: My heart is fixed, O God, my heart is fixed: I will sing, yea, I will sing praises.
verses.Ps.57.8: Awake up, my glory; awake, psaltery and harp: I myself will awake right early.
verses.Ps.57.9: I will give thanks unto thee, O Lord, among the peoples: I will sing praises unto thee among the nations.
verses.Ps.57.10: For thy lovingkindness is great unto the heavens, And thy truth unto the skies.
verses.Ps.57.11: Be thou exalted, O God, above the heavens; Let thy glory be above all the earth.
verses.Ps.58.1: For the Chief Musician; set to Al-tashheth. A Psalm of David. Michtam. Do ye indeed in silence speak righteousness? Do ye judge uprightly, O ye sons of men?
verses.Ps.58.2: Nay, in heart ye work wickedness; Ye weigh out the violence of your hands in the earth.
verses.Ps.58.3: The wicked are estranged from the womb: They go astray as soon as they are born, speaking lies.
verses.Ps.58.4: Their poison is like the poison of a serpent: They are like the deaf adder that stoppeth her ear,
verses.Ps.58.5: Which hearkeneth not to the voice of charmers, Charming never so wisely.
verses.Ps.58.6: Break their teeth, O God, in their mouth: Break out the great teeth of the young lions, O Jehovah.
verses.Ps.58.7: Let them melt away as water that runneth apace: When he aimeth his arrows, let them be as though they were cut off.
verses.Ps.58.8: Let them be as a snail which melteth and passeth away, Like the untimely birth of a woman, that hath not seen the sun.
verses.Ps.58.9: Before your pots can feel the thorns, He will take them away with a whirlwind, the green and the burning alike.
verses.Ps.58.10: The righteous shall rejoice when he seeth the vengeance: He shall wash his feet in the blood of the wicked;
verses.Ps.58.11: So that men shall say, Verily there is a reward for the righteous: Verily there is a God that judgeth in the earth.
verses.Ps.59.1: For the Chief Musician; set to Al-tashheth. A Psalm of David. Michtam; when Saul sent, and they watched the house to kill him. Deliver me from mine enemies, O my God: Set me on high from them that rise up against me.
verses.Ps.59.2: Deliver me from the workers of iniquity, And save me from the bloodthirsty men.
verses.Ps.59.3: For, lo, they lie in wait for my soul; The mighty gather themselves together against me: Not for my transgression, nor for my sin, O Jehovah.
verses.Ps.59.4: They run and prepare themselves without my fault: Awake thou to help me, and behold.
verses.Ps.59.5: Even thou, O Jehovah God of hosts, the God of Israel, Arise to visit all the nations: Be not merciful to any wicked transgressors. [Selah
verses.Ps.59.6: They return at evening, they howl like a dog, And go round about the city.
verses.Ps.59.7: Behold, they belch out with their mouth; Swords are in their lips: For who, say they, doth hear?
verses.Ps.59.8: But thou, O Jehovah, wilt laugh at them; Thou wilt have all the nations in derision.
verses.Ps.59.9: Because of his strength I will give heed unto thee; For God is my high tower.
verses.Ps.59.10: My God with his lovingkindness will meet me: God will let me see my desire upon mine enemies.
verses.Ps.59.11: Slay them not, lest my people forget: Scatter them by thy power, and bring them down, O Lord our shield.
verses.Ps.59.12: For the sin of their mouth, and the words of their lips, Let them even be taken in their pride, And for cursing and lying which they speak.
verses.Ps.59.13: Consume them in wrath, consume them, so that they shall be no more: And let them know that God ruleth in Jacob, Unto the ends of the earth. [Selah
verses.Ps.59.14: And at evening let them return, let them howl like a dog, And go round about the city.
verses.Ps.59.15: They shall wander up and down for food, And tarry all night if they be not satisfied.
verses.Ps.59.16: But I will sing of thy strength; Yea, I will sing aloud of thy lovingkindness in the morning: For thou hast been my high tower, And a refuge in the day of my distress.
verses.Ps.59.17: Unto thee, O my strength, will I sing praises: For God is my high tower, the God of my mercy.
verses.Ps.60.1: For the Chief Musician; set to Shushan Eduth. Michtam of David, to teach; when he strove with Aram-naharaim and with Aram-zobah, and Joab returned, and smote of Edom in the Valley of Salt twelve thousand. O God thou hast cast us off, thou hast broken us down; Thou hast been angry; oh restore us again.
verses.Ps.60.2: Thou hast made the land to tremble; thou hast rent it: Heal the breaches thereof; for it shaketh.
verses.Ps.60.3: Thou hast showed thy people hard things: Thou hast made us to drink the wine of staggering.
verses.Ps.60.4: Thou hast given a banner to them that fear thee, That it may be displayed because of the truth. [Selah
verses.Ps.60.5: That thy beloved may be delivered, Save with thy right hand, and answer us.
verses.Ps.60.6: God hath spoken in his holiness: I will exult; I will divide Shechem, and mete out the valley of Succoth.
verses.Ps.60.7: Gilead is mine, and Manasseh is mine; Ephraim also is the defence of my head; Judah is my sceptre.
verses.Ps.60.8: Moab is my washpot; Upon Edom will I cast my shoe: Philistia, shout thou because of me.
verses.Ps.60.9: Who will bring me into the strong city? Who hath led me unto Edom?
verses.Ps.60.10: Hast not thou, O God, cast us off? And thou goest not forth, O God, with our hosts.
verses.Ps.60.11: Give us help against the adversary; For vain is the help of man.
verses.Ps.60.12: Through God we shall do valiantly; For he it is that will tread down our adversaries.
verses.Ps.61.1: For the Chief Musician; on a stringed instrument. A Psalm of David. Hear my cry, O God; Attend unto my prayer.
verses.Ps.61.2: From the end of the earth will I call unto thee, when my heart is overwhelmed: Lead me to the rock that is higher than I.
verses.Ps.61.3: For thou hast been a refuge for me, A strong tower from the enemy.
verses.Ps.61.4: I will dwell in thy tabernacle for ever: I will take refuge in the covert of thy wings. [Selah
verses.Ps.61.5: For thou, O God, hast heard my vows: Thou hast given me the heritage of those that fear thy name.
verses.Ps.61.6: Thou wilt prolong the king’s life; His years shall be as many generations.
verses.Ps.61.7: He shall abide before God for ever: Oh prepare lovingkindness and truth, that they may preserve him.
verses.Ps.61.8: So will I sing praise unto thy name for ever, That I may daily perform my vows.
verses.Ps.62.1: For the Chief Musician; after the manner of Jeduthun. A Psalm of David. My soul waiteth in silence for God only: From him cometh my salvation.
verses.Ps.62.2: He only is my rock and my salvation: He is my high tower; I shall not be greatly moved.
verses.Ps.62.3: How long will ye set upon a man, That ye may slay him, all of you, Like a leaning wall, like a tottering fence?
verses.Ps.62.4: They only consult to thrust him down from his dignity; They delight in lies; They bless with their mouth, but they curse inwardly. [Selah
verses.Ps.62.5: My soul, wait thou in silence for God only; For my expectation is from him.
verses.Ps.62.6: He only is my rock and my salvation: He is my high tower; I shall not be moved.
verses.Ps.62.7: With God is my salvation and my glory: The rock of my strength, and my refuge, is in God.
verses.Ps.62.8: Trust in him at all times, ye people; Pour out your heart before him: God is a refuge for us. [Selah
verses.Ps.62.9: Surely men of low degree are vanity, and men of high degree are a lie: In the balances they will go up; They are together lighter than vanity.
verses.Ps.62.10: Trust not in oppression, And become not vain in robbery: If riches increase, set not your heart thereon.
verses.Ps.62.11: God hath spoken once, Twice have I heard this, That power belongeth unto God.
verses.Ps.62.12: Also unto thee, O Lord, belongeth lovingkindness; For thou renderest to every man according to his work.
verses.Ps.63.1: A Psalm of David, when he was in the wilderness of Judah. O God, thou art my God; earnestly will I seek thee: My soul thirsteth for thee, my flesh longeth for thee, In a dry and weary land, where no water is.
verses.Ps.63.2: So have I looked upon thee in the sanctuary, To see thy power and thy glory.
verses.Ps.63.3: Because thy lovingkindness is better than life, My lips shall praise thee.
verses.Ps.63.4: So will I bless thee while I live: I will lift up my hands in thy name.
verses.Ps.63.5: My soul shall be satisfied as with marrow and fatness; And my mouth shall praise thee with joyful lips;
verses.Ps.63.6: When I remember thee upon my bed, And meditate on thee in the night-watches.
verses.Ps.63.7: For thou hast been my help, And in the shadow of thy wings will I rejoice.
verses.Ps.63.8: My soul followeth hard after thee: Thy right hand upholdeth me.
verses.Ps.63.9: But those that seek my soul, to destroy it, Shall go into the lower parts of the earth.
verses.Ps.63.10: They shall be given over to the power of the sword: They shall be a portion for foxes.
verses.Ps.63.11: But the king shall rejoice in God: Every one that sweareth by him shall glory; For the mouth of them that speak lies shall be stopped.
verses.Ps.64.1: For the Chief Musician. A Psalm of David. Hear my voice, O God, in my complaint: Preserve my life from fear of the enemy.
verses.Ps.64.2: Hide me from the secret counsel of evil-doers, From the tumult of the workers of iniquity;
verses.Ps.64.3: Who have whet their tongue like a sword, And have aimed their arrows, even bitter words,
verses.Ps.64.4: That they may shoot in secret places at the perfect: Suddenly do they shoot at him, and fear not.
verses.Ps.64.5: They encourage themselves in an evil purpose; They commune of laying snares privily; They say, Who will see them?
verses.Ps.64.6: They search out iniquities; We have accomplished, say they, a diligent search: And the inward thought and the heart of every one is deep.
verses.Ps.64.7: But God will shoot at them; With an arrow suddenly shall they be wounded.
verses.Ps.64.8: So they shall be made to stumble, their own tongue being against them: All that see them shall wag the head.
verses.Ps.64.9: And all men shall fear; And they shall declare the work of God, And shall wisely consider of his doing.
verses.Ps.64.10: The righteous shall be glad in Jehovah, and shall take refuge in him; And all the upright in heart shall glory.
verses.Ps.65.1: For the Chief Musician. A Psalm. A Song of David. Praise waiteth for thee, O God, in Zion; And unto thee shall the vow be performed.
verses.Ps.65.2: O thou that hearest prayer, Unto thee shall all flesh come.
verses.Ps.65.3: Iniquities prevail against me: As for our transgressions, thou wilt forgive them.
verses.Ps.65.4: Blessed is the man whom thou choosest, and causest to approach unto thee, That he may dwell in thy courts: We shall be satisfied with the goodness of thy house, Thy holy temple.
verses.Ps.65.5: By terrible things thou wilt answer us in righteousness, O God of our salvation, Thou that art the confidence of all the ends of the earth, And of them that are afar off upon the sea:
verses.Ps.65.6: Who by his strength setteth fast the mountains, Being girded about with might;
verses.Ps.65.7: Who stilleth the roaring of the seas, The roaring of their waves, And the tumult of the peoples.
verses.Ps.65.8: They also that dwell in the uttermost parts are afraid at thy tokens: Thou makest the outgoings of the morning and evening to rejoice.
verses.Ps.65.9: Thou visitest the earth, and waterest it, Thou greatly enrichest it; The river of God is full of water: Thou providest them grain, when thou hast so prepared the earth.
verses.Ps.65.10: Thou waterest its furrows abundantly; Thou settlest the ridges thereof: Thou makest it soft with showers; Thou blessest the springing thereof.
verses.Ps.65.11: Thou crownest the year with thy goodness; And thy paths drop fatness.
verses.Ps.65.12: They drop upon the pastures of the wilderness; And the hills are girded with joy.
verses.Ps.65.13: The pastures are clothed with flocks; The valleys also are covered over with grain; They shout for joy, they also sing.
verses.Ps.66.1: For the Chief Musician. A Song, a Psalm. Make a joyful noise unto God, all the earth:
verses.Ps.66.2: Sing forth the glory of his name: Make his praise glorious.
verses.Ps.66.3: Say unto God, How terrible are thy works! Through the greatness of thy power shall thine enemies submit themselves unto thee.
verses.Ps.66.4: All the earth shall worship thee, And shall sing unto thee; They shall sing to thy name. [Selah
verses.Ps.66.5: Come, and see the works of God; He is terrible in his doing toward the children of men.
verses.Ps.66.6: He turned the sea into dry land; They went through the river on foot: There did we rejoice in him.
verses.Ps.66.7: He ruleth by his might for ever; His eyes observe the nations: Let not the rebellious exalt themselves. [Selah
verses.Ps.66.8: Oh bless our God, ye peoples, And make the voice of his praise to be heard;
verses.Ps.66.9: Who holdeth our soul in life, And suffereth not our feet to be moved.
verses.Ps.66.10: For thou, O God, hast proved us: Thou hast tried us, as silver is tried.
verses.Ps.66.11: Thou broughtest us into the net; Thou layedst a sore burden upon our loins.
verses.Ps.66.12: Thou didst cause men to ride over our heads; We went through fire and through water; But thou broughtest us out into a wealthy place.
verses.Ps.66.13: I will come into thy house with burnt-offerings; I will pay thee my vows,
verses.Ps.66.14: Which my lips uttered, And my mouth spake, when I was in distress.
verses.Ps.66.15: I will offer unto thee burnt-offerings of fatlings, With the incense of rams; I will offer bullocks with goats. [Selah
verses.Ps.66.16: Come, and hear, all ye that fear God, And I will declare what he hath done for my soul.
verses.Ps.66.17: I cried unto him with my mouth, And he was extolled with my tongue.
verses.Ps.66.18: If I regard iniquity in my heart, The Lord will not hear:
verses.Ps.66.19: But verily God hath heard; He hath attended to the voice of my prayer.
verses.Ps.66.20: Blessed be God, Who hath not turned away my prayer, Nor his lovingkindness from me.
verses.Ps.67.1: For the Chief Musician; on stringed instruments. A Psalm, a Song. God be merciful unto us, and bless us, And cause his face to shine upon us; [Selah
verses.Ps.67.2: That thy way may be known upon earth, Thy salvation among all nations.
verses.Ps.67.3: Let the peoples praise thee, O God; Let all the peoples praise thee.
verses.Ps.67.4: Oh let the nations be glad and sing for joy; For thou wilt judge the peoples with equity, And govern the nations upon earth. [Selah
verses.Ps.67.5: Let the peoples praise thee, O God; Let all the peoples praise thee.
verses.Ps.67.6: The earth hath yielded its increase: God, even our own God, will bless us.
verses.Ps.67.7: God will bless us; And all the ends of the earth shall fear him.
verses.Ps.68.1: For the Chief Musician; A Psalm of David, a Song. Let God arise, let his enemies be scattered; Let them also that hate him flee before him.
verses.Ps.68.2: As smoke is driven away, so drive them away: As wax melteth before the fire, So let the wicked perish at the presence of God.
verses.Ps.68.3: But let the righteous be glad; let them exult before God: Yea, let them rejoice with gladness.
verses.Ps.68.4: Sing unto God, sing praises to his name: Cast up a highway for him that rideth through the deserts; His name is Jehovah; and exult ye before him.
verses.Ps.68.5: A father of the fatherless, and a judge of the widows, Is God in his holy habitation.
verses.Ps.68.6: God setteth the solitary in families: He bringeth out the prisoners into prosperity; But the rebellious dwell in a parched land.
verses.Ps.68.7: O God, when thou wentest forth before thy people, When thou didst march through the wilderness; [Selah
verses.Ps.68.8: The earth trembled, The heavens also dropped rain at the presence of God: Yon Sinai trembled at the presence of God, the God of Israel.
verses.Ps.68.9: Thou, O God, didst send a plentiful rain, Thou didst confirm thine inheritance, when it was weary.
verses.Ps.68.10: Thy congregation dwelt therein: Thou, O God, didst prepare of thy goodness for the poor.
verses.Ps.68.11: The Lord giveth the word: The women that publish the tidings are a great host.
verses.Ps.68.12: Kings of armies flee, they flee; And she that tarrieth at home divideth the spoil.
verses.Ps.68.13: When ye lie among the sheepfolds, It is as the wings of a dove covered with silver, And her pinions with yellow gold.
verses.Ps.68.14: When the Almighty scattered kings therein, It was as when it snoweth in Zalmon.
verses.Ps.68.15: A mountain of God is the mountain of Bashan; A high mountain is the mountain of Bashan.
verses.Ps.68.16: Why look ye askance, ye high mountains, At the mountain which God hath desired for his abode? Yea, Jehovah will dwell in it for ever.
verses.Ps.68.17: The chariots of God are twenty thousand, even thousands upon thousands: The Lord is among them, as in Sinai, in the sanctuary.
verses.Ps.68.18: Thou hast ascended on high, thou hast led away captives; Thou hast received gifts among men, Yea, among the rebellious also, that Jehovah God might dwell with them.
verses.Ps.68.19: Blessed be the Lord, who daily beareth our burden, Even the God who is our salvation. [Selah
verses.Ps.68.20: God is unto us a God of deliverances; And unto Jehovah the Lord belongeth escape from death.
verses.Ps.68.21: But God will smite through the head of his enemies, The hairy scalp of such a one as goeth on still in his guiltiness.
verses.Ps.68.22: The Lord said, I will bring again from Bashan, I will bring them again from the depths of the sea;
verses.Ps.68.23: That thou mayest crush them, dipping thy foot in blood, That the tongue of thy dogs may have its portion from thine enemies.
verses.Ps.68.24: They have seen thy goings, O God, Even the goings of my God, my King, into the sanctuary.
verses.Ps.68.25: The singers went before, the minstrels followed after, In the midst of the damsels playing with timbrels.
verses.Ps.68.26: Bless ye God in the congregations, Even the Lord, ye that are of the fountain of Israel.
verses.Ps.68.27: There is little Benjamin their ruler, The princes of Judah and their council, The princes of Zebulun, the princes of Naphtali.
verses.Ps.68.28: Thy God hath commanded thy strength: Strengthen, O God, that which thou hast wrought for us.
verses.Ps.68.29: Because of thy temple at Jerusalem Kings shall bring presents unto thee.
verses.Ps.68.30: Rebuke the wild beast of the reeds, The multitude of the bulls, with the calves of the peoples, Trampling under foot the pieces of silver: He hath scattered the peoples that delight in war.
verses.Ps.68.31: Princes shall come out of Egypt; Ethiopia shall haste to stretch out her hands unto God.
verses.Ps.68.32: Sing unto God, ye kingdoms of the earth; Oh sing praises unto the Lord; [Selah
verses.Ps.68.33: To him that rideth upon the heaven of heavens, which are of old; Lo, he uttereth his voice, a mighty voice.
verses.Ps.68.34: Ascribe ye strength unto God: His excellency is over Israel, And his strength is in the skies.
verses.Ps.68.35: O God, thou art terrible out of thy holy places: The God of Israel, he giveth strength and power unto his people. Blessed be God.
verses.Ps.69.1: For the Chief Musician; set to Shoshannim. A Psalm of David. Save me, O God; For the waters are come in unto my soul.
verses.Ps.69.2: I sink in deep mire, where there is no standing: I am come into deep waters, where the floods overflow me.
verses.Ps.69.3: I am weary with my crying; my throat is dried: Mine eyes fail while I wait for my God.
verses.Ps.69.4: They that hate me without a cause are more than the hairs of my head: They that would cut me off, being mine enemies wrongfully, are mighty: That which I took not away I have to restore.
verses.Ps.69.5: O God, thou knowest my foolishness; And my sins are not hid from thee.
verses.Ps.69.6: Let not them that wait for thee be put to shame through me, O Lord Jehovah of hosts: Let not those that seek thee be brought to dishonor through me, O God of Israel.
verses.Ps.69.7: Because for thy sake I have borne reproach; Shame hath covered my face.
verses.Ps.69.8: I am become a stranger unto my brethren, And an alien unto my mother’s children.
verses.Ps.69.9: For the zeal of thy house hath eaten me up; And the reproaches of them that reproach thee are fallen upon me.
verses.Ps.69.10: When I wept, and chastened my soul with fasting, That was to my reproach.
verses.Ps.69.11: When I made sackcloth my clothing, I became a byword unto them.
verses.Ps.69.12: They that sit in the gate talk of me; And I am the song of the drunkards.
verses.Ps.69.13: But as for me, my prayer is unto thee, O Jehovah, in an acceptable time: O God, in the abundance of thy lovingkindness, Answer me in the truth of thy salvation.
verses.Ps.69.14: Deliver me out of the mire, and let me not sink: Let me be delivered from them that hate me, and out of the deep waters.
verses.Ps.69.15: Let not the waterflood overwhelm me, Neither let the deep swallow me up; And let not the pit shut its mouth upon me.
verses.Ps.69.16: Answer me, O Jehovah; for thy lovingkindness is good: According to the multitude of thy tender mercies turn thou unto me.
verses.Ps.69.17: And hide not thy face from thy servant; For I am in distress; answer me speedily.
verses.Ps.69.18: Draw nigh unto my soul, and redeem it: Ransom me because of mine enemies.
verses.Ps.69.19: Thou knowest my reproach, and my shame, and my dishonor: Mine adversaries are all before thee.
verses.Ps.69.20: Reproach hath broken my heart; and I am full of heaviness: And I looked for some to take pity, but there was none; And for comforters, but I found none.
verses.Ps.69.21: They gave me also gall for my food; And in my thirst they gave me vinegar to drink.
verses.Ps.69.22: Let their table before them become a snare; And when they are in peace, let it become a trap.
verses.Ps.69.23: Let their eyes be darkened, so that they cannot see; And make their loins continually to shake.
verses.Ps.69.24: Pour out thine indignation upon them, And let the fierceness of thine anger overtake them.
verses.Ps.69.25: Let their habitation be desolate; Let none dwell in their tents.
verses.Ps.69.26: For they persecute him whom thou hast smitten; And they tell of the sorrow of those whom thou hast wounded.
verses.Ps.69.27: Add iniquity unto their iniquity; And let them not come into thy righteousness.
verses.Ps.69.28: Let them be blotted out of the book of life, And not be written with the righteous.
verses.Ps.69.29: But I am poor and sorrowful: Let thy salvation, O God, set me up on high.
verses.Ps.69.30: I will praise the name of God with a song, And will magnify him with thanksgiving.
verses.Ps.69.31: And it will please Jehovah better than an ox, Or a bullock that hath horns and hoofs.
verses.Ps.69.32: The meek have seen it, and are glad: Ye that seek after God, let your heart live.
verses.Ps.69.33: For Jehovah heareth the needy, And despiseth not his prisoners.
verses.Ps.69.34: Let heaven and earth praise him, The seas, and everything that moveth therein.
verses.Ps.69.35: For God will save Zion, and build the cities of Judah; And they shall abide there, and have it in possession.
verses.Ps.69.36: The seed also of his servants shall inherit it; And they that love his name shall dwell therein.
verses.Ps.70.1: For the Chief Musician. A Psalm of David; to bring to remembrance. Make haste, O God, to deliver me; Make haste to help me, O Jehovah.
verses.Ps.70.2: Let them be put to shame and confounded That seek after my soul: Let them be turned backward and brought to dishonor That delight in my hurt.
verses.Ps.70.3: Let them be turned back by reason of their shame That say, Aha, aha.
verses.Ps.70.4: Let all those that seek thee rejoice and be glad in thee; And let such as love thy salvation say continually, Let God be magnified.
verses.Ps.70.5: But I am poor and needy; Make haste unto me, O God: Thou art my help and my deliverer; O Jehovah, make no tarrying.
verses.Ps.71.1: In thee, O Jehovah, do I take refuge: Let me never be put to shame.
verses.Ps.71.2: Deliver me in thy righteousness, and rescue me: Bow down thine ear unto me, and save me.
verses.Ps.71.3: Be thou to me a rock of habitation, whereunto I may continually resort: Thou hast given commandment to save me; For thou art my rock and my fortress.
verses.Ps.71.4: Rescue me, O my God, out of the hand of the wicked, Out of the hand of the unrighteous and cruel man.
verses.Ps.71.5: For thou art my hope, O Lord Jehovah: Thou art my trust from my youth.
verses.Ps.71.6: By thee have I been holden up from the womb; Thou art he that took me out of my mother’s bowels: My praise shall be continually of thee.
verses.Ps.71.7: I am as a wonder unto many; But thou art my strong refuge.
verses.Ps.71.8: My mouth shall be filled with thy praise, And with thy honor all the day.
verses.Ps.71.9: Cast me not off in the time of old age; Forsake me not when my strength faileth.
verses.Ps.71.10: For mine enemies speak concerning me; And they that watch for my soul take counsel together,
verses.Ps.71.11: Saying, God hath forsaken him: Pursue and take him; for there is none to deliver.
verses.Ps.71.12: O God, be not far from me; O my God, make haste to help me.
verses.Ps.71.13: Let them be put to shame and consumed that are adversaries to my soul; Let them be covered with reproach and dishonor that seek my hurt.
verses.Ps.71.14: But I will hope continually, And will praise thee yet more and more.
verses.Ps.71.15: My mouth shall tell of thy righteousness, And of thy salvation all the day; For I know not the numbers thereof.
verses.Ps.71.16: I will come with the mighty acts of the Lord Jehovah: I will make mention of thy righteousness, even of thine only.
verses.Ps.71.17: O God, thou hast taught me from my youth; And hitherto have I declared thy wondrous works.
verses.Ps.71.18: Yea, even when I am old and grayheaded, O God, forsake me not, Until I have declared thy strength unto the next generation, Thy might to every one that is to come.
verses.Ps.71.19: Thy righteousness also, O God, is very high; Thou who hast done great things, O God, who is like unto thee?
verses.Ps.71.20: Thou, who hast showed us many and sore troubles, Wilt quicken us again, And wilt bring us up again from the depths of the earth.
verses.Ps.71.21: Increase thou my greatness, And turn again and comfort me.
verses.Ps.71.22: I will also praise thee with the psaltery, Even thy truth, O my God: Unto thee will I sing praises with the harp, O thou Holy One of Israel.
verses.Ps.71.23: My lips shall shout for joy when I sing praises unto thee; And my soul, which thou hast redeemed.
verses.Ps.71.24: My tongue also shall talk of thy righteousness all the day long; For they are put to shame, for they are confounded, that seek my hurt.
verses.Ps.72.1: A Psalm of Solomon. Give the king thy judgments, O God, And thy righteousness unto the king’s son.
verses.Ps.72.2: He will judge thy people with righteousness, And thy poor with justice.
verses.Ps.72.3: The mountains shall bring peace to the people, And the hills, in righteousness.
verses.Ps.72.4: He will judge the poor of the people, He will save the children of the needy, And will break in pieces the oppressor.
verses.Ps.72.5: They shall fear thee while the sun endureth, And so long as the moon, throughout all generations.
verses.Ps.72.6: He will come down like rain upon the mown grass, As showers that water the earth.
verses.Ps.72.7: In his days shall the righteous flourish, And abundance of peace, till the moon be no more.
verses.Ps.72.8: He shall have dominion also from sea to sea, And from the River unto the ends of the earth.
verses.Ps.72.9: They that dwell in the wilderness shall bow before him; And his enemies shall lick the dust.
verses.Ps.72.10: The kings of Tarshish and of the isles shall render tribute: The kings of Sheba and Seba shall offer gifts.
verses.Ps.72.11: Yea, all kings shall fall down before him; All nations shall serve him.
verses.Ps.72.12: For he will deliver the needy when he crieth, And the poor, that hath no helper.
verses.Ps.72.13: He will have pity on the poor and needy, And the souls of the needy he will save.
verses.Ps.72.14: He will redeem their soul from oppression and violence; And precious will their blood be in his sight:
verses.Ps.72.15: And they shall live; and to him shall be given of the gold of Sheba: And men shall pray for him continually; They shall bless him all the day long.
verses.Ps.72.16: There shall be abundance of grain in the earth upon the top of the mountains; The fruit thereof shall shake like Lebanon: And they of the city shall flourish like grass of the earth.
verses.Ps.72.17: His name shall endure for ever; His name shall be continued as long as the sun: And men shall be blessed in him; All nations shall call him happy.
verses.Ps.72.18: Blessed be Jehovah God, the God of Israel, Who only doeth wondrous things:
verses.Ps.72.19: And blessed be his glorious name for ever; And let the whole earth be filled with his glory. Amen, and Amen.
verses.Ps.72.20: The prayers of David the son of Jesse are ended.
verses.Ps.73.1: A Psalm of Asaph. Surely God is good to Israel, Even to such as are pure in heart.
verses.Ps.73.2: But as for me, my feet were almost gone; My steps had well nigh slipped.
verses.Ps.73.3: For I was envious at the arrogant, When I saw the prosperity of the wicked.
verses.Ps.73.4: For there are no pangs in their death; But their strength is firm.
verses.Ps.73.5: They are not in trouble as other men; Neither are they plagued like other men.
verses.Ps.73.6: Therefore pride is as a chain about their neck; Violence covereth them as a garment.
verses.Ps.73.7: Their eyes stand out with fatness: They have more than heart could wish.
verses.Ps.73.8: They scoff, and in wickedness utter oppression: They speak loftily.
verses.Ps.73.9: They have set their mouth in the heavens, And their tongue walketh through the earth.
verses.Ps.73.10: Therefore his people return hither: And waters of a full cup are drained by them.
verses.Ps.73.11: And they say, How doth God know? And is there knowledge in the Most High?
verses.Ps.73.12: Behold, these are the wicked; And, being alway at ease, they increase in riches.
verses.Ps.73.13: Surely in vain have I cleansed my heart, And washed my hands in innocency;
verses.Ps.73.14: For all the day long have I been plagued, And chastened every morning.
verses.Ps.73.15: If I had said, I will speak thus; Behold, I had dealt treacherously with the generation of thy children.
verses.Ps.73.16: When I thought how I might know this, It was too painful for me;
verses.Ps.73.17: Until I went into the sanctuary of God, And considered their latter end.
verses.Ps.73.18: Surely thou settest them in slippery places: Thou castest them down to destruction.
verses.Ps.73.19: How are they become a desolation in a moment! They are utterly consumed with terrors.
verses.Ps.73.20: As a dream when one awaketh, So, O Lord, when thou awakest, thou wilt despise their image.
verses.Ps.73.21: For my soul was grieved, And I was pricked in my heart:
verses.Ps.73.22: So brutish was I, and ignorant; I was as a beast before thee.
verses.Ps.73.23: Nevertheless I am continually with thee: Thou hast holden my right hand.
verses.Ps.73.24: Thou wilt guide me with thy counsel, And afterward receive me to glory.
verses.Ps.73.25: Whom have I in heaven but thee? And there is none upon earth that I desire besides thee.
verses.Ps.73.26: My flesh and my heart faileth; But God is the strength of my heart and my portion for ever.
verses.Ps.73.27: For, lo, they that are far from thee shall perish: Thou hast destroyed all them that play the harlot, departing from thee.
verses.Ps.73.28: But it is good for me to draw near unto God: I have made the Lord Jehovah my refuge, That I may tell of all thy works.
verses.Ps.74.1: Maschil of Asaph. O God, why hast thou cast us off for ever? Why doth thine anger smoke against the sheep of thy pasture?
verses.Ps.74.2: Remember thy congregation, which thou hast gotten of old, Which thou hast redeemed to be the tribe of thine inheritance; And mount Zion, wherein thou hast dwelt.
verses.Ps.74.3: Lift up thy feet unto the perpetual ruins, All the evil that the enemy hath done in the sanctuary.
verses.Ps.74.4: Thine adversaries have roared in the midst of thine assembly; They have set up their ensigns for signs.
verses.Ps.74.5: They seemed as men that lifted up Axes upon a thicket of trees.
verses.Ps.74.6: And now all the carved work thereof They break down with hatchet and hammers.
verses.Ps.74.7: They have set thy sanctuary on fire; They have profaned the dwelling-place of thy name by casting it to the ground.
verses.Ps.74.8: They said in their heart, Let us make havoc of them altogether: They have burned up all the synagogues of God in the land.
verses.Ps.74.9: We see not our signs: There is no more any prophet; Neither is there among us any that knoweth how long.
verses.Ps.74.10: How long, O God, shall the adversary reproach? Shall the enemy blaspheme thy name for ever?
verses.Ps.74.11: Why drawest thou back thy hand, even thy right hand? Pluck it out of thy bosom and consume them.
verses.Ps.74.12: Yet God is my King of old, Working salvation in the midst of the earth.
verses.Ps.74.13: Thou didst divide the sea by thy strength: Thou brakest the heads of the sea-monsters in the waters.
verses.Ps.74.14: Thou brakest the heads of leviathan in pieces; Thou gavest him to be food to the people inhabiting the wilderness.
verses.Ps.74.15: Thou didst cleave fountain and flood: Thou driedst up mighty rivers.
verses.Ps.74.16: The day is thine, the night also is thine: Thou hast prepared the light and the sun.
verses.Ps.74.17: Thou hast set all the borders of the earth: Thou hast made summer and winter.
verses.Ps.74.18: Remember this, that the enemy hath reproached, O Jehovah, And that a foolish people hath blasphemed thy name.
verses.Ps.74.19: Oh deliver not the soul of thy turtle-dove unto the wild beast: Forget not the life of thy poor for ever.
verses.Ps.74.20: Have respect unto the covenant; For the dark places of the earth are full of the habitations of violence.
verses.Ps.74.21: Oh let not the oppressed return ashamed: Let the poor and needy praise thy name.
verses.Ps.74.22: Arise, O God, plead thine own cause: Remember how the foolish man reproacheth thee all the day.
verses.Ps.74.23: Forget not the voice of thine adversaries: The tumult of those that rise up against thee ascendeth continually.
verses.Ps.75.1: For the Chief Musician; set to Al-tashheth. A Psalm of Asaph, a Song. We give thanks unto thee, O God; We give thanks, for thy name is near: Men tell of thy wondrous works.
verses.Ps.75.2: When I shall find the set time, I will judge uprightly.
verses.Ps.75.3: The earth and all the inhabitants thereof are dissolved: I have set up the pillars of it. [Selah
verses.Ps.75.4: I said unto the arrogant, Deal not arrogantly; And to the wicked, Lift not up the horn:
verses.Ps.75.5: Lift not up your horn on high; Speak not with a stiff neck.
verses.Ps.75.6: For neither from the east, nor from the west, Nor yet from the south, cometh lifting up.
verses.Ps.75.7: But God is the judge: He putteth down one, and lifteth up another.
verses.Ps.75.8: For in the hand of Jehovah there is a cup, and the wine foameth; It is full of mixture, and he poureth out of the same: Surely the dregs thereof, all the wicked of the earth shall drain them, and drink them.
verses.Ps.75.9: But I will declare for ever, I will sing praises to the God of Jacob.
verses.Ps.75.10: All the horns of the wicked also will I cut off; But the horns of the righteous shall be lifted up.
verses.Ps.76.1: For the Chief Musician; on stringed instruments. A Psalm of Asaph, a Song. In Judah is God known: His name is great in Israel.
verses.Ps.76.2: In Salem also is his tabernacle, And his dwelling-place in Zion.
verses.Ps.76.3: There he brake the arrows of the bow; The shield, and the sword, and the battle. [Selah
verses.Ps.76.4: Glorious art thou and excellent, From the mountains of prey.
verses.Ps.76.5: The stouthearted are made a spoil, They have slept their sleep; And none of the men of might have found their hands.
verses.Ps.76.6: At thy rebuke, O God of Jacob, Both chariot and horse are cast into a dead sleep.
verses.Ps.76.7: Thou, even thou, art to be feared; And who may stand in thy sight when once thou art angry?
verses.Ps.76.8: Thou didst cause sentence to be heard from heaven; The earth feared, and was still,
verses.Ps.76.9: When God arose to judgment, To save all the meek of the earth. [Selah
verses.Ps.76.10: Surely the wrath of man shall praise thee: The residue of wrath shalt thou gird upon thee.
verses.Ps.76.11: Vow, and pay unto Jehovah your God: Let all that are round about him bring presents unto him that ought to be feared.
verses.Ps.76.12: He will cut off the spirit of princes: He is terrible to the kings of the earth.
verses.Ps.77.1: For the Chief Musician; after the manner of Jeduthun. A Psalm of Asaph. I will cry unto God with my voice, Even unto God with my voice; and he will give ear unto me.
verses.Ps.77.2: In the day of my trouble I sought the Lord: My hand was stretched out in the night, and slacked not; My soul refused to be comforted.
verses.Ps.77.3: I remember God, and am disquieted: I complain, and my spirit is overwhelmed. [Selah
verses.Ps.77.4: Thou holdest mine eyes watching: I am so troubled that I cannot speak.
verses.Ps.77.5: I have considered the days of old, The years of ancient times.
verses.Ps.77.6: I call to remembrance my song in the night: I commune with mine own heart; And my spirit maketh diligent search.
verses.Ps.77.7: Will the Lord cast off for ever? And will he be favorable no more?
verses.Ps.77.8: Is his lovingkindness clean gone for ever? Doth his promise fail for evermore?
verses.Ps.77.9: Hath God forgotten to be gracious? Hath he in anger shut up his tender mercies? [Selah
verses.Ps.77.10: And I said, This is my infirmity; But I will remember the years of the right hand of the Most High.
verses.Ps.77.11: I will make mention of the deeds of Jehovah; For I will remember thy wonders of old.
verses.Ps.77.12: I will meditate also upon all thy work, And muse on thy doings.
verses.Ps.77.13: Thy way, O God, is in the sanctuary: Who is a great god like unto God?
verses.Ps.77.14: Thou art the God that doest wonders: Thou hast made known thy strength among the peoples.
verses.Ps.77.15: Thou hast with thine arm redeemed thy people, The sons of Jacob and Joseph. [Selah
verses.Ps.77.16: The waters saw thee, O God; The waters saw thee, they were afraid: The depths also trembled.
verses.Ps.77.17: The clouds poured out water; The skies sent out a sound: Thine arrows also went abroad.
verses.Ps.77.18: The voice of thy thunder was in the whirlwind; The lightnings lightened the world: The earth trembled and shook.
verses.Ps.77.19: Thy way was in the sea, And thy paths in the great waters, And thy footsteps were not known.
verses.Ps.77.20: Thou leddest thy people like a flock, By the hand of Moses and Aaron.
verses.Ps.78.1: Maschil of Asaph. Give ear, O my people, to my law: Incline your ears to the words of my mouth.
verses.Ps.78.2: I will open my mouth in a parable; I will utter dark sayings of old,
verses.Ps.78.3: Which we have heard and known, And our fathers have told us.
verses.Ps.78.4: We will not hide them from their children, Telling to the generation to come the praises of Jehovah, And his strength, and his wondrous works that he hath done.
verses.Ps.78.5: For he established a testimony in Jacob, And appointed a law in Israel, Which he commanded our fathers, That they should make them known to their children;
verses.Ps.78.6: That the generation to come might know them, even the children that should be born; Who should arise and tell them to their children,
verses.Ps.78.7: That they might set their hope in God, And not forget the works of God, But keep his commandments,
verses.Ps.78.8: And might not be as their fathers, A stubborn and rebellious generation, A generation that set not their heart aright, And whose spirit was not stedfast with God.
verses.Ps.78.9: The children of Ephraim, being armed and carrying bows, Turned back in the day of battle.
verses.Ps.78.10: They kept not the covenant of God, And refused to walk in his law;
verses.Ps.78.11: And they forgat his doings, And his wondrous works that he had showed them.
verses.Ps.78.12: Marvellous things did he in the sight of their fathers, In the land of Egypt, in the field of Zoan.
verses.Ps.78.13: He clave the sea, and caused them to pass through; And he made the waters to stand as a heap.
verses.Ps.78.14: In the day-time also he led them with a cloud, And all the night with a light of fire.
verses.Ps.78.15: He clave rocks in the wilderness, And gave them drink abundantly as out of the depths.
verses.Ps.78.16: He brought streams also out of the rock, And caused waters to run down like rivers.
verses.Ps.78.17: Yet went they on still to sin against him, To rebel against the Most High in the desert.
verses.Ps.78.18: And they tempted God in their heart By asking food according to their desire.
verses.Ps.78.19: Yea, they spake against God; They said, Can God prepare a table in the wilderness?
verses.Ps.78.20: Behold, he smote the rock, so that waters gushed out, And streams overflowed; Can he give bread also? Will he provide flesh for his people?
verses.Ps.78.21: Therefore Jehovah heard, and was wroth; And a fire was kindled against Jacob, And anger also went up against Israel;
verses.Ps.78.22: Because they believed not in God, And trusted not in his salvation.
verses.Ps.78.23: Yet he commanded the skies above, And opened the doors of heaven;
verses.Ps.78.24: And he rained down manna upon them to eat, And gave them food from heaven.
verses.Ps.78.25: Man did eat the bread of the mighty: He sent them food to the full.
verses.Ps.78.26: He caused the east wind to blow in the heavens; And by his power he guided the south wind.
verses.Ps.78.27: He rained flesh also upon them as the dust, And winged birds as the sand of the seas:
verses.Ps.78.28: And he let it fall in the midst of their camp, Round about their habitations.
verses.Ps.78.29: So they did eat, and were well filled; And he gave them their own desire.
verses.Ps.78.30: They were not estranged from that which they desired, Their food was yet in their mouths,
verses.Ps.78.31: When the anger of God went up against them, And slew of the fattest of them, And smote down the young men of Israel.
verses.Ps.78.32: For all this they sinned still, And believed not in his wondrous works.
verses.Ps.78.33: Therefore their days did he consume in vanity, And their years in terror.
verses.Ps.78.34: When he slew them, then they inquired after him; And they returned and sought God earnestly.
verses.Ps.78.35: And they remembered that God was their rock, And the Most High God their redeemer.
verses.Ps.78.36: But they flattered him with their mouth, And lied unto him with their tongue.
verses.Ps.78.37: For their heart was not right with him, Neither were they faithful in his covenant.
verses.Ps.78.38: But he, being merciful, forgave their iniquity, and destroyed them not: Yea, many a time turned he his anger away, And did not stir up all his wrath.
verses.Ps.78.39: And he remembered that they were but flesh, A wind that passeth away, and cometh not again.
verses.Ps.78.40: How oft did they rebel against him in the wilderness, And grieve him in the desert!
verses.Ps.78.41: And they turned again and tempted God, And provoked the Holy One of Israel.
verses.Ps.78.42: They remembered not his hand, Nor the day when he redeemed them from the adversary;
verses.Ps.78.43: How he set his signs in Egypt, And his wonders in the field of Zoan,
verses.Ps.78.44: And turned their rivers into blood, And their streams, so that they could not drink.
verses.Ps.78.45: He sent among them swarms of flies, which devoured them; And frogs, which destroyed them.
verses.Ps.78.46: He gave also their increase unto the caterpillar, And their labor unto the locust.
verses.Ps.78.47: He destroyed their vines with hail, And their sycomore-trees with frost.
verses.Ps.78.48: He gave over their cattle also to the hail, And their flocks to hot thunderbolts.
verses.Ps.78.49: He cast upon them the fierceness of his anger, Wrath, and indignation, and trouble, A band of angels of evil.
verses.Ps.78.50: He made a path for his anger; He spared not their soul from death, But gave their life over to the pestilence,
verses.Ps.78.51: And smote all the first-born in Egypt, The chief of their strength in the tents of Ham.
verses.Ps.78.52: But he led forth his own people like sheep, And guided them in the wilderness like a flock.
verses.Ps.78.53: And he led them safely, so that they feared not; But the sea overwhelmed their enemies.
verses.Ps.78.54: And he brought them to the border of his sanctuary, To this mountain, which his right hand had gotten.
verses.Ps.78.55: He drove out the nations also before them, And allotted them for an inheritance by line, And made the tribes of Israel to dwell in their tents.
verses.Ps.78.56: Yet they tempted and rebelled against the Most High God, And kept not his testimonies;
verses.Ps.78.57: But turned back, and dealt treacherously like their fathers: They were turned aside like a deceitful bow.
verses.Ps.78.58: For they provoked him to anger with their high places, And moved him to jealousy with their graven images.
verses.Ps.78.59: When God heard this, he was wroth, And greatly abhorred Israel;
verses.Ps.78.60: So that he forsook the tabernacle of Shiloh, The tent which he placed among men;
verses.Ps.78.61: And delivered his strength into captivity, And his glory into the adversary’s hand.
verses.Ps.78.62: He gave his people over also unto the sword, And was wroth with his inheritance.
verses.Ps.78.63: Fire devoured their young men; And their virgins had no marriage-song.
verses.Ps.78.64: Their priests fell by the sword; And their widows made no lamentation.
verses.Ps.78.65: Then the Lord awaked as one out of sleep, Like a mighty man that shouteth by reason of wine.
verses.Ps.78.66: And he smote his adversaries backward: He put them to a perpetual reproach.
verses.Ps.78.67: Moreover he refused the tent of Joseph, And chose not the tribe of Ephraim,
verses.Ps.78.68: But chose the tribe of Judah, The mount Zion which he loved.
verses.Ps.78.69: And he built his sanctuary like the heights, Like the earth which he hath established for ever.
verses.Ps.78.70: He chose David also his servant, And took him from the sheepfolds:
verses.Ps.78.71: From following the ewes that have their young he brought him, To be the shepherd of Jacob his people, and Israel his inheritance.
verses.Ps.78.72: So he was their shepherd according to the integrity of his heart, And guided them by the skilfulness of his hands.
verses.Ps.79.1: A Psalm of Asaph. O God, the nations are come into thine inheritance; Thy holy temple have they defiled; They have laid Jerusalem in heaps.
verses.Ps.79.2: The dead bodies of thy servants have they given to be food unto the birds of the heavens, The flesh of thy saints unto the beasts of the earth.
verses.Ps.79.3: Their blood have they shed like water round about Jerusalem; And there was none to bury them.
verses.Ps.79.4: We are become a reproach to our neighbors, A scoffing and derision to them that are round about us.
verses.Ps.79.5: How long, O Jehovah? wilt thou be angry for ever? Shall thy jealousy burn like fire?
verses.Ps.79.6: Pour out thy wrath upon the nations that know thee not, And upon the kingdoms that call not upon thy name.
verses.Ps.79.7: For they have devoured Jacob, And laid waste his habitation.
verses.Ps.79.8: Remember not against us the iniquities of our forefathers: Let thy tender mercies speedily meet us; For we are brought very low.
verses.Ps.79.9: Help us, O God of our salvation, for the glory of thy name; And deliver us, and forgive our sins, for thy name’s sake.
verses.Ps.79.10: Wherefore should the nations say, Where is their God? Let the avenging of the blood of thy servants which is shed Be known among the nations in our sight.
verses.Ps.79.11: Let the sighing of the prisoner come before thee: According to the greatness of thy power preserve thou those that are appointed to death;
verses.Ps.79.12: And render unto our neighbors sevenfold into their bosom Their reproach, wherewith they have reproached thee, O Lord.
verses.Ps.79.13: So we thy people and sheep of thy pasture Will give thee thanks for ever: We will show forth thy praise to all generations.
verses.Ps.80.1: For the Chief Musician; set to Shoshannim Eduth. A Psalm of Asaph. Give ear, O Shepherd of Israel, Thou that leadest Joseph like a flock; Thou that sittest above the cherubim, shine forth.
verses.Ps.80.2: Before Ephraim and Benjamin and Manasseh, stir up thy might, And come to save us.
verses.Ps.80.3: Turn us again, O God; And cause thy face to shine, and we shall be saved.
verses.Ps.80.4: O Jehovah God of hosts, How long wilt thou be angry against the prayer of thy people?
verses.Ps.80.5: Thou hast fed them with the bread of tears, And given them tears to drink in large measure.
verses.Ps.80.6: Thou makest us a strife unto our neighbors; And our enemies laugh among themselves.
verses.Ps.80.7: Turn us again, O God of hosts; And cause thy face to shine, and we shall be saved.
verses.Ps.80.8: Thou broughtest a vine out of Egypt: Thou didst drive out the nations, and plantedst it.
verses.Ps.80.9: Thou preparedst room before it, And it took deep root, and filled the land.
verses.Ps.80.10: The mountains were covered with the shadow of it, And the boughs thereof were like cedars of God.
verses.Ps.80.11: It sent out its branches unto the sea, And its shoots unto the River.
verses.Ps.80.12: Why hast thou broken down its walls, So that all they that pass by the way do pluck it?
verses.Ps.80.13: The boar out of the wood doth ravage it, And the wild beasts of the field feed on it.
verses.Ps.80.14: Turn again, we beseech thee, O God of hosts: Look down from heaven, and behold, and visit this vine,
verses.Ps.80.15: And the stock which thy right hand planted, And the branch that thou madest strong for thyself.
verses.Ps.80.16: It is burned with fire, it is cut down: They perish at the rebuke of thy countenance.
verses.Ps.80.17: Let thy hand be upon the man of thy right hand, Upon the son of man whom thou madest strong for thyself.
verses.Ps.80.18: So shall we not go back from thee: Quicken thou us, and we will call upon thy name.
verses.Ps.80.19: Turn us again, O Jehovah God of hosts; Cause thy face to shine, and we shall be saved.
verses.Ps.81.1: For the Chief Musician; set to the Gittith. A Psalm of Asaph. Sing aloud unto God our strength: Make a joyful noise unto the God of Jacob.
verses.Ps.81.2: Raise a song, and bring hither the timbrel, The pleasant harp with the psaltery.
verses.Ps.81.3: Blow the trumpet at the new moon, At the full moon, on our feast-day.
verses.Ps.81.4: For it is a statute for Israel, An ordinance of the God of Jacob.
verses.Ps.81.5: He appointed it in Joseph for a testimony, When he went out over the land of Egypt, Where I heard a language that I knew not.
verses.Ps.81.6: I removed his shoulder from the burden: His hands were freed from the basket.
verses.Ps.81.7: Thou calledst in trouble, and I delivered thee; I answered thee in the secret place of thunder; I proved thee at the waters of Meribah. [Selah
verses.Ps.81.8: Hear, O my people, and I will testify unto thee: O Israel, if thou wouldest hearken unto me!
verses.Ps.81.9: There shall no strange god be in thee; Neither shalt thou worship any foreign god.
verses.Ps.81.10: I am Jehovah thy God, Who brought thee up out of the land of Egypt: Open thy mouth wide, and I will fill it.
verses.Ps.81.11: But my people hearkened not to my voice; And Israel would none of me.
verses.Ps.81.12: So I let them go after the stubbornness of their heart, That they might walk in their own counsels.
verses.Ps.81.13: Oh that my people would hearken unto me, That Israel would walk in my ways!
verses.Ps.81.14: I would soon subdue their enemies, And turn my hand against their adversaries.
verses.Ps.81.15: The haters of Jehovah should submit themselves unto him: But their time should endure for ever.
verses.Ps.81.16: He would feed them also with the finest of the wheat; And with honey out of the rock would I satisfy thee.
verses.Ps.82.1: A Psalm of Asaph. God standeth in the congregation of God; He judgeth among the gods.
verses.Ps.82.2: How long will ye judge unjustly, And respect the persons of the wicked? [Selah
verses.Ps.82.3: Judge the poor and fatherless: Do justice to the afflicted and destitute.
verses.Ps.82.4: Rescue the poor and needy: Deliver them out of the hand of the wicked.
verses.Ps.82.5: They know not, neither do they understand; They walk to and fro in darkness: All the foundations of the earth are shaken.
verses.Ps.82.6: I said, Ye are gods, And all of you sons of the Most High.
verses.Ps.82.7: Nevertheless ye shall die like men, And fall like one of the princes.
verses.Ps.82.8: Arise, O God, judge the earth; For thou shalt inherit all the nations.
verses.Ps.83.1: A Song, a Psalm of Asaph. O God, keep not thou silence: Hold not thy peace, and be not still, O God.
verses.Ps.83.2: For, lo, thine enemies make a tumult; And they that hate thee have lifted up the head.
verses.Ps.83.3: They take crafty counsel against thy people, And consult together against thy hidden ones.
verses.Ps.83.4: They have said, Come, and let us cut them off from being a nation; That the name of Israel may be no more in remembrance.
verses.Ps.83.5: For they have consulted together with one consent; Against thee do they make a covenant:
verses.Ps.83.6: The tents of Edom and the Ishmaelites; Moab, and the Hagarenes;
verses.Ps.83.7: Gebal, and Ammon, and Amalek; Philistia with the inhabitants of Tyre:
verses.Ps.83.8: Assyria also is joined with them; They have helped the children of Lot. [Selah
verses.Ps.83.9: Do thou unto them as unto Midian, As to Sisera, as to Jabin, at the river Kishon;
verses.Ps.83.10: Who perished at Endor, Who became as dung for the earth.
verses.Ps.83.11: Make their nobles like Oreb and Zeeb; Yea, all their princes like Zebah and Zalmunna;
verses.Ps.83.12: Who said, Let us take to ourselves in possession The habitations of God.
verses.Ps.83.13: O my God, make them like the whirling dust; As stubble before the wind.
verses.Ps.83.14: As the fire that burneth the forest, And as the flame that setteth the mountains on fire,
verses.Ps.83.15: So pursue them with thy tempest, And terrify them with thy storm.
verses.Ps.83.16: Fill their faces with confusion, That they may seek thy name, O Jehovah.
verses.Ps.83.17: Let them be put to shame and dismayed for ever; Yea, let them be confounded and perish;
verses.Ps.83.18: That they may know that thou alone, whose name is Jehovah, Art the Most High over all the earth.
verses.Ps.84.1: For the Chief Musician; set to the Gittith. A Psalm of the sons of Korah. How amiable are thy tabernacles, O Jehovah of hosts!
verses.Ps.84.2: My soul longeth, yea, even fainteth for the courts of Jehovah; My heart and my flesh cry out unto the living God.
verses.Ps.84.3: Yea, the sparrow hath found her a house, And the swallow a nest for herself, where she may lay her young, Even thine altars, O Jehovah of hosts, My King, and my God.
verses.Ps.84.4: Blessed are they that dwell in thy house: They will be still praising thee. [Selah
verses.Ps.84.5: Blessed is the man whose strength is in thee; In whose heart are the highways to Zion.
verses.Ps.84.6: Passing through the valley of Weeping they make it a place of springs; Yea, the early rain covereth it with blessings.
verses.Ps.84.7: They go from strength to strength; Every one of them appeareth before God in Zion.
verses.Ps.84.8: O Jehovah God of hosts, hear my prayer; Give ear, O God of Jacob. [Selah
verses.Ps.84.9: Behold, O God our shield, And look upon the face of thine anointed.
verses.Ps.84.10: For a day in thy courts is better than a thousand. I had rather be a doorkeeper in the house of my God, Than to dwell in the tents of wickedness.
verses.Ps.84.11: For Jehovah God is a sun and a shield: Jehovah will give grace and glory; No good thing will he withhold from them that walk uprightly.
verses.Ps.84.12: O Jehovah of hosts, Blessed is the man that trusteth in thee.
verses.Ps.85.1: For the Chief Musician. A Psalm of the sons of Korah. Jehovah, thou hast been favorable unto thy land; Thou hast brought back the captivity of Jacob.
verses.Ps.85.2: Thou hast forgiven the iniquity of thy people; Thou hast covered all their sin. [Selah
verses.Ps.85.3: Thou hast taken away all thy wrath; Thou hast turned thyself from the fierceness of thine anger.
verses.Ps.85.4: Turn us, O God of our salvation, And cause thine indignation toward us to cease.
verses.Ps.85.5: Wilt thou be angry with us for ever? Wilt thou draw out thine anger to all generations?
verses.Ps.85.6: Wilt thou not quicken us again, That thy people may rejoice in thee?
verses.Ps.85.7: Show us thy lovingkindness, O Jehovah, And grant us thy salvation.
verses.Ps.85.8: I will hear what God Jehovah will speak; For he will speak peace unto his people, and to his saints: But let them not turn again to folly.
verses.Ps.85.9: Surely his salvation is nigh them that fear him, That glory may dwell in our land.
verses.Ps.85.10: Mercy and truth are met together; Righteousness and peace have kissed each other.
verses.Ps.85.11: Truth springeth out of the earth; And righteousness hath looked down from heaven.
verses.Ps.85.12: Yea, Jehovah will give that which is good; And our land shall yield its increase.
verses.Ps.85.13: Righteousness shall go before him, And shall make his footsteps a way to walk in.
verses.Ps.86.1: A Prayer of David. Bow down thine ear, O Jehovah, and answer me; For I am poor and needy.
verses.Ps.86.2: Preserve my soul; for I am godly: O thou my God, save thy servant that trusteth in thee.
verses.Ps.86.3: Be merciful unto me, O Lord; For unto thee do I cry all the day long.
verses.Ps.86.4: Rejoice the soul of thy servant; For unto thee, O Lord, do I lift up my soul.
verses.Ps.86.5: For thou, Lord, art good, and ready to forgive, And abundant in lovingkindness unto all them that call upon thee.
verses.Ps.86.6: Give ear, O Jehovah, unto my prayer; And hearken unto the voice of my supplications.
verses.Ps.86.7: In the day of my trouble I will call upon thee; For thou wilt answer me.
verses.Ps.86.8: There is none like unto thee among the gods, O Lord; Neither are there any works like unto thy works.
verses.Ps.86.9: All nations whom thou hast made shall come and worship before thee, O Lord; And they shall glorify thy name.
verses.Ps.86.10: For thou art great, and doest wondrous things: Thou art God alone.
verses.Ps.86.11: Teach me thy way, O Jehovah; I will walk in thy truth: Unite my heart to fear thy name.
verses.Ps.86.12: I will praise thee, O Lord my God, with my whole heart; And I will glorify thy name for evermore.
verses.Ps.86.13: For great is thy lovingkindness toward me; And thou hast delivered my soul from the lowest Sheol.
verses.Ps.86.14: O God, the proud are risen up against me, And a company of violent men have sought after my soul, And have not set thee before them.
verses.Ps.86.15: But thou, O Lord, art a God merciful and gracious, Slow to anger, and abundant in lovingkindness and truth.
verses.Ps.86.16: Oh turn unto me, and have mercy upon me; Give thy strength unto thy servant, And save the son of thy handmaid.
verses.Ps.86.17: Show me a token for good, That they who hate me may see it, and be put to shame, Because thou, Jehovah, hast helped me, and comforted me.
verses.Ps.87.1: A Psalm of the sons of Korah; a Song. His foundation is in the holy mountains.
verses.Ps.87.2: Jehovah loveth the gates of Zion More than all the dwellings of Jacob.
verses.Ps.87.3: Glorious things are spoken of thee, O city of God. [Selah
verses.Ps.87.4: I will make mention of Rahab and Babylon as among them that know me: Behold, Philistia, and Tyre, with Ethiopia: This one was born there.
verses.Ps.87.5: Yea, of Zion it shall be said, This one and that one was born in her; And the Most High himself will establish her.
verses.Ps.87.6: Jehovah will count, when he writeth up the peoples, This one was born there. [Selah
verses.Ps.87.7: They that sing as well as they that dance shall say, All my fountains are in thee.
verses.Ps.88.1: A Song, a Psalm of the sons of Korah; for the Chief Musician; set to Mahalath Leannoth. Maschil of Heman the Ezrahite. O Jehovah, the God of my salvation, I have cried day and night before thee.
verses.Ps.88.2: Let my prayer enter into thy presence; Incline thine ear unto my cry.
verses.Ps.88.3: For my soul is full of troubles, And my life draweth nigh unto Sheol.
verses.Ps.88.4: I am reckoned with them that go down into the pit; I am as a man that hath no help,
verses.Ps.88.5: Cast off among the dead, Like the slain that lie in the grave, Whom thou rememberest no more, And they are cut off from thy hand.
verses.Ps.88.6: Thou hast laid me in the lowest pit, In dark places, in the deeps.
verses.Ps.88.7: Thy wrath lieth hard upon me, And thou hast afflicted me with all thy waves. [Selah
verses.Ps.88.8: Thou hast put mine acquaintance far from me; Thou hast made me an abomination unto them: I am shut up, and I cannot come forth.
verses.Ps.88.9: Mine eye wasteth away by reason of affliction: I have called daily upon thee, O Jehovah; I have spread forth my hands unto thee.
verses.Ps.88.10: Wilt thou show wonders to the dead? Shall they that are deceased arise and praise thee? [Selah
verses.Ps.88.11: Shall thy lovingkindness be declared in the grave? Or thy faithfulness in Destruction?
verses.Ps.88.12: Shall thy wonders be known in the dark? And thy righteousness in the land of forgetfulness?
verses.Ps.88.13: But unto thee, O Jehovah, have I cried; And in the morning shall my prayer come before thee.
verses.Ps.88.14: Jehovah, why castest thou off my soul? Why hidest thou thy face from me?
verses.Ps.88.15: I am afflicted and ready to die from my youth up: While I suffer thy terrors I am distracted.
verses.Ps.88.16: Thy fierce wrath is gone over me; Thy terrors have cut me off.
verses.Ps.88.17: They came round about me like water all the day long; They compassed me about together.
verses.Ps.88.18: Lover and friend hast thou put far from me, And mine acquaintance into darkness.
verses.Ps.89.1: Maschil of Ethan the Ezrahite. I will sing of the lovingkindness of Jehovah for ever: With my mouth will I make known thy faithfulness to all generations.
verses.Ps.89.2: For I have said, Mercy shall be built up for ever; Thy faithfulness wilt thou establish in the very heavens.
verses.Ps.89.3: I have made a covenant with my chosen, I have sworn unto David my servant:
verses.Ps.89.4: Thy seed will I establish for ever, And build up thy throne to all generations. [Selah
verses.Ps.89.5: And the heavens shall praise thy wonders, O Jehovah; Thy faithfulness also in the assembly of the holy ones.
verses.Ps.89.6: For who in the skies can be compared unto Jehovah? Who among the sons of the mighty is like unto Jehovah,
verses.Ps.89.7: A God very terrible in the council of the holy ones, And to be feared above all them that are round about him?
verses.Ps.89.8: O Jehovah God of hosts, Who is a mighty one, like unto thee, O Jehovah? And thy faithfulness is round about thee.
verses.Ps.89.9: Thou rulest the pride of the sea: When the waves thereof arise, thou stillest them.
verses.Ps.89.10: Thou hast broken Rahab in pieces, as one that is slain; Thou hast scattered thine enemies with the arm of thy strength.
verses.Ps.89.11: The heavens are thine, the earth also is thine: The world and the fulness thereof, thou hast founded them.
verses.Ps.89.12: The north and the south, thou hast created them: Tabor and Hermon rejoice in thy name.
verses.Ps.89.13: Thou hast a mighty arm; Strong is thy hand, and high is thy right hand.
verses.Ps.89.14: Righteousness and justice are the foundation of thy throne: Lovingkindness and truth go before thy face.
verses.Ps.89.15: Blessed is the people that know the joyful sound: They walk, O Jehovah, in the light of thy countenance.
verses.Ps.89.16: In thy name do they rejoice all the day; And in thy righteousness are they exalted.
verses.Ps.89.17: For thou art the glory of their strength; And in thy favor our horn shall be exalted.
verses.Ps.89.18: For our shield belongeth unto Jehovah; And our king to the Holy One of Israel.
verses.Ps.89.19: Then thou spakest in vision to thy saints, And saidst, I have laid help upon one that is mighty; I have exalted one chosen out of the people.
verses.Ps.89.20: I have found David my servant; With my holy oil have I anointed him:
verses.Ps.89.21: With whom my hand shall be established; Mine arm also shall strengthen him.
verses.Ps.89.22: The enemy shall not exact from him, Nor the son of wickedness afflict him.
verses.Ps.89.23: And I will beat down his adversaries before him, And smite them that hate him.
verses.Ps.89.24: But my faithfulness and my lovingkindness shall be with him; And in my name shall his horn be exalted.
verses.Ps.89.25: I will set his hand also on the sea, And his right hand on the rivers.
verses.Ps.89.26: He shall cry unto me, Thou art my Father, My God, and the rock of my salvation.
verses.Ps.89.27: I also will make him my first-born, The highest of the kings of the earth.
verses.Ps.89.28: My lovingkindness will I keep for him for evermore; And my covenant shall stand fast with him.
verses.Ps.89.29: His seed also will I make to endure for ever, And his throne as the days of heaven.
verses.Ps.89.30: If his children forsake my law, And walk not in mine ordinances;
verses.Ps.89.31: If they break my statutes, And keep not my commandments;
verses.Ps.89.32: Then will I visit their transgression with the rod, And their iniquity with stripes.
verses.Ps.89.33: But my lovingkindness will I not utterly take from him, Nor suffer my faithfulness to fail.
verses.Ps.89.34: My covenant will I not break, Nor alter the thing that is gone out of my lips.
verses.Ps.89.35: Once have I sworn by my holiness: I will not lie unto David:
verses.Ps.89.36: His seed shall endure for ever, And his throne as the sun before me.
verses.Ps.89.37: It shall be established for ever as the moon, And as the faithful witness in the sky. [Selah
verses.Ps.89.38: But thou hast cast off and rejected, Thou hast been wroth with thine anointed.
verses.Ps.89.39: Thou hast abhorred the covenant of thy servant: Thou hast profaned his crown by casting it to the ground.
verses.Ps.89.40: Thou hast broken down all his hedges; Thou hast brought his strongholds to ruin.
verses.Ps.89.41: All that pass by the way rob him: He is become a reproach to his neighbors.
verses.Ps.89.42: Thou hast exalted the right hand of his adversaries; Thou hast made all his enemies to rejoice.
verses.Ps.89.43: Yea, thou turnest back the edge of his sword, And hast not made him to stand in the battle.
verses.Ps.89.44: Thou hast made his brightness to cease, And cast his throne down to the ground.
verses.Ps.89.45: The days of his youth hast thou shortened: Thou hast covered him with shame. [Selah
verses.Ps.89.46: How long, O Jehovah? wilt thou hide thyself for ever? How long shall thy wrath burn like fire?
verses.Ps.89.47: Oh remember how short my time is: For what vanity hast thou created all the children of men!
verses.Ps.89.48: What man is he that shall live and not see death, That shall deliver his soul from the power of Sheol? [Selah
verses.Ps.89.49: Lord, where are thy former lovingkindnesses, Which thou swarest unto David in thy faithfulness?
verses.Ps.89.50: Remember, Lord, the reproach of thy servants; How I do bear in my bosom the reproach of all the mighty peoples,
verses.Ps.89.51: Wherewith thine enemies have reproached, O Jehovah, Wherewith they have reproached the footsteps of thine anointed.
verses.Ps.89.52: Blessed be Jehovah for evermore. Amen, and Amen.
verses.Ps.90.1: A Prayer of Moses the man of God. Lord, thou hast been our dwelling-place In all generations.
verses.Ps.90.2: Before the mountains were brought forth, Or ever thou hadst formed the earth and the world, Even from everlasting to everlasting, thou art God.
verses.Ps.90.3: Thou turnest man to destruction, And sayest, Return, ye children of men.
verses.Ps.90.4: For a thousand years in thy sight Are but as yesterday when it is past, And as a watch in the night.
verses.Ps.90.5: Thou carriest them away as with a flood; they are as a sleep: In the morning they are like grass which groweth up.
verses.Ps.90.6: In the morning it flourisheth, and groweth up; In the evening it is cut down, and withereth.
