verses.Prov.18.19: A brother offended is harder to be won than a strong city; And such contentions are like the bars of a castle.
verses.Prov.18.20: A man’s belly shall be filled with the fruit of his mouth; With the increase of his lips shall he be satisfied.
verses.Prov.18.21: Death and life are in the power of the tongue; And they that love it shall eat the fruit thereof.
verses.Prov.18.22: Whoso findeth a wife findeth a good thing, And obtaineth favor of Jehovah.
verses.Prov.18.23: The poor useth entreaties; But the rich answereth roughly.
verses.Prov.18.24: He that maketh many friends doeth it to his own destruction; But there is a friend that sticketh closer than a brother.
verses.Prov.19.1: Better is the poor that walketh in his integrity Than he that is perverse in his lips and is a fool.
verses.Prov.19.2: Also, that the soul be without knowledge is not good; And he that hasteth with his feet sinneth.
verses.Prov.19.3: The foolishness of man subverteth his way; And his heart fretteth against Jehovah.
verses.Prov.19.4: Wealth addeth many friends; But the poor is separated from his friend.
verses.Prov.19.5: A false witness shall not be unpunished; And he that uttereth lies shall not escape.
verses.Prov.19.6: Many will entreat the favor of the liberal man; And every man is a friend to him that giveth gifts.
verses.Prov.19.7: All the brethren of the poor do hate him: How much more do his friends go far from him! He pursueth them with words, but they are gone.
verses.Prov.19.8: He that getteth wisdom loveth his own soul: He that keepeth understanding shall find good.
verses.Prov.19.9: A false witness shall not be unpunished; And he that uttereth lies shall perish.
verses.Prov.19.10: Delicate living is not seemly for a fool; Much less for a servant to have rule over princes.
verses.Prov.19.11: The discretion of a man maketh him slow to anger; And it is his glory to pass over a transgression.
verses.Prov.19.12: The king’s wrath is as the roaring of a lion; But his favor is as dew upon the grass.
verses.Prov.19.13: A foolish son is the calamity of his father; And the contentions of a wife are a continual dropping.
verses.Prov.19.14: House and riches are an inheritance from fathers; But a prudent wife is from Jehovah.
verses.Prov.19.15: Slothfulness casteth into a deep sleep; And the idle soul shall suffer hunger.
verses.Prov.19.16: He that keepeth the commandment keepeth his soul; But he that is careless of his ways shall die.
verses.Prov.19.17: He that hath pity upon the poor lendeth unto Jehovah, And his good deed will he pay him again.
verses.Prov.19.18: Chasten thy son, seeing there is hope; And set not thy heart on his destruction.
verses.Prov.19.19: A man of great wrath shall bear the penalty; For if thou deliver him, thou must do it yet again.
verses.Prov.19.20: Hear counsel, and receive instruction, That thou mayest be wise in thy latter end.
verses.Prov.19.21: There are many devices in a man’s heart; But the counsel of Jehovah, that shall stand.
verses.Prov.19.22: That which maketh a man to be desired is his kindness; And a poor man is better than a liar.
verses.Prov.19.23: The fear of Jehovah tendeth to life; And he that hath it shall abide satisfied; He shall not be visited with evil.
verses.Prov.19.24: The sluggard burieth his hand in the dish, And will not so much as bring it to his mouth again.
verses.Prov.19.25: Smite a scoffer, and the simple will learn prudence; And reprove one that hath understanding, and he will understand knowledge.
verses.Prov.19.26: He that doeth violence to his father, and chaseth away his mother, Is a son that causeth shame and bringeth reproach.
verses.Prov.19.27: Cease, my son, to hear instruction Only to err from the words of knowledge.
verses.Prov.19.28: A worthless witness mocketh at justice; And the mouth of the wicked swalloweth iniquity.
verses.Prov.19.29: Judgments are prepared for scoffers, And stripes for the back of fools.
verses.Prov.20.1: Wine is a mocker, strong drink a brawler; And whosoever erreth thereby is not wise.
verses.Prov.20.2: The terror of a king is as the roaring of a lion: He that provoketh him to anger sinneth against his own life.
verses.Prov.20.3: It is an honor for a man to keep aloof from strife; But every fool will be quarrelling.
verses.Prov.20.4: The sluggard will not plow by reason of the winter; Therefore he shall beg in harvest, and have nothing.
verses.Prov.20.5: Counsel in the heart of man is like deep water; But a man of understanding will draw it out.
verses.Prov.20.6: Most men will proclaim every one his own kindness; But a faithful man who can find?
verses.Prov.20.7: A righteous man that walketh in his integrity, Blessed are his children after him.
verses.Prov.20.8: A king that sitteth on the throne of judgment Scattereth away all evil with his eyes.
verses.Prov.20.9: Who can say, I have made my heart clean, I am pure from my sin?
verses.Prov.20.10: Diverse weights, and diverse measures, Both of them alike are an abomination to Jehovah.
verses.Prov.20.11: Even a child maketh himself known by his doings, Whether his work be pure, and whether it be right.
verses.Prov.20.12: The hearing ear, and the seeing eye, Jehovah hath made even both of them.
verses.Prov.20.13: Love not sleep, lest thou come to poverty; Open thine eyes, and thou shalt be satisfied with bread.
verses.Prov.20.14: It is bad, it is bad, saith the buyer; But when he is gone his way, then he boasteth.
verses.Prov.20.15: There is gold, and abundance of rubies; But the lips of knowledge are a precious jewel.
verses.Prov.20.16: Take his garment that is surety for a stranger; And hold him in pledge that is surety for foreigners.
verses.Prov.20.17: Bread of falsehood is sweet to a man; But afterwards his mouth shall be filled with gravel.
verses.Prov.20.18: Every purpose is established by counsel; And by wise guidance make thou war.
verses.Prov.20.19: He that goeth about as a tale-bearer revealeth secrets; Therefore company not with him that openeth wide his lips.
verses.Prov.20.20: Whoso curseth his father or his mother, His lamp shall be put out in blackness of darkness.
verses.Prov.20.21: An inheritance may be gotten hastily at the beginning; But the end thereof shall not be blessed.
verses.Prov.20.22: Say not thou, I will recompense evil: Wait for Jehovah, and he will save thee.
verses.Prov.20.23: Diverse weights are an abomination to Jehovah; And a false balance is not good.
verses.Prov.20.24: A man’s goings are of Jehovah; How then can man understand his way?
verses.Prov.20.25: It is a snare to a man rashly to say, It is holy, And after vows to make inquiry.
verses.Prov.20.26: A wise king winnoweth the wicked, And bringeth the threshing -wheel over them.
verses.Prov.20.27: The spirit of man is the lamp of Jehovah, Searching all his innermost parts.
verses.Prov.20.28: Kindness and truth preserve the king; And his throne is upholden by kindness.
verses.Prov.20.29: The glory of young men is their strength; And the beauty of old men is the hoary head.
verses.Prov.20.30: Stripes that wound cleanse away evil; And strokes reach the innermost parts.
verses.Prov.21.1: The king’s heart is in the hand of Jehovah as the watercourses: He turneth it whithersoever he will.
verses.Prov.21.2: Every way of a man is right in his own eyes; But Jehovah weigheth the hearts.
verses.Prov.21.3: To do righteousness and justice Is more acceptable to Jehovah than sacrifice.
verses.Prov.21.4: A high look, and a proud heart, Even the lamp of the wicked, is sin.
verses.Prov.21.5: The thoughts of the diligent tend only to plenteousness; But every one that is hasty hasteth only to want.
verses.Prov.21.6: The getting of treasures by a lying tongue Is a vapor driven to and fro by them that seek death.
verses.Prov.21.7: The violence of the wicked shall sweep them away, Because they refuse to do justice.
verses.Prov.21.8: The way of him that is laden with guilt is exceeding crooked; But as for the pure, his work is right.
verses.Prov.21.9: It is better to dwell in the corner of the housetop, Than with a contentious woman in a wide house.
verses.Prov.21.10: The soul of the wicked desireth evil: His neighbor findeth no favor in his eyes.
verses.Prov.21.11: When the scoffer is punished, the simple is made wise; And when the wise is instructed, he receiveth knowledge.
verses.Prov.21.12: The righteous man considereth the house of the wicked, How the wicked are overthrown to their ruin.
verses.Prov.21.13: Whoso stoppeth his ears at the cry of the poor, He also shall cry, but shall not be heard.
verses.Prov.21.14: A gift in secret pacifieth anger; And a present in the bosom, strong wrath.
verses.Prov.21.15: It is joy to the righteous to do justice; But it is a destruction to the workers of iniquity.
verses.Prov.21.16: The man that wandereth out of the way of understanding Shall rest in the assembly of the dead.
verses.Prov.21.17: He that loveth pleasure shall be a poor man: He that loveth wine and oil shall not be rich.
verses.Prov.21.18: The wicked is a ransom for the righteous; And the treacherous cometh in the stead of the upright.
verses.Prov.21.19: It is better to dwell in a desert land, Than with a contentious and fretful woman.
verses.Prov.21.20: There is precious treasure and oil in the dwelling of the wise; But a foolish man swalloweth it up.
verses.Prov.21.21: He that followeth after righteousness and kindness Findeth life, righteousness, and honor.
verses.Prov.21.22: A wise man scaleth the city of the mighty, And bringeth down the strength of the confidence thereof.
verses.Prov.21.23: Whoso keepeth his mouth and his tongue Keepeth his soul from troubles.
verses.Prov.21.24: The proud and haughty man, scoffer is his name; He worketh in the arrogance of pride.
verses.Prov.21.25: The desire of the sluggard killeth him; For his hands refuse to labor.
verses.Prov.21.26: There is that coveteth greedily all the day long; But the righteous giveth and withholdeth not.
verses.Prov.21.27: The sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination; How much more, when he bringeth it with a wicked mind!
verses.Prov.21.28: A false witness shall perish; But the man that heareth shall speak so as to endure.
verses.Prov.21.29: A wicked man hardeneth his face; But as for the upright, he establisheth his ways.
verses.Prov.21.30: There is no wisdom nor understanding Nor counsel against Jehovah.
verses.Prov.21.31: The horse is prepared against the day of battle; But victory is of Jehovah.
verses.Prov.22.1: A good name is rather to be chosen than great riches, And loving favor rather than silver and gold.
verses.Prov.22.2: The rich and the poor meet together: Jehovah is the maker of them all.
verses.Prov.22.3: A prudent man seeth the evil, and hideth himself; But the simple pass on, and suffer for it.
verses.Prov.22.4: The reward of humility and the fear of Jehovah Is riches, and honor, and life.
verses.Prov.22.5: Thorns and snares are in the way of the perverse: He that keepeth his soul shall be far from them.
verses.Prov.22.6: Train up a child in the way he should go, And even when he is old he will not depart from it.
verses.Prov.22.7: The rich ruleth over the poor; And the borrower is servant to the lender.
verses.Prov.22.8: He that soweth iniquity shall reap calamity; And the rod of his wrath shall fail.
verses.Prov.22.9: He that hath a bountiful eye shall be blessed; For he giveth of his bread to the poor.
verses.Prov.22.10: Cast out the scoffer, and contention will go out; Yea, strife and ignominy will cease.
verses.Prov.22.11: He that loveth pureness of heart, For the grace of his lips the king will be his friend.
verses.Prov.22.12: The eyes of Jehovah preserve him that hath knowledge; But he overthroweth the words of the treacherous man.
verses.Prov.22.13: The sluggard saith, There is a lion without; I shall be slain in the streets.
verses.Prov.22.14: The mouth of strange women is a deep pit; He that is abhorred of Jehovah shall fall therein.
verses.Prov.22.15: Foolishness is bound up in the heart of a child; But the rod of correction shall drive it far from him.
verses.Prov.22.16: He that oppresseth the poor to increase his gain, And he that giveth to the rich, shall come only to want.
verses.Prov.22.17: Incline thine ear, and hear the words of the wise, And apply thy heart unto my knowledge.
verses.Prov.22.18: For it is a pleasant thing if thou keep them within thee, If they be established together upon thy lips.
verses.Prov.22.19: That thy trust may be in Jehovah, I have made them known to thee this day, even to thee.
verses.Prov.22.20: Have not I written unto thee excellent things Of counsels and knowledge,
verses.Prov.22.21: To make thee know the certainty of the words of truth, That thou mayest carry back words of truth to them that send thee?
verses.Prov.22.22: Rob not the poor, because he is poor; Neither oppress the afflicted in the gate:
verses.Prov.22.23: For Jehovah will plead their cause, And despoil of life those that despoil them.
verses.Prov.22.24: Make no friendship with a man that is given to anger; And with a wrathful man thou shalt not go:
verses.Prov.22.25: Lest thou learn his ways, And get a snare to thy soul.
verses.Prov.22.26: Be thou not one of them that strike hands, Or of them that are sureties for debts.
verses.Prov.22.27: If thou hast not wherewith to pay, Why should he take away thy bed from under thee?
verses.Prov.22.28: Remove not the ancient landmark, Which thy fathers have set.
verses.Prov.22.29: Seest thou a man diligent in his business? he shall stand before kings; He shall not stand before mean men.
verses.Prov.23.1: When thou sittest to eat with a ruler, Consider diligently him that is before thee;
verses.Prov.23.2: And put a knife to thy throat, If thou be a man given to appetite.
verses.Prov.23.3: Be not desirous of his dainties; Seeing they are deceitful food.
verses.Prov.23.4: Weary not thyself to be rich; Cease from thine own wisdom.
verses.Prov.23.5: Wilt thou set thine eyes upon that which is not? For riches certainly make themselves wings, Like an eagle that flieth toward heaven.
verses.Prov.23.6: Eat thou not the bread of him that hath an evil eye, Neither desire thou his dainties:
verses.Prov.23.7: For as he thinketh within himself, so is he: Eat and drink, saith he to thee; But his heart is not with thee.
verses.Prov.23.8: The morsel which thou hast eaten shalt thou vomit up, And lose thy sweet words.
verses.Prov.23.9: Speak not in the hearing of a fool; For he will despise the wisdom of thy words.
verses.Prov.23.10: Remove not the ancient landmark; And enter not into the fields of the fatherless:
verses.Prov.23.11: For their Redeemer is strong; He will plead their cause against thee.
verses.Prov.23.12: Apply thy heart unto instruction, And thine ears to the words of knowledge.
verses.Prov.23.13: Withhold not correction from the child; For if thou beat him with the rod, he will not die.
verses.Prov.23.14: Thou shalt beat him with the rod, And shalt deliver his soul from Sheol.
verses.Prov.23.15: My son, if thy heart be wise, My heart will be glad, even mine:
verses.Prov.23.16: Yea, my heart will rejoice, When thy lips speak right things.
verses.Prov.23.17: Let not thy heart envy sinners; But be thou in the fear of Jehovah all the day long:
verses.Prov.23.18: For surely there is a reward; And thy hope shall not be cut off.
verses.Prov.23.19: Hear thou, my son, and be wise, And guide thy heart in the way.
verses.Prov.23.20: Be not among winebibbers, Among gluttonous eaters of flesh:
verses.Prov.23.21: For the drunkard and the glutton shall come to poverty; And drowsiness will clothe a man with rags.
verses.Prov.23.22: Hearken unto thy father that begat thee, And despise not thy mother when she is old.
verses.Prov.23.23: Buy the truth, and sell it not; Yea, wisdom, and instruction, and understanding.
verses.Prov.23.24: The father of the righteous will greatly rejoice; And he that begetteth a wise child will have joy of him.
verses.Prov.23.25: Let thy father and thy mother be glad, And let her that bare thee rejoice.
verses.Prov.23.26: My son, give me thy heart; And let thine eyes delight in my ways.
verses.Prov.23.27: For a harlot is a deep ditch; And a foreign woman is a narrow pit.
verses.Prov.23.28: Yea, she lieth in wait as a robber, And increaseth the treacherous among men.
verses.Prov.23.29: Who hath woe? who hath sorrow? who hath contentions? Who hath complaining? who hath wounds without cause? Who hath redness of eyes?
verses.Prov.23.30: They that tarry long at the wine; They that go to seek out mixed wine.
verses.Prov.23.31: Look not thou upon the wine when it is red, When it sparkleth in the cup, When it goeth down smoothly:
verses.Prov.23.32: At the last it biteth like a serpent, And stingeth like an adder.
verses.Prov.23.33: Thine eyes shall behold strange things, And thy heart shall utter perverse things.
verses.Prov.23.34: Yea, thou shalt be as he that lieth down in the midst of the sea, Or as he that lieth upon the top of a mast.
verses.Prov.23.35: They have stricken me, shalt thou say, and I was not hurt; They have beaten me, and I felt it not: When shall I awake? I will seek it yet again.
verses.Prov.24.1: Be not thou envious against evil men; Neither desire to be with them:
verses.Prov.24.2: For their heart studieth oppression, And their lips talk of mischief.
verses.Prov.24.3: Through wisdom is a house builded; And by understanding it is established;
verses.Prov.24.4: And by knowledge are the chambers filled With all precious and pleasant riches.
verses.Prov.24.5: A wise man is strong; Yea, a man of knowledge increaseth might.
verses.Prov.24.6: For by wise guidance thou shalt make thy war; And in the multitude of counsellors there is safety.
verses.Prov.24.7: Wisdom is too high for a fool: He openeth not his mouth in the gate.
verses.Prov.24.8: He that deviseth to do evil, Men shall call him a mischief-maker.
verses.Prov.24.9: The thought of foolishness is sin; And the scoffer is an abomination to men.
verses.Prov.24.10: If thou faint in the day of adversity, Thy strength is small.
verses.Prov.24.11: Deliver them that are carried away unto death, And those that are ready to be slain see that thou hold back.
verses.Prov.24.12: If thou sayest, Behold, we knew not this; Doth not he that weigheth the hearts consider it? And he that keepeth thy soul, doth not he know it? And shall not he render to every man according to his work?
verses.Prov.24.13: My son, eat thou honey, for it is good; And the droppings of the honeycomb, which are sweet to thy taste:
verses.Prov.24.14: So shalt thou know wisdom to be unto thy soul; If thou hast found it, then shall there be a reward, And thy hope shall not be cut off.
verses.Prov.24.15: Lay not wait, O wicked man, against the habitation of the righteous; Destroy not his resting-place:
verses.Prov.24.16: For a righteous man falleth seven times, and riseth up again; But the wicked are overthrown by calamity.
verses.Prov.24.17: Rejoice not when thine enemy falleth, And let not thy heart be glad when he is overthrown;
verses.Prov.24.18: Lest Jehovah see it, and it displease him, And he turn away his wrath from him.
verses.Prov.24.19: Fret not thyself because of evil-doers; Neither be thou envious at the wicked:
verses.Prov.24.20: For there shall be no reward to the evil man; The lamp of the wicked shall be put out.
verses.Prov.24.21: My son, fear thou Jehovah and the king; And company not with them that are given to change:
verses.Prov.24.22: For their calamity shall rise suddenly; And the destruction from them both, who knoweth it?
verses.Prov.24.23: These also are sayings of the wise. To have respect of persons in judgment is not good.
verses.Prov.24.24: He that saith unto the wicked, Thou art righteous, Peoples shall curse him, nations shall abhor him;
verses.Prov.24.25: But to them that rebuke him shall be delight, And a good blessing shall come upon them.
verses.Prov.24.26: He kisseth the lips Who giveth a right answer.
verses.Prov.24.27: Prepare thy work without, And make it ready for thee in the field; And afterwards build thy house.
verses.Prov.24.28: Be not a witness against thy neighbor without cause; And deceive not with thy lips.
verses.Prov.24.29: Say not, I will do so to him as he hath done to me; I will render to the man according to his work.
verses.Prov.24.30: I went by the field of the sluggard, And by the vineyard of the man void of understanding;
verses.Prov.24.31: And, lo, it was all grown over with thorns, The face thereof was covered with nettles, And the stone wall thereof was broken down.
verses.Prov.24.32: Then I beheld, and considered well; I saw, and received instruction:
verses.Prov.24.33: Yet a little sleep, a little slumber, A little folding of the hands to sleep;
verses.Prov.24.34: So shall thy poverty come as a robber, And thy want as an armed man.
verses.Prov.25.1: These also are proverbs of Solomon, which the men of Hezekiah king of Judah copied out.
verses.Prov.25.2: It is the glory of God to conceal a thing; But the glory of kings is to search out a matter.
verses.Prov.25.3: As the heavens for height, and the earth for depth, So the heart of kings is unsearchable.
verses.Prov.25.4: Take away the dross from the silver, And there cometh forth a vessel for the refiner:
verses.Prov.25.5: Take away the wicked from before the king, And his throne shall be established in righteousness.
verses.Prov.25.6: Put not thyself forward in the presence of the king, And stand not in the place of great men:
verses.Prov.25.7: For better is it that it be said unto thee, Come up hither, Than that thou shouldest be put lower in the presence of the prince, Whom thine eyes have seen.
verses.Prov.25.8: Go not forth hastily to strive, Lest thou know not what to do in the end thereof, When thy neighbor hath put thee to shame.
verses.Prov.25.9: Debate thy cause with thy neighbor himself, And disclose not the secret of another;
verses.Prov.25.10: Lest he that heareth it revile thee, And thine infamy turn not away.
verses.Prov.25.11: A word fitly spoken Is like apples of gold in network of silver.
verses.Prov.25.12: As an ear-ring of gold, and an ornament of fine gold, So is a wise reprover upon an obedient ear.
verses.Prov.25.13: As the cold of snow in the time of harvest, So is a faithful messenger to them that send him; For he refresheth the soul of his masters.
verses.Prov.25.14: As clouds and wind without rain, So is he that boasteth himself of his gifts falsely.
verses.Prov.25.15: By long forbearing is a ruler persuaded, And a soft tongue breaketh the bone.
verses.Prov.25.16: Hast thou found honey? eat so much as is sufficient for thee, Lest thou be filled therewith, and vomit it.
verses.Prov.25.17: Let thy foot be seldom in thy neighbor’s house, Lest he be weary of thee, and hate thee.
verses.Prov.25.18: A man that beareth false witness against his neighbor Is a maul, and a sword, and a sharp arrow.
verses.Prov.25.19: Confidence in an unfaithful man in time of trouble Is like a broken tooth, and a foot out of joint.
verses.Prov.25.20: As one that taketh off a garment in cold weather, and as vinegar upon soda, So is he that singeth songs to a heavy heart.
verses.Prov.25.21: If thine enemy be hungry, give him bread to eat; And if he be thirsty, give him water to drink:
verses.Prov.25.22: For thou wilt heap coals of fire upon his head, And Jehovah will reward thee.
verses.Prov.25.23: The north wind bringeth forth rain; So doth a backbiting tongue an angry countenance.
verses.Prov.25.24: It is better to dwell in the corner of the housetop, Than with a contentious woman in a wide house.
verses.Prov.25.25: As cold waters to a thirsty soul, So is good news from a far country.
verses.Prov.25.26: As a troubled fountain, and a corrupted spring, So is a righteous man that giveth way before the wicked.
verses.Prov.25.27: It is not good to eat much honey; So for men to search out their own glory is grievous.
verses.Prov.25.28: He whose spirit is without restraint Is like a city that is broken down and without walls.
verses.Prov.26.1: As snow in summer, and as rain in harvest, So honor is not seemly for a fool.
verses.Prov.26.2: As the sparrow in her wandering, as the swallow in her flying, So the curse that is causeless alighteth not.
verses.Prov.26.3: A whip for the horse, a bridle for the ass, And a rod for the back of fools.
verses.Prov.26.4: Answer not a fool according to his folly, Lest thou also be like unto him.
verses.Prov.26.5: Answer a fool according to his folly, Lest he be wise in his own conceit.
verses.Prov.26.6: He that sendeth a message by the hand of a fool Cutteth off his own feet, and drinketh in damage.
verses.Prov.26.7: The legs of the lame hang loose; So is a parable in the mouth of fools.
verses.Prov.26.8: As one that bindeth a stone in a sling, So is he that giveth honor to a fool.
verses.Prov.26.9: As a thorn that goeth up into the hand of a drunkard, So is a parable in the mouth of fools.
verses.Prov.26.10: As an archer that woundeth all, So is he that hireth a fool and he that hireth them that pass by.
verses.Prov.26.11: As a dog that returneth to his vomit, So is a fool that repeateth his folly.
verses.Prov.26.12: Seest thou a man wise in his own conceit? There is more hope of a fool than of him.
verses.Prov.26.13: The sluggard saith, There is a lion in the way; A lion is in the streets.
verses.Prov.26.14: As the door turneth upon its hinges, So doth the sluggard upon his bed.
verses.Prov.26.15: The sluggard burieth his hand in the dish; It wearieth him to bring it again to his mouth.
verses.Prov.26.16: The sluggard is wiser in his own conceit Than seven men that can render a reason.
verses.Prov.26.17: He that passeth by, and vexeth himself with strife belonging not to him, Is like one that taketh a dog by the ears.
verses.Prov.26.18: As a madman who casteth firebrands, Arrows, and death,
verses.Prov.26.19: So is the man that deceiveth his neighbor, And saith, Am not I in sport?
verses.Prov.26.20: For lack of wood the fire goeth out; And where there is no whisperer, contention ceaseth.
verses.Prov.26.21: As coals are to hot embers, and wood to fire, So is a contentious man to inflame strife.
verses.Prov.26.22: The words of a whisperer are as dainty morsels, And they go down into the innermost parts.
verses.Prov.26.23: Fervent lips and a wicked heart Are like an earthen vessel overlaid with silver dross.
verses.Prov.26.24: He that hateth dissembleth with his lips; But he layeth up deceit within him:
verses.Prov.26.25: When he speaketh fair, believe him not; For there are seven abominations in his heart:
verses.Prov.26.26: Though his hatred cover itself with guile, His wickedness shall be openly showed before the assembly.
verses.Prov.26.27: Whoso diggeth a pit shall fall therein; And he that rolleth a stone, it shall return upon him.
verses.Prov.26.28: A lying tongue hateth those whom it hath wounded; And a flattering mouth worketh ruin.
verses.Prov.27.1: Boast not thyself of to-morrow; For thou knowest not what a day may bring forth.
verses.Prov.27.2: Let another man praise thee, and not thine own mouth; A stranger, and not thine own lips.
verses.Prov.27.3: A stone is heavy, and the sand weighty; But a fool’s vexation is heavier than they both.
verses.Prov.27.4: Wrath is cruel, and anger is overwhelming; But who is able to stand before jealousy?
verses.Prov.27.5: Better is open rebuke Than love that is hidden.
verses.Prov.27.6: Faithful are the wounds of a friend; But the kisses of an enemy are profuse.
verses.Prov.27.7: The full soul loatheth a honeycomb; But to the hungry soul every bitter thing is sweet.
verses.Prov.27.8: As a bird that wandereth from her nest, So is a man that wandereth from his place.
verses.Prov.27.9: Oil and perfume rejoice the heart; So doth the sweetness of a man’s friend that cometh of hearty counsel.
verses.Prov.27.10: Thine own friend, and thy father’s friend, forsake not; And go not to thy brother’s house in the day of thy calamity: Better is a neighbor that is near than a brother far off.
verses.Prov.27.11: My son, be wise, and make my heart glad, That I may answer him that reproacheth me.
verses.Prov.27.12: A prudent man seeth the evil, and hideth himself; But the simple pass on, and suffer for it.
verses.Prov.27.13: Take his garment that is surety for a stranger; And hold him in pledge that is surety for a foreign woman.
verses.Prov.27.14: He that blesseth his friend with a loud voice, rising early in the morning, It shall be counted a curse to him.
verses.Prov.27.15: A continual dropping in a very rainy day And a contentious woman are alike:
verses.Prov.27.16: He that would restrain her restraineth the wind; And his right hand encountereth oil.
verses.Prov.27.17: Iron sharpeneth iron; So a man sharpeneth the countenance of his friend.
verses.Prov.27.18: Whoso keepeth the fig-tree shall eat the fruit thereof; And he that regardeth his master shall be honored.
verses.Prov.27.19: As in water face answereth to face, So the heart of man to man.
verses.Prov.27.20: Sheol and Abaddon are never satisfied; And the eyes of man are never satisfied.
verses.Prov.27.21: The refining pot is for silver, and the furnace for gold; And a man is tried by his praise.
verses.Prov.27.22: Though thou shouldest bray a fool in a mortar with a pestle along with bruised grain, Yet will not his foolishness depart from him.
verses.Prov.27.23: Be thou diligent to know the state of thy flocks, And look well to thy herds:
verses.Prov.27.24: For riches are not for ever; And doth the crown endure unto all generations?
verses.Prov.27.25: The hay is carried, and the tender grass showeth itself, And the herbs of the mountains are gathered in.
verses.Prov.27.26: The lambs are for thy clothing, And the goats are the price of the field;
verses.Prov.27.27: And there will be goats’ milk enough for thy food, for the food of thy household, And maintenance for thy maidens.
verses.Prov.28.1: The wicked flee when no man pursueth; But the righteous are bold as a lion.
verses.Prov.28.2: For the transgression of a land many are the princes thereof; But by men of understanding and knowledge the state thereof shall be prolonged.
verses.Prov.28.3: A needy man that oppresseth the poor Is like a sweeping rain which leaveth no food.
verses.Prov.28.4: They that forsake the law praise the wicked; But such as keep the law contend with them.
verses.Prov.28.5: Evil men understand not justice; But they that seek Jehovah understand all things.
verses.Prov.28.6: Better is the poor that walketh in his integrity, Than he that is perverse in his ways, though he be rich.
verses.Prov.28.7: Whoso keepeth the law is a wise son; But he that is a companion of gluttons shameth his father.
verses.Prov.28.8: He that augmenteth his substance by interest and increase, Gathereth it for him that hath pity on the poor.
verses.Prov.28.9: He that turneth away his ear from hearing the law, Even his prayer is an abomination.
verses.Prov.28.10: Whoso causeth the upright to go astray in an evil way, He shall fall himself into his own pit; But the perfect shall inherit good.
verses.Prov.28.11: The rich man is wise in his own conceit; But the poor that hath understanding searcheth him out.
verses.Prov.28.12: When the righteous triumph, there is great glory; But when the wicked rise, men hide themselves.
verses.Prov.28.13: He that covereth his transgressions shall not prosper; But whoso confesseth and forsaketh them shall obtain mercy.
verses.Prov.28.14: Happy is the man that feareth alway; But he that hardeneth his heart shall fall into mischief.
verses.Prov.28.15: As a roaring lion, and a ranging bear, So is a wicked ruler over a poor people.
verses.Prov.28.16: The prince that lacketh understanding is also a great oppressor; But he that hateth covetousness shall prolong his days.
verses.Prov.28.17: A man that is laden with the blood of any person Shall flee unto the pit; let no man stay him.
verses.Prov.28.18: Whoso walketh uprightly shall be delivered; But he that is perverse in his ways shall fall at once.
verses.Prov.28.19: He that tilleth his land shall have plenty of bread; But he that followeth after vain persons shall have poverty enough.
verses.Prov.28.20: A faithful man shall abound with blessings; But he that maketh haste to be rich shall not be unpunished.
verses.Prov.28.21: To have respect of persons is not good; Neither that a man should transgress for a piece of bread.
verses.Prov.28.22: He that hath an evil eye hasteth after riches, And knoweth not that want shall come upon him.
verses.Prov.28.23: He that rebuketh a man shall afterward find more favor Than he that flattereth with the tongue.
verses.Prov.28.24: Whoso robbeth his father or his mother, and saith, It is no transgression, The same is the companion of a destroyer.
verses.Prov.28.25: He that is of a greedy spirit stirreth up strife; But he that putteth his trust in Jehovah shall be made fat.
verses.Prov.28.26: He that trusteth in his own heart is a fool; But whoso walketh wisely, he shall be delivered.
verses.Prov.28.27: He that giveth unto the poor shall not lack; But he that hideth his eyes shall have many a curse.
verses.Prov.28.28: When the wicked rise, men hide themselves; But when they perish, the righteous increase.
verses.Prov.29.1: He that being often reproved hardeneth his neck Shall suddenly be destroyed, and that without remedy.
verses.Prov.29.2: When the righteous are increased, the people rejoice; But when a wicked man beareth rule, the people sigh.
verses.Prov.29.3: Whoso loveth wisdom rejoiceth his father; But he that keepeth company with harlots wasteth his substance.
verses.Prov.29.4: The king by justice establisheth the land; But he that exacteth gifts overthroweth it.
verses.Prov.29.5: A man that flattereth his neighbor Spreadeth a net for his steps.
verses.Prov.29.6: In the transgression of an evil man there is a snare; But the righteous doth sing and rejoice.
verses.Prov.29.7: The righteous taketh knowledge of the cause of the poor; The wicked hath not understanding to know it.
verses.Prov.29.8: Scoffers set a city in a flame; But wise men turn away wrath.
verses.Prov.29.9: If a wise man hath a controversy with a foolish man, Whether he be angry or laugh, there will be no rest.
verses.Prov.29.10: The bloodthirsty hate him that is perfect; And as for the upright, they seek his life.
verses.Prov.29.11: A fool uttereth all his anger; But a wise man keepeth it back and stilleth it.
verses.Prov.29.12: If a ruler hearkeneth to falsehood, All his servants are wicked.
verses.Prov.29.13: The poor man and the oppressor meet together; Jehovah lighteneth the eyes of them both.
verses.Prov.29.14: The king that faithfully judgeth the poor, His throne shall be established for ever.
verses.Prov.29.15: The rod and reproof give wisdom; But a child left to himself causeth shame to his mother.
verses.Prov.29.16: When the wicked are increased, transgression increaseth; But the righteous shall look upon their fall.
verses.Prov.29.17: Correct thy son, and he will give thee rest; Yea, he will give delight unto thy soul.
verses.Prov.29.18: Where there is no vision, the people cast off restraint; But he that keepeth the law, happy is he.
verses.Prov.29.19: A servant will not be corrected by words; For though he understand, he will not give heed.
verses.Prov.29.20: Seest thou a man that is hasty in his words? There is more hope of a fool than of him.
verses.Prov.29.21: He that delicately bringeth up his servant from a child Shall have him become a son at the last.
verses.Prov.29.22: An angry man stirreth up strife, And a wrathful man aboundeth in transgression.
verses.Prov.29.23: A man’s pride shall bring him low; But he that is of a lowly spirit shall obtain honor.
verses.Prov.29.24: Whoso is partner with a thief hateth his own soul; He heareth the adjuration and uttereth nothing.
verses.Prov.29.25: The fear of man bringeth a snare; But whoso putteth his trust in Jehovah shall be safe.
verses.Prov.29.26: Many seek the ruler’s favor; But a man’s judgment cometh from Jehovah.
verses.Prov.29.27: An unjust man is an abomination to the righteous; And he that is upright in the way is an abomination to the wicked.
verses.Prov.30.1: The words of Agur the son of Jakeh; the oracle. The man saith unto Ithiel, unto Ithiel and Ucal:
verses.Prov.30.2: Surely I am more brutish than any man, And have not the understanding of a man;
verses.Prov.30.3: And I have not learned wisdom, Neither have I the knowledge of the Holy One.
verses.Prov.30.4: Who hath ascended up into heaven, and descended? Who hath gathered the wind in his fists? Who hath bound the waters in his garment? Who hath established all the ends of the earth? What is his name, and what is his son’s name, if thou knowest?
verses.Prov.30.5: Every word of God is tried: He is a shield unto them that take refuge in him.
verses.Prov.30.6: Add thou not unto his words, Lest he reprove thee, and thou be found a liar.
verses.Prov.30.7: Two things have I asked of thee; Deny me them not before I die:
verses.Prov.30.8: Remove far from me falsehood and lies; Give me neither poverty nor riches; Feed me with the food that is needful for me:
verses.Prov.30.9: Lest I be full, and deny thee, and say, Who is Jehovah? Or lest I be poor, and steal, And use profanely the name of my God.
verses.Prov.30.10: Slander not a servant unto his master, Lest he curse thee, and thou be held guilty.
verses.Prov.30.11: There is a generation that curse their father, And bless not their mother.
verses.Prov.30.12: There is a generation that are pure in their own eyes, And yet are not washed from their filthiness.
verses.Prov.30.13: There is a generation, oh how lofty are their eyes! And their eyelids are lifted up.
verses.Prov.30.14: There is a generation whose teeth are as swords, and their jaw teeth as knives, To devour the poor from off the earth, and the needy from among men.
verses.Prov.30.15: The horseleach hath two daughters, crying, Give, give. There are three things that are never satisfied, Yea, four that say not, Enough:
verses.Prov.30.16: Sheol; and the barren womb; The earth that is not satisfied with water; And the fire that saith not, Enough.
verses.Prov.30.17: The eye that mocketh at his father, And despiseth to obey his mother, The ravens of the valley shall pick it out, And the young eagles shall eat it.
verses.Prov.30.18: There are three things which are too wonderful for me, Yea, four which I know not:
verses.Prov.30.19: The way of an eagle in the air; The way of a serpent upon a rock; The way of a ship in the midst of the sea; And the way of a man with a maiden.
verses.Prov.30.20: So is the way of an adulterous woman; She eateth, and wipeth her mouth, And saith, I have done no wickedness.
verses.Prov.30.21: For three things the earth doth tremble, And for four, which it cannot bear:
verses.Prov.30.22: For a servant when he is king; And a fool when he is filled with food;
verses.Prov.30.23: For an odious woman when she is married; And a handmaid that is heir to her mistress.
verses.Prov.30.24: There are four things which are little upon the earth, But they are exceeding wise:
verses.Prov.30.25: The ants are a people not strong, Yet they provide their food in the summer;
verses.Prov.30.26: The conies are but a feeble folk, Yet make they their houses in the rocks;
verses.Prov.30.27: The locusts have no king, Yet go they forth all of them by bands;
verses.Prov.30.28: The lizard taketh hold with her hands, Yet is she in kings’ palaces.
verses.Prov.30.29: There are three things which are stately in their march, Yea, four which are stately in going:
verses.Prov.30.30: The lion, which is mightiest among beasts, And turneth not away for any;
verses.Prov.30.31: The greyhound; the he-goat also; And the king against whom there is no rising up.
verses.Prov.30.32: If thou hast done foolishly in lifting up thyself, Or if thou hast thought evil, Lay thy hand upon thy mouth.
verses.Prov.30.33: For the churning of milk bringeth forth butter, And the wringing of the nose bringeth forth blood; So the forcing of wrath bringeth forth strife.
verses.Prov.31.1: The words of king Lemuel; the oracle which his mother taught him.
verses.Prov.31.2: What, my son? and what, O son of my womb? And what, O son of my vows?
verses.Prov.31.3: Give not thy strength unto women, Nor thy ways to that which destroyeth kings.
verses.Prov.31.4: It is not for kings, O Lemuel, it is not for kings to drink wine; Nor for princes to say, Where is strong drink?
verses.Prov.31.5: Lest they drink, and forget the law, And pervert the justice due to any that is afflicted.
verses.Prov.31.6: Give strong drink unto him that is ready to perish, And wine unto the bitter in soul:
verses.Prov.31.7: Let him drink, and forget his poverty, And remember his misery no more.
verses.Prov.31.8: Open thy mouth for the dumb, In the cause of all such as are left desolate.
verses.Prov.31.9: Open thy mouth, judge righteously, And minister justice to the poor and needy.
verses.Prov.31.10: A worthy woman who can find? For her price is far above rubies.
verses.Prov.31.11: The heart of her husband trusteth in her, And he shall have no lack of gain.
verses.Prov.31.12: She doeth him good and not evil All the days of her life.
verses.Prov.31.13: She seeketh wool and flax, And worketh willingly with her hands.
verses.Prov.31.14: She is like the merchant-ships; She bringeth her bread from afar.
verses.Prov.31.15: She riseth also while it is yet night, And giveth food to her household, And their task to her maidens.
verses.Prov.31.16: She considereth a field, and buyeth it; With the fruit of her hands she planteth a vineyard.
verses.Prov.31.17: She girdeth her loins with strength, And maketh strong her arms.
verses.Prov.31.18: She perceiveth that her merchandise is profitable; Her lamp goeth not out by night.
verses.Prov.31.19: She layeth her hands to the distaff, And her hands hold the spindle.
verses.Prov.31.20: She stretcheth out her hand to the poor; Yea, she reacheth forth her hands to the needy.
verses.Prov.31.21: She is not afraid of the snow for her household; For all her household are clothed with scarlet.
verses.Prov.31.22: She maketh for herself carpets of tapestry; Her clothing is fine linen and purple.
verses.Prov.31.23: Her husband is known in the gates, When he sitteth among the elders of the land.
verses.Prov.31.24: She maketh linen garments and selleth them, And delivereth girdles unto the merchant.
verses.Prov.31.25: Strength and dignity are her clothing; And she laugheth at the time to come.
verses.Prov.31.26: She openeth her mouth with wisdom; And the law of kindness is on her tongue.
verses.Prov.31.27: She looketh well to the ways of her household, And eateth not the bread of idleness.
verses.Prov.31.28: Her children rise up, and call her blessed; Her husband also, and he praiseth her, saying:
verses.Prov.31.29: Many daughters have done worthily, But thou excellest them all.
verses.Prov.31.30: Grace is deceitful, and beauty is vain; But a woman that feareth Jehovah, she shall be praised.
verses.Prov.31.31: Give her of the fruit of her hands; And let her works praise her in the gates.
verses.Eccl.1.1: The words of the Preacher, the son of David, king in Jerusalem.
verses.Eccl.1.2: Vanity of vanities, saith the Preacher; vanity of vanities, all is vanity.
verses.Eccl.1.3: What profit hath man of all his labor wherein he laboreth under the sun?
verses.Eccl.1.4: One generation goeth, and another generation cometh; but the earth abideth for ever.
verses.Eccl.1.5: The sun also ariseth, and the sun goeth down, and hasteth to its place where it ariseth.
verses.Eccl.1.6: The wind goeth toward the south, and turneth about unto the north; it turneth about continually in its course, and the wind returneth again to its circuits.
verses.Eccl.1.7: All the rivers run into the sea, yet the sea is not full; unto the place whither the rivers go, thither they go again.
verses.Eccl.1.8: All things are full of weariness; man cannot utter it: the eye is not satisfied with seeing, nor the ear filled with hearing.
verses.Eccl.1.9: That which hath been is that which shall be; and that which hath been done is that which shall be done: and there is no new thing under the sun.
verses.Eccl.1.10: Is there a thing whereof it may be said, See, this is new? it hath been long ago, in the ages which were before us.
verses.Eccl.1.11: There is no remembrance of the former generations; neither shall there be any remembrance of the latter generations that are to come, among those that shall come after.
verses.Eccl.1.12: I the Preacher was king over Israel in Jerusalem.
verses.Eccl.1.13: And I applied my heart to seek and to search out by wisdom concerning all that is done under heaven: it is a sore travail that God hath given to the sons of men to be exercised therewith.
verses.Eccl.1.14: I have seen all the works that are done under the sun; and, behold, all is vanity and a striving after wind.
verses.Eccl.1.15: That which is crooked cannot be made straight; and that which is wanting cannot be numbered.
verses.Eccl.1.16: I communed with mine own heart, saying, Lo, I have gotten me great wisdom above all that were before me in Jerusalem; yea, my heart hath had great experience of wisdom and knowledge.
verses.Eccl.1.17: And I applied my heart to know wisdom, and to know madness and folly: I perceived that this also was a striving after wind.
verses.Eccl.1.18: For in much wisdom is much grief; and he that increaseth knowledge increaseth sorrow.
verses.Eccl.2.1: I said in my heart, Come now, I will prove thee with mirth; therefore enjoy pleasure: and, behold, this also was vanity.
verses.Eccl.2.2: I said of laughter, It is mad; and of mirth, What doeth it?
verses.Eccl.2.3: I searched in my heart how to cheer my flesh with wine, my heart yet guiding me with wisdom, and how to lay hold on folly, till I might see what it was good for the sons of men that they should do under heaven all the days of their life.
verses.Eccl.2.4: I made me great works; I builded me houses; I planted me vineyards;
verses.Eccl.2.5: I made me gardens and parks, and I planted trees in them of all kinds of fruit;
verses.Eccl.2.6: I made me pools of water, to water therefrom the forest where trees were reared;
verses.Eccl.2.7: I bought men-servants and maid-servants, and had servants born in my house; also I had great possessions of herds and flocks, above all that were before me in Jerusalem;
verses.Eccl.2.8: I gathered me also silver and gold, and the treasure of kings and of the provinces; I gat me men-singers and women-singers, and the delights of the sons of men, musical instruments, and that of all sorts.
verses.Eccl.2.9: So I was great, and increased more than all that were before me in Jerusalem: also my wisdom remained with me.
verses.Eccl.2.10: And whatsoever mine eyes desired I kept not from them; I withheld not my heart from any joy; for my heart rejoiced because of all my labor; and this was my portion from all my labor.
verses.Eccl.2.11: Then I looked on all the works that my hands had wrought, and on the labor that I had labored to do; and, behold, all was vanity and a striving after wind, and there was no profit under the sun.
verses.Eccl.2.12: And I turned myself to behold wisdom, and madness, and folly: for what can the man do that cometh after the king? even that which hath been done long ago.
verses.Eccl.2.13: Then I saw that wisdom excelleth folly, as far as light excelleth darkness.
verses.Eccl.2.14: The wise man’s eyes are in his head, and the fool walketh in darkness: and yet I perceived that one event happeneth to them all.
verses.Eccl.2.15: Then said I in my heart, As it happeneth to the fool, so will it happen even to me; and why was I then more wise? Then said I in my heart, that this also is vanity.
verses.Eccl.2.16: For of the wise man, even as of the fool, there is no remembrance for ever; seeing that in the days to come all will have been long forgotten. And how doth the wise man die even as the fool!
verses.Eccl.2.17: So I hated life, because the work that is wrought under the sun was grievous unto me; for all is vanity and a striving after wind.
verses.Eccl.2.18: And I hated all my labor wherein I labored under the sun, seeing that I must leave it unto the man that shall be after me.
verses.Eccl.2.19: And who knoweth whether he will be a wise man or a fool? yet will he have rule over all my labor wherein I have labored, and wherein I have showed myself wise under the sun. This also is vanity.
verses.Eccl.2.20: Therefore I turned about to cause my heart to despair concerning all the labor wherein I had labored under the sun.
verses.Eccl.2.21: For there is a man whose labor is with wisdom, and with knowledge, and with skilfulness; yet to a man that hath not labored therein shall he leave it for his portion. This also is vanity and a great evil.
verses.Eccl.2.22: For what hath a man of all his labor, and of the striving of his heart, wherein he laboreth under the sun?
verses.Eccl.2.23: For all his days are but sorrows, and his travail is grief; yea, even in the night his heart taketh no rest. This also is vanity.
verses.Eccl.2.24: There is nothing better for a man than that he should eat and drink, and make his soul enjoy good in his labor. This also I saw, that it is from the hand of God.
verses.Eccl.2.25: For who can eat, or who can have enjoyment, more than I?
verses.Eccl.2.26: For to the man that pleaseth him God giveth wisdom, and knowledge, and joy; but to the sinner he giveth travail, to gather and to heap up, that he may give to him that pleaseth God. This also is vanity and a striving after wind.
verses.Eccl.3.1: For everything there is a season, and a time for every purpose under heaven:
verses.Eccl.3.2: a time to be born, and a time to die; a time to plant, and a time to pluck up that which is planted;
verses.Eccl.3.3: a time to kill, and a time to heal; a time to break down, and a time to build up;
verses.Eccl.3.4: a time to weep, and a time to laugh; a time to mourn, and a time to dance;
verses.Eccl.3.5: a time to cast away stones, and a time to gather stones together; a time to embrace, and a time to refrain from embracing;
verses.Eccl.3.6: a time to seek, and a time to lose; a time to keep, and a time to cast away;
verses.Eccl.3.7: a time to rend, and a time to sew; a time to keep silence, and a time to speak;
verses.Eccl.3.8: a time to love, and a time to hate; a time for war, and a time for peace.
verses.Eccl.3.9: What profit hath he that worketh in that wherein he laboreth?
verses.Eccl.3.10: I have seen the travail which God hath given to the sons of men to be exercised therewith.
verses.Eccl.3.11: He hath made everything beautiful in its time: also he hath set eternity in their heart, yet so that man cannot find out the work that God hath done from the beginning even to the end.
verses.Eccl.3.12: I know that there is nothing better for them, than to rejoice, and to do good so long as they live.
verses.Eccl.3.13: And also that every man should eat and drink, and enjoy good in all his labor, is the gift of God.
verses.Eccl.3.14: I know that, whatsoever God doeth, it shall be for ever: nothing can be put to it, nor anything taken from it; and God hath done it, that men should fear before him.
verses.Eccl.3.15: That which is hath been long ago; and that which is to be hath long ago been: and God seeketh again that which is passed away.
verses.Eccl.3.16: And moreover I saw under the sun, in the place of justice, that wickedness was there; and in the place of righteousness, that wickedness was there.
verses.Eccl.3.17: I said in my heart, God will judge the righteous and the wicked; for there is a time there for every purpose and for every work.
verses.Eccl.3.18: I said in my heart, It is because of the sons of men, that God may prove them, and that they may see that they themselves are but as beasts.
verses.Eccl.3.19: For that which befalleth the sons of men befalleth beasts; even one thing befalleth them: as the one dieth, so dieth the other; yea, they have all one breath; and man hath no preeminence above the beasts: for all is vanity.
verses.Eccl.3.20: All go unto one place; all are of the dust, and all turn to dust again.
verses.Eccl.3.21: Who knoweth the spirit of man, whether it goeth upward, and the spirit of the beast, whether it goeth downward to the earth?
verses.Eccl.3.22: Wherefore I saw that there is nothing better, than that a man should rejoice in his works; for that is his portion: for who shall bring him back to see what shall be after him?
verses.Eccl.4.1: Then I returned and saw all the oppressions that are done under the sun: and, behold, the tears of such as were oppressed, and they had no comforter; and on the side of their oppressors there was power; but they had no comforter.
verses.Eccl.4.2: Wherefore I praised the dead that have been long dead more than the living that are yet alive;
verses.Eccl.4.3: yea, better than them both did I esteem him that hath not yet been, who hath not seen the evil work that is done under the sun.
verses.Eccl.4.4: Then I saw all labor and every skilful work, that for this a man is envied of his neighbor. This also is vanity and a striving after wind.
verses.Eccl.4.5: The fool foldeth his hands together, and eateth his own flesh.
verses.Eccl.4.6: Better is a handful, with quietness, than two handfuls with labor and striving after wind.
verses.Eccl.4.7: Then I returned and saw vanity under the sun.
verses.Eccl.4.8: There is one that is alone, and he hath not a second; yea, he hath neither son nor brother; yet is there no end of all his labor, neither are his eyes satisfied with riches. For whom then, saith he, do I labor, and deprive my soul of good? This also is vanity, yea, it is a sore travail.
verses.Eccl.4.9: Two are better than one, because they have a good reward for their labor.
verses.Eccl.4.10: For if they fall, the one will lift up his fellow; but woe to him that is alone when he falleth, and hath not another to lift him up.
verses.Eccl.4.11: Again, if two lie together, then they have warmth; but how can one be warm alone?
verses.Eccl.4.12: And if a man prevail against him that is alone, two shall withstand him; and a threefold cord is not quickly broken.
verses.Eccl.4.13: Better is a poor and wise youth than an old and foolish king, who knoweth not how to receive admonition any more.
verses.Eccl.4.14: For out of prison he came forth to be king; yea, even in his kingdom he was born poor.
verses.Eccl.4.15: I saw all the living that walk under the sun, that they were with the youth, the second, that stood up in his stead.
verses.Eccl.4.16: There was no end of all the people, even of all them over whom he was: yet they that come after shall not rejoice in him. Surely this also is vanity and a striving after wind.
verses.Eccl.5.1: Keep thy foot when thou goest to the house of God; for to draw nigh to hear is better than to give the sacrifice of fools: for they know not that they do evil.
verses.Eccl.5.2: Be not rash with thy mouth, and let not thy heart be hasty to utter anything before God; for God is in heaven, and thou upon earth: therefore let thy words be few.
verses.Eccl.5.3: For a dream cometh with a multitude of business, and a fool’s voice with a multitude of words.
verses.Eccl.5.4: When thou vowest a vow unto God, defer not to pay it; for he hath no pleasure in fools: pay that which thou vowest.
verses.Eccl.5.5: Better is it that thou shouldest not vow, than that thou shouldest vow and not pay.
verses.Eccl.5.6: Suffer not thy mouth to cause thy flesh to sin; neither say thou before the angel, that it was an error: wherefore should God be angry at thy voice, and destroy the work of thy hands?
verses.Eccl.5.7: For in the multitude of dreams there are vanities, and in many words: but fear thou God.
verses.Eccl.5.8: If thou seest the oppression of the poor, and the violent taking away of justice and righteousness in a province, marvel not at the matter: for one higher than the high regardeth; and there are higher than they.
verses.Eccl.5.9: Moreover the profit of the earth is for all: the king himself is served by the field.
verses.Eccl.5.10: He that loveth silver shall not be satisfied with silver; nor he that loveth abundance, with increase: this also is vanity.
verses.Eccl.5.11: When goods increase, they are increased that eat them; and what advantage is there to the owner thereof, save the beholding of them with his eyes?
verses.Eccl.5.12: The sleep of a laboring man is sweet, whether he eat little or much; but the fulness of the rich will not suffer him to sleep.
verses.Eccl.5.13: There is a grievous evil which I have seen under the sun, namely, riches kept by the owner thereof to his hurt:
verses.Eccl.5.14: and those riches perish by evil adventure; and if he hath begotten a son, there is nothing in his hand.
verses.Eccl.5.15: As he came forth from his mother’s womb, naked shall he go again as he came, and shall take nothing for his labor, which he may carry away in his hand.
verses.Eccl.5.16: And this also is a grievous evil, that in all points as he came, so shall he go: and what profit hath he that he laboreth for the wind?
verses.Eccl.5.17: All his days also he eateth in darkness, and he is sore vexed, and hath sickness and wrath.
verses.Eccl.5.18: Behold, that which I have seen to be good and to be comely is for one to eat and to drink, and to enjoy good in all his labor, wherein he laboreth under the sun, all the days of his life which God hath given him: for this is his portion.
verses.Eccl.5.19: Every man also to whom God hath given riches and wealth, and hath given him power to eat thereof, and to take his portion, and to rejoice in his labor—this is the gift of God.
verses.Eccl.5.20: For he shall not much remember the days of his life; because God answereth him in the joy of his heart.
verses.Eccl.6.1: There is an evil which I have seen under the sun, and it is heavy upon men:
verses.Eccl.6.2: a man to whom God giveth riches, wealth, and honor, so that he lacketh nothing for his soul of all that he desireth, yet God giveth him not power to eat thereof, but an alien eateth it; this is vanity, and it is an evil disease.
verses.Eccl.6.3: If a man beget a hundred children, and live many years, so that the days of his years are many, but his soul be not filled with good, and moreover he have no burial; I say, that an untimely birth is better than he:
verses.Eccl.6.4: for it cometh in vanity, and departeth in darkness, and the name thereof is covered with darkness;
verses.Eccl.6.5: moreover it hath not seen the sun nor known it; this hath rest rather than the other:
verses.Eccl.6.6: yea, though he live a thousand years twice told, and yet enjoy no good, do not all go to one place?
verses.Eccl.6.7: All the labor of man is for his mouth, and yet the appetite is not filled.
verses.Eccl.6.8: For what advantage hath the wise more than the fool? or what hath the poor man, that knoweth how to walk before the living?
verses.Eccl.6.9: Better is the sight of the eyes than the wandering of the desire: this also is vanity and a striving after wind.
verses.Eccl.6.10: Whatsoever hath been, the name thereof was given long ago; and it is known what man is; neither can he contend with him that is mightier than he.
verses.Eccl.6.11: Seeing there are many things that increase vanity, what is man the better?
verses.Eccl.6.12: For who knoweth what is good for man in his life, all the days of his vain life which he spendeth as a shadow? for who can tell a man what shall be after him under the sun?
verses.Eccl.7.1: A good name is better than precious oil; and the day of death, than the day of one’s birth.
verses.Eccl.7.2: It is better to go to the house of mourning than to go to the house of feasting: for that is the end of all men; and the living will lay it to his heart.
verses.Eccl.7.3: Sorrow is better than laughter; for by the sadness of the countenance the heart is made glad.
verses.Eccl.7.4: The heart of the wise is in the house of mourning; but the heart of fools is in the house of mirth.
verses.Eccl.7.5: It is better to hear the rebuke of the wise, than for a man to hear the song of fools.
verses.Eccl.7.6: For as the crackling of thorns under a pot, so is the laughter of the fool: this also is vanity.
verses.Eccl.7.7: Surely extortion maketh the wise man foolish; and a bribe destroyeth the understanding.
verses.Eccl.7.8: Better is the end of a thing than the beginning thereof; and the patient in spirit is better than the proud in spirit.
verses.Eccl.7.9: Be not hasty in thy spirit to be angry; for anger resteth in the bosom of fools.
verses.Eccl.7.10: Say not thou, What is the cause that the former days were better than these? for thou dost not inquire wisely concerning this.
verses.Eccl.7.11: Wisdom is as good as an inheritance; yea, more excellent is it for them that see the sun.
verses.Eccl.7.12: For wisdom is a defence, even as money is a defence; but the excellency of knowledge is, that wisdom preserveth the life of him that hath it.
verses.Eccl.7.13: Consider the work of God: for who can make that straight, which he hath made crooked?
verses.Eccl.7.14: In the day of prosperity be joyful, and in the day of adversity consider; yea, God hath made the one side by side with the other, to the end that man should not find out anything that shall be after him.
verses.Eccl.7.15: All this have I seen in my days of vanity: there is a righteous man that perisheth in his righteousness, and there is a wicked man that prolongeth his life in his evil-doing.
verses.Eccl.7.16: Be not righteous overmuch; neither make thyself overwise: why shouldest thou destroy thyself?
verses.Eccl.7.17: Be not overmuch wicked, neither be thou foolish: why shouldest thou die before thy time?
verses.Eccl.7.18: It is good that thou shouldest take hold of this; yea, also from that withdraw not thy hand: for he that feareth God shall come forth from them all.
verses.Eccl.7.19: Wisdom is a strength to the wise man more than ten rulers that are in a city.
verses.Eccl.7.20: Surely there is not a righteous man upon earth, that doeth good, and sinneth not.
verses.Eccl.7.21: Also take not heed unto all words that are spoken, lest thou hear thy servant curse thee;
verses.Eccl.7.22: for oftentimes also thine own heart knoweth that thou thyself likewise hast cursed others.
verses.Eccl.7.23: All this have I proved in wisdom: I said, I will be wise; but it was far from me.
verses.Eccl.7.24: That which is, is far off and exceeding deep; who can find it out?
verses.Eccl.7.25: I turned about, and my heart was set to know and to search out, and to seek wisdom and the reason of things, and to know that wickedness is folly, and that foolishness is madness.
verses.Eccl.7.26: And I find more bitter than death the woman whose heart is snares and nets, and whose hands are bands: whoso pleaseth God shall escape from her; but the sinner shall be taken by her.
verses.Eccl.7.27: Behold, this have I found, saith the Preacher, laying one thing to another, to find out the account;
verses.Eccl.7.28: which my soul still seeketh, but I have not found: one man among a thousand have I found; but a woman among all those have I not found.
verses.Eccl.7.29: Behold, this only have I found: that God made man upright; but they have sought out many inventions.
verses.Eccl.8.1: Who is as the wise man? and who knoweth the interpretation of a thing? A man’s wisdom maketh his face to shine, and the hardness of his face is changed.
verses.Eccl.8.2: I counsel thee, Keep the king’s command, and that in regard of the oath of God.
verses.Eccl.8.3: Be not hasty to go out of his presence; persist not in an evil thing: for he doeth whatsoever pleaseth him.
verses.Eccl.8.4: For the king’s word hath power; and who may say unto him, What doest thou?
verses.Eccl.8.5: Whoso keepeth the commandment shall know no evil thing; and a wise man’s heart discerneth time and judgment:
verses.Eccl.8.6: for to every purpose there is a time and judgment; because the misery of man is great upon him:
verses.Eccl.8.7: for he knoweth not that which shall be; for who can tell him how it shall be?
verses.Eccl.8.8: There is no man that hath power over the spirit to retain the spirit; neither hath he power over the day of death; and there is no discharge in war: neither shall wickedness deliver him that is given to it.
verses.Eccl.8.9: All this have I seen, and applied my heart unto every work that is done under the sun: there is a time wherein one man hath power over another to his hurt.
verses.Eccl.8.10: So I saw the wicked buried, and they came to the grave; and they that had done right went away from the holy place, and were forgotten in the city: this also is vanity.
verses.Eccl.8.11: Because sentence against an evil work is not executed speedily, therefore the heart of the sons of men is fully set in them to do evil.
verses.Eccl.8.12: Though a sinner do evil a hundred times, and prolong his days, yet surely I know that it shall be well with them that fear God, that fear before him:
verses.Eccl.8.13: but it shall not be well with the wicked, neither shall he prolong his days, which are as a shadow; because he feareth not before God.
verses.Eccl.8.14: There is a vanity which is done upon the earth, that there are righteous men unto whom it happeneth according to the work of the wicked; again, there are wicked men to whom it happeneth according to the work of the righteous: I said that this also is vanity.
verses.Eccl.8.15: Then I commended mirth, because a man hath no better thing under the sun, than to eat, and to drink, and to be joyful: for that shall abide with him in his labor all the days of his life which God hath given him under the sun.
verses.Eccl.8.16: When I applied my heart to know wisdom, and to see the business that is done upon the earth (for also there is that neither day nor night seeth sleep with his eyes),
verses.Eccl.8.17: then I beheld all the work of God, that man cannot find out the work that is done under the sun: because however much a man labor to seek it out, yet he shall not find it; yea moreover, though a wise man think to know it, yet shall he not be able to find it.
verses.Eccl.9.1: For all this I laid to my heart, even to explore all this: that the righteous, and the wise, and their works, are in the hand of God; whether it be love or hatred, man knoweth it not; all is before them.
verses.Eccl.9.2: All things come alike to all: there is one event to the righteous and to the wicked; to the good and to the clean and to the unclean; to him that sacrificeth and to him that sacrificeth not; as is the good, so is the sinner; and he that sweareth, as he that feareth an oath.
verses.Eccl.9.3: This is an evil in all that is done under the sun, that there is one event unto all: yea also, the heart of the sons of men is full of evil, and madness is in their heart while they live, and after that they go to the dead.
verses.Eccl.9.4: For to him that is joined with all the living there is hope; for a living dog is better than a dead lion.
verses.Eccl.9.5: For the living know that they shall die: but the dead know not anything, neither have they any more a reward; for the memory of them is forgotten.
verses.Eccl.9.6: As well their love, as their hatred and their envy, is perished long ago; neither have they any more a portion for ever in anything that is done under the sun.
verses.Eccl.9.7: Go thy way, eat thy bread with joy, and drink thy wine with a merry heart; for God hath already accepted thy works.
verses.Eccl.9.8: Let thy garments be always white; and let not thy head lack oil.
verses.Eccl.9.9: Live joyfully with the wife whom thou lovest all the days of thy life of vanity, which he hath given thee under the sun, all thy days of vanity: for that is thy portion in life, and in thy labor wherein thou laborest under the sun.
verses.Eccl.9.10: Whatsoever thy hand findeth to do, do it with thy might; for there is no work, nor device, nor knowledge, nor wisdom, in Sheol, whither thou goest.
verses.Eccl.9.11: I returned, and saw under the sun, that the race is not to the swift, nor the battle to the strong, neither yet bread to the wise, nor yet riches to men of understanding, nor yet favor to men of skill; but time and chance happeneth to them all.
verses.Eccl.9.12: For man also knoweth not his time: as the fishes that are taken in an evil net, and as the birds that are caught in the snare, even so are the sons of men snared in an evil time, when it falleth suddenly upon them.
verses.Eccl.9.13: I have also seen wisdom under the sun on this wise, and it seemed great unto me:
verses.Eccl.9.14: There was a little city, and few men within it; and there came a great king against it, and besieged it, and built great bulwarks against it.
verses.Eccl.9.15: Now there was found in it a poor wise man, and he by his wisdom delivered the city; yet no man remembered that same poor man.
verses.Eccl.9.16: Then said I, Wisdom is better than strength: nevertheless the poor man’s wisdom is despised, and his words are not heard.
verses.Eccl.9.17: The words of the wise heard in quiet are better than the cry of him that ruleth among fools.
verses.Eccl.9.18: Wisdom is better than weapons of war; but one sinner destroyeth much good.
verses.Eccl.10.1: Dead flies cause the oil of the perfumer to send forth an evil odor; so doth a little folly outweigh wisdom and honor.
verses.Eccl.10.2: A wise man’s heart is at his right hand; but a fool’s heart at his left.
verses.Eccl.10.3: Yea also, when the fool walketh by the way, his understanding faileth him, and he saith to every one that he is a fool.
verses.Eccl.10.4: If the spirit of the ruler rise up against thee, leave not thy place; for gentleness allayeth great offences.
verses.Eccl.10.5: There is an evil which I have seen under the sun, as it were an error which proceedeth from the ruler:
verses.Eccl.10.6: folly is set in great dignity, and the rich sit in a low place.
verses.Eccl.10.7: I have seen servants upon horses, and princes walking like servants upon the earth.
verses.Eccl.10.8: He that diggeth a pit shall fall into it; and whoso breaketh through a wall, a serpent shall bite him.
verses.Eccl.10.9: Whoso heweth out stones shall be hurt therewith; and he that cleaveth wood is endangered thereby.
verses.Eccl.10.10: If the iron be blunt, and one do not whet the edge, then must he put to more strength: but wisdom is profitable to direct.
verses.Eccl.10.11: If the serpent bite before it is charmed, then is there no advantage in the charmer.
verses.Eccl.10.12: The words of a wise man’s mouth are gracious; but the lips of a fool will swallow up himself.
verses.Eccl.10.13: The beginning of the words of his mouth is foolishness; and the end of his talk is mischievous madness.
verses.Eccl.10.14: A fool also multiplieth words: yet man knoweth not what shall be; and that which shall be after him, who can tell him?
verses.Eccl.10.15: The labor of fools wearieth every one of them; for he knoweth not how to go to the city.
verses.Eccl.10.16: Woe to thee, O land, when thy king is a child, and thy princes eat in the morning!
verses.Eccl.10.17: Happy art thou, O land, when thy king is the son of nobles, and thy princes eat in due season, for strength, and not for drunkenness!
verses.Eccl.10.18: By slothfulness the roof sinketh in; and through idleness of the hands the house leaketh.
verses.Eccl.10.19: A feast is made for laughter, and wine maketh glad the life; and money answereth all things.
verses.Eccl.10.20: Revile not the king, no, not in thy thought; and revile not the rich in thy bedchamber: for a bird of the heavens shall carry the voice, and that which hath wings shall tell the matter.
verses.Eccl.11.1: Cast thy bread upon the waters; for thou shalt find it after many days.
verses.Eccl.11.2: Give a portion to seven, yea, even unto eight; for thou knowest not what evil shall be upon the earth.
verses.Eccl.11.3: If the clouds be full of rain, they empty themselves upon the earth; and if a tree fall toward the south, or toward the north, in the place where the tree falleth, there shall it be.
verses.Eccl.11.4: He that observeth the wind shall not sow; and he that regardeth the clouds shall not reap.
verses.Eccl.11.5: As thou knowest not what is the way of the wind, nor how the bones do grow in the womb of her that is with child; even so thou knowest not the work of God who doeth all.
verses.Eccl.11.6: In the morning sow thy seed, and in the evening withhold not thy hand; for thou knowest not which shall prosper, whether this or that, or whether they both shall be alike good.
verses.Eccl.11.7: Truly the light is sweet, and a pleasant thing it is for the eyes to behold the sun.
verses.Eccl.11.8: Yea, if a man live many years, let him rejoice in them all; but let him remember the days of darkness, for they shall be many. All that cometh is vanity.
verses.Eccl.11.9: Rejoice, O young man, in thy youth, and let thy heart cheer thee in the days of thy youth, and walk in the ways of thy heart, and in the sight of thine eyes; but know thou, that for all these things God will bring thee into judgment.
verses.Eccl.11.10: Therefore remove sorrow from thy heart, and put away evil from thy flesh; for youth and the dawn of life are vanity.
verses.Eccl.12.1: Remember also thy Creator in the days of thy youth, before the evil days come, and the years draw nigh, when thou shalt say, I have no pleasure in them;
verses.Eccl.12.2: before the sun, and the light, and the moon, and the stars, are darkened, and the clouds return after the rain;
verses.Eccl.12.3: in the day when the keepers of the house shall tremble, and the strong men shall bow themselves, and the grinders cease because they are few, and those that look out of the windows shall be darkened,
verses.Eccl.12.4: and the doors shall be shut in the street; when the sound of the grinding is low, and one shall rise up at the voice of a bird, and all the daughters of music shall be brought low;
verses.Eccl.12.5: yea, they shall be afraid of that which is high, and terrors shall be in the way; and the almond-tree shall blossom, and the grasshopper shall be a burden, and desire shall fail; because man goeth to his everlasting home, and the mourners go about the streets:
verses.Eccl.12.6: before the silver cord is loosed, or the golden bowl is broken, or the pitcher is broken at the fountain, or the wheel broken at the cistern,
verses.Eccl.12.7: and the dust returneth to the earth as it was, and the spirit returneth unto God who gave it.
verses.Eccl.12.8: Vanity of vanities, saith the Preacher; all is vanity.
verses.Eccl.12.9: And further, because the Preacher was wise, he still taught the people knowledge; yea, he pondered, and sought out, and set in order many proverbs.
verses.Eccl.12.10: The Preacher sought to find out acceptable words, and that which was written uprightly, even words of truth.
verses.Eccl.12.11: The words of the wise are as goads; and as nails well fastened are the words of the masters of assemblies, which are given from one shepherd.
verses.Eccl.12.12: And furthermore, my son, be admonished: of making many books there is no end; and much study is a weariness of the flesh.
verses.Eccl.12.13: This is the end of the matter; all hath been heard: Fear God, and keep his commandments; for this is the whole duty of man.
verses.Eccl.12.14: For God will bring every work into judgment, with every hidden thing, whether it be good, or whether it be evil.
verses.Song.1.1: The Song of songs, which is Solomon’s.
verses.Song.1.2: Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth; For thy love is better than wine.
verses.Song.1.3: Thine oils have a goodly fragrance; Thy name is as oil poured forth; Therefore do the virgins love thee.
verses.Song.1.4: Draw me; we will run after thee: The king hath brought me into his chambers; We will be glad and rejoice in thee; We will make mention of thy love more than of wine: Rightly do they love thee.
verses.Song.1.5: I am black, but comely, Oh ye daughters of Jerusalem, As the tents of Kedar, As the curtains of Solomon.
verses.Song.1.6: Look not upon me, because I am swarthy, Because the sun hath scorched me. My mother’s sons were incensed against me; They made me keeper of the vineyards; But mine own vineyard have I not kept.
verses.Song.1.7: Tell me, O thou whom my soul loveth, Where thou feedest thy flock, Where thou makest it to rest at noon: For why should I be as one that is veiled Beside the flocks of thy companions?
verses.Song.1.8: If thou know not, O thou fairest among women, Go thy way forth by the footsteps of the flock, And feed thy kids beside the shepherds’ tents.
verses.Song.1.9: I have compared thee, O my love, To a steed in Pharaoh’s chariots.
verses.Song.1.10: Thy cheeks are comely with plaits of hair, Thy neck with strings of jewels.
verses.Song.1.11: We will make thee plaits of gold With studs of silver.
verses.Song.1.12: While the king sat at his table, My spikenard sent forth its fragrance.
verses.Song.1.13: My beloved is unto me as a bundle of myrrh, That lieth betwixt my breasts.
verses.Song.1.14: My beloved is unto me as a cluster of henna-flowers In the vineyards of En-gedi.
verses.Song.1.15: Behold, thou art fair, my love; Behold thou art fair; Thine eyes are as doves.
verses.Song.1.16: Behold, thou art fair, my beloved, yea, pleasant: Also our couch is green.
verses.Song.1.17: The beams of our house are cedars, And our rafters are firs.
verses.Song.2.1: I am a rose of Sharon, A lily of the valleys.
verses.Song.2.2: As a lily among thorns, So is my love among the daughters.
verses.Song.2.3: As the apple-tree among the trees of the wood, So is my beloved among the sons. I sat down under his shadow with great delight, And his fruit was sweet to my taste.
verses.Song.2.4: He brought me to the banqueting-house, And his banner over me was love.
verses.Song.2.5: Stay ye me with raisins, refresh me with apples; For I am sick from love.
verses.Song.2.6: His left hand is under my head, And his right hand doth embrace me.
verses.Song.2.7: I adjure you, O daughters of Jerusalem, By the roes, or by the hinds of the field, That ye stir not up, nor awake my love, Until he please.
verses.Song.2.8: The voice of my beloved! behold, he cometh, Leaping upon the mountains, Skipping upon the hills.
verses.Song.2.9: My beloved is like a roe or a young hart: Behold, he standeth behind our wall; He looketh in at the windows; He glanceth through the lattice.
verses.Song.2.10: My beloved spake, and said unto me, Rise up, my love, my fair one, and come away.
verses.Song.2.11: For, lo, the winter is past; The rain is over and gone;
verses.Song.2.12: The flowers appear on the earth; The time of the singing of birds is come, And the voice of the turtle-dove is heard in our land;
verses.Song.2.13: The fig-tree ripeneth her green figs, And the vines are in blossom; They give forth their fragrance. Arise, my love, my fair one, and come away.
verses.Song.2.14: O my dove, that art in the clefts of the rock, In the covert of the steep place, Let me see thy countenance, Let me hear thy voice; For sweet is thy voice, and thy countenance is comely.
verses.Song.2.15: Take us the foxes, the little foxes, That spoil the vineyards; For our vineyards are in blossom.
verses.Song.2.16: My beloved is mine, and I am his: He feedeth his flock among the lilies.
verses.Song.2.17: Until the day be cool, and the shadows flee away, Turn, my beloved, and be thou like a roe or a young hart Upon the mountains of Bether.
verses.Song.3.1: By night on my bed I sought him whom my soul loveth: I sought him, but I found him not.
verses.Song.3.2: I said, I will rise now, and go about the city; In the streets and in the broad ways I will seek him whom my soul loveth: I sought him, but I found him not.
