verses.Matt.22.3: and sent out his servants to call those who were invited to the wedding feast, but they would not come.
verses.Matt.22.4: Again he sent out other servants, saying, ‘Tell those who are invited, “Behold, I have prepared my dinner. My cattle and my fatlings are killed, and all things are ready. Come to the wedding feast!”’
verses.Matt.22.5: But they made light of it, and went their ways, one to his own farm, another to his merchandise;
verses.Matt.22.6: and the rest grabbed his servants, treated them shamefully, and killed them.
verses.Matt.22.7: When the king heard that, he was angry, and sent his armies, destroyed those murderers, and burned their city.
verses.Matt.22.8: “Then he said to his servants, ‘The wedding is ready, but those who were invited weren’t worthy.
verses.Matt.22.9: Go therefore to the intersections of the highways, and as many as you may find, invite to the wedding feast.’
verses.Matt.22.10: Those servants went out into the highways and gathered together as many as they found, both bad and good. The wedding was filled with guests.
verses.Matt.22.11: “But when the king came in to see the guests, he saw there a man who didn’t have on wedding clothing,
verses.Matt.22.12: and he said to him, ‘Friend, how did you come in here not wearing wedding clothing?’ He was speechless.
verses.Matt.22.13: Then the king said to the servants, ‘Bind him hand and foot, take him away, and throw him into the outer darkness. That is where the weeping and grinding of teeth will be.’
verses.Matt.22.14: For many are called, but few chosen.”
verses.Matt.22.15: Then the Pharisees went and took counsel how they might entrap him in his talk.
verses.Matt.22.16: They sent their disciples to him, along with the Herodians, saying, “Teacher, we know that you are honest, and teach the way of God in truth, no matter whom you teach; for you aren’t partial to anyone.
verses.Matt.22.17: Tell us therefore, what do you think? Is it lawful to pay taxes to Caesar, or not?”
verses.Matt.22.18: But Jesus perceived their wickedness, and said, “Why do you test me, you hypocrites?
verses.Matt.22.19: Show me the tax money.” They brought to him a denarius.
verses.Matt.22.20: He asked them, “Whose is this image and inscription?”
verses.Matt.22.21: They said to him, “Caesar’s.” Then he said to them, “Give therefore to Caesar the things that are Caesar’s, and to God the things that are God’s.”
verses.Matt.22.22: When they heard it, they marveled, and left him and went away.
verses.Matt.22.23: On that day Sadducees (those who say that there is no resurrection) came to him. They asked him,
verses.Matt.22.24: saying, “Teacher, Moses said, ‘If a man dies, having no children, his brother shall marry his wife and raise up offspring for his brother.’
verses.Matt.22.25: Now there were with us seven brothers. The first married and died, and having no offspring left his wife to his brother.
verses.Matt.22.26: In the same way, the second also, and the third, to the seventh.
verses.Matt.22.27: After them all, the woman died.
verses.Matt.22.28: In the resurrection therefore, whose wife will she be of the seven? For they all had her.”
verses.Matt.22.29: But Jesus answered them, “You are mistaken, not knowing the Scriptures, nor the power of God.
verses.Matt.22.30: For in the resurrection they neither marry nor are given in marriage, but are like God’s angels in heaven.
verses.Matt.22.31: But concerning the resurrection of the dead, haven’t you read that which was spoken to you by God, saying,
verses.Matt.22.32: ‘I am the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob’? God is not the God of the dead, but of the living.”
verses.Matt.22.33: When the multitudes heard it, they were astonished at his teaching.
verses.Matt.22.34: But the Pharisees, when they heard that he had silenced the Sadducees, gathered themselves together.
verses.Matt.22.35: One of them, a lawyer, asked him a question, testing him.
verses.Matt.22.36: “Teacher, which is the greatest commandment in the law?”
verses.Matt.22.37: Jesus said to him, “‘You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your mind.’
verses.Matt.22.38: This is the first and great commandment.
verses.Matt.22.39: A second likewise is this, ‘You shall love your neighbor as yourself.’
verses.Matt.22.40: The whole law and the prophets depend on these two commandments.”
verses.Matt.22.41: Now while the Pharisees were gathered together, Jesus asked them a question,
verses.Matt.22.42: saying, “What do you think of the Christ? Whose son is he?” They said to him, “Of David.”
verses.Matt.22.43: He said to them, “How then does David in the Spirit call him Lord, saying,
verses.Matt.22.44:
‘The Lord said to my Lord,
sit on my right hand,
until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet’?
verses.Matt.22.45: “If then David calls him Lord, how is he his son?”
verses.Matt.22.46: No one was able to answer him a word, neither did any man dare ask him any more questions from that day forward.
verses.Matt.23.1: Then Jesus spoke to the multitudes and to his disciples,
verses.Matt.23.2: saying, “The scribes and the Pharisees sit on Moses’ seat.
verses.Matt.23.3: All things therefore whatever they tell you to observe, observe and do, but don’t do their works; for they say, and don’t do.
verses.Matt.23.4: For they bind heavy burdens that are grievous to be borne, and lay them on men’s shoulders; but they themselves will not lift a finger to help them.
verses.Matt.23.5: But they do all their works to be seen by men. They make their phylacteries broad and enlarge the fringes of their garments,
verses.Matt.23.6: and love the place of honor at feasts, the best seats in the synagogues,
verses.Matt.23.7: the salutations in the marketplaces, and to be called ‘Rabbi, Rabbi’ by men.
verses.Matt.23.8: But you are not to be called ‘Rabbi’, for one is your teacher, the Christ, and all of you are brothers.
verses.Matt.23.9: Call no man on the earth your father, for one is your Father, he who is in heaven.
verses.Matt.23.10: Neither be called masters, for one is your master, the Christ.
verses.Matt.23.11: But he who is greatest among you will be your servant.
verses.Matt.23.12: Whoever exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted.
verses.Matt.23.13: “Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you devour widows’ houses, and as a pretense you make long prayers. Therefore you will receive greater condemnation.
verses.Matt.23.14: “But woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! Because you shut up the Kingdom of Heaven against men; for you don’t enter in yourselves, neither do you allow those who are entering in to enter.
verses.Matt.23.15: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you travel around by sea and land to make one proselyte; and when he becomes one, you make him twice as much a son of Gehenna as yourselves.
verses.Matt.23.16: “Woe to you, you blind guides, who say, ‘Whoever swears by the temple, it is nothing; but whoever swears by the gold of the temple, he is obligated.’
verses.Matt.23.17: You blind fools! For which is greater, the gold or the temple that sanctifies the gold?
verses.Matt.23.18: And, ‘Whoever swears by the altar, it is nothing; but whoever swears by the gift that is on it, he is obligated.’
verses.Matt.23.19: You blind fools! For which is greater, the gift, or the altar that sanctifies the gift?
verses.Matt.23.20: He therefore who swears by the altar, swears by it and by everything on it.
verses.Matt.23.21: He who swears by the temple, swears by it and by him who has been living in it.
verses.Matt.23.22: He who swears by heaven, swears by the throne of God and by him who sits on it.
verses.Matt.23.23: “Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you tithe mint, dill, and cumin, and have left undone the weightier matters of the law: justice, mercy, and faith. But you ought to have done these, and not to have left the other undone.
verses.Matt.23.24: You blind guides, who strain out a gnat, and swallow a camel!
verses.Matt.23.25: “Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you clean the outside of the cup and of the platter, but within they are full of extortion and unrighteousness.
verses.Matt.23.26: You blind Pharisee, first clean the inside of the cup and of the platter, that its outside may become clean also.
verses.Matt.23.27: “Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you are like whitened tombs, which outwardly appear beautiful, but inwardly are full of dead men’s bones and of all uncleanness.
verses.Matt.23.28: Even so you also outwardly appear righteous to men, but inwardly you are full of hypocrisy and iniquity.
verses.Matt.23.29: “Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you build the tombs of the prophets and decorate the tombs of the righteous,
verses.Matt.23.30: and say, ‘If we had lived in the days of our fathers, we wouldn’t have been partakers with them in the blood of the prophets.’
verses.Matt.23.31: Therefore you testify to yourselves that you are children of those who killed the prophets.
verses.Matt.23.32: Fill up, then, the measure of your fathers.
verses.Matt.23.33: You serpents, you offspring of vipers, how will you escape the judgment of Gehenna?
verses.Matt.23.34: Therefore, behold, I send to you prophets, wise men, and scribes. Some of them you will kill and crucify; and some of them you will scourge in your synagogues and persecute from city to city,
verses.Matt.23.35: that on you may come all the righteous blood shed on the earth, from the blood of righteous Abel to the blood of Zachariah son of Barachiah, whom you killed between the sanctuary and the altar.
verses.Matt.23.36: Most certainly I tell you, all these things will come upon this generation.
verses.Matt.23.37: “Jerusalem, Jerusalem, who kills the prophets and stones those who are sent to her! How often I would have gathered your children together, even as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings, and you would not!
verses.Matt.23.38: Behold, your house is left to you desolate.
verses.Matt.23.39: For I tell you, you will not see me from now on, until you say, ‘Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord!’”
verses.Mark.1.1: The beginning of the Good News of Jesus Christ, the Son of God.
verses.Mark.1.2:
As it is written in the prophets,
“Behold, I send my messenger before your face,
who will prepare your way before you:
verses.Mark.1.3:
the voice of one crying in the wilderness,
‘Make ready the way of the Lord!
Make his paths straight!’”
verses.Mark.1.4: John came baptizing in the wilderness and preaching the baptism of repentance for forgiveness of sins.
verses.Mark.1.5: All the country of Judea and all those of Jerusalem went out to him. They were baptized by him in the Jordan river, confessing their sins.
verses.Mark.1.6: John was clothed with camel’s hair and a leather belt around his waist. He ate locusts and wild honey.
verses.Mark.1.7: He preached, saying, “After me comes he who is mightier than I, the strap of whose sandals I am not worthy to stoop down and loosen.
verses.Mark.1.8: I baptized you in water, but he will baptize you in the Holy Spirit.”
verses.Mark.1.9: In those days, Jesus came from Nazareth of Galilee, and was baptized by John in the Jordan.
verses.Mark.1.10: Immediately coming up from the water, he saw the heavens parting and the Spirit descending on him like a dove.
verses.Mark.1.11: A voice came out of the sky, “You are my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.”
verses.Mark.1.12: Immediately the Spirit drove him out into the wilderness.
verses.Mark.1.13: He was there in the wilderness forty days, tempted by Satan. He was with the wild animals; and the angels were serving him.
verses.Mark.1.14: Now after John was taken into custody, Jesus came into Galilee, preaching the Good News of God’s Kingdom,
verses.Mark.1.15: and saying, “The time is fulfilled, and God’s Kingdom is at hand! Repent, and believe in the Good News.”
verses.Mark.1.16: Passing along by the sea of Galilee, he saw Simon and Andrew, the brother of Simon, casting a net into the sea, for they were fishermen.
verses.Mark.1.17: Jesus said to them, “Come after me, and I will make you into fishers for men.”
verses.Mark.1.18: Immediately they left their nets, and followed him.
verses.Mark.1.19: Going on a little further from there, he saw James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother, who were also in the boat mending the nets.
verses.Mark.1.20: Immediately he called them, and they left their father, Zebedee, in the boat with the hired servants, and went after him.
verses.Mark.1.21: They went into Capernaum, and immediately on the Sabbath day he entered into the synagogue and taught.
verses.Mark.1.22: They were astonished at his teaching, for he taught them as having authority, and not as the scribes.
verses.Mark.1.23: Immediately there was in their synagogue a man with an unclean spirit, and he cried out,
verses.Mark.1.24: saying, “Ha! What do we have to do with you, Jesus, you Nazarene? Have you come to destroy us? I know who you are: the Holy One of God!”
verses.Mark.1.25: Jesus rebuked him, saying, “Be quiet, and come out of him!”
verses.Mark.1.26: The unclean spirit, convulsing him and crying with a loud voice, came out of him.
verses.Mark.1.27: They were all amazed, so that they questioned among themselves, saying, “What is this? What can this new doctrine be? For with authority he commands even the unclean spirits, and they obey him!”
verses.Mark.1.28: The report of him went out immediately into all the region of Galilee and its surrounding area.
verses.Mark.1.29: Immediately, when they had come out of the synagogue, they came into the house of Simon and Andrew, with James and John.
verses.Mark.1.30: Now Simon’s wife’s mother lay sick with a fever, and immediately they told him about her.
verses.Mark.1.31: He came and took her by the hand and raised her up. The fever left her immediately, and she served them.
verses.Mark.1.32: At evening, when the sun had set, they brought to him all who were sick and those who were possessed by demons.
verses.Mark.1.33: All the city was gathered together at the door.
verses.Mark.1.34: He healed many who were sick with various diseases and cast out many demons. He didn’t allow the demons to speak, because they knew him.
verses.Mark.1.35: Early in the morning, while it was still dark, he rose up and went out, and departed into a deserted place, and prayed there.
verses.Mark.1.36: Simon and those who were with him searched for him.
verses.Mark.1.37: They found him and told him, “Everyone is looking for you.”
verses.Mark.1.38: He said to them, “Let’s go elsewhere into the next towns, that I may preach there also, because I came out for this reason.”
verses.Mark.1.39: He went into their synagogues throughout all Galilee, preaching and casting out demons.
verses.Mark.1.40: A leper came to him, begging him, kneeling down to him, and saying to him, “If you want to, you can make me clean.”
verses.Mark.1.41: Being moved with compassion, he stretched out his hand, and touched him, and said to him, “I want to. Be made clean.”
verses.Mark.1.42: When he had said this, immediately the leprosy departed from him and he was made clean.
verses.Mark.1.43: He strictly warned him and immediately sent him out,
verses.Mark.1.44: and said to him, “See that you say nothing to anybody, but go show yourself to the priest and offer for your cleansing the things which Moses commanded, for a testimony to them.”
verses.Mark.1.45: But he went out, and began to proclaim it much, and to spread about the matter, so that Jesus could no more openly enter into a city, but was outside in desert places. People came to him from everywhere.
verses.Mark.2.1: When he entered again into Capernaum after some days, it was heard that he was at home.
verses.Mark.2.2: Immediately many were gathered together, so that there was no more room, not even around the door; and he spoke the word to them.
verses.Mark.2.3: Four people came, carrying a paralytic to him.
verses.Mark.2.4: When they could not come near to him for the crowd, they removed the roof where he was. When they had broken it up, they let down the mat that the paralytic was lying on.
verses.Mark.2.5: Jesus, seeing their faith, said to the paralytic, “Son, your sins are forgiven you.”
verses.Mark.2.6: But there were some of the scribes sitting there and reasoning in their hearts,
verses.Mark.2.7: “Why does this man speak blasphemies like that? Who can forgive sins but God alone?”
verses.Mark.2.8: Immediately Jesus, perceiving in his spirit that they so reasoned within themselves, said to them, “Why do you reason these things in your hearts?
verses.Mark.2.9: Which is easier, to tell the paralytic, ‘Your sins are forgiven;’ or to say, ‘Arise, and take up your bed, and walk’?
verses.Mark.2.10: But that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins”—he said to the paralytic—
verses.Mark.2.11: “I tell you, arise, take up your mat, and go to your house.”
verses.Mark.2.12: He arose, and immediately took up the mat and went out in front of them all, so that they were all amazed and glorified God, saying, “We never saw anything like this!”
verses.Mark.2.13: He went out again by the seaside. All the multitude came to him, and he taught them.
verses.Mark.2.14: As he passed by, he saw Levi the son of Alphaeus sitting at the tax office. He said to him, “Follow me.” And he arose and followed him.
verses.Mark.2.15: He was reclining at the table in his house, and many tax collectors and sinners sat down with Jesus and his disciples, for there were many, and they followed him.
verses.Mark.2.16: The scribes and the Pharisees, when they saw that he was eating with the sinners and tax collectors, said to his disciples, “Why is it that he eats and drinks with tax collectors and sinners?”
verses.Mark.2.17: When Jesus heard it, he said to them, “Those who are healthy have no need for a physician, but those who are sick. I came not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.”
verses.Mark.2.18: John’s disciples and the Pharisees were fasting, and they came and asked him, “Why do John’s disciples and the disciples of the Pharisees fast, but your disciples don’t fast?”
verses.Mark.2.19: Jesus said to them, “Can the groomsmen fast while the bridegroom is with them? As long as they have the bridegroom with them, they can’t fast.
verses.Mark.2.20: But the days will come when the bridegroom will be taken away from them, and then they will fast in that day.
verses.Mark.2.21: No one sews a piece of unshrunk cloth on an old garment, or else the patch shrinks and the new tears away from the old, and a worse hole is made.
verses.Mark.2.22: No one puts new wine into old wineskins; or else the new wine will burst the skins, and the wine pours out, and the skins will be destroyed; but they put new wine into fresh wineskins.”
verses.Mark.2.23: He was going on the Sabbath day through the grain fields; and his disciples began, as they went, to pluck the ears of grain.
verses.Mark.2.24: The Pharisees said to him, “Behold, why do they do that which is not lawful on the Sabbath day?”
verses.Mark.2.25: He said to them, “Did you never read what David did when he had need and was hungry—he, and those who were with him?
verses.Mark.2.26: How he entered into God’s house at the time of Abiathar the high priest, and ate the show bread, which is not lawful to eat except for the priests, and gave also to those who were with him?”
verses.Mark.2.27: He said to them, “The Sabbath was made for man, not man for the Sabbath.
verses.Mark.2.28: Therefore the Son of Man is lord even of the Sabbath.”
verses.Matt.27.1: Now when morning had come, all the chief priests and the elders of the people took counsel against Jesus to put him to death.
verses.Matt.27.2: They bound him, led him away, and delivered him up to Pontius Pilate, the governor.
verses.Matt.27.3: Then Judas, who betrayed him, when he saw that Jesus was condemned, felt remorse, and brought back the thirty pieces of silver to the chief priests and elders,
verses.Matt.27.4: saying, “I have sinned in that I betrayed innocent blood.” But they said, “What is that to us? You see to it.”
verses.Matt.27.5: He threw down the pieces of silver in the sanctuary and departed. Then he went away and hanged himself.
verses.Matt.27.6: The chief priests took the pieces of silver and said, “It’s not lawful to put them into the treasury, since it is the price of blood.”
verses.Matt.27.7: They took counsel, and bought the potter’s field with them to bury strangers in.
verses.Matt.27.8: Therefore that field has been called “The Field of Blood” to this day.
verses.Matt.27.9:
Then that which was spoken through Jeremiah the prophet was fulfilled, saying,
“They took the thirty pieces of silver,
the price of him upon whom a price had been set,
whom some of the children of Israel priced,
verses.Matt.27.10:
and they gave them for the potter’s field,
as the Lord commanded me.”
verses.Matt.27.11: Now Jesus stood before the governor; and the governor asked him, saying, “Are you the King of the Jews?” Jesus said to him, “So you say.”
verses.Matt.27.12: When he was accused by the chief priests and elders, he answered nothing.
verses.Matt.27.13: Then Pilate said to him, “Don’t you hear how many things they testify against you?”
verses.Matt.27.14: He gave him no answer, not even one word, so that the governor marveled greatly.
verses.Matt.27.15: Now at the feast the governor was accustomed to release to the multitude one prisoner whom they desired.
verses.Matt.27.16: They had then a notable prisoner called Barabbas.
verses.Matt.27.17: When therefore they were gathered together, Pilate said to them, “Whom do you want me to release to you? Barabbas, or Jesus who is called Christ?”
verses.Matt.27.18: For he knew that because of envy they had delivered him up.
verses.Matt.27.19: While he was sitting on the judgment seat, his wife sent to him, saying, “Have nothing to do with that righteous man, for I have suffered many things today in a dream because of him.”
verses.Matt.27.20: Now the chief priests and the elders persuaded the multitudes to ask for Barabbas and destroy Jesus.
verses.Matt.27.21: But the governor answered them, “Which of the two do you want me to release to you?” They said, “Barabbas!”
verses.Matt.27.22: Pilate said to them, “What then shall I do to Jesus who is called Christ?” They all said to him, “Let him be crucified!”
verses.Matt.27.23: But the governor said, “Why? What evil has he done?” But they cried out exceedingly, saying, “Let him be crucified!”
verses.Matt.27.24: So when Pilate saw that nothing was being gained, but rather that a disturbance was starting, he took water and washed his hands before the multitude, saying, “I am innocent of the blood of this righteous person. You see to it.”
verses.Matt.27.25: All the people answered, “May his blood be on us and on our children!”
verses.Matt.27.26: Then he released Barabbas to them, but Jesus he flogged and delivered to be crucified.
verses.Matt.27.27: Then the governor’s soldiers took Jesus into the Praetorium, and gathered the whole garrison together against him.
verses.Matt.27.28: They stripped him and put a scarlet robe on him.
verses.Matt.27.29: They braided a crown of thorns and put it on his head, and a reed in his right hand; and they kneeled down before him and mocked him, saying, “Hail, King of the Jews!”
verses.Matt.27.30: They spat on him, and took the reed and struck him on the head.
verses.Matt.27.31: When they had mocked him, they took the robe off him, and put his clothes on him, and led him away to crucify him.
verses.Matt.27.32: As they came out, they found a man of Cyrene, Simon by name, and they compelled him to go with them, that he might carry his cross.
verses.Matt.27.33: When they came to a place called “Golgotha”, that is to say, “The place of a skull,”
verses.Matt.27.34: they gave him sour wine to drink mixed with gall. When he had tasted it, he would not drink.
verses.Matt.27.35: When they had crucified him, they divided his clothing among them, casting lots,
verses.Matt.27.36: and they sat and watched him there.
verses.Matt.27.37: They set up over his head the accusation against him written, “THIS IS JESUS, THE KING OF THE JEWS.”
verses.Matt.27.38: Then there were two robbers crucified with him, one on his right hand and one on the left.
verses.Matt.27.39: Those who passed by blasphemed him, wagging their heads
verses.Matt.27.40: and saying, “You who destroy the temple and build it in three days, save yourself! If you are the Son of God, come down from the cross!”
verses.Matt.27.41: Likewise the chief priests also mocking with the scribes, the Pharisees, and the elders, said,
verses.Matt.27.42: “He saved others, but he can’t save himself. If he is the King of Israel, let him come down from the cross now, and we will believe in him.
verses.Matt.27.43: He trusts in God. Let God deliver him now, if he wants him; for he said, ‘I am the Son of God.’”
verses.Matt.27.44: The robbers also who were crucified with him cast on him the same reproach.
verses.Matt.27.45: Now from the sixth hour there was darkness over all the land until the ninth hour.
verses.Matt.27.46: About the ninth hour Jesus cried with a loud voice, saying, “Eli, Eli, lima sabachthani?” That is, “My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?”
verses.Matt.27.47: Some of them who stood there, when they heard it, said, “This man is calling Elijah.”
verses.Matt.27.48: Immediately one of them ran and took a sponge, filled it with vinegar, put it on a reed, and gave him a drink.
verses.Matt.27.49: The rest said, “Let him be. Let’s see whether Elijah comes to save him.”
verses.Matt.27.50: Jesus cried again with a loud voice, and yielded up his spirit.
verses.Matt.27.51: Behold, the veil of the temple was torn in two from the top to the bottom. The earth quaked and the rocks were split.
verses.Matt.27.52: The tombs were opened, and many bodies of the saints who had fallen asleep were raised;
verses.Matt.27.53: and coming out of the tombs after his resurrection, they entered into the holy city and appeared to many.
verses.Matt.27.54: Now the centurion and those who were with him watching Jesus, when they saw the earthquake and the things that were done, were terrified, saying, “Truly this was the Son of God!”
verses.Matt.27.55: Many women were there watching from afar, who had followed Jesus from Galilee, serving him.
verses.Matt.27.56: Among them were Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James and Joses, and the mother of the sons of Zebedee.
verses.Matt.27.57: When evening had come, a rich man from Arimathaea named Joseph, who himself was also Jesus’ disciple, came.
verses.Matt.27.58: This man went to Pilate and asked for Jesus’ body. Then Pilate commanded the body to be given up.
verses.Matt.27.59: Joseph took the body and wrapped it in a clean linen cloth
verses.Matt.27.60: and laid it in his own new tomb, which he had cut out in the rock. Then he rolled a large stone against the door of the tomb, and departed.
verses.Matt.27.61: Mary Magdalene was there, and the other Mary, sitting opposite the tomb.
verses.Matt.27.62: Now on the next day, which was the day after the Preparation Day, the chief priests and the Pharisees were gathered together to Pilate,
verses.Matt.27.63: saying, “Sir, we remember what that deceiver said while he was still alive: ‘After three days I will rise again.’
verses.Matt.27.64: Command therefore that the tomb be made secure until the third day, lest perhaps his disciples come at night and steal him away, and tell the people, ‘He is risen from the dead;’ and the last deception will be worse than the first.”
verses.Matt.27.65: Pilate said to them, “You have a guard. Go, make it as secure as you can.”
verses.Matt.27.66: So they went with the guard and made the tomb secure, sealing the stone.
verses.Matt.26.1: When Jesus had finished all these words, he said to his disciples,
verses.Matt.26.2: “You know that after two days the Passover is coming, and the Son of Man will be delivered up to be crucified.”
verses.Matt.26.3: Then the chief priests, the scribes, and the elders of the people were gathered together in the court of the high priest, who was called Caiaphas.
verses.Matt.26.4: They took counsel together that they might take Jesus by deceit and kill him.
verses.Matt.26.5: But they said, “Not during the feast, lest a riot occur among the people.”
verses.Matt.26.6: Now when Jesus was in Bethany, in the house of Simon the leper,
verses.Matt.26.7: a woman came to him having an alabaster jar of very expensive ointment, and she poured it on his head as he sat at the table.
verses.Matt.26.8: But when his disciples saw this, they were indignant, saying, “Why this waste?
verses.Matt.26.9: For this ointment might have been sold for much and given to the poor.”
verses.Matt.26.10: However, knowing this, Jesus said to them, “Why do you trouble the woman? She has done a good work for me.
verses.Matt.26.11: For you always have the poor with you, but you don’t always have me.
verses.Matt.26.12: For in pouring this ointment on my body, she did it to prepare me for burial.
verses.Matt.26.13: Most certainly I tell you, wherever this Good News is preached in the whole world, what this woman has done will also be spoken of as a memorial of her.”
verses.Matt.26.14: Then one of the twelve, who was called Judas Iscariot, went to the chief priests
verses.Matt.26.15: and said, “What are you willing to give me if I deliver him to you?” So they weighed out for him thirty pieces of silver.
verses.Matt.26.16: From that time he sought opportunity to betray him.
verses.Matt.26.17: Now on the first day of unleavened bread, the disciples came to Jesus, saying to him, “Where do you want us to prepare for you to eat the Passover?”
verses.Matt.26.18: He said, “Go into the city to a certain person, and tell him, ‘The Teacher says, “My time is at hand. I will keep the Passover at your house with my disciples.”’”
verses.Matt.26.19: The disciples did as Jesus commanded them, and they prepared the Passover.
verses.Matt.26.20: Now when evening had come, he was reclining at the table with the twelve disciples.
verses.Matt.26.21: As they were eating, he said, “Most certainly I tell you that one of you will betray me.”
verses.Matt.26.22: They were exceedingly sorrowful, and each began to ask him, “It isn’t me, is it, Lord?”
verses.Matt.26.23: He answered, “He who dipped his hand with me in the dish will betray me.
verses.Matt.26.24: The Son of Man goes even as it is written of him, but woe to that man through whom the Son of Man is betrayed! It would be better for that man if he had not been born.”
verses.Matt.26.25: Judas, who betrayed him, answered, “It isn’t me, is it, Rabbi?” He said to him, “You said it.”
verses.Matt.26.26: As they were eating, Jesus took bread, gave thanks for it, and broke it. He gave to the disciples and said, “Take, eat; this is my body.”
verses.Matt.26.27: He took the cup, gave thanks, and gave to them, saying, “All of you drink it,
verses.Matt.26.28: for this is my blood of the new covenant, which is poured out for many for the remission of sins.
verses.Matt.26.29: But I tell you that I will not drink of this fruit of the vine from now on, until that day when I drink it anew with you in my Father’s Kingdom.”
verses.Matt.26.30: When they had sung a hymn, they went out to the Mount of Olives.
verses.Matt.26.31: Then Jesus said to them, “All of you will be made to stumble because of me tonight, for it is written, ‘I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep of the flock will be scattered.’
verses.Matt.26.32: But after I am raised up, I will go before you into Galilee.”
verses.Matt.26.33: But Peter answered him, “Even if all will be made to stumble because of you, I will never be made to stumble.”
verses.Matt.26.34: Jesus said to him, “Most certainly I tell you that tonight, before the rooster crows, you will deny me three times.”
verses.Matt.26.35: Peter said to him, “Even if I must die with you, I will not deny you.” All of the disciples also said likewise.
verses.Matt.26.36: Then Jesus came with them to a place called Gethsemane, and said to his disciples, “Sit here, while I go there and pray.”
verses.Matt.26.37: He took with him Peter and the two sons of Zebedee, and began to be sorrowful and severely troubled.
verses.Matt.26.38: Then Jesus said to them, “My soul is exceedingly sorrowful, even to death. Stay here and watch with me.”
verses.Matt.26.39: He went forward a little, fell on his face, and prayed, saying, “My Father, if it is possible, let this cup pass away from me; nevertheless, not what I desire, but what you desire.”
verses.Matt.26.40: He came to the disciples and found them sleeping, and said to Peter, “What, couldn’t you watch with me for one hour?
verses.Matt.26.41: Watch and pray, that you don’t enter into temptation. The spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak.”
verses.Matt.26.42: Again, a second time he went away and prayed, saying, “My Father, if this cup can’t pass away from me unless I drink it, your desire be done.”
verses.Matt.26.43: He came again and found them sleeping, for their eyes were heavy.
verses.Matt.26.44: He left them again, went away, and prayed a third time, saying the same words.
verses.Matt.26.45: Then he came to his disciples and said to them, “Are you still sleeping and resting? Behold, the hour is at hand, and the Son of Man is betrayed into the hands of sinners.
verses.Matt.26.46: Arise, let’s be going. Behold, he who betrays me is at hand.”
verses.Matt.26.47: While he was still speaking, behold, Judas, one of the twelve, came, and with him a great multitude with swords and clubs, from the chief priests and elders of the people.
verses.Matt.26.48: Now he who betrayed him had given them a sign, saying, “Whoever I kiss, he is the one. Seize him.”
verses.Matt.26.49: Immediately he came to Jesus, and said, “Greetings, Rabbi!” and kissed him.
verses.Matt.26.50: Jesus said to him, “Friend, why are you here?” Then they came and laid hands on Jesus, and took him.
verses.Matt.26.51: Behold, one of those who were with Jesus stretched out his hand and drew his sword, and struck the servant of the high priest, and cut off his ear.
verses.Matt.26.52: Then Jesus said to him, “Put your sword back into its place, for all those who take the sword will die by the sword.
verses.Matt.26.53: Or do you think that I couldn’t ask my Father, and he would even now send me more than twelve legions of angels?
verses.Matt.26.54: How then would the Scriptures be fulfilled that it must be so?”
verses.Matt.26.55: In that hour Jesus said to the multitudes, “Have you come out as against a robber with swords and clubs to seize me? I sat daily in the temple teaching, and you didn’t arrest me.
verses.Matt.26.56: But all this has happened that the Scriptures of the prophets might be fulfilled.” Then all the disciples left him and fled.
verses.Matt.26.57: Those who had taken Jesus led him away to Caiaphas the high priest, where the scribes and the elders were gathered together.
verses.Matt.26.58: But Peter followed him from a distance to the court of the high priest, and entered in and sat with the officers, to see the end.
verses.Matt.26.59: Now the chief priests, the elders, and the whole council sought false testimony against Jesus, that they might put him to death,
verses.Matt.26.60: and they found none. Even though many false witnesses came forward, they found none. But at last two false witnesses came forward
verses.Matt.26.61: and said, “This man said, ‘I am able to destroy the temple of God, and to build it in three days.’”
verses.Matt.26.62: The high priest stood up and said to him, “Have you no answer? What is this that these testify against you?”
verses.Matt.26.63: But Jesus stayed silent. The high priest answered him, “I adjure you by the living God that you tell us whether you are the Christ, the Son of God.”
verses.Matt.26.64: Jesus said to him, “You have said so. Nevertheless, I tell you, after this you will see the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of Power, and coming on the clouds of the sky.”
verses.Matt.26.65: Then the high priest tore his clothing, saying, “He has spoken blasphemy! Why do we need any more witnesses? Behold, now you have heard his blasphemy.
verses.Matt.26.66: What do you think?” They answered, “He is worthy of death!”
verses.Matt.26.67: Then they spat in his face and beat him with their fists, and some slapped him,
verses.Matt.26.68: saying, “Prophesy to us, you Christ! Who hit you?”
verses.Matt.26.69: Now Peter was sitting outside in the court, and a maid came to him, saying, “You were also with Jesus, the Galilean!”
verses.Matt.26.70: But he denied it before them all, saying, “I don’t know what you are talking about.”
verses.Matt.26.71: When he had gone out onto the porch, someone else saw him and said to those who were there, “This man also was with Jesus of Nazareth.”
verses.Matt.26.72: Again he denied it with an oath, “I don’t know the man.”
verses.Matt.26.73: After a little while those who stood by came and said to Peter, “Surely you are also one of them, for your speech makes you known.”
verses.Matt.26.74: Then he began to curse and to swear, “I don’t know the man!” Immediately the rooster crowed.
verses.Matt.26.75: Peter remembered the word which Jesus had said to him, “Before the rooster crows, you will deny me three times.” Then he went out and wept bitterly.
verses.Matt.28.1: Now after the Sabbath, as it began to dawn on the first day of the week, Mary Magdalene and the other Mary came to see the tomb.
verses.Matt.28.2: Behold, there was a great earthquake, for an angel of the Lord descended from the sky and came and rolled away the stone from the door and sat on it.
verses.Matt.28.3: His appearance was like lightning, and his clothing white as snow.
verses.Matt.28.4: For fear of him, the guards shook, and became like dead men.
verses.Matt.28.5: The angel answered the women, “Don’t be afraid, for I know that you seek Jesus, who has been crucified.
verses.Matt.28.6: He is not here, for he has risen, just like he said. Come, see the place where the Lord was lying.
verses.Matt.28.7: Go quickly and tell his disciples, ‘He has risen from the dead, and behold, he goes before you into Galilee; there you will see him.’ Behold, I have told you.”
verses.Matt.28.8: They departed quickly from the tomb with fear and great joy, and ran to bring his disciples word.
verses.Matt.28.9: As they went to tell his disciples, behold, Jesus met them, saying, “Rejoice!” They came and took hold of his feet, and worshiped him.
verses.Matt.28.10: Then Jesus said to them, “Don’t be afraid. Go tell my brothers that they should go into Galilee, and there they will see me.”
verses.Matt.28.11: Now while they were going, behold, some of the guards came into the city and told the chief priests all the things that had happened.
verses.Matt.28.12: When they were assembled with the elders and had taken counsel, they gave a large amount of silver to the soldiers,
verses.Matt.28.13: saying, “Say that his disciples came by night and stole him away while we slept.
verses.Matt.28.14: If this comes to the governor’s ears, we will persuade him and make you free of worry.”
verses.Matt.28.15: So they took the money and did as they were told. This saying was spread abroad among the Jews, and continues until today.
verses.Matt.28.16: But the eleven disciples went into Galilee, to the mountain where Jesus had sent them.
verses.Matt.28.17: When they saw him, they bowed down to him; but some doubted.
verses.Matt.28.18: Jesus came to them and spoke to them, saying, “All authority has been given to me in heaven and on earth.
verses.Matt.28.19: Go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit,
verses.Matt.28.20: teaching them to observe all things that I commanded you. Behold, I am with you always, even to the end of the age.” Amen.
verses.Matt.24.1: Jesus went out from the temple, and was going on his way. His disciples came to him to show him the buildings of the temple.
verses.Matt.24.2: But he answered them, “You see all of these things, don’t you? Most certainly I tell you, there will not be left here one stone on another, that will not be thrown down.”
verses.Matt.24.3: As he sat on the Mount of Olives, the disciples came to him privately, saying, “Tell us, when will these things be? What is the sign of your coming, and of the end of the age?”
verses.Matt.24.4: Jesus answered them, “Be careful that no one leads you astray.
verses.Matt.24.5: For many will come in my name, saying, ‘I am the Christ,’ and will lead many astray.
verses.Matt.24.6: You will hear of wars and rumors of wars. See that you aren’t troubled, for all this must happen, but the end is not yet.
verses.Matt.24.7: For nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom; and there will be famines, plagues, and earthquakes in various places.
verses.Matt.24.8: But all these things are the beginning of birth pains.
verses.Matt.24.9: “Then they will deliver you up to oppression and will kill you. You will be hated by all of the nations for my name’s sake.
verses.Matt.24.10: Then many will stumble, and will deliver up one another, and will hate one another.
verses.Matt.24.11: Many false prophets will arise and will lead many astray.
verses.Matt.24.12: Because iniquity will be multiplied, the love of many will grow cold.
verses.Matt.24.13: But he who endures to the end will be saved.
verses.Matt.24.14: This Good News of the Kingdom will be preached in the whole world for a testimony to all the nations, and then the end will come.
verses.Matt.24.15: “When, therefore, you see the abomination of desolation, which was spoken of through Daniel the prophet, standing in the holy place (let the reader understand),
verses.Matt.24.16: then let those who are in Judea flee to the mountains.
verses.Matt.24.17: Let him who is on the housetop not go down to take out the things that are in his house.
verses.Matt.24.18: Let him who is in the field not return back to get his clothes.
verses.Matt.24.19: But woe to those who are with child and to nursing mothers in those days!
verses.Matt.24.20: Pray that your flight will not be in the winter nor on a Sabbath,
verses.Matt.24.21: for then there will be great suffering, such as has not been from the beginning of the world until now, no, nor ever will be.
verses.Matt.24.22: Unless those days had been shortened, no flesh would have been saved. But for the sake of the chosen ones, those days will be shortened.
verses.Matt.24.23: “Then if any man tells you, ‘Behold, here is the Christ!’ or, ‘There!’ don’t believe it.
verses.Matt.24.24: For false christs and false prophets will arise, and they will show great signs and wonders, so as to lead astray, if possible, even the chosen ones.
verses.Matt.24.26: “If therefore they tell you, ‘Behold, he is in the wilderness,’ don’t go out; or ‘Behold, he is in the inner rooms,’ don’t believe it.
verses.Matt.24.27: For as the lightning flashes from the east, and is seen even to the west, so will the coming of the Son of Man be.
verses.Matt.24.28: For wherever the carcass is, that is where the vultures gather together.
verses.Matt.24.29: “But immediately after the suffering of those days, the sun will be darkened, the moon will not give its light, the stars will fall from the sky, and the powers of the heavens will be shaken;
verses.Matt.24.30: and then the sign of the Son of Man will appear in the sky. Then all the tribes of the earth will mourn, and they will see the Son of Man coming on the clouds of the sky with power and great glory.
verses.Matt.24.31: He will send out his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they will gather together his chosen ones from the four winds, from one end of the sky to the other.
verses.Matt.24.32: “Now from the fig tree learn this parable: When its branch has now become tender and produces its leaves, you know that the summer is near.
verses.Matt.24.33: Even so you also, when you see all these things, know that he is near, even at the doors.
verses.Matt.24.34: Most certainly I tell you, this generation will not pass away until all these things are accomplished.
verses.Matt.24.35: Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will not pass away.
verses.Matt.24.36: “But no one knows of that day and hour, not even the angels of heaven, but my Father only.
verses.Matt.24.37: As the days of Noah were, so will the coming of the Son of Man be.
verses.Matt.24.38: For as in those days which were before the flood they were eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage, until the day that Noah entered into the ship,
verses.Matt.24.39: and they didn’t know until the flood came and took them all away, so will the coming of the Son of Man be.
verses.Matt.24.40: Then two men will be in the field: one will be taken and one will be left.
verses.Matt.24.41: Two women will be grinding at the mill: one will be taken and one will be left.
verses.Matt.24.42: Watch therefore, for you don’t know in what hour your Lord comes.
verses.Matt.24.43: But know this, that if the master of the house had known in what watch of the night the thief was coming, he would have watched, and would not have allowed his house to be broken into.
verses.Matt.24.44: Therefore also be ready, for in an hour that you don’t expect, the Son of Man will come.
verses.Matt.24.45: “Who then is the faithful and wise servant, whom his lord has set over his household, to give them their food in due season?
verses.Matt.24.46: Blessed is that servant whom his lord finds doing so when he comes.
verses.Matt.24.47: Most certainly I tell you that he will set him over all that he has.
verses.Matt.24.48: But if that evil servant should say in his heart, ‘My lord is delaying his coming,’
verses.Matt.24.49: and begins to beat his fellow servants, and eat and drink with the drunkards,
verses.Matt.24.50: the lord of that servant will come in a day when he doesn’t expect it and in an hour when he doesn’t know it,
verses.Matt.24.51: and will cut him in pieces and appoint his portion with the hypocrites. That is where the weeping and grinding of teeth will be.
verses.Matt.25.1: “Then the Kingdom of Heaven will be like ten virgins who took their lamps and went out to meet the bridegroom.
verses.Matt.25.2: Five of them were foolish, and five were wise.
verses.Matt.25.3: Those who were foolish, when they took their lamps, took no oil with them,
verses.Matt.25.4: but the wise took oil in their vessels with their lamps.
verses.Matt.25.5: Now while the bridegroom delayed, they all slumbered and slept.
verses.Matt.25.6: But at midnight there was a cry, ‘Behold! The bridegroom is coming! Come out to meet him!’
verses.Matt.25.7: Then all those virgins arose, and trimmed their lamps.
verses.Matt.25.8: The foolish said to the wise, ‘Give us some of your oil, for our lamps are going out.’
verses.Matt.25.9: But the wise answered, saying, ‘What if there isn’t enough for us and you? You go rather to those who sell, and buy for yourselves.’
verses.Matt.25.10: While they went away to buy, the bridegroom came, and those who were ready went in with him to the wedding feast, and the door was shut.
verses.Matt.25.11: Afterward the other virgins also came, saying, ‘Lord, Lord, open to us.’
verses.Matt.25.12: But he answered, ‘Most certainly I tell you, I don’t know you.’
verses.Matt.25.13: Watch therefore, for you don’t know the day nor the hour in which the Son of Man is coming.
verses.Matt.25.14: “For it is like a man going into another country, who called his own servants and entrusted his goods to them.
verses.Matt.25.15: To one he gave five talents, to another two, to another one, to each according to his own ability. Then he went on his journey.
verses.Matt.25.16: Immediately he who received the five talents went and traded with them, and made another five talents.
verses.Matt.25.17: In the same way, he also who got the two gained another two.
verses.Matt.25.18: But he who received the one talent went away and dug in the earth and hid his lord’s money.
verses.Matt.25.19: “Now after a long time the lord of those servants came, and settled accounts with them.
verses.Matt.25.20: He who received the five talents came and brought another five talents, saying, ‘Lord, you delivered to me five talents. Behold, I have gained another five talents in addition to them.’
verses.Matt.25.21: “His lord said to him, ‘Well done, good and faithful servant. You have been faithful over a few things, I will set you over many things. Enter into the joy of your lord.’
verses.Matt.25.22: “He also who got the two talents came and said, ‘Lord, you delivered to me two talents. Behold, I have gained another two talents in addition to them.’
verses.Matt.25.23: “His lord said to him, ‘Well done, good and faithful servant. You have been faithful over a few things. I will set you over many things. Enter into the joy of your lord.’
verses.Matt.25.24: “He also who had received the one talent came and said, ‘Lord, I knew you that you are a hard man, reaping where you didn’t sow, and gathering where you didn’t scatter.
verses.Matt.25.25: I was afraid, and went away and hid your talent in the earth. Behold, you have what is yours.’
verses.Matt.25.26: “But his lord answered him, ‘You wicked and slothful servant. You knew that I reap where I didn’t sow, and gather where I didn’t scatter.
verses.Matt.25.27: You ought therefore to have deposited my money with the bankers, and at my coming I should have received back my own with interest.
verses.Matt.25.28: Take away therefore the talent from him and give it to him who has the ten talents.
verses.Matt.25.29: For to everyone who has will be given, and he will have abundance, but from him who doesn’t have, even that which he has will be taken away.
verses.Matt.25.30: Throw out the unprofitable servant into the outer darkness, where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.’
verses.Matt.25.31: “But when the Son of Man comes in his glory, and all the holy angels with him, then he will sit on the throne of his glory.
verses.Matt.25.32: Before him all the nations will be gathered, and he will separate them one from another, as a shepherd separates the sheep from the goats.
verses.Matt.25.33: He will set the sheep on his right hand, but the goats on the left.
verses.Matt.25.34: Then the King will tell those on his right hand, ‘Come, blessed of my Father, inherit the Kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world;
verses.Matt.25.35: for I was hungry and you gave me food to eat. I was thirsty and you gave me drink. I was a stranger and you took me in.
verses.Matt.25.36: I was naked and you clothed me. I was sick and you visited me. I was in prison and you came to me.’
verses.Matt.25.37: “Then the righteous will answer him, saying, ‘Lord, when did we see you hungry and feed you, or thirsty and give you a drink?
verses.Matt.25.38: When did we see you as a stranger and take you in, or naked and clothe you?
verses.Matt.25.39: When did we see you sick or in prison and come to you?’
verses.Matt.25.40: “The King will answer them, ‘Most certainly I tell you, because you did it to one of the least of these my brothers, you did it to me.’
verses.Matt.25.41: Then he will say also to those on the left hand, ‘Depart from me, you cursed, into the eternal fire which is prepared for the devil and his angels;
verses.Matt.25.42: for I was hungry, and you didn’t give me food to eat; I was thirsty, and you gave me no drink;
verses.Matt.25.43: I was a stranger, and you didn’t take me in; naked, and you didn’t clothe me; sick, and in prison, and you didn’t visit me.’
verses.Matt.25.44: “Then they will also answer, saying, ‘Lord, when did we see you hungry, or thirsty, or a stranger, or naked, or sick, or in prison, and didn’t help you?’
verses.Matt.25.45: “Then he will answer them, saying, ‘Most certainly I tell you, because you didn’t do it to one of the least of these, you didn’t do it to me.’
verses.Matt.25.46: These will go away into eternal punishment, but the righteous into eternal life.”
verses.Mark.9.1: He said to them, “Most certainly I tell you, there are some standing here who will in no way taste death until they see God’s Kingdom come with power.”
verses.Mark.9.2: After six days Jesus took with him Peter, James, and John, and brought them up onto a high mountain privately by themselves, and he was changed into another form in front of them.
verses.Mark.9.3: His clothing became glistening, exceedingly white, like snow, such as no launderer on earth can whiten them.
verses.Mark.9.4: Elijah and Moses appeared to them, and they were talking with Jesus.
verses.Mark.9.5: Peter answered Jesus, “Rabbi, it is good for us to be here. Let’s make three tents: one for you, one for Moses, and one for Elijah.”
verses.Mark.9.6: For he didn’t know what to say, for they were very afraid.
verses.Mark.9.7: A cloud came, overshadowing them, and a voice came out of the cloud, “This is my beloved Son. Listen to him.”
verses.Mark.9.8: Suddenly looking around, they saw no one with them any more, except Jesus only.
verses.Mark.9.9: As they were coming down from the mountain, he commanded them that they should tell no one what things they had seen, until after the Son of Man had risen from the dead.
verses.Mark.9.10: They kept this saying to themselves, questioning what the “rising from the dead” meant.
verses.Mark.9.11: They asked him, saying, “Why do the scribes say that Elijah must come first?”
verses.Mark.9.12: He said to them, “Elijah indeed comes first, and restores all things. How is it written about the Son of Man, that he should suffer many things and be despised?
verses.Mark.9.13: But I tell you that Elijah has come, and they have also done to him whatever they wanted to, even as it is written about him.”
verses.Mark.9.14: Coming to the disciples, he saw a great multitude around them, and scribes questioning them.
verses.Mark.9.15: Immediately all the multitude, when they saw him, were greatly amazed, and running to him, greeted him.
verses.Mark.9.16: He asked the scribes, “What are you asking them?”
verses.Mark.9.17: One of the multitude answered, “Teacher, I brought to you my son, who has a mute spirit;
verses.Mark.9.18: and wherever it seizes him, it throws him down; and he foams at the mouth, grinds his teeth, and becomes rigid. I asked your disciples to cast it out, and they weren’t able.”
verses.Mark.9.19: He answered him, “Unbelieving generation, how long shall I be with you? How long shall I bear with you? Bring him to me.”
verses.Mark.9.20: They brought him to him, and when he saw him, immediately the spirit convulsed him and he fell on the ground, wallowing and foaming at the mouth.
verses.Mark.9.21: He asked his father, “How long has it been since this has been happening to him?” He said, “From childhood.
verses.Mark.9.22: Often it has cast him both into the fire and into the water to destroy him. But if you can do anything, have compassion on us and help us.”
verses.Mark.9.23: Jesus said to him, “If you can believe, all things are possible to him who believes.”
verses.Mark.9.24: Immediately the father of the child cried out with tears, “I believe. Help my unbelief!”
verses.Mark.9.25: When Jesus saw that a multitude came running together, he rebuked the unclean spirit, saying to him, “You mute and deaf spirit, I command you, come out of him, and never enter him again!”
verses.Mark.9.26: After crying out and convulsing him greatly, it came out of him. The boy became like one dead, so much that most of them said, “He is dead.”
verses.Mark.9.27: But Jesus took him by the hand and raised him up; and he arose.
verses.Mark.9.28: When he had come into the house, his disciples asked him privately, “Why couldn’t we cast it out?”
verses.Mark.9.29: He said to them, “This kind can come out by nothing but by prayer and fasting.”
verses.Mark.9.30: They went out from there and passed through Galilee. He didn’t want anyone to know it,
verses.Mark.9.31: for he was teaching his disciples, and said to them, “The Son of Man is being handed over to the hands of men, and they will kill him; and when he is killed, on the third day he will rise again.”
verses.Mark.9.32: But they didn’t understand the saying, and were afraid to ask him.
verses.Mark.9.33: He came to Capernaum, and when he was in the house he asked them, “What were you arguing among yourselves on the way?”
verses.Mark.9.34: But they were silent, for they had disputed with one another on the way about who was the greatest.
verses.Mark.9.35: He sat down and called the twelve; and he said to them, “If any man wants to be first, he shall be last of all, and servant of all.”
verses.Mark.9.36: He took a little child and set him in the middle of them. Taking him in his arms, he said to them,
verses.Mark.9.37: “Whoever receives one such little child in my name receives me; and whoever receives me, doesn’t receive me, but him who sent me.”
verses.Mark.9.38: John said to him, “Teacher, we saw someone who doesn’t follow us casting out demons in your name; and we forbade him, because he doesn’t follow us.”
verses.Mark.9.39: But Jesus said, “Don’t forbid him, for there is no one who will do a mighty work in my name and be able quickly to speak evil of me.
verses.Mark.9.40: For whoever is not against us is on our side.
verses.Mark.9.41: For whoever will give you a cup of water to drink in my name because you are Christ’s, most certainly I tell you, he will in no way lose his reward.
verses.Mark.9.42: “Whoever will cause one of these little ones who believe in me to stumble, it would be better for him if he were thrown into the sea with a millstone hung around his neck.
verses.Mark.9.43: If your hand causes you to stumble, cut it off. It is better for you to enter into life maimed, rather than having your two hands to go into Gehenna, into the unquenchable fire,
verses.Mark.9.44: ‘where their worm doesn’t die, and the fire is not quenched.’
verses.Mark.9.45: If your foot causes you to stumble, cut it off. It is better for you to enter into life lame, rather than having your two feet to be cast into Gehenna, into the fire that will never be quenched—
verses.Mark.9.46: ‘where their worm doesn’t die, and the fire is not quenched.’
verses.Mark.9.47: If your eye causes you to stumble, throw it out. It is better for you to enter into God’s Kingdom with one eye, rather than having two eyes to be cast into the Gehenna of fire,
verses.Mark.9.48: ‘where their worm doesn’t die, and the fire is not quenched.’
verses.Mark.9.49: For everyone will be salted with fire, and every sacrifice will be seasoned with salt.
verses.Mark.9.50: Salt is good, but if the salt has lost its saltiness, with what will you season it? Have salt in yourselves, and be at peace with one another.”
verses.Mark.10.1: He arose from there and came into the borders of Judea and beyond the Jordan. Multitudes came together to him again. As he usually did, he was again teaching them.
verses.Mark.10.2: Pharisees came to him testing him, and asked him, “Is it lawful for a man to divorce his wife?”
verses.Mark.10.3: He answered, “What did Moses command you?”
verses.Mark.10.4: They said, “Moses allowed a certificate of divorce to be written, and to divorce her.”
verses.Mark.10.5: But Jesus said to them, “For your hardness of heart, he wrote you this commandment.
verses.Mark.10.6: But from the beginning of the creation, God made them male and female.
verses.Mark.10.7: For this cause a man will leave his father and mother, and will join to his wife,
verses.Mark.10.8: and the two will become one flesh, so that they are no longer two, but one flesh.
verses.Mark.10.9: What therefore God has joined together, let no man separate.”
verses.Mark.10.10: In the house, his disciples asked him again about the same matter.
verses.Mark.10.11: He said to them, “Whoever divorces his wife and marries another commits adultery against her.
verses.Mark.10.12: If a woman herself divorces her husband and marries another, she commits adultery.”
verses.Mark.10.13: They were bringing to him little children, that he should touch them, but the disciples rebuked those who were bringing them.
verses.Mark.10.14: But when Jesus saw it, he was moved with indignation and said to them, “Allow the little children to come to me! Don’t forbid them, for God’s Kingdom belongs to such as these.
verses.Mark.10.15: Most certainly I tell you, whoever will not receive God’s Kingdom like a little child, he will in no way enter into it.”
verses.Mark.10.16: He took them in his arms and blessed them, laying his hands on them.
verses.Mark.10.17: As he was going out into the way, one ran to him, knelt before him, and asked him, “Good Teacher, what shall I do that I may inherit eternal life?”
verses.Mark.10.18: Jesus said to him, “Why do you call me good? No one is good except one—God.
verses.Mark.10.19: You know the commandments: ‘Do not murder,’ ‘Do not commit adultery,’ ‘Do not steal,’ ‘Do not give false testimony,’ ‘Do not defraud,’ ‘Honor your father and mother.’”
verses.Mark.10.20: He said to him, “Teacher, I have observed all these things from my youth.”
verses.Mark.10.21: Jesus looking at him loved him, and said to him, “One thing you lack. Go, sell whatever you have and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven; and come, follow me, taking up the cross.”
verses.Mark.10.22: But his face fell at that saying, and he went away sorrowful, for he was one who had great possessions.
verses.Mark.10.23: Jesus looked around and said to his disciples, “How difficult it is for those who have riches to enter into God’s Kingdom!”
verses.Mark.10.24: The disciples were amazed at his words. But Jesus answered again, “Children, how hard it is for those who trust in riches to enter into God’s Kingdom!
verses.Mark.10.25: It is easier for a camel to go through a needle’s eye than for a rich man to enter into God’s Kingdom.”
verses.Mark.10.26: They were exceedingly astonished, saying to him, “Then who can be saved?”
verses.Mark.10.27: Jesus, looking at them, said, “With men it is impossible, but not with God, for all things are possible with God.”
verses.Mark.10.28: Peter began to tell him, “Behold, we have left all and have followed you.”
verses.Mark.10.29: Jesus said, “Most certainly I tell you, there is no one who has left house, or brothers, or sisters, or father, or mother, or wife, or children, or land, for my sake, and for the sake of the Good News,
verses.Mark.10.30: but he will receive one hundred times more now in this time: houses, brothers, sisters, mothers, children, and land, with persecutions; and in the age to come eternal life.
verses.Mark.10.31: But many who are first will be last, and the last first.”
verses.Mark.10.32: They were on the way, going up to Jerusalem; and Jesus was going in front of them, and they were amazed; and those who followed were afraid. He again took the twelve, and began to tell them the things that were going to happen to him.
verses.Mark.10.33: “Behold, we are going up to Jerusalem. The Son of Man will be delivered to the chief priests and the scribes. They will condemn him to death, and will deliver him to the Gentiles.
verses.Mark.10.34: They will mock him, spit on him, scourge him, and kill him. On the third day he will rise again.”
verses.Mark.10.35: James and John, the sons of Zebedee, came near to him, saying, “Teacher, we want you to do for us whatever we will ask.”
verses.Mark.10.36: He said to them, “What do you want me to do for you?”
verses.Mark.10.37: They said to him, “Grant to us that we may sit, one at your right hand and one at your left hand, in your glory.”
verses.Mark.10.38: But Jesus said to them, “You don’t know what you are asking. Are you able to drink the cup that I drink, and to be baptized with the baptism that I am baptized with?”
verses.Mark.10.39: They said to him, “We are able.” Jesus said to them, “You shall indeed drink the cup that I drink, and you shall be baptized with the baptism that I am baptized with;
verses.Mark.10.40: but to sit at my right hand and at my left hand is not mine to give, but for whom it has been prepared.”
verses.Mark.10.41: When the ten heard it, they began to be indignant toward James and John.
verses.Mark.10.42: Jesus summoned them and said to them, “You know that they who are recognized as rulers over the nations lord it over them, and their great ones exercise authority over them.
verses.Mark.10.43: But it shall not be so among you, but whoever wants to become great among you shall be your servant.
verses.Mark.10.44: Whoever of you wants to become first among you shall be bondservant of all.
verses.Mark.10.45: For the Son of Man also came not to be served but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many.”
verses.Mark.10.46: They came to Jericho. As he went out from Jericho with his disciples and a great multitude, the son of Timaeus, Bartimaeus, a blind beggar, was sitting by the road.
verses.Mark.10.47: When he heard that it was Jesus the Nazarene, he began to cry out and say, “Jesus, you son of David, have mercy on me!”
verses.Mark.10.48: Many rebuked him, that he should be quiet, but he cried out much more, “You son of David, have mercy on me!”
verses.Mark.10.49: Jesus stood still and said, “Call him.” They called the blind man, saying to him, “Cheer up! Get up. He is calling you!”
verses.Mark.10.50: He, casting away his cloak, sprang up, and came to Jesus.
verses.Mark.10.51: Jesus asked him, “What do you want me to do for you?” The blind man said to him, “Rabboni, that I may see again.”
verses.Mark.10.52: Jesus said to him, “Go your way. Your faith has made you well.” Immediately he received his sight and followed Jesus on the way.
verses.Mark.7.1: Then the Pharisees and some of the scribes gathered together to him, having come from Jerusalem.
verses.Mark.7.2: Now when they saw some of his disciples eating bread with defiled, that is unwashed, hands, they found fault.
verses.Mark.7.3: (For the Pharisees and all the Jews don’t eat unless they wash their hands and forearms, holding to the tradition of the elders.
verses.Mark.7.4: They don’t eat when they come from the marketplace unless they bathe themselves, and there are many other things which they have received to hold to: washings of cups, pitchers, bronze vessels, and couches.)
verses.Mark.7.5: The Pharisees and the scribes asked him, “Why don’t your disciples walk according to the tradition of the elders, but eat their bread with unwashed hands?”
verses.Mark.7.6:
He answered them, “Well did Isaiah prophesy of you hypocrites, as it is written,
‘This people honors me with their lips,
but their heart is far from me.
verses.Mark.7.7:
They worship me in vain,
teaching as doctrines the commandments of men.’
verses.Mark.7.8: “For you set aside the commandment of God, and hold tightly to the tradition of men—the washing of pitchers and cups, and you do many other such things.”
verses.Mark.7.9: He said to them, “Full well do you reject the commandment of God, that you may keep your tradition.
verses.Mark.7.10: For Moses said, ‘Honor your father and your mother;’ and, ‘He who speaks evil of father or mother, let him be put to death.’
verses.Mark.7.11: But you say, ‘If a man tells his father or his mother, “Whatever profit you might have received from me is Corban,”’” that is to say, given to God,
verses.Mark.7.12: “then you no longer allow him to do anything for his father or his mother,
verses.Mark.7.13: making void the word of God by your tradition which you have handed down. You do many things like this.”
verses.Mark.7.14: He called all the multitude to himself and said to them, “Hear me, all of you, and understand.
verses.Mark.7.15: There is nothing from outside of the man that going into him can defile him; but the things which proceed out of the man are those that defile the man.
verses.Mark.7.16: If anyone has ears to hear, let him hear!”
verses.Mark.7.17: When he had entered into a house away from the multitude, his disciples asked him about the parable.
verses.Mark.7.18: He said to them, “Are you also without understanding? Don’t you perceive that whatever goes into the man from outside can’t defile him,
verses.Mark.7.19: because it doesn’t go into his heart, but into his stomach, then into the latrine, making all foods clean?”
verses.Mark.7.20: He said, “That which proceeds out of the man, that defiles the man.
verses.Mark.7.21: For from within, out of the hearts of men, proceed evil thoughts, adulteries, sexual sins, murders, thefts,
verses.Mark.7.22: covetings, wickedness, deceit, lustful desires, an evil eye, blasphemy, pride, and foolishness.
verses.Mark.7.23: All these evil things come from within and defile the man.”
verses.Mark.7.24: From there he arose and went away into the borders of Tyre and Sidon. He entered into a house and didn’t want anyone to know it, but he couldn’t escape notice.
verses.Mark.7.25: For a woman whose little daughter had an unclean spirit, having heard of him, came and fell down at his feet.
verses.Mark.7.26: Now the woman was a Greek, a Syrophoenician by race. She begged him that he would cast the demon out of her daughter.
verses.Mark.7.27: But Jesus said to her, “Let the children be filled first, for it is not appropriate to take the children’s bread and throw it to the dogs.”
verses.Mark.7.28: But she answered him, “Yes, Lord. Yet even the dogs under the table eat the children’s crumbs.”
verses.Mark.7.29: He said to her, “For this saying, go your way. The demon has gone out of your daughter.”
verses.Mark.7.30: She went away to her house, and found the child having been laid on the bed, with the demon gone out.
verses.Mark.7.31: Again he departed from the borders of Tyre and Sidon, and came to the sea of Galilee through the middle of the region of Decapolis.
verses.Mark.7.32: They brought to him one who was deaf and had an impediment in his speech. They begged him to lay his hand on him.
verses.Mark.7.33: He took him aside from the multitude privately and put his fingers into his ears; and he spat and touched his tongue.
verses.Mark.7.34: Looking up to heaven, he sighed, and said to him, “Ephphatha!” that is, “Be opened!”
verses.Mark.7.35: Immediately his ears were opened, and the impediment of his tongue was released, and he spoke clearly.
verses.Mark.7.36: He commanded them that they should tell no one, but the more he commanded them, so much the more widely they proclaimed it.
verses.Mark.7.37: They were astonished beyond measure, saying, “He has done all things well. He makes even the deaf hear and the mute speak!”
verses.Mark.12.1: He began to speak to them in parables. “A man planted a vineyard, put a hedge around it, dug a pit for the wine press, built a tower, rented it out to a farmer, and went into another country.
verses.Mark.12.2: When it was time, he sent a servant to the farmer to get from the farmer his share of the fruit of the vineyard.
verses.Mark.12.3: They took him, beat him, and sent him away empty.
verses.Mark.12.4: Again, he sent another servant to them; and they threw stones at him, wounded him in the head, and sent him away shamefully treated.
verses.Mark.12.5: Again he sent another, and they killed him, and many others, beating some, and killing some.
verses.Mark.12.6: Therefore still having one, his beloved son, he sent him last to them, saying, ‘They will respect my son.’
verses.Mark.12.7: But those farmers said among themselves, ‘This is the heir. Come, let’s kill him, and the inheritance will be ours.’
verses.Mark.12.8: They took him, killed him, and cast him out of the vineyard.
verses.Mark.12.9: What therefore will the lord of the vineyard do? He will come and destroy the farmers, and will give the vineyard to others.
verses.Mark.12.10:
Haven’t you even read this Scripture:
‘The stone which the builders rejected
was made the head of the corner.
verses.Mark.12.11:
This was from the Lord.
It is marvelous in our eyes’?”
verses.Mark.12.12: They tried to seize him, but they feared the multitude; for they perceived that he spoke the parable against them. They left him and went away.
verses.Mark.12.13: They sent some of the Pharisees and the Herodians to him, that they might trap him with words.
verses.Mark.12.14: When they had come, they asked him, “Teacher, we know that you are honest, and don’t defer to anyone; for you aren’t partial to anyone, but truly teach the way of God. Is it lawful to pay taxes to Caesar, or not?
verses.Mark.12.15: Shall we give, or shall we not give?” But he, knowing their hypocrisy, said to them, “Why do you test me? Bring me a denarius, that I may see it.”
verses.Mark.12.16: They brought it. He said to them, “Whose is this image and inscription?” They said to him, “Caesar’s.”
verses.Mark.12.17: Jesus answered them, “Give to Caesar the things that are Caesar’s, and to God the things that are God’s.” They marveled greatly at him.
verses.Mark.12.18: Some Sadducees, who say that there is no resurrection, came to him. They asked him, saying,
verses.Mark.12.19: “Teacher, Moses wrote to us, ‘If a man’s brother dies and leaves a wife behind him, and leaves no children, that his brother should take his wife and raise up offspring for his brother.’
verses.Mark.12.20: There were seven brothers. The first took a wife, and dying left no offspring.
verses.Mark.12.21: The second took her, and died, leaving no children behind him. The third likewise;
verses.Mark.12.22: and the seven took her and left no children. Last of all the woman also died.
verses.Mark.12.23: In the resurrection, when they rise, whose wife will she be of them? For the seven had her as a wife.”
verses.Mark.12.24: Jesus answered them, “Isn’t this because you are mistaken, not knowing the Scriptures nor the power of God?
verses.Mark.12.25: For when they will rise from the dead, they neither marry nor are given in marriage, but are like angels in heaven.
verses.Mark.12.26: But about the dead, that they are raised, haven’t you read in the book of Moses about the Bush, how God spoke to him, saying, ‘I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob’?
verses.Mark.12.27: He is not the God of the dead, but of the living. You are therefore badly mistaken.”
verses.Mark.12.28: One of the scribes came and heard them questioning together, and knowing that he had answered them well, asked him, “Which commandment is the greatest of all?”
verses.Mark.12.29: Jesus answered, “The greatest is: ‘Hear, Israel, the Lord our God, the Lord is one.
verses.Mark.12.30: You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, with all your mind, and with all your strength.’ This is the first commandment.
verses.Mark.12.31: The second is like this: ‘You shall love your neighbor as yourself.’ There is no other commandment greater than these.”
verses.Mark.12.32: The scribe said to him, “Truly, teacher, you have said well that he is one, and there is none other but he;
verses.Mark.12.33: and to love him with all the heart, with all the understanding, all the soul, and with all the strength, and to love his neighbor as himself, is more important than all whole burnt offerings and sacrifices.”
verses.Mark.12.34: When Jesus saw that he answered wisely, he said to him, “You are not far from God’s Kingdom.” No one dared ask him any question after that.
verses.Mark.12.35: Jesus responded, as he taught in the temple, “How is it that the scribes say that the Christ is the son of David?
verses.Mark.12.36:
For David himself said in the Holy Spirit,
‘The Lord said to my Lord,
“Sit at my right hand,
until I make your enemies the footstool of your feet.”’
verses.Mark.12.37: Therefore David himself calls him Lord, so how can he be his son?” The common people heard him gladly.
verses.Mark.12.38: In his teaching he said to them, “Beware of the scribes, who like to walk in long robes, and to get greetings in the marketplaces,
verses.Mark.12.39: and to get the best seats in the synagogues and the best places at feasts,
verses.Mark.12.40: those who devour widows’ houses, and for a pretense make long prayers. These will receive greater condemnation.”
verses.Mark.12.41: Jesus sat down opposite the treasury and saw how the multitude cast money into the treasury. Many who were rich cast in much.
verses.Mark.12.42: A poor widow came and she cast in two small brass coins, which equal a quadrans coin.
verses.Mark.12.43: He called his disciples to himself and said to them, “Most certainly I tell you, this poor widow gave more than all those who are giving into the treasury,
verses.Mark.12.44: for they all gave out of their abundance, but she, out of her poverty, gave all that she had to live on.”
verses.Mark.6.1: He went out from there. He came into his own country, and his disciples followed him.
verses.Mark.6.2: When the Sabbath had come, he began to teach in the synagogue, and many hearing him were astonished, saying, “Where did this man get these things?” and, “What is the wisdom that is given to this man, that such mighty works come about by his hands?
verses.Mark.6.3: Isn’t this the carpenter, the son of Mary and brother of James, Joses, Judah, and Simon? Aren’t his sisters here with us?” So they were offended at him.
verses.Mark.6.4: Jesus said to them, “A prophet is not without honor, except in his own country, and among his own relatives, and in his own house.”
verses.Mark.6.5: He could do no mighty work there, except that he laid his hands on a few sick people and healed them.
verses.Mark.6.6: He marveled because of their unbelief. He went around the villages teaching.
verses.Mark.6.7: He called to himself the twelve, and began to send them out two by two; and he gave them authority over the unclean spirits.
verses.Mark.6.8: He commanded them that they should take nothing for their journey, except a staff only: no bread, no wallet, no money in their purse,
verses.Mark.6.9: but to wear sandals, and not put on two tunics.
verses.Mark.6.10: He said to them, “Wherever you enter into a house, stay there until you depart from there.
verses.Mark.6.11: Whoever will not receive you nor hear you, as you depart from there, shake off the dust that is under your feet for a testimony against them. Assuredly, I tell you, it will be more tolerable for Sodom and Gomorrah in the day of judgment than for that city!”
verses.Mark.6.12: They went out and preached that people should repent.
verses.Mark.6.13: They cast out many demons, and anointed many with oil who were sick and healed them.
verses.Mark.6.14: King Herod heard this, for his name had become known, and he said, “John the Baptizer has risen from the dead, and therefore these powers are at work in him.”
verses.Mark.6.15: But others said, “He is Elijah.” Others said, “He is a prophet, or like one of the prophets.”
verses.Mark.6.16: But Herod, when he heard this, said, “This is John, whom I beheaded. He has risen from the dead.”
verses.Mark.6.17: For Herod himself had sent out and arrested John and bound him in prison for the sake of Herodias, his brother Philip’s wife, for he had married her.
verses.Mark.6.18: For John had said to Herod, “It is not lawful for you to have your brother’s wife.”
verses.Mark.6.19: Herodias set herself against him and desired to kill him, but she couldn’t,
verses.Mark.6.20: for Herod feared John, knowing that he was a righteous and holy man, and kept him safe. When he heard him, he did many things, and he heard him gladly.
verses.Mark.6.21: Then a convenient day came when Herod on his birthday made a supper for his nobles, the high officers, and the chief men of Galilee.
verses.Mark.6.22: When the daughter of Herodias herself came in and danced, she pleased Herod and those sitting with him. The king said to the young lady, “Ask me whatever you want, and I will give it to you.”
