verses.Mark.6.23: He swore to her, “Whatever you ask of me, I will give you, up to half of my kingdom.”
verses.Mark.6.24: She went out and said to her mother, “What shall I ask?” She said, “The head of John the Baptizer.”
verses.Mark.6.25: She came in immediately with haste to the king and requested, “I want you to give me right now the head of John the Baptizer on a platter.”
verses.Mark.6.26: The king was exceedingly sorry, but for the sake of his oaths and of his dinner guests, he didn’t wish to refuse her.
verses.Mark.6.27: Immediately the king sent out a soldier of his guard and commanded to bring John’s head; and he went and beheaded him in the prison,
verses.Mark.6.28: and brought his head on a platter, and gave it to the young lady; and the young lady gave it to her mother.
verses.Mark.6.29: When his disciples heard this, they came and took up his corpse and laid it in a tomb.
verses.Mark.6.30: The apostles gathered themselves together to Jesus, and they told him all things, whatever they had done, and whatever they had taught.
verses.Mark.6.31: He said to them, “Come away into a deserted place, and rest awhile.” For there were many coming and going, and they had no leisure so much as to eat.
verses.Mark.6.32: They went away in the boat to a deserted place by themselves.
verses.Mark.6.33: They saw them going, and many recognized him and ran there on foot from all the cities. They arrived before them and came together to him.
verses.Mark.6.34: Jesus came out, saw a great multitude, and he had compassion on them because they were like sheep without a shepherd; and he began to teach them many things.
verses.Mark.6.35: When it was late in the day, his disciples came to him and said, “This place is deserted, and it is late in the day.
verses.Mark.6.36: Send them away, that they may go into the surrounding country and villages and buy themselves bread, for they have nothing to eat.”
verses.Mark.6.37: But he answered them, “You give them something to eat.” They asked him, “Shall we go and buy two hundred denarii worth of bread and give them something to eat?”
verses.Mark.6.38: He said to them, “How many loaves do you have? Go see.” When they knew, they said, “Five, and two fish.”
verses.Mark.6.39: He commanded them that everyone should sit down in groups on the green grass.
verses.Mark.6.40: They sat down in ranks, by hundreds and by fifties.
verses.Mark.6.41: He took the five loaves and the two fish; and looking up to heaven, he blessed and broke the loaves, and he gave to his disciples to set before them, and he divided the two fish among them all.
verses.Mark.6.42: They all ate and were filled.
verses.Mark.6.43: They took up twelve baskets full of broken pieces and also of the fish.
verses.Mark.6.44: Those who ate the loaves were five thousand men.
verses.Mark.6.45: Immediately he made his disciples get into the boat and go ahead to the other side, to Bethsaida, while he himself sent the multitude away.
verses.Mark.6.46: After he had taken leave of them, he went up the mountain to pray.
verses.Mark.6.47: When evening had come, the boat was in the middle of the sea, and he was alone on the land.
verses.Mark.6.48: Seeing them distressed in rowing, for the wind was contrary to them, about the fourth watch of the night he came to them, walking on the sea; and he would have passed by them,
verses.Mark.6.49: but they, when they saw him walking on the sea, supposed that it was a ghost, and cried out;
verses.Mark.6.50: for they all saw him and were troubled. But he immediately spoke with them and said to them, “Cheer up! It is I! Don’t be afraid.”
verses.Mark.6.51: He got into the boat with them; and the wind ceased, and they were very amazed among themselves, and marveled;
verses.Mark.6.52: for they hadn’t understood about the loaves, but their hearts were hardened.
verses.Mark.6.53: When they had crossed over, they came to land at Gennesaret and moored to the shore.
verses.Mark.6.54: When they had come out of the boat, immediately the people recognized him,
verses.Mark.6.55: and ran around that whole region, and began to bring those who were sick on their mats to where they heard he was.
verses.Mark.6.56: Wherever he entered—into villages, or into cities, or into the country—they laid the sick in the marketplaces and begged him that they might just touch the fringe of his garment; and as many as touched him were made well.
verses.Mark.11.1: When they came near to Jerusalem, to Bethsphage and Bethany, at the Mount of Olives, he sent two of his disciples
verses.Mark.11.2: and said to them, “Go your way into the village that is opposite you. Immediately as you enter into it, you will find a young donkey tied, on which no one has sat. Untie him and bring him.
verses.Mark.11.3: If anyone asks you, ‘Why are you doing this?’ say, ‘The Lord needs him;’ and immediately he will send him back here.”
verses.Mark.11.4: They went away, and found a young donkey tied at the door outside in the open street, and they untied him.
verses.Mark.11.5: Some of those who stood there asked them, “What are you doing, untying the young donkey?”
verses.Mark.11.6: They said to them just as Jesus had said, and they let them go.
verses.Mark.11.7: They brought the young donkey to Jesus and threw their garments on it, and Jesus sat on it.
verses.Mark.11.8: Many spread their garments on the way, and others were cutting down branches from the trees and spreading them on the road.
verses.Mark.11.9: Those who went in front and those who followed cried out, “Hosanna! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord!
verses.Mark.11.10: Blessed is the kingdom of our father David that is coming in the name of the Lord! Hosanna in the highest!”
verses.Mark.11.11: Jesus entered into the temple in Jerusalem. When he had looked around at everything, it being now evening, he went out to Bethany with the twelve.
verses.Mark.11.12: The next day, when they had come out from Bethany, he was hungry.
verses.Mark.11.13: Seeing a fig tree afar off having leaves, he came to see if perhaps he might find anything on it. When he came to it, he found nothing but leaves, for it was not the season for figs.
verses.Mark.11.14: Jesus told it, “May no one ever eat fruit from you again!” and his disciples heard it.
verses.Mark.11.15: They came to Jerusalem, and Jesus entered into the temple and began to throw out those who sold and those who bought in the temple, and overthrew the money changers’ tables and the seats of those who sold the doves.
verses.Mark.11.16: He would not allow anyone to carry a container through the temple.
verses.Mark.11.17: He taught, saying to them, “Isn’t it written, ‘My house will be called a house of prayer for all the nations’? But you have made it a den of robbers!”
verses.Mark.11.18: The chief priests and the scribes heard it, and sought how they might destroy him. For they feared him, because all the multitude was astonished at his teaching.
verses.Mark.11.19: When evening came, he went out of the city.
verses.Mark.11.20: As they passed by in the morning, they saw the fig tree withered away from the roots.
verses.Mark.11.21: Peter, remembering, said to him, “Rabbi, look! The fig tree which you cursed has withered away.”
verses.Mark.11.22: Jesus answered them, “Have faith in God.
verses.Mark.11.23: For most certainly I tell you, whoever may tell this mountain, ‘Be taken up and cast into the sea,’ and doesn’t doubt in his heart, but believes that what he says is happening, he shall have whatever he says.
verses.Mark.11.24: Therefore I tell you, all things whatever you pray and ask for, believe that you have received them, and you shall have them.
verses.Mark.11.25: Whenever you stand praying, forgive, if you have anything against anyone; so that your Father, who is in heaven, may also forgive you your transgressions.
verses.Mark.11.26: But if you do not forgive, neither will your Father in heaven forgive your transgressions.”
verses.Mark.11.27: They came again to Jerusalem, and as he was walking in the temple, the chief priests, the scribes, and the elders came to him,
verses.Mark.11.28: and they began saying to him, “By what authority do you do these things? Or who gave you this authority to do these things?”
verses.Mark.11.29: Jesus said to them, “I will ask you one question. Answer me, and I will tell you by what authority I do these things.
verses.Mark.11.30: The baptism of John—was it from heaven, or from men? Answer me.”
verses.Mark.11.31: They reasoned with themselves, saying, “If we should say, ‘From heaven;’ he will say, ‘Why then did you not believe him?’
verses.Mark.11.32: If we should say, ‘From men’”—they feared the people, for all held John to really be a prophet.
verses.Mark.11.33: They answered Jesus, “We don’t know.” Jesus said to them, “Neither will I tell you by what authority I do these things.”
verses.Mark.3.1: He entered again into the synagogue, and there was a man there whose hand was withered.
verses.Mark.3.2: They watched him, whether he would heal him on the Sabbath day, that they might accuse him.
verses.Mark.3.3: He said to the man whose hand was withered, “Stand up.”
verses.Mark.3.4: He said to them, “Is it lawful on the Sabbath day to do good or to do harm? To save a life or to kill?” But they were silent.
verses.Mark.3.5: When he had looked around at them with anger, being grieved at the hardening of their hearts, he said to the man, “Stretch out your hand.” He stretched it out, and his hand was restored as healthy as the other.
verses.Mark.3.6: The Pharisees went out, and immediately conspired with the Herodians against him, how they might destroy him.
verses.Mark.3.7: Jesus withdrew to the sea with his disciples; and a great multitude followed him from Galilee, from Judea,
verses.Mark.3.8: from Jerusalem, from Idumaea, beyond the Jordan, and those from around Tyre and Sidon. A great multitude, hearing what great things he did, came to him.
verses.Mark.3.9: He spoke to his disciples that a little boat should stay near him because of the crowd, so that they wouldn’t press on him.
verses.Mark.3.10: For he had healed many, so that as many as had diseases pressed on him that they might touch him.
verses.Mark.3.11: The unclean spirits, whenever they saw him, fell down before him and cried, “You are the Son of God!”
verses.Mark.3.12: He sternly warned them that they should not make him known.
verses.Mark.3.13: He went up into the mountain and called to himself those whom he wanted, and they went to him.
verses.Mark.3.14: He appointed twelve, that they might be with him, and that he might send them out to preach
verses.Mark.3.15: and to have authority to heal sicknesses and to cast out demons:
verses.Mark.3.16: Simon (to whom he gave the name Peter);
verses.Mark.3.17: James the son of Zebedee; and John, the brother of James, (whom he called Boanerges, which means, Sons of Thunder);
verses.Mark.3.18: Andrew; Philip; Bartholomew; Matthew; Thomas; James, the son of Alphaeus; Thaddaeus; Simon the Zealot;
verses.Mark.3.19: and Judas Iscariot, who also betrayed him. Then he came into a house.
verses.Mark.3.20: The multitude came together again, so that they could not so much as eat bread.
verses.Mark.3.21: When his friends heard it, they went out to seize him; for they said, “He is insane.”
verses.Mark.3.22: The scribes who came down from Jerusalem said, “He has Beelzebul,” and, “By the prince of the demons he casts out the demons.”
verses.Mark.3.23: He summoned them and said to them in parables, “How can Satan cast out Satan?
verses.Mark.3.24: If a kingdom is divided against itself, that kingdom cannot stand.
verses.Mark.3.25: If a house is divided against itself, that house cannot stand.
verses.Mark.3.26: If Satan has risen up against himself, and is divided, he can’t stand, but has an end.
verses.Mark.3.27: But no one can enter into the house of the strong man to plunder unless he first binds the strong man; then he will plunder his house.
verses.Mark.3.28: “Most certainly I tell you, all sins of the descendants of man will be forgiven, including their blasphemies with which they may blaspheme;
verses.Mark.3.29: but whoever may blaspheme against the Holy Spirit never has forgiveness, but is subject to eternal condemnation.”
verses.Mark.3.30: —because they said, “He has an unclean spirit.”
verses.Mark.3.31: His mother and his brothers came, and standing outside, they sent to him, calling him.
verses.Mark.3.32: A multitude was sitting around him, and they told him, “Behold, your mother, your brothers, and your sisters are outside looking for you.”
verses.Mark.3.33: He answered them, “Who are my mother and my brothers?”
verses.Mark.3.34: Looking around at those who sat around him, he said, “Behold, my mother and my brothers!
verses.Mark.3.35: For whoever does the will of God is my brother, my sister, and mother.”
verses.Mark.8.1: In those days, when there was a very great multitude, and they had nothing to eat, Jesus called his disciples to himself and said to them,
verses.Mark.8.2: “I have compassion on the multitude, because they have stayed with me now three days and have nothing to eat.
verses.Mark.8.3: If I send them away fasting to their home, they will faint on the way, for some of them have come a long way.”
verses.Mark.8.4: His disciples answered him, “From where could one satisfy these people with bread here in a deserted place?”
verses.Mark.8.5: He asked them, “How many loaves do you have?” They said, “Seven.”
verses.Mark.8.6: He commanded the multitude to sit down on the ground, and he took the seven loaves. Having given thanks, he broke them and gave them to his disciples to serve, and they served the multitude.
verses.Mark.8.7: They also had a few small fish. Having blessed them, he said to serve these also.
verses.Mark.8.8: They ate and were filled. They took up seven baskets of broken pieces that were left over.
verses.Mark.8.9: Those who had eaten were about four thousand. Then he sent them away.
verses.Mark.8.10: Immediately he entered into the boat with his disciples and came into the region of Dalmanutha.
verses.Mark.8.11: The Pharisees came out and began to question him, seeking from him a sign from heaven and testing him.
verses.Mark.8.12: He sighed deeply in his spirit and said, “Why does this generation seek a sign? Most certainly I tell you, no sign will be given to this generation.”
verses.Mark.8.13: He left them, and again entering into the boat, departed to the other side.
verses.Mark.8.14: They forgot to take bread; and they didn’t have more than one loaf in the boat with them.
verses.Mark.8.15: He warned them, saying, “Take heed: beware of the yeast of the Pharisees and the yeast of Herod.”
verses.Mark.8.16: They reasoned with one another, saying, “It’s because we have no bread.”
verses.Mark.8.17: Jesus, perceiving it, said to them, “Why do you reason that it’s because you have no bread? Don’t you perceive yet or understand? Is your heart still hardened?
verses.Mark.8.18: Having eyes, don’t you see? Having ears, don’t you hear? Don’t you remember?
verses.Mark.8.19: When I broke the five loaves among the five thousand, how many baskets full of broken pieces did you take up?” They told him, “Twelve.”
verses.Mark.8.20: “When the seven loaves fed the four thousand, how many baskets full of broken pieces did you take up?” They told him, “Seven.”
verses.Mark.8.21: He asked them, “Don’t you understand yet?”
verses.Mark.8.22: He came to Bethsaida. They brought a blind man to him and begged him to touch him.
verses.Mark.8.23: He took hold of the blind man by the hand, and brought him out of the village. When he had spat on his eyes, and laid his hands on him, he asked him if he saw anything.
verses.Mark.8.24: He looked up, and said, “I see men, but I see them like walking trees.”
verses.Mark.8.25: Then again he laid his hands on his eyes. He looked intently, and was restored, and saw everyone clearly.
verses.Mark.8.26: He sent him away to his house, saying, “Don’t enter into the village, nor tell anyone in the village.”
verses.Mark.8.27: Jesus went out, with his disciples, into the villages of Caesarea Philippi. On the way he asked his disciples, “Who do men say that I am?”
verses.Mark.8.28: They told him, “John the Baptizer, and others say Elijah, but others, one of the prophets.”
verses.Mark.8.29: He said to them, “But who do you say that I am?” Peter answered, “You are the Christ.”
verses.Mark.8.30: He commanded them that they should tell no one about him.
verses.Mark.8.31: He began to teach them that the Son of Man must suffer many things, and be rejected by the elders, the chief priests, and the scribes, and be killed, and after three days rise again.
verses.Mark.8.32: He spoke to them openly. Peter took him and began to rebuke him.
verses.Mark.8.33: But he, turning around and seeing his disciples, rebuked Peter, and said, “Get behind me, Satan! For you have in mind not the things of God, but the things of men.”
verses.Mark.8.34: He called the multitude to himself with his disciples and said to them, “Whoever wants to come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and follow me.
verses.Mark.8.35: For whoever wants to save his life will lose it; and whoever will lose his life for my sake and the sake of the Good News will save it.
verses.Mark.8.36: For what does it profit a man to gain the whole world and forfeit his life?
verses.Mark.8.37: For what will a man give in exchange for his life?
verses.Mark.8.38: For whoever will be ashamed of me and of my words in this adulterous and sinful generation, the Son of Man also will be ashamed of him when he comes in his Father’s glory with the holy angels.”
verses.Mark.5.1: They came to the other side of the sea, into the country of the Gadarenes.
verses.Mark.5.2: When he had come out of the boat, immediately a man with an unclean spirit met him out of the tombs.
verses.Mark.5.3: He lived in the tombs. Nobody could bind him any more, not even with chains,
verses.Mark.5.4: because he had been often bound with fetters and chains, and the chains had been torn apart by him, and the fetters broken in pieces. Nobody had the strength to tame him.
verses.Mark.5.5: Always, night and day, in the tombs and in the mountains, he was crying out, and cutting himself with stones.
verses.Mark.5.6: When he saw Jesus from afar, he ran and bowed down to him,
verses.Mark.5.7: and crying out with a loud voice, he said, “What have I to do with you, Jesus, you Son of the Most High God? I adjure you by God, don’t torment me.”
verses.Mark.5.8: For he said to him, “Come out of the man, you unclean spirit!”
verses.Mark.5.9: He asked him, “What is your name?” He said to him, “My name is Legion, for we are many.”
verses.Mark.5.10: He begged him much that he would not send them away out of the country.
verses.Mark.5.11: Now on the mountainside there was a great herd of pigs feeding.
verses.Mark.5.12: All the demons begged him, saying, “Send us into the pigs, that we may enter into them.”
verses.Mark.5.13: At once Jesus gave them permission. The unclean spirits came out and entered into the pigs. The herd of about two thousand rushed down the steep bank into the sea, and they were drowned in the sea.
verses.Mark.5.14: Those who fed the pigs fled, and told it in the city and in the country. The people came to see what it was that had happened.
verses.Mark.5.15: They came to Jesus, and saw him who had been possessed by demons sitting, clothed, and in his right mind, even him who had the legion; and they were afraid.
verses.Mark.5.16: Those who saw it declared to them what happened to him who was possessed by demons, and about the pigs.
verses.Mark.5.17: They began to beg him to depart from their region.
verses.Mark.5.18: As he was entering into the boat, he who had been possessed by demons begged him that he might be with him.
verses.Mark.5.19: He didn’t allow him, but said to him, “Go to your house, to your friends, and tell them what great things the Lord has done for you and how he had mercy on you.”
verses.Mark.5.20: He went his way, and began to proclaim in Decapolis how Jesus had done great things for him, and everyone marveled.
verses.Mark.5.21: When Jesus had crossed back over in the boat to the other side, a great multitude was gathered to him; and he was by the sea.
verses.Mark.5.22: Behold, one of the rulers of the synagogue, Jairus by name, came; and seeing him, he fell at his feet
verses.Mark.5.23: and begged him much, saying, “My little daughter is at the point of death. Please come and lay your hands on her, that she may be made healthy, and live.”
verses.Mark.5.24: He went with him, and a great multitude followed him, and they pressed upon him on all sides.
verses.Mark.5.25: A certain woman who had a discharge of blood for twelve years,
verses.Mark.5.26: and had suffered many things by many physicians, and had spent all that she had, and was no better, but rather grew worse,
verses.Mark.5.27: having heard the things concerning Jesus, came up behind him in the crowd and touched his clothes.
verses.Mark.5.28: For she said, “If I just touch his clothes, I will be made well.”
verses.Mark.5.29: Immediately the flow of her blood was dried up, and she felt in her body that she was healed of her affliction.
verses.Mark.5.30: Immediately Jesus, perceiving in himself that the power had gone out from him, turned around in the crowd and asked, “Who touched my clothes?”
verses.Mark.5.31: His disciples said to him, “You see the multitude pressing against you, and you say, ‘Who touched me?’”
verses.Mark.5.32: He looked around to see her who had done this thing.
verses.Mark.5.33: But the woman, fearing and trembling, knowing what had been done to her, came and fell down before him, and told him all the truth.
verses.Mark.5.34: He said to her, “Daughter, your faith has made you well. Go in peace, and be cured of your disease.”
verses.Mark.5.35: While he was still speaking, people came from the synagogue ruler’s house, saying, “Your daughter is dead. Why bother the Teacher any more?”
verses.Mark.5.36: But Jesus, when he heard the message spoken, immediately said to the ruler of the synagogue, “Don’t be afraid, only believe.”
verses.Mark.5.37: He allowed no one to follow him except Peter, James, and John the brother of James.
verses.Mark.5.38: He came to the synagogue ruler’s house, and he saw an uproar, weeping, and great wailing.
verses.Mark.5.39: When he had entered in, he said to them, “Why do you make an uproar and weep? The child is not dead, but is asleep.”
verses.Mark.5.40: They ridiculed him. But he, having put them all out, took the father of the child, her mother, and those who were with him, and went in where the child was lying.
verses.Mark.5.41: Taking the child by the hand, he said to her, “Talitha cumi!” which means, being interpreted, “Girl, I tell you, get up!”
verses.Mark.5.42: Immediately the girl rose up and walked, for she was twelve years old. They were amazed with great amazement.
verses.Mark.5.43: He strictly ordered them that no one should know this, and commanded that something should be given to her to eat.
verses.Mark.4.1: Again he began to teach by the seaside. A great multitude was gathered to him, so that he entered into a boat in the sea and sat down. All the multitude were on the land by the sea.
verses.Mark.4.2: He taught them many things in parables, and told them in his teaching,
verses.Mark.4.3: “Listen! Behold, the farmer went out to sow.
verses.Mark.4.4: As he sowed, some seed fell by the road, and the birds came and devoured it.
verses.Mark.4.5: Others fell on the rocky ground, where it had little soil, and immediately it sprang up, because it had no depth of soil.
verses.Mark.4.6: When the sun had risen, it was scorched; and because it had no root, it withered away.
verses.Mark.4.7: Others fell among the thorns, and the thorns grew up and choked it, and it yielded no fruit.
verses.Mark.4.8: Others fell into the good ground and yielded fruit, growing up and increasing. Some produced thirty times, some sixty times, and some one hundred times as much.”
verses.Mark.4.9: He said, “Whoever has ears to hear, let him hear.”
verses.Mark.4.10: When he was alone, those who were around him with the twelve asked him about the parables.
verses.Mark.4.11: He said to them, “To you is given the mystery of God’s Kingdom, but to those who are outside, all things are done in parables,
verses.Mark.4.12: that ‘seeing they may see and not perceive, and hearing they may hear and not understand, lest perhaps they should turn again, and their sins should be forgiven them.’”
verses.Mark.4.13: He said to them, “Don’t you understand this parable? How will you understand all of the parables?
verses.Mark.4.15: The ones by the road are the ones where the word is sown; and when they have heard, immediately Satan comes and takes away the word which has been sown in them.
verses.Mark.4.16: These in the same way are those who are sown on the rocky places, who, when they have heard the word, immediately receive it with joy.
verses.Mark.4.17: They have no root in themselves, but are short-lived. When oppression or persecution arises because of the word, immediately they stumble.
verses.Mark.4.18: Others are those who are sown among the thorns. These are those who have heard the word,
verses.Mark.4.19: and the cares of this age, and the deceitfulness of riches, and the lusts of other things entering in choke the word, and it becomes unfruitful.
verses.Mark.4.20: Those which were sown on the good ground are those who hear the word, accept it, and bear fruit, some thirty times, some sixty times, and some one hundred times.”
verses.Mark.4.21: He said to them, “Is a lamp brought to be put under a basket or under a bed? Isn’t it put on a stand?
verses.Mark.4.22: For there is nothing hidden except that it should be made known, neither was anything made secret but that it should come to light.
verses.Mark.4.23: If any man has ears to hear, let him hear.”
verses.Mark.4.24: He said to them, “Take heed what you hear. With whatever measure you measure, it will be measured to you; and more will be given to you who hear.
verses.Mark.4.25: For whoever has, to him more will be given; and he who doesn’t have, even that which he has will be taken away from him.”
verses.Mark.4.26: He said, “God’s Kingdom is as if a man should cast seed on the earth,
verses.Mark.4.27: and should sleep and rise night and day, and the seed should spring up and grow, though he doesn’t know how.
verses.Mark.4.28: For the earth bears fruit by itself: first the blade, then the ear, then the full grain in the ear.
verses.Mark.4.29: But when the fruit is ripe, immediately he puts in the sickle, because the harvest has come.”
verses.Mark.4.30: He said, “How will we liken God’s Kingdom? Or with what parable will we illustrate it?
verses.Mark.4.31: It’s like a grain of mustard seed, which, when it is sown in the earth, though it is less than all the seeds that are on the earth,
verses.Mark.4.32: yet when it is sown, grows up and becomes greater than all the herbs, and puts out great branches, so that the birds of the sky can lodge under its shadow.”
verses.Mark.4.33: With many such parables he spoke the word to them, as they were able to hear it.
verses.Mark.4.34: Without a parable he didn’t speak to them; but privately to his own disciples he explained everything.
verses.Mark.4.35: On that day, when evening had come, he said to them, “Let’s go over to the other side.”
verses.Mark.4.36: Leaving the multitude, they took him with them, even as he was, in the boat. Other small boats were also with him.
verses.Mark.4.37: A big wind storm arose, and the waves beat into the boat, so much that the boat was already filled.
verses.Mark.4.38: He himself was in the stern, asleep on the cushion; and they woke him up and asked him, “Teacher, don’t you care that we are dying?”
verses.Mark.4.39: He awoke and rebuked the wind, and said to the sea, “Peace! Be still!” The wind ceased and there was a great calm.
verses.Mark.4.40: He said to them, “Why are you so afraid? How is it that you have no faith?”
verses.Mark.4.41: They were greatly afraid and said to one another, “Who then is this, that even the wind and the sea obey him?”
verses.Luke.3.1: Now in the fifteenth year of the reign of Tiberius Caesar, Pontius Pilate being governor of Judea, and Herod being tetrarch of Galilee, and his brother Philip tetrarch of the region of Ituraea and Trachonitis, and Lysanias tetrarch of Abilene,
verses.Luke.3.2: during the high priesthood of Annas and Caiaphas, the word of God came to John, the son of Zacharias, in the wilderness.
verses.Luke.3.3: He came into all the region around the Jordan, preaching the baptism of repentance for remission of sins.
verses.Luke.3.4:
As it is written in the book of the words of Isaiah the prophet,
“The voice of one crying in the wilderness,
‘Make ready the way of the Lord.
Make his paths straight.
verses.Luke.3.5:
Every valley will be filled.
Every mountain and hill will be brought low.
The crooked will become straight,
and the rough ways smooth.
verses.Luke.3.6: All flesh will see God’s salvation.’”
verses.Luke.3.7: He said therefore to the multitudes who went out to be baptized by him, “You offspring of vipers, who warned you to flee from the wrath to come?
verses.Luke.3.8: Therefore produce fruits worthy of repentance, and don’t begin to say among yourselves, ‘We have Abraham for our father;’ for I tell you that God is able to raise up children to Abraham from these stones!
verses.Luke.3.9: Even now the ax also lies at the root of the trees. Every tree therefore that doesn’t produce good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire.”
verses.Luke.3.10: The multitudes asked him, “What then must we do?”
verses.Luke.3.11: He answered them, “He who has two coats, let him give to him who has none. He who has food, let him do likewise.”
verses.Luke.3.12: Tax collectors also came to be baptized, and they said to him, “Teacher, what must we do?”
verses.Luke.3.13: He said to them, “Collect no more than that which is appointed to you.”
verses.Luke.3.14: Soldiers also asked him, saying, “What about us? What must we do?” He said to them, “Extort from no one by violence, neither accuse anyone wrongfully. Be content with your wages.”
verses.Luke.3.15: As the people were in expectation, and all men reasoned in their hearts concerning John, whether perhaps he was the Christ,
verses.Luke.3.16: John answered them all, “I indeed baptize you with water, but he comes who is mightier than I, the strap of whose sandals I am not worthy to loosen. He will baptize you in the Holy Spirit and fire.
verses.Luke.3.17: His winnowing fan is in his hand, and he will thoroughly cleanse his threshing floor, and will gather the wheat into his barn; but he will burn up the chaff with unquenchable fire.”
verses.Luke.3.18: Then with many other exhortations he preached good news to the people,
verses.Luke.3.19: but Herod the tetrarch, being reproved by him for Herodias, his brother’s wife, and for all the evil things which Herod had done,
verses.Luke.3.20: added this also to them all, that he shut up John in prison.
verses.Luke.3.21: Now when all the people were baptized, Jesus also had been baptized and was praying. The sky was opened,
verses.Luke.3.22: and the Holy Spirit descended in a bodily form like a dove on him; and a voice came out of the sky, saying “You are my beloved Son. In you I am well pleased.”
verses.Luke.3.23: Jesus himself, when he began to teach, was about thirty years old, being the son (as was supposed) of Joseph, the son of Heli,
verses.Luke.3.24: the son of Matthat, the son of Levi, the son of Melchi, the son of Jannai, the son of Joseph,
verses.Luke.3.25: the son of Mattathias, the son of Amos, the son of Nahum, the son of Esli, the son of Naggai,
verses.Luke.3.26: the son of Maath, the son of Mattathias, the son of Semein, the son of Joseph, the son of Judah,
verses.Luke.3.27: the son of Joanan, the son of Rhesa, the son of Zerubbabel, the son of Shealtiel, the son of Neri,
verses.Luke.3.28: the son of Melchi, the son of Addi, the son of Cosam, the son of Elmodam, the son of Er,
verses.Luke.3.29: the son of Jose, the son of Eliezer, the son of Jorim, the son of Matthat, the son of Levi,
verses.Luke.3.30: the son of Simeon, the son of Judah, the son of Joseph, the son of Jonan, the son of Eliakim,
verses.Luke.3.31: the son of Melea, the son of Menan, the son of Mattatha, the son of Nathan, the son of David,
verses.Luke.3.32: the son of Jesse, the son of Obed, the son of Boaz, the son of Salmon, the son of Nahshon,
verses.Luke.3.33: the son of Amminadab, the son of Aram, the son of Hezron, the son of Perez, the son of Judah,
verses.Luke.3.34: the son of Jacob, the son of Isaac, the son of Abraham, the son of Terah, the son of Nahor,
verses.Luke.3.35: the son of Serug, the son of Reu, the son of Peleg, the son of Eber, the son of Shelah,
verses.Luke.3.36: the son of Cainan, the son of Arphaxad, the son of Shem, the son of Noah, the son of Lamech,
verses.Luke.3.37: the son of Methuselah, the son of Enoch, the son of Jared, the son of Mahalaleel, the son of Cainan,
verses.Luke.3.38: the son of Enos, the son of Seth, the son of Adam, the son of God.
verses.Luke.5.1: Now while the multitude pressed on him and heard the word of God, he was standing by the lake of Gennesaret.
verses.Luke.5.2: He saw two boats standing by the lake, but the fishermen had gone out of them and were washing their nets.
verses.Luke.5.3: He entered into one of the boats, which was Simon’s, and asked him to put out a little from the land. He sat down and taught the multitudes from the boat.
verses.Luke.5.4: When he had finished speaking, he said to Simon, “Put out into the deep and let down your nets for a catch.”
verses.Luke.5.5: Simon answered him, “Master, we worked all night and caught nothing; but at your word I will let down the net.”
verses.Luke.5.6: When they had done this, they caught a great multitude of fish, and their net was breaking.
verses.Luke.5.7: They beckoned to their partners in the other boat, that they should come and help them. They came and filled both boats, so that they began to sink.
verses.Luke.5.8: But Simon Peter, when he saw it, fell down at Jesus’ knees, saying, “Depart from me, for I am a sinful man, Lord.”
verses.Luke.5.9: For he was amazed, and all who were with him, at the catch of fish which they had caught;
verses.Luke.5.10: and so also were James and John, sons of Zebedee, who were partners with Simon. Jesus said to Simon, “Don’t be afraid. From now on you will be catching people alive.”
verses.Luke.5.11: When they had brought their boats to land, they left everything, and followed him.
verses.Luke.5.12: While he was in one of the cities, behold, there was a man full of leprosy. When he saw Jesus, he fell on his face and begged him, saying, “Lord, if you want to, you can make me clean.”
verses.Luke.5.13: He stretched out his hand and touched him, saying, “I want to. Be made clean.” Immediately the leprosy left him.
verses.Luke.5.14: He commanded him to tell no one, “But go your way and show yourself to the priest, and offer for your cleansing according to what Moses commanded, for a testimony to them.”
verses.Luke.5.15: But the report concerning him spread much more, and great multitudes came together to hear and to be healed by him of their infirmities.
verses.Luke.5.16: But he withdrew himself into the desert and prayed.
verses.Luke.5.17: On one of those days, he was teaching; and there were Pharisees and teachers of the law sitting by who had come out of every village of Galilee, Judea, and Jerusalem. The power of the Lord was with him to heal them.
verses.Luke.5.18: Behold, men brought a paralyzed man on a cot, and they sought to bring him in to lay before Jesus.
verses.Luke.5.19: Not finding a way to bring him in because of the multitude, they went up to the housetop and let him down through the tiles with his cot into the middle before Jesus.
verses.Luke.5.20: Seeing their faith, he said to him, “Man, your sins are forgiven you.”
verses.Luke.5.21: The scribes and the Pharisees began to reason, saying, “Who is this who speaks blasphemies? Who can forgive sins, but God alone?”
verses.Luke.5.22: But Jesus, perceiving their thoughts, answered them, “Why are you reasoning so in your hearts?
verses.Luke.5.23: Which is easier to say, ‘Your sins are forgiven you,’ or to say, ‘Arise and walk’?
verses.Luke.5.24: But that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins,” he said to the paralyzed man, “I tell you, arise, take up your cot, and go to your house.”
verses.Luke.5.25: Immediately he rose up before them, and took up that which he was laying on, and departed to his house, glorifying God.
verses.Luke.5.26: Amazement took hold on all, and they glorified God. They were filled with fear, saying, “We have seen strange things today.”
verses.Luke.5.27: After these things he went out and saw a tax collector named Levi sitting at the tax office, and said to him, “Follow me!”
verses.Luke.5.28: He left everything, and rose up and followed him.
verses.Luke.5.29: Levi made a great feast for him in his house. There was a great crowd of tax collectors and others who were reclining with them.
verses.Luke.5.30: Their scribes and the Pharisees murmured against his disciples, saying, “Why do you eat and drink with the tax collectors and sinners?”
verses.Luke.5.31: Jesus answered them, “Those who are healthy have no need for a physician, but those who are sick do.
verses.Luke.5.32: I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners, to repentance.”
verses.Luke.5.33: They said to him, “Why do John’s disciples often fast and pray, likewise also the disciples of the Pharisees, but yours eat and drink?”
verses.Luke.5.34: He said to them, “Can you make the friends of the bridegroom fast while the bridegroom is with them?
verses.Luke.5.35: But the days will come when the bridegroom will be taken away from them. Then they will fast in those days.”
verses.Luke.5.36: He also told a parable to them. “No one puts a piece from a new garment on an old garment, or else he will tear the new, and also the piece from the new will not match the old.
verses.Luke.5.37: No one puts new wine into old wineskins, or else the new wine will burst the skins, and it will be spilled and the skins will be destroyed.
verses.Luke.5.38: But new wine must be put into fresh wineskins, and both are preserved.
verses.Luke.5.39: No man having drunk old wine immediately desires new, for he says, ‘The old is better.’”
verses.Mark.15.1: Immediately in the morning the chief priests, with the elders, scribes, and the whole council, held a consultation, bound Jesus, carried him away, and delivered him up to Pilate.
verses.Mark.15.2: Pilate asked him, “Are you the King of the Jews?” He answered, “So you say.”
verses.Mark.15.3: The chief priests accused him of many things.
verses.Mark.15.4: Pilate again asked him, “Have you no answer? See how many things they testify against you!”
verses.Mark.15.5: But Jesus made no further answer, so that Pilate marveled.
verses.Mark.15.6: Now at the feast he used to release to them one prisoner, whomever they asked of him.
verses.Mark.15.7: There was one called Barabbas, bound with his fellow insurgents, men who in the insurrection had committed murder.
verses.Mark.15.8: The multitude, crying aloud, began to ask him to do as he always did for them.
verses.Mark.15.9: Pilate answered them, saying, “Do you want me to release to you the King of the Jews?”
verses.Mark.15.10: For he perceived that for envy the chief priests had delivered him up.
verses.Mark.15.11: But the chief priests stirred up the multitude, that he should release Barabbas to them instead.
verses.Mark.15.12: Pilate again asked them, “What then should I do to him whom you call the King of the Jews?”
verses.Mark.15.14: Pilate said to them, “Why, what evil has he done?” But they cried out exceedingly, “Crucify him!”
verses.Mark.15.15: Pilate, wishing to please the multitude, released Barabbas to them, and handed over Jesus, when he had flogged him, to be crucified.
verses.Mark.15.16: The soldiers led him away within the court, which is the Praetorium; and they called together the whole cohort.
verses.Mark.15.17: They clothed him with purple; and weaving a crown of thorns, they put it on him.
verses.Mark.15.18: They began to salute him, “Hail, King of the Jews!”
verses.Mark.15.19: They struck his head with a reed and spat on him, and bowing their knees, did homage to him.
verses.Mark.15.20: When they had mocked him, they took the purple cloak off him, and put his own garments on him. They led him out to crucify him.
verses.Mark.15.21: They compelled one passing by, coming from the country, Simon of Cyrene, the father of Alexander and Rufus, to go with them that he might bear his cross.
verses.Mark.15.22: They brought him to the place called Golgotha, which is, being interpreted, “The place of a skull.”
verses.Mark.15.23: They offered him wine mixed with myrrh to drink, but he didn’t take it.
verses.Mark.15.24: Crucifying him, they parted his garments among them, casting lots on them, what each should take.
verses.Mark.15.25: It was the third hour when they crucified him.
verses.Mark.15.26: The superscription of his accusation was written over him: “THE KING OF THE JEWS.”
verses.Mark.15.27: With him they crucified two robbers, one on his right hand, and one on his left.
verses.Mark.15.28: The Scripture was fulfilled which says, “He was counted with transgressors.”
verses.Mark.15.29: Those who passed by blasphemed him, wagging their heads and saying, “Ha! You who destroy the temple and build it in three days,
verses.Mark.15.30: save yourself, and come down from the cross!”
verses.Mark.15.31: Likewise, also the chief priests mocking among themselves with the scribes said, “He saved others. He can’t save himself.
verses.Mark.15.32: Let the Christ, the King of Israel, now come down from the cross, that we may see and believe him.” Those who were crucified with him also insulted him.
verses.Mark.15.33: When the sixth hour had come, there was darkness over the whole land until the ninth hour.
verses.Mark.15.34: At the ninth hour Jesus cried with a loud voice, saying, “Eloi, Eloi, lama sabachthani?” which is, being interpreted, “My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?”
verses.Mark.15.35: Some of those who stood by, when they heard it, said, “Behold, he is calling Elijah.”
verses.Mark.15.36: One ran, and filling a sponge full of vinegar, put it on a reed and gave it to him to drink, saying, “Let him be. Let’s see whether Elijah comes to take him down.”
verses.Mark.15.37: Jesus cried out with a loud voice, and gave up the spirit.
verses.Mark.15.38: The veil of the temple was torn in two from the top to the bottom.
verses.Mark.15.39: When the centurion, who stood by opposite him, saw that he cried out like this and breathed his last, he said, “Truly this man was the Son of God!”
verses.Mark.15.40: There were also women watching from afar, among whom were both Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of James the less and of Joses, and Salome;
verses.Mark.15.41: who, when he was in Galilee, followed him and served him; and many other women who came up with him to Jerusalem.
verses.Mark.15.42: When evening had now come, because it was the Preparation Day, that is, the day before the Sabbath,
verses.Mark.15.43: Joseph of Arimathaea, a prominent council member who also himself was looking for God’s Kingdom, came. He boldly went in to Pilate, and asked for Jesus’ body.
verses.Mark.15.44: Pilate was surprised to hear that he was already dead; and summoning the centurion, he asked him whether he had been dead long.
verses.Mark.15.45: When he found out from the centurion, he granted the body to Joseph.
verses.Mark.15.46: He bought a linen cloth, and taking him down, wound him in the linen cloth and laid him in a tomb which had been cut out of a rock. He rolled a stone against the door of the tomb.
verses.Mark.15.47: Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of Joses, saw where he was laid.
verses.Luke.1.1: Since many have undertaken to set in order a narrative concerning those matters which have been fulfilled among us,
verses.Luke.1.2: even as those who from the beginning were eyewitnesses and servants of the word delivered them to us,
verses.Luke.1.3: it seemed good to me also, having traced the course of all things accurately from the first, to write to you in order, most excellent Theophilus;
verses.Luke.1.4: that you might know the certainty concerning the things in which you were instructed.
verses.Luke.1.5: There was in the days of Herod, the king of Judea, a certain priest named Zacharias, of the priestly division of Abijah. He had a wife of the daughters of Aaron, and her name was Elizabeth.
verses.Luke.1.6: They were both righteous before God, walking blamelessly in all the commandments and ordinances of the Lord.
verses.Luke.1.7: But they had no child, because Elizabeth was barren, and they both were well advanced in years.
verses.Luke.1.8: Now while he executed the priest’s office before God in the order of his division
verses.Luke.1.9: according to the custom of the priest’s office, his lot was to enter into the temple of the Lord and burn incense.
verses.Luke.1.10: The whole multitude of the people were praying outside at the hour of incense.
verses.Luke.1.11: An angel of the Lord appeared to him, standing on the right side of the altar of incense.
verses.Luke.1.12: Zacharias was troubled when he saw him, and fear fell upon him.
verses.Luke.1.13: But the angel said to him, “Don’t be afraid, Zacharias, because your request has been heard. Your wife, Elizabeth, will bear you a son, and you shall call his name John.
verses.Luke.1.14: You will have joy and gladness, and many will rejoice at his birth.
verses.Luke.1.15: For he will be great in the sight of the Lord, and he will drink no wine nor strong drink. He will be filled with the Holy Spirit, even from his mother’s womb.
verses.Luke.1.16: He will turn many of the children of Israel to the Lord their God.
verses.Luke.1.17: He will go before him in the spirit and power of Elijah, ‘to turn the hearts of the fathers to the children,’ and the disobedient to the wisdom of the just; to prepare a people prepared for the Lord.”
verses.Luke.1.18: Zacharias said to the angel, “How can I be sure of this? For I am an old man, and my wife is well advanced in years.”
verses.Luke.1.19: The angel answered him, “I am Gabriel, who stands in the presence of God. I was sent to speak to you and to bring you this good news.
verses.Luke.1.20: Behold, you will be silent and not able to speak until the day that these things will happen, because you didn’t believe my words, which will be fulfilled in their proper time.”
verses.Luke.1.21: The people were waiting for Zacharias, and they marveled that he delayed in the temple.
verses.Luke.1.22: When he came out, he could not speak to them. They perceived that he had seen a vision in the temple. He continued making signs to them, and remained mute.
verses.Luke.1.23: When the days of his service were fulfilled, he departed to his house.
verses.Luke.1.24: After these days Elizabeth his wife conceived, and she hid herself five months, saying,
verses.Luke.1.25: “Thus has the Lord done to me in the days in which he looked at me, to take away my reproach among men.”
verses.Luke.1.26: Now in the sixth month, the angel Gabriel was sent from God to a city of Galilee named Nazareth,
verses.Luke.1.27: to a virgin pledged to be married to a man whose name was Joseph, of David’s house. The virgin’s name was Mary.
verses.Luke.1.28: Having come in, the angel said to her, “Rejoice, you highly favored one! The Lord is with you. Blessed are you among women!”
verses.Luke.1.29: But when she saw him, she was greatly troubled at the saying, and considered what kind of salutation this might be.
verses.Luke.1.30: The angel said to her, “Don’t be afraid, Mary, for you have found favor with God.
verses.Luke.1.31: Behold, you will conceive in your womb and give birth to a son, and shall name him ‘Jesus.’
verses.Luke.1.32: He will be great and will be called the Son of the Most High. The Lord God will give him the throne of his father David,
verses.Luke.1.33: and he will reign over the house of Jacob forever. There will be no end to his Kingdom.”
verses.Luke.1.34: Mary said to the angel, “How can this be, seeing I am a virgin?”
verses.Luke.1.35: The angel answered her, “The Holy Spirit will come on you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you. Therefore also the holy one who is born from you will be called the Son of God.
verses.Luke.1.36: Behold, Elizabeth your relative also has conceived a son in her old age; and this is the sixth month with her who was called barren.
verses.Luke.1.37: For nothing spoken by God is impossible.”
verses.Luke.1.38: Mary said, “Behold, the servant of the Lord; let it be done to me according to your word.” Then the angel departed from her.
verses.Luke.1.39: Mary arose in those days and went into the hill country with haste, into a city of Judah,
verses.Luke.1.40: and entered into the house of Zacharias and greeted Elizabeth.
verses.Luke.1.41: When Elizabeth heard Mary’s greeting, the baby leaped in her womb; and Elizabeth was filled with the Holy Spirit.
verses.Luke.1.42: She called out with a loud voice and said, “Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb!
verses.Luke.1.43: Why am I so favored, that the mother of my Lord should come to me?
verses.Luke.1.44: For behold, when the voice of your greeting came into my ears, the baby leaped in my womb for joy!
verses.Luke.1.45: Blessed is she who believed, for there will be a fulfillment of the things which have been spoken to her from the Lord!”
verses.Luke.1.46:
Mary said,
“My soul magnifies the Lord.
verses.Luke.1.47: My spirit has rejoiced in God my Savior,
verses.Luke.1.48:
for he has looked at the humble state of his servant.
For behold, from now on, all generations will call me blessed.
verses.Luke.1.49:
For he who is mighty has done great things for me.
Holy is his name.
verses.Luke.1.50: His mercy is for generations and generations on those who fear him.
verses.Luke.1.51:
He has shown strength with his arm.
He has scattered the proud in the imagination of their hearts.
verses.Luke.1.52:
He has put down princes from their thrones,
and has exalted the lowly.
verses.Luke.1.53:
He has filled the hungry with good things.
He has sent the rich away empty.
verses.Luke.1.54: He has given help to Israel, his servant, that he might remember mercy,
verses.Luke.1.55:
as he spoke to our fathers,
to Abraham and his offspring forever.”
verses.Luke.1.56: Mary stayed with her about three months, and then returned to her house.
verses.Luke.1.57: Now the time that Elizabeth should give birth was fulfilled, and she gave birth to a son.
verses.Luke.1.58: Her neighbors and her relatives heard that the Lord had magnified his mercy toward her, and they rejoiced with her.
verses.Luke.1.59: On the eighth day, they came to circumcise the child; and they would have called him Zacharias, after the name of his father.
verses.Luke.1.60: His mother answered, “Not so; but he will be called John.”
verses.Luke.1.61: They said to her, “There is no one among your relatives who is called by this name.”
verses.Luke.1.62: They made signs to his father, what he would have him called.
verses.Luke.1.63: He asked for a writing tablet, and wrote, “His name is John.” They all marveled.
verses.Luke.1.64: His mouth was opened immediately and his tongue freed, and he spoke, blessing God.
verses.Luke.1.65: Fear came on all who lived around them, and all these sayings were talked about throughout all the hill country of Judea.
verses.Luke.1.66: All who heard them laid them up in their heart, saying, “What then will this child be?” The hand of the Lord was with him.
verses.Luke.1.67: His father Zacharias was filled with the Holy Spirit, and prophesied, saying,
verses.Luke.1.68:
“Blessed be the Lord, the God of Israel,
for he has visited and redeemed his people;
verses.Luke.1.69: and has raised up a horn of salvation for us in the house of his servant David
verses.Luke.1.70: (as he spoke by the mouth of his holy prophets who have been from of old),
verses.Luke.1.71: salvation from our enemies and from the hand of all who hate us;
verses.Luke.1.72:
to show mercy toward our fathers,
to remember his holy covenant,
verses.Luke.1.73: the oath which he swore to Abraham our father,
verses.Luke.1.74:
to grant to us that we, being delivered out of the hand of our enemies,
should serve him without fear,
verses.Luke.1.75: in holiness and righteousness before him all the days of our life.
verses.Luke.1.76:
And you, child, will be called a prophet of the Most High;
for you will go before the face of the Lord to prepare his ways,
verses.Luke.1.77: to give knowledge of salvation to his people by the remission of their sins,
verses.Luke.1.78:
because of the tender mercy of our God,
by which the dawn from on high will visit us,
verses.Luke.1.79:
to shine on those who sit in darkness and the shadow of death;
to guide our feet into the way of peace.”
verses.Luke.1.80: The child was growing and becoming strong in spirit, and was in the desert until the day of his public appearance to Israel.
verses.Luke.4.1: Jesus, full of the Holy Spirit, returned from the Jordan and was led by the Spirit into the wilderness
verses.Luke.4.2: for forty days, being tempted by the devil. He ate nothing in those days. Afterward, when they were completed, he was hungry.
verses.Luke.4.3: The devil said to him, “If you are the Son of God, command this stone to become bread.”
verses.Luke.4.4: Jesus answered him, saying, “It is written, ‘Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word of God.’”
verses.Luke.4.5: The devil, leading him up on a high mountain, showed him all the kingdoms of the world in a moment of time.
verses.Luke.4.6: The devil said to him, “I will give you all this authority and their glory, for it has been delivered to me, and I give it to whomever I want.
verses.Luke.4.7: If you therefore will worship before me, it will all be yours.”
verses.Luke.4.8: Jesus answered him, “Get behind me, Satan! For it is written, ‘You shall worship the Lord your God, and you shall serve him only.’”
verses.Luke.4.9: He led him to Jerusalem and set him on the pinnacle of the temple, and said to him, “If you are the Son of God, cast yourself down from here,
verses.Luke.4.10:
for it is written,
‘He will put his angels in charge of you, to guard you;’
verses.Luke.4.11:
and,
‘On their hands they will bear you up,
lest perhaps you dash your foot against a stone.’”
verses.Luke.4.12: Jesus answering, said to him, “It has been said, ‘You shall not tempt the Lord your God.’”
verses.Luke.4.13: When the devil had completed every temptation, he departed from him until another time.
verses.Luke.4.14: Jesus returned in the power of the Spirit into Galilee, and news about him spread through all the surrounding area.
verses.Luke.4.15: He taught in their synagogues, being glorified by all.
verses.Luke.4.16: He came to Nazareth, where he had been brought up. He entered, as was his custom, into the synagogue on the Sabbath day, and stood up to read.
verses.Luke.4.17: The book of the prophet Isaiah was handed to him. He opened the book, and found the place where it was written,
verses.Luke.4.18:
“The Spirit of the Lord is on me,
because he has anointed me to preach good news to the poor.
He has sent me to heal the broken hearted,
to proclaim release to the captives,
recovering of sight to the blind,
to deliver those who are crushed,
verses.Luke.4.19: and to proclaim the acceptable year of the Lord.”
verses.Luke.4.20: He closed the book, gave it back to the attendant, and sat down. The eyes of all in the synagogue were fastened on him.
verses.Luke.4.21: He began to tell them, “Today, this Scripture has been fulfilled in your hearing.”
verses.Luke.4.22: All testified about him and wondered at the gracious words which proceeded out of his mouth; and they said, “Isn’t this Joseph’s son?”
verses.Luke.4.23: He said to them, “Doubtless you will tell me this proverb, ‘Physician, heal yourself! Whatever we have heard done at Capernaum, do also here in your hometown.’”
verses.Luke.4.24: He said, “Most certainly I tell you, no prophet is acceptable in his hometown.
verses.Luke.4.25: But truly I tell you, there were many widows in Israel in the days of Elijah, when the sky was shut up three years and six months, when a great famine came over all the land.
verses.Luke.4.26: Elijah was sent to none of them, except to Zarephath, in the land of Sidon, to a woman who was a widow.
verses.Luke.4.27: There were many lepers in Israel in the time of Elisha the prophet, yet not one of them was cleansed, except Naaman, the Syrian.”
verses.Luke.4.28: They were all filled with wrath in the synagogue as they heard these things.
verses.Luke.4.29: They rose up, threw him out of the city, and led him to the brow of the hill that their city was built on, that they might throw him off the cliff.
verses.Luke.4.30: But he, passing through the middle of them, went his way.
verses.Luke.4.31: He came down to Capernaum, a city of Galilee. He was teaching them on the Sabbath day,
verses.Luke.4.32: and they were astonished at his teaching, for his word was with authority.
verses.Luke.4.33: In the synagogue there was a man who had a spirit of an unclean demon; and he cried out with a loud voice,
verses.Luke.4.34: saying, “Ah! what have we to do with you, Jesus of Nazareth? Have you come to destroy us? I know who you are: the Holy One of God!”
verses.Luke.4.35: Jesus rebuked him, saying, “Be silent and come out of him!” When the demon had thrown him down in the middle of them, he came out of him, having done him no harm.
verses.Luke.4.36: Amazement came on all and they spoke together, one with another, saying, “What is this word? For with authority and power he commands the unclean spirits, and they come out!”
verses.Luke.4.37: News about him went out into every place of the surrounding region.
verses.Luke.4.38: He rose up from the synagogue and entered into Simon’s house. Simon’s mother-in-law was afflicted with a great fever, and they begged him to help her.
verses.Luke.4.39: He stood over her and rebuked the fever, and it left her. Immediately she rose up and served them.
verses.Luke.4.40: When the sun was setting, all those who had any sick with various diseases brought them to him; and he laid his hands on every one of them, and healed them.
verses.Luke.4.41: Demons also came out of many, crying out and saying, “You are the Christ, the Son of God!” Rebuking them, he didn’t allow them to speak, because they knew that he was the Christ.
verses.Luke.4.42: When it was day, he departed and went into an uninhabited place and the multitudes looked for him, and came to him, and held on to him, so that he wouldn’t go away from them.
verses.Luke.4.43: But he said to them, “I must preach the good news of God’s Kingdom to the other cities also. For this reason I have been sent.”
verses.Luke.4.44: He was preaching in the synagogues of Galilee.
verses.Mark.14.1: It was now two days before the Passover and the Feast of Unleavened Bread, and the chief priests and the scribes sought how they might seize him by deception and kill him.
verses.Mark.14.2: For they said, “Not during the feast, because there might be a riot among the people.”
verses.Mark.14.3: While he was at Bethany, in the house of Simon the leper, as he sat at the table, a woman came having an alabaster jar of ointment of pure nard—very costly. She broke the jar and poured it over his head.
verses.Mark.14.4: But there were some who were indignant among themselves, saying, “Why has this ointment been wasted?
verses.Mark.14.5: For this might have been sold for more than three hundred denarii and given to the poor.” So they grumbled against her.
verses.Mark.14.6: But Jesus said, “Leave her alone. Why do you trouble her? She has done a good work for me.
verses.Mark.14.7: For you always have the poor with you, and whenever you want to, you can do them good; but you will not always have me.
verses.Mark.14.8: She has done what she could. She has anointed my body beforehand for the burying.
verses.Mark.14.9: Most certainly I tell you, wherever this Good News may be preached throughout the whole world, that which this woman has done will also be spoken of for a memorial of her.”
verses.Mark.14.10: Judas Iscariot, who was one of the twelve, went away to the chief priests, that he might deliver him to them.
verses.Mark.14.11: They, when they heard it, were glad, and promised to give him money. He sought how he might conveniently deliver him.
verses.Mark.14.12: On the first day of unleavened bread, when they sacrificed the Passover, his disciples asked him, “Where do you want us to go and prepare that you may eat the Passover?”
verses.Mark.14.13: He sent two of his disciples and said to them, “Go into the city, and there a man carrying a pitcher of water will meet you. Follow him,
verses.Mark.14.14: and wherever he enters in, tell the master of the house, ‘The Teacher says, “Where is the guest room, where I may eat the Passover with my disciples?”’
verses.Mark.14.15: He will himself show you a large upper room furnished and ready. Get ready for us there.”
verses.Mark.14.16: His disciples went out, and came into the city, and found things as he had said to them, and they prepared the Passover.
verses.Mark.14.17: When it was evening he came with the twelve.
verses.Mark.14.18: As they sat and were eating, Jesus said, “Most certainly I tell you, one of you will betray me—he who eats with me.”
verses.Mark.14.19: They began to be sorrowful, and to ask him one by one, “Surely not I?” And another said, “Surely not I?”
verses.Mark.14.20: He answered them, “It is one of the twelve, he who dips with me in the dish.
verses.Mark.14.21: For the Son of Man goes as it is written about him, but woe to that man by whom the Son of Man is betrayed! It would be better for that man if he had not been born.”
verses.Mark.14.22: As they were eating, Jesus took bread, and when he had blessed it, he broke it and gave to them, and said, “Take, eat. This is my body.”
verses.Mark.14.23: He took the cup, and when he had given thanks, he gave to them. They all drank of it.
verses.Mark.14.24: He said to them, “This is my blood of the new covenant, which is poured out for many.
verses.Mark.14.25: Most certainly I tell you, I will no more drink of the fruit of the vine until that day when I drink it anew in God’s Kingdom.”
verses.Mark.14.26: When they had sung a hymn, they went out to the Mount of Olives.
verses.Mark.14.27: Jesus said to them, “All of you will be made to stumble because of me tonight, for it is written, ‘I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered.’
verses.Mark.14.28: However, after I am raised up, I will go before you into Galilee.”
verses.Mark.14.29: But Peter said to him, “Although all will be offended, yet I will not.”
verses.Mark.14.30: Jesus said to him, “Most certainly I tell you that you today, even this night, before the rooster crows twice, you will deny me three times.”
verses.Mark.14.31: But he spoke all the more, “If I must die with you, I will not deny you.” They all said the same thing.
verses.Mark.14.32: They came to a place which was named Gethsemane. He said to his disciples, “Sit here while I pray.”
verses.Mark.14.33: He took with him Peter, James, and John, and began to be greatly troubled and distressed.
verses.Mark.14.34: He said to them, “My soul is exceedingly sorrowful, even to death. Stay here and watch.”
verses.Mark.14.35: He went forward a little, and fell on the ground, and prayed that if it were possible, the hour might pass away from him.
verses.Mark.14.36: He said, “Abba, Father, all things are possible to you. Please remove this cup from me. However, not what I desire, but what you desire.”
verses.Mark.14.37: He came and found them sleeping, and said to Peter, “Simon, are you sleeping? Couldn’t you watch one hour?
verses.Mark.14.38: Watch and pray, that you may not enter into temptation. The spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak.”
verses.Mark.14.39: Again he went away and prayed, saying the same words.
verses.Mark.14.40: Again he returned and found them sleeping, for their eyes were very heavy; and they didn’t know what to answer him.
verses.Mark.14.41: He came the third time and said to them, “Sleep on now, and take your rest. It is enough. The hour has come. Behold, the Son of Man is betrayed into the hands of sinners.
verses.Mark.14.42: Arise! Let’s get going. Behold, he who betrays me is at hand.”
verses.Mark.14.43: Immediately, while he was still speaking, Judas, one of the twelve, came—and with him a multitude with swords and clubs, from the chief priests, the scribes, and the elders.
verses.Mark.14.44: Now he who betrayed him had given them a sign, saying, “Whomever I will kiss, that is he. Seize him, and lead him away safely.”
verses.Mark.14.45: When he had come, immediately he came to him and said, “Rabbi! Rabbi!” and kissed him.
verses.Mark.14.46: They laid their hands on him and seized him.
verses.Mark.14.47: But a certain one of those who stood by drew his sword and struck the servant of the high priest, and cut off his ear.
verses.Mark.14.48: Jesus answered them, “Have you come out, as against a robber, with swords and clubs to seize me?
verses.Mark.14.49: I was daily with you in the temple teaching, and you didn’t arrest me. But this is so that the Scriptures might be fulfilled.”
verses.Mark.14.50: They all left him, and fled.
verses.Mark.14.51: A certain young man followed him, having a linen cloth thrown around himself over his naked body. The young men grabbed him,
verses.Mark.14.52: but he left the linen cloth and fled from them naked.
verses.Mark.14.53: They led Jesus away to the high priest. All the chief priests, the elders, and the scribes came together with him.
verses.Mark.14.54: Peter had followed him from a distance, until he came into the court of the high priest. He was sitting with the officers, and warming himself in the light of the fire.
verses.Mark.14.55: Now the chief priests and the whole council sought witnesses against Jesus to put him to death, and found none.
verses.Mark.14.56: For many gave false testimony against him, and their testimony didn’t agree with each other.
verses.Mark.14.57: Some stood up and gave false testimony against him, saying,
verses.Mark.14.58: “We heard him say, ‘I will destroy this temple that is made with hands, and in three days I will build another made without hands.’”
verses.Mark.14.59: Even so, their testimony didn’t agree.
verses.Mark.14.60: The high priest stood up in the middle, and asked Jesus, “Have you no answer? What is it which these testify against you?”
verses.Mark.14.61: But he stayed quiet, and answered nothing. Again the high priest asked him, “Are you the Christ, the Son of the Blessed?”
verses.Mark.14.62: Jesus said, “I am. You will see the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of Power, and coming with the clouds of the sky.”
verses.Mark.14.63: The high priest tore his clothes and said, “What further need have we of witnesses?
verses.Mark.14.64: You have heard the blasphemy! What do you think?” They all condemned him to be worthy of death.
verses.Mark.14.65: Some began to spit on him, and to cover his face, and to beat him with fists, and to tell him, “Prophesy!” The officers struck him with the palms of their hands.
verses.Mark.14.66: As Peter was in the courtyard below, one of the maids of the high priest came,
verses.Mark.14.67: and seeing Peter warming himself, she looked at him and said, “You were also with the Nazarene, Jesus!”
verses.Mark.14.68: But he denied it, saying, “I neither know nor understand what you are saying.” He went out on the porch, and the rooster crowed.
verses.Mark.14.69: The maid saw him and began again to tell those who stood by, “This is one of them.”
verses.Mark.14.70: But he again denied it. After a little while again those who stood by said to Peter, “You truly are one of them, for you are a Galilean, and your speech shows it.”
verses.Mark.14.71: But he began to curse and to swear, “I don’t know this man of whom you speak!”
verses.Mark.14.72: The rooster crowed the second time. Peter remembered the words that Jesus said to him, “Before the rooster crows twice, you will deny me three times.” When he thought about that, he wept.
verses.Mark.13.1: As he went out of the temple, one of his disciples said to him, “Teacher, see what kind of stones and what kind of buildings!”
verses.Mark.13.2: Jesus said to him, “Do you see these great buildings? There will not be left here one stone on another, which will not be thrown down.”
verses.Mark.13.3: As he sat on the Mount of Olives opposite the temple, Peter, James, John, and Andrew asked him privately,
verses.Mark.13.4: “Tell us, when will these things be? What is the sign that these things are all about to be fulfilled?”
verses.Mark.13.5: Jesus, answering, began to tell them, “Be careful that no one leads you astray.
verses.Mark.13.6: For many will come in my name, saying, ‘I am he!’ and will lead many astray.
verses.Mark.13.7: “When you hear of wars and rumors of wars, don’t be troubled. For those must happen, but the end is not yet.
verses.Mark.13.8: For nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom. There will be earthquakes in various places. There will be famines and troubles. These things are the beginning of birth pains.
verses.Mark.13.9: “But watch yourselves, for they will deliver you up to councils. You will be beaten in synagogues. You will stand before rulers and kings for my sake, for a testimony to them.
verses.Mark.13.10: The Good News must first be preached to all the nations.
verses.Mark.13.11: When they lead you away and deliver you up, don’t be anxious beforehand or premeditate what you will say, but say whatever will be given you in that hour. For it is not you who speak, but the Holy Spirit.
verses.Mark.13.12: “Brother will deliver up brother to death, and the father his child. Children will rise up against parents and cause them to be put to death.
verses.Mark.13.13: You will be hated by all men for my name’s sake, but he who endures to the end will be saved.
verses.Mark.13.14: “But when you see the abomination of desolation, spoken of by Daniel the prophet, standing where it ought not” (let the reader understand), “then let those who are in Judea flee to the mountains,
verses.Mark.13.15: and let him who is on the housetop not go down, nor enter in, to take anything out of his house.
verses.Mark.13.16: Let him who is in the field not return back to take his cloak.
verses.Mark.13.17: But woe to those who are with child and to those who nurse babies in those days!
verses.Mark.13.18: Pray that your flight won’t be in the winter.
verses.Mark.13.19: For in those days there will be oppression, such as there has not been the like from the beginning of the creation which God created until now, and never will be.
verses.Mark.13.20: Unless the Lord had shortened the days, no flesh would have been saved; but for the sake of the chosen ones, whom he picked out, he shortened the days.
verses.Mark.13.21: Then if anyone tells you, ‘Look, here is the Christ!’ or, ‘Look, there!’ don’t believe it.
verses.Mark.13.22: For false christs and false prophets will arise and will show signs and wonders, that they may lead astray, if possible, even the chosen ones.
verses.Mark.13.23: But you watch. “Behold, I have told you all things beforehand.
verses.Mark.13.24: But in those days, after that oppression, the sun will be darkened, the moon will not give its light,
verses.Mark.13.25: the stars will be falling from the sky, and the powers that are in the heavens will be shaken.
verses.Mark.13.26: Then they will see the Son of Man coming in clouds with great power and glory.
verses.Mark.13.27: Then he will send out his angels, and will gather together his chosen ones from the four winds, from the ends of the earth to the ends of the sky.
verses.Mark.13.28: “Now from the fig tree, learn this parable. When the branch has now become tender and produces its leaves, you know that the summer is near;
verses.Mark.13.29: even so you also, when you see these things coming to pass, know that it is near, at the doors.
verses.Mark.13.30: Most certainly I say to you, this generation will not pass away until all these things happen.
verses.Mark.13.31: Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will not pass away.
verses.Mark.13.32: “But of that day or that hour no one knows—not even the angels in heaven, nor the Son, but only the Father.
verses.Mark.13.33: Watch, keep alert, and pray; for you don’t know when the time is.
verses.Mark.13.34: “It is like a man traveling to another country, having left his house and given authority to his servants, and to each one his work, and also commanded the doorkeeper to keep watch.
verses.Mark.13.35: Watch therefore, for you don’t know when the lord of the house is coming—whether at evening, or at midnight, or when the rooster crows, or in the morning;
verses.Mark.13.36: lest, coming suddenly, he might find you sleeping.
verses.Mark.13.37: What I tell you, I tell all: Watch!”
verses.Luke.6.1: Now on the second Sabbath after the first, he was going through the grain fields. His disciples plucked the heads of grain and ate, rubbing them in their hands.
verses.Luke.6.2: But some of the Pharisees said to them, “Why do you do that which is not lawful to do on the Sabbath day?”
verses.Luke.6.3: Jesus, answering them, said, “Haven’t you read what David did when he was hungry, he and those who were with him,
verses.Luke.6.4: how he entered into God’s house, and took and ate the show bread, and gave also to those who were with him, which is not lawful to eat except for the priests alone?”
verses.Luke.6.5: He said to them, “The Son of Man is lord of the Sabbath.”
verses.Luke.6.6: It also happened on another Sabbath that he entered into the synagogue and taught. There was a man there, and his right hand was withered.
verses.Luke.6.7: The scribes and the Pharisees watched him, to see whether he would heal on the Sabbath, that they might find an accusation against him.
verses.Luke.6.8: But he knew their thoughts; and he said to the man who had the withered hand, “Rise up and stand in the middle.” He arose and stood.
verses.Luke.6.9: Then Jesus said to them, “I will ask you something: Is it lawful on the Sabbath to do good, or to do harm? To save a life, or to kill?”
verses.Luke.6.10: He looked around at them all, and said to the man, “Stretch out your hand.” He did, and his hand was restored as sound as the other.
verses.Luke.6.11: But they were filled with rage, and talked with one another about what they might do to Jesus.
verses.Luke.6.12: In these days, he went out to the mountain to pray, and he continued all night in prayer to God.
verses.Luke.6.13: When it was day, he called his disciples, and from them he chose twelve, whom he also named apostles:
verses.Luke.6.14: Simon, whom he also named Peter; Andrew, his brother; James; John; Philip; Bartholomew;
verses.Luke.6.15: Matthew; Thomas; James the son of Alphaeus; Simon who was called the Zealot;
verses.Luke.6.16: Judas the son of James; and Judas Iscariot, who also became a traitor.
verses.Luke.6.17: He came down with them and stood on a level place, with a crowd of his disciples and a great number of the people from all Judea and Jerusalem and the sea coast of Tyre and Sidon, who came to hear him and to be healed of their diseases,
verses.Luke.6.18: as well as those who were troubled by unclean spirits; and they were being healed.
verses.Luke.6.19: All the multitude sought to touch him, for power came out of him and healed them all.
verses.Luke.6.20:
He lifted up his eyes to his disciples, and said:
“Blessed are you who are poor,
for God’s Kingdom is yours.
verses.Luke.6.21:
Blessed are you who hunger now,
for you will be filled.
Blessed are you who weep now,
for you will laugh.
verses.Luke.6.22: Blessed are you when men hate you, and when they exclude and mock you, and throw out your name as evil, for the Son of Man’s sake.
verses.Luke.6.23: Rejoice in that day and leap for joy, for behold, your reward is great in heaven, for their fathers did the same thing to the prophets.
verses.Luke.6.24:
“But woe to you who are rich!
For you have received your consolation.
verses.Luke.6.25:
Woe to you, you who are full now,
for you will be hungry.
Woe to you who laugh now,
for you will mourn and weep.
verses.Luke.6.26:
Woe, when men speak well of you,
for their fathers did the same thing to the false prophets.
verses.Luke.6.27: “But I tell you who hear: love your enemies, do good to those who hate you,
verses.Luke.6.28: bless those who curse you, and pray for those who mistreat you.
verses.Luke.6.29: To him who strikes you on the cheek, offer also the other; and from him who takes away your cloak, don’t withhold your coat also.
verses.Luke.6.30: Give to everyone who asks you, and don’t ask him who takes away your goods to give them back again.
verses.Luke.6.31: “As you would like people to do to you, do exactly so to them.
verses.Luke.6.32: “If you love those who love you, what credit is that to you? For even sinners love those who love them.
verses.Luke.6.33: If you do good to those who do good to you, what credit is that to you? For even sinners do the same.
verses.Luke.6.34: If you lend to those from whom you hope to receive, what credit is that to you? Even sinners lend to sinners, to receive back as much.
verses.Luke.6.35: But love your enemies, and do good, and lend, expecting nothing back; and your reward will be great, and you will be children of the Most High; for he is kind toward the unthankful and evil.
verses.Luke.6.36:
“Therefore be merciful,
even as your Father is also merciful.
verses.Luke.6.37:
Don’t judge,
and you won’t be judged.
Don’t condemn,
and you won’t be condemned.
Set free,
and you will be set free.
verses.Luke.6.38: “Give, and it will be given to you: good measure, pressed down, shaken together, and running over, will be given to you. For with the same measure you measure it will be measured back to you.”
verses.Luke.6.39: He spoke a parable to them. “Can the blind guide the blind? Won’t they both fall into a pit?
verses.Luke.6.40: A disciple is not above his teacher, but everyone when he is fully trained will be like his teacher.
verses.Luke.6.41: Why do you see the speck of chaff that is in your brother’s eye, but don’t consider the beam that is in your own eye?
verses.Luke.6.42: Or how can you tell your brother, ‘Brother, let me remove the speck of chaff that is in your eye,’ when you yourself don’t see the beam that is in your own eye? You hypocrite! First remove the beam from your own eye, and then you can see clearly to remove the speck of chaff that is in your brother’s eye.
verses.Luke.6.43: “For there is no good tree that produces rotten fruit, nor again a rotten tree that produces good fruit.
verses.Luke.6.44: For each tree is known by its own fruit. For people don’t gather figs from thorns, nor do they gather grapes from a bramble bush.
verses.Luke.6.45: The good man out of the good treasure of his heart brings out that which is good, and the evil man out of the evil treasure of his heart brings out that which is evil, for out of the abundance of the heart, his mouth speaks.
verses.Luke.6.46: “Why do you call me, ‘Lord, Lord,’ and don’t do the things which I say?
verses.Luke.6.47: Everyone who comes to me, and hears my words and does them, I will show you who he is like.
