verses.Luke.6.48: He is like a man building a house, who dug and went deep and laid a foundation on the rock. When a flood arose, the stream broke against that house, and could not shake it, because it was founded on the rock.
verses.Luke.6.49: But he who hears and doesn’t do, is like a man who built a house on the earth without a foundation, against which the stream broke, and immediately it fell; and the ruin of that house was great.”
verses.Luke.2.1: Now in those days, a decree went out from Caesar Augustus that all the world should be enrolled.
verses.Luke.2.2: This was the first enrollment made when Quirinius was governor of Syria.
verses.Luke.2.3: All went to enroll themselves, everyone to his own city.
verses.Luke.2.4: Joseph also went up from Galilee, out of the city of Nazareth, into Judea, to David’s city, which is called Bethlehem, because he was of the house and family of David,
verses.Luke.2.5: to enroll himself with Mary, who was pledged to be married to him as wife, being pregnant.
verses.Luke.2.6: While they were there, the day had come for her to give birth.
verses.Luke.2.7: She gave birth to her firstborn son. She wrapped him in bands of cloth and laid him in a feeding trough, because there was no room for them in the inn.
verses.Luke.2.8: There were shepherds in the same country staying in the field, and keeping watch by night over their flock.
verses.Luke.2.9: Behold, an angel of the Lord stood by them, and the glory of the Lord shone around them, and they were terrified.
verses.Luke.2.10: The angel said to them, “Don’t be afraid, for behold, I bring you good news of great joy which will be to all the people.
verses.Luke.2.11: For there is born to you today, in David’s city, a Savior, who is Christ the Lord.
verses.Luke.2.12: This is the sign to you: you will find a baby wrapped in strips of cloth, lying in a feeding trough.”
verses.Luke.2.13: Suddenly, there was with the angel a multitude of the heavenly army praising God and saying,
verses.Luke.2.14:
“Glory to God in the highest,
on earth peace, good will toward men.”
verses.Luke.2.15: When the angels went away from them into the sky, the shepherds said to one another, “Let’s go to Bethlehem, now, and see this thing that has happened, which the Lord has made known to us.”
verses.Luke.2.16: They came with haste and found both Mary and Joseph, and the baby was lying in the feeding trough.
verses.Luke.2.17: When they saw it, they publicized widely the saying which was spoken to them about this child.
verses.Luke.2.18: All who heard it wondered at the things which were spoken to them by the shepherds.
verses.Luke.2.19: But Mary kept all these sayings, pondering them in her heart.
verses.Luke.2.20: The shepherds returned, glorifying and praising God for all the things that they had heard and seen, just as it was told them.
verses.Luke.2.21: When eight days were fulfilled for the circumcision of the child, his name was called Jesus, which was given by the angel before he was conceived in the womb.
verses.Luke.2.22: When the days of their purification according to the law of Moses were fulfilled, they brought him up to Jerusalem to present him to the Lord
verses.Luke.2.23: (as it is written in the law of the Lord, “Every male who opens the womb shall be called holy to the Lord”),
verses.Luke.2.24: and to offer a sacrifice according to that which is said in the law of the Lord, “A pair of turtledoves, or two young pigeons.”
verses.Luke.2.25: Behold, there was a man in Jerusalem whose name was Simeon. This man was righteous and devout, looking for the consolation of Israel, and the Holy Spirit was on him.
verses.Luke.2.26: It had been revealed to him by the Holy Spirit that he should not see death before he had seen the Lord’s Christ.
verses.Luke.2.27: He came in the Spirit into the temple. When the parents brought in the child, Jesus, that they might do concerning him according to the custom of the law,
verses.Luke.2.28: then he received him into his arms and blessed God, and said,
verses.Luke.2.29:
“Now you are releasing your servant, Master,
according to your word, in peace;
verses.Luke.2.30: for my eyes have seen your salvation,
verses.Luke.2.31: which you have prepared before the face of all peoples;
verses.Luke.2.32:
a light for revelation to the nations,
and the glory of your people Israel.”
verses.Luke.2.33: Joseph and his mother were marveling at the things which were spoken concerning him.
verses.Luke.2.34: Simeon blessed them, and said to Mary, his mother, “Behold, this child is appointed for the falling and the rising of many in Israel, and for a sign which is spoken against.
verses.Luke.2.35: Yes, a sword will pierce through your own soul, that the thoughts of many hearts may be revealed.”
verses.Luke.2.36: There was one Anna, a prophetess, the daughter of Phanuel, of the tribe of Asher (she was of a great age, having lived with a husband seven years from her virginity,
verses.Luke.2.37: and she had been a widow for about eighty-four years), who didn’t depart from the temple, worshiping with fastings and petitions night and day.
verses.Luke.2.38: Coming up at that very hour, she gave thanks to the Lord, and spoke of him to all those who were looking for redemption in Jerusalem.
verses.Luke.2.39: When they had accomplished all things that were according to the law of the Lord, they returned into Galilee, to their own city, Nazareth.
verses.Luke.2.40: The child was growing, and was becoming strong in spirit, being filled with wisdom, and the grace of God was upon him.
verses.Luke.2.41: His parents went every year to Jerusalem at the feast of the Passover.
verses.Luke.2.42: When he was twelve years old, they went up to Jerusalem according to the custom of the feast;
verses.Luke.2.43: and when they had fulfilled the days, as they were returning, the boy Jesus stayed behind in Jerusalem. Joseph and his mother didn’t know it,
verses.Luke.2.44: but supposing him to be in the company, they went a day’s journey; and they looked for him among their relatives and acquaintances.
verses.Luke.2.45: When they didn’t find him, they returned to Jerusalem, looking for him.
verses.Luke.2.46: After three days they found him in the temple, sitting in the middle of the teachers, both listening to them and asking them questions.
verses.Luke.2.47: All who heard him were amazed at his understanding and his answers.
verses.Luke.2.48: When they saw him, they were astonished; and his mother said to him, “Son, why have you treated us this way? Behold, your father and I were anxiously looking for you.”
verses.Luke.2.49: He said to them, “Why were you looking for me? Didn’t you know that I must be in my Father’s house?”
verses.Luke.2.50: They didn’t understand the saying which he spoke to them.
verses.Luke.2.51: And he went down with them and came to Nazareth. He was subject to them, and his mother kept all these sayings in her heart.
verses.Luke.2.52: And Jesus increased in wisdom and stature, and in favor with God and men.
verses.Mark.16.1: When the Sabbath was past, Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of James, and Salome bought spices, that they might come and anoint him.
verses.Mark.16.2: Very early on the first day of the week, they came to the tomb when the sun had risen.
verses.Mark.16.3: They were saying among themselves, “Who will roll away the stone from the door of the tomb for us?”
verses.Mark.16.4: for it was very big. Looking up, they saw that the stone was rolled back.
verses.Mark.16.5: Entering into the tomb, they saw a young man sitting on the right side, dressed in a white robe; and they were amazed.
verses.Mark.16.6: He said to them, “Don’t be amazed. You seek Jesus, the Nazarene, who has been crucified. He has risen! He is not here. See the place where they laid him!
verses.Mark.16.7: But go, tell his disciples and Peter, ‘He goes before you into Galilee. There you will see him, as he said to you.’”
verses.Mark.16.8: They went out, and fled from the tomb, for trembling and astonishment had come on them. They said nothing to anyone; for they were afraid.
verses.Mark.16.9: Now when he had risen early on the first day of the week, he appeared first to Mary Magdalene, from whom he had cast out seven demons.
verses.Mark.16.10: She went and told those who had been with him, as they mourned and wept.
verses.Mark.16.11: When they heard that he was alive and had been seen by her, they disbelieved.
verses.Mark.16.12: After these things he was revealed in another form to two of them as they walked, on their way into the country.
verses.Mark.16.13: They went away and told it to the rest. They didn’t believe them, either.
verses.Mark.16.14: Afterward he was revealed to the eleven themselves as they sat at the table; and he rebuked them for their unbelief and hardness of heart, because they didn’t believe those who had seen him after he had risen.
verses.Mark.16.15: He said to them, “Go into all the world and preach the Good News to the whole creation.
verses.Mark.16.16: He who believes and is baptized will be saved; but he who disbelieves will be condemned.
verses.Mark.16.17: These signs will accompany those who believe: in my name they will cast out demons; they will speak with new languages;
verses.Mark.16.18: they will take up serpents; and if they drink any deadly thing, it will in no way hurt them; they will lay hands on the sick, and they will recover.”
verses.Mark.16.19: So then the Lord, after he had spoken to them, was received up into heaven and sat down at the right hand of God.
verses.Mark.16.20: They went out and preached everywhere, the Lord working with them and confirming the word by the signs that followed. Amen.
verses.Luke.10.1: Now after these things, the Lord also appointed seventy others, and sent them two by two ahead of him into every city and place where he was about to come.
verses.Luke.10.2: Then he said to them, “The harvest is indeed plentiful, but the laborers are few. Pray therefore to the Lord of the harvest, that he may send out laborers into his harvest.
verses.Luke.10.3: Go your ways. Behold, I send you out as lambs among wolves.
verses.Luke.10.4: Carry no purse, nor wallet, nor sandals. Greet no one on the way.
verses.Luke.10.5: Into whatever house you enter, first say, ‘Peace be to this house.’
verses.Luke.10.6: If a son of peace is there, your peace will rest on him; but if not, it will return to you.
verses.Luke.10.7: Remain in that same house, eating and drinking the things they give, for the laborer is worthy of his wages. Don’t go from house to house.
verses.Luke.10.8: Into whatever city you enter and they receive you, eat the things that are set before you.
verses.Luke.10.9: Heal the sick who are there and tell them, ‘God’s Kingdom has come near to you.’
verses.Luke.10.10: But into whatever city you enter and they don’t receive you, go out into its streets and say,
verses.Luke.10.11: ‘Even the dust from your city that clings to us, we wipe off against you. Nevertheless know this, that God’s Kingdom has come near to you.’
verses.Luke.10.12: I tell you, it will be more tolerable in that day for Sodom than for that city.
verses.Luke.10.13: “Woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida! For if the mighty works had been done in Tyre and Sidon which were done in you, they would have repented long ago, sitting in sackcloth and ashes.
verses.Luke.10.14: But it will be more tolerable for Tyre and Sidon in the judgment than for you.
verses.Luke.10.15: You, Capernaum, who are exalted to heaven, will be brought down to Hades.
verses.Luke.10.16: Whoever listens to you listens to me, and whoever rejects you rejects me. Whoever rejects me rejects him who sent me.”
verses.Luke.10.17: The seventy returned with joy, saying, “Lord, even the demons are subject to us in your name!”
verses.Luke.10.18: He said to them, “I saw Satan having fallen like lightning from heaven.
verses.Luke.10.19: Behold, I give you authority to tread on serpents and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy. Nothing will in any way hurt you.
verses.Luke.10.20: Nevertheless, don’t rejoice in this, that the spirits are subject to you, but rejoice that your names are written in heaven.”
verses.Luke.10.21: In that same hour, Jesus rejoiced in the Holy Spirit, and said, “I thank you, O Father, Lord of heaven and earth, that you have hidden these things from the wise and understanding, and revealed them to little children. Yes, Father, for so it was well-pleasing in your sight.”
verses.Luke.10.22: Turning to the disciples, he said, “All things have been delivered to me by my Father. No one knows who the Son is, except the Father, and who the Father is, except the Son, and he to whomever the Son desires to reveal him.”
verses.Luke.10.23: Turning to the disciples, he said privately, “Blessed are the eyes which see the things that you see,
verses.Luke.10.24: for I tell you that many prophets and kings desired to see the things which you see, and didn’t see them, and to hear the things which you hear, and didn’t hear them.”
verses.Luke.10.25: Behold, a certain lawyer stood up and tested him, saying, “Teacher, what shall I do to inherit eternal life?”
verses.Luke.10.26: He said to him, “What is written in the law? How do you read it?”
verses.Luke.10.27: He answered, “You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, with all your strength, and with all your mind; and your neighbor as yourself.”
verses.Luke.10.28: He said to him, “You have answered correctly. Do this, and you will live.”
verses.Luke.10.29: But he, desiring to justify himself, asked Jesus, “Who is my neighbor?”
verses.Luke.10.30: Jesus answered, “A certain man was going down from Jerusalem to Jericho, and he fell among robbers, who both stripped him and beat him, and departed, leaving him half dead.
verses.Luke.10.31: By chance a certain priest was going down that way. When he saw him, he passed by on the other side.
verses.Luke.10.32: In the same way a Levite also, when he came to the place and saw him, passed by on the other side.
verses.Luke.10.33: But a certain Samaritan, as he traveled, came where he was. When he saw him, he was moved with compassion,
verses.Luke.10.34: came to him, and bound up his wounds, pouring on oil and wine. He set him on his own animal, brought him to an inn, and took care of him.
verses.Luke.10.35: On the next day, when he departed, he took out two denarii, gave them to the host, and said to him, ‘Take care of him. Whatever you spend beyond that, I will repay you when I return.’
verses.Luke.10.36: Now which of these three do you think seemed to be a neighbor to him who fell among the robbers?”
verses.Luke.10.37: He said, “He who showed mercy on him.” Then Jesus said to him, “Go and do likewise.”
verses.Luke.10.38: As they went on their way, he entered into a certain village, and a certain woman named Martha received him into her house.
verses.Luke.10.39: She had a sister called Mary, who also sat at Jesus’ feet and heard his word.
verses.Luke.10.40: But Martha was distracted with much serving, and she came up to him, and said, “Lord, don’t you care that my sister left me to serve alone? Ask her therefore to help me.”
verses.Luke.10.41: Jesus answered her, “Martha, Martha, you are anxious and troubled about many things,
verses.Luke.10.42: but one thing is needed. Mary has chosen the good part, which will not be taken away from her.”
verses.Luke.16.1: He also said to his disciples, “There was a certain rich man who had a manager. An accusation was made to him that this man was wasting his possessions.
verses.Luke.16.2: He called him, and said to him, ‘What is this that I hear about you? Give an accounting of your management, for you can no longer be manager.’
verses.Luke.16.3: “The manager said within himself, ‘What will I do, seeing that my lord is taking away the management position from me? I don’t have strength to dig. I am ashamed to beg.
verses.Luke.16.4: I know what I will do, so that when I am removed from management, they may receive me into their houses.’
verses.Luke.16.5: Calling each one of his lord’s debtors to him, he said to the first, ‘How much do you owe to my lord?’
verses.Luke.16.6: He said, ‘A hundred batos of oil.’ He said to him, ‘Take your bill, and sit down quickly and write fifty.’
verses.Luke.16.7: Then he said to another, ‘How much do you owe?’ He said, ‘A hundred cors of wheat.’ He said to him, ‘Take your bill, and write eighty.’
verses.Luke.16.8: “His lord commended the dishonest manager because he had done wisely, for the children of this world are, in their own generation, wiser than the children of the light.
verses.Luke.16.9: I tell you, make for yourselves friends by means of unrighteous mammon, so that when you fail, they may receive you into the eternal tents.
verses.Luke.16.10: He who is faithful in a very little is faithful also in much. He who is dishonest in a very little is also dishonest in much.
verses.Luke.16.11: If therefore you have not been faithful in the unrighteous mammon, who will commit to your trust the true riches?
verses.Luke.16.12: If you have not been faithful in that which is another’s, who will give you that which is your own?
verses.Luke.16.13: No servant can serve two masters, for either he will hate the one and love the other; or else he will hold to one and despise the other. You aren’t able to serve God and Mammon.”
verses.Luke.16.14: The Pharisees, who were lovers of money, also heard all these things, and they scoffed at him.
verses.Luke.16.15: He said to them, “You are those who justify yourselves in the sight of men, but God knows your hearts. For that which is exalted among men is an abomination in the sight of God.
verses.Luke.16.16: “The law and the prophets were until John. From that time the Good News of God’s Kingdom is preached, and everyone is forcing his way into it.
verses.Luke.16.17: But it is easier for heaven and earth to pass away than for one tiny stroke of a pen in the law to fall.
verses.Luke.16.18: “Everyone who divorces his wife and marries another commits adultery. He who marries one who is divorced from a husband commits adultery.
verses.Luke.16.19: “Now there was a certain rich man, and he was clothed in purple and fine linen, living in luxury every day.
verses.Luke.16.20: A certain beggar, named Lazarus, was taken to his gate, full of sores,
verses.Luke.16.21: and desiring to be fed with the crumbs that fell from the rich man’s table. Yes, even the dogs came and licked his sores.
verses.Luke.16.22: The beggar died, and he was carried away by the angels to Abraham’s bosom. The rich man also died and was buried.
verses.Luke.16.23: In Hades, he lifted up his eyes, being in torment, and saw Abraham far off, and Lazarus at his bosom.
verses.Luke.16.24: He cried and said, ‘Father Abraham, have mercy on me, and send Lazarus, that he may dip the tip of his finger in water and cool my tongue! For I am in anguish in this flame.’
verses.Luke.16.25: “But Abraham said, ‘Son, remember that you, in your lifetime, received your good things, and Lazarus, in the same way, bad things. But here he is now comforted and you are in anguish.
verses.Luke.16.26: Besides all this, between us and you there is a great gulf fixed, that those who want to pass from here to you are not able, and that no one may cross over from there to us.’
verses.Luke.16.27: “He said, ‘I ask you therefore, father, that you would send him to my father’s house—
verses.Luke.16.28: for I have five brothers—that he may testify to them, so they won’t also come into this place of torment.’
verses.Luke.16.29: “But Abraham said to him, ‘They have Moses and the prophets. Let them listen to them.’
verses.Luke.16.30: “He said, ‘No, father Abraham, but if one goes to them from the dead, they will repent.’
verses.Luke.16.31: “He said to him, ‘If they don’t listen to Moses and the prophets, neither will they be persuaded if one rises from the dead.’”
verses.Luke.11.1: When he finished praying in a certain place, one of his disciples said to him, “Lord, teach us to pray, just as John also taught his disciples.”
verses.Luke.11.2:
He said to them, “When you pray, say,
‘Our Father in heaven,
may your name be kept holy.
May your Kingdom come.
May your will be done on earth, as it is in heaven.
verses.Luke.11.3: Give us day by day our daily bread.
verses.Luke.11.4:
Forgive us our sins,
for we ourselves also forgive everyone who is indebted to us.
Bring us not into temptation,
but deliver us from the evil one.’”
verses.Luke.11.5: He said to them, “Which of you, if you go to a friend at midnight and tell him, ‘Friend, lend me three loaves of bread,
verses.Luke.11.6: for a friend of mine has come to me from a journey, and I have nothing to set before him,’
verses.Luke.11.7: and he from within will answer and say, ‘Don’t bother me. The door is now shut, and my children are with me in bed. I can’t get up and give it to you’?
verses.Luke.11.8: I tell you, although he will not rise and give it to him because he is his friend, yet because of his persistence, he will get up and give him as many as he needs.
verses.Luke.11.9: “I tell you, keep asking, and it will be given you. Keep seeking, and you will find. Keep knocking, and it will be opened to you.
verses.Luke.11.10: For everyone who asks receives. He who seeks finds. To him who knocks it will be opened.
verses.Luke.11.11: “Which of you fathers, if your son asks for bread, will give him a stone? Or if he asks for a fish, he won’t give him a snake instead of a fish, will he?
verses.Luke.11.12: Or if he asks for an egg, he won’t give him a scorpion, will he?
verses.Luke.11.13: If you then, being evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your heavenly Father give the Holy Spirit to those who ask him?”
verses.Luke.11.14: He was casting out a demon, and it was mute. When the demon had gone out, the mute man spoke; and the multitudes marveled.
verses.Luke.11.15: But some of them said, “He casts out demons by Beelzebul, the prince of the demons.”
verses.Luke.11.16: Others, testing him, sought from him a sign from heaven.
verses.Luke.11.17: But he, knowing their thoughts, said to them, “Every kingdom divided against itself is brought to desolation. A house divided against itself falls.
verses.Luke.11.18: If Satan also is divided against himself, how will his kingdom stand? For you say that I cast out demons by Beelzebul.
verses.Luke.11.19: But if I cast out demons by Beelzebul, by whom do your children cast them out? Therefore they will be your judges.
verses.Luke.11.20: But if I by God’s finger cast out demons, then God’s Kingdom has come to you.
verses.Luke.11.21: “When the strong man, fully armed, guards his own dwelling, his goods are safe.
verses.Luke.11.22: But when someone stronger attacks him and overcomes him, he takes from him his whole armor in which he trusted, and divides his plunder.
verses.Luke.11.23: “He who is not with me is against me. He who doesn’t gather with me scatters.
verses.Luke.11.24: The unclean spirit, when he has gone out of the man, passes through dry places, seeking rest; and finding none, he says, ‘I will turn back to my house from which I came out.’
verses.Luke.11.25: When he returns, he finds it swept and put in order.
verses.Luke.11.26: Then he goes and takes seven other spirits more evil than himself, and they enter in and dwell there. The last state of that man becomes worse than the first.”
verses.Luke.11.27: It came to pass, as he said these things, a certain woman out of the multitude lifted up her voice and said to him, “Blessed is the womb that bore you, and the breasts which nursed you!”
verses.Luke.11.28: But he said, “On the contrary, blessed are those who hear the word of God, and keep it.”
verses.Luke.11.29: When the multitudes were gathering together to him, he began to say, “This is an evil generation. It seeks after a sign. No sign will be given to it but the sign of Jonah the prophet.
verses.Luke.11.30: For even as Jonah became a sign to the Ninevites, so the Son of Man will also be to this generation.
verses.Luke.11.31: The Queen of the South will rise up in the judgment with the men of this generation and will condemn them, for she came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon; and behold, one greater than Solomon is here.
verses.Luke.11.32: The men of Nineveh will stand up in the judgment with this generation, and will condemn it, for they repented at the preaching of Jonah; and behold, one greater than Jonah is here.
verses.Luke.11.33: “No one, when he has lit a lamp, puts it in a cellar or under a basket, but on a stand, that those who come in may see the light.
verses.Luke.11.34: The lamp of the body is the eye. Therefore when your eye is good, your whole body is also full of light; but when it is evil, your body also is full of darkness.
verses.Luke.11.35: Therefore see whether the light that is in you isn’t darkness.
verses.Luke.11.36: If therefore your whole body is full of light, having no part dark, it will be wholly full of light, as when the lamp with its bright shining gives you light.”
verses.Luke.11.37: Now as he spoke, a certain Pharisee asked him to dine with him. He went in and sat at the table.
verses.Luke.11.38: When the Pharisee saw it, he marveled that he had not first washed himself before dinner.
verses.Luke.11.39: The Lord said to him, “Now you Pharisees cleanse the outside of the cup and of the platter, but your inward part is full of extortion and wickedness.
verses.Luke.11.40: You foolish ones, didn’t he who made the outside make the inside also?
verses.Luke.11.41: But give for gifts to the needy those things which are within, and behold, all things will be clean to you.
verses.Luke.11.42: But woe to you Pharisees! For you tithe mint and rue and every herb, but you bypass justice and God’s love. You ought to have done these, and not to have left the other undone.
verses.Luke.11.43: Woe to you Pharisees! For you love the best seats in the synagogues and the greetings in the marketplaces.
verses.Luke.11.44: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you are like hidden graves, and the men who walk over them don’t know it.”
verses.Luke.11.45: One of the lawyers answered him, “Teacher, in saying this you insult us also.”
verses.Luke.11.46: He said, “Woe to you lawyers also! For you load men with burdens that are difficult to carry, and you yourselves won’t even lift one finger to help carry those burdens.
verses.Luke.11.47: Woe to you! For you build the tombs of the prophets, and your fathers killed them.
verses.Luke.11.48: So you testify and consent to the works of your fathers. For they killed them, and you build their tombs.
verses.Luke.11.49: Therefore also the wisdom of God said, ‘I will send to them prophets and apostles; and some of them they will kill and persecute,
verses.Luke.11.50: that the blood of all the prophets, which was shed from the foundation of the world, may be required of this generation,
verses.Luke.11.51: from the blood of Abel to the blood of Zachariah, who perished between the altar and the sanctuary.’ Yes, I tell you, it will be required of this generation.
verses.Luke.11.52: Woe to you lawyers! For you took away the key of knowledge. You didn’t enter in yourselves, and those who were entering in, you hindered.”
verses.Luke.11.53: As he said these things to them, the scribes and the Pharisees began to be terribly angry, and to draw many things out of him,
verses.Luke.11.54: lying in wait for him, and seeking to catch him in something he might say, that they might accuse him.
verses.Luke.15.1: Now all the tax collectors and sinners were coming close to him to hear him.
verses.Luke.15.2: The Pharisees and the scribes murmured, saying, “This man welcomes sinners, and eats with them.”
verses.Luke.15.4: “Which of you men, if you had one hundred sheep and lost one of them, wouldn’t leave the ninety-nine in the wilderness and go after the one that was lost, until he found it?
verses.Luke.15.5: When he has found it, he carries it on his shoulders, rejoicing.
verses.Luke.15.6: When he comes home, he calls together his friends and his neighbors, saying to them, ‘Rejoice with me, for I have found my sheep which was lost!’
verses.Luke.15.7: I tell you that even so there will be more joy in heaven over one sinner who repents, than over ninety-nine righteous people who need no repentance.
verses.Luke.15.8: “Or what woman, if she had ten drachma coins, if she lost one drachma coin, wouldn’t light a lamp, sweep the house, and seek diligently until she found it?
verses.Luke.15.9: When she has found it, she calls together her friends and neighbors, saying, ‘Rejoice with me, for I have found the drachma which I had lost!’
verses.Luke.15.10: Even so, I tell you, there is joy in the presence of the angels of God over one sinner repenting.”
verses.Luke.15.11: He said, “A certain man had two sons.
verses.Luke.15.12: The younger of them said to his father, ‘Father, give me my share of your property.’ So he divided his livelihood between them.
verses.Luke.15.13: Not many days after, the younger son gathered all of this together and traveled into a far country. There he wasted his property with riotous living.
verses.Luke.15.14: When he had spent all of it, there arose a severe famine in that country, and he began to be in need.
verses.Luke.15.15: He went and joined himself to one of the citizens of that country, and he sent him into his fields to feed pigs.
verses.Luke.15.16: He wanted to fill his belly with the pods that the pigs ate, but no one gave him any.
verses.Luke.15.17: But when he came to himself, he said, ‘How many hired servants of my father’s have bread enough to spare, and I’m dying with hunger!
verses.Luke.15.18: I will get up and go to my father, and will tell him, “Father, I have sinned against heaven and in your sight.
verses.Luke.15.19: I am no more worthy to be called your son. Make me as one of your hired servants.”’
verses.Luke.15.20: “He arose and came to his father. But while he was still far off, his father saw him and was moved with compassion, and ran, fell on his neck, and kissed him.
verses.Luke.15.21: The son said to him, ‘Father, I have sinned against heaven and in your sight. I am no longer worthy to be called your son.’
verses.Luke.15.22: “But the father said to his servants, ‘Bring out the best robe and put it on him. Put a ring on his hand and sandals on his feet.
verses.Luke.15.23: Bring the fattened calf, kill it, and let’s eat and celebrate;
verses.Luke.15.24: for this, my son, was dead and is alive again. He was lost and is found.’ Then they began to celebrate.
verses.Luke.15.25: “Now his elder son was in the field. As he came near to the house, he heard music and dancing.
verses.Luke.15.26: He called one of the servants to him and asked what was going on.
verses.Luke.15.27: He said to him, ‘Your brother has come, and your father has killed the fattened calf, because he has received him back safe and healthy.’
verses.Luke.15.28: But he was angry and would not go in. Therefore his father came out and begged him.
verses.Luke.15.29: But he answered his father, ‘Behold, these many years I have served you, and I never disobeyed a commandment of yours, but you never gave me a goat, that I might celebrate with my friends.
verses.Luke.15.30: But when this your son came, who has devoured your living with prostitutes, you killed the fattened calf for him.’
verses.Luke.15.31: “He said to him, ‘Son, you are always with me, and all that is mine is yours.
verses.Luke.15.32: But it was appropriate to celebrate and be glad, for this, your brother, was dead, and is alive again. He was lost, and is found.’”
verses.Luke.9.1: He called the twelve together and gave them power and authority over all demons, and to cure diseases.
verses.Luke.9.2: He sent them out to preach God’s Kingdom and to heal the sick.
verses.Luke.9.3: He said to them, “Take nothing for your journey—no staffs, nor wallet, nor bread, nor money. Don’t have two tunics each.
verses.Luke.9.4: Into whatever house you enter, stay there, and depart from there.
verses.Luke.9.5: As many as don’t receive you, when you depart from that city, shake off even the dust from your feet for a testimony against them.”
verses.Luke.9.6: They departed and went throughout the villages, preaching the Good News and healing everywhere.
verses.Luke.9.7: Now Herod the tetrarch heard of all that was done by him; and he was very perplexed, because it was said by some that John had risen from the dead,
verses.Luke.9.8: and by some that Elijah had appeared, and by others that one of the old prophets had risen again.
verses.Luke.9.9: Herod said, “I beheaded John, but who is this about whom I hear such things?” He sought to see him.
verses.Luke.9.10: The apostles, when they had returned, told him what things they had done. He took them and withdrew apart to a desert region of a city called Bethsaida.
verses.Luke.9.11: But the multitudes, perceiving it, followed him. He welcomed them, spoke to them of God’s Kingdom, and he cured those who needed healing.
verses.Luke.9.12: The day began to wear away; and the twelve came and said to him, “Send the multitude away, that they may go into the surrounding villages and farms and lodge and get food, for we are here in a deserted place.”
verses.Luke.9.13: But he said to them, “You give them something to eat.” They said, “We have no more than five loaves and two fish, unless we should go and buy food for all these people.”
verses.Luke.9.14: For they were about five thousand men. He said to his disciples, “Make them sit down in groups of about fifty each.”
verses.Luke.9.15: They did so, and made them all sit down.
verses.Luke.9.16: He took the five loaves and the two fish, and looking up to the sky, he blessed them, broke them, and gave them to the disciples to set before the multitude.
verses.Luke.9.17: They ate and were all filled. They gathered up twelve baskets of broken pieces that were left over.
verses.Luke.9.18: As he was praying alone, the disciples were near him, and he asked them, “Who do the multitudes say that I am?”
verses.Luke.9.19: They answered, “‘John the Baptizer,’ but others say, ‘Elijah,’ and others, that one of the old prophets has risen again.”
verses.Luke.9.20: He said to them, “But who do you say that I am?” Peter answered, “The Christ of God.”
verses.Luke.9.21: But he warned them and commanded them to tell this to no one,
verses.Luke.9.22: saying, “The Son of Man must suffer many things, and be rejected by the elders, chief priests, and scribes, and be killed, and the third day be raised up.”
verses.Luke.9.23: He said to all, “If anyone desires to come after me, let him deny himself, take up his cross, and follow me.
verses.Luke.9.24: For whoever desires to save his life will lose it, but whoever will lose his life for my sake will save it.
verses.Luke.9.25: For what does it profit a man if he gains the whole world, and loses or forfeits his own self?
verses.Luke.9.26: For whoever will be ashamed of me and of my words, of him will the Son of Man be ashamed when he comes in his glory, and the glory of the Father, and of the holy angels.
verses.Luke.9.27: But I tell you the truth: There are some of those who stand here who will in no way taste of death until they see God’s Kingdom.”
verses.Luke.9.28: About eight days after these sayings, he took with him Peter, John, and James, and went up onto the mountain to pray.
verses.Luke.9.29: As he was praying, the appearance of his face was altered, and his clothing became white and dazzling.
verses.Luke.9.30: Behold, two men were talking with him, who were Moses and Elijah,
verses.Luke.9.31: who appeared in glory and spoke of his departure, which he was about to accomplish at Jerusalem.
verses.Luke.9.32: Now Peter and those who were with him were heavy with sleep, but when they were fully awake, they saw his glory, and the two men who stood with him.
verses.Luke.9.33: As they were parting from him, Peter said to Jesus, “Master, it is good for us to be here. Let’s make three tents: one for you, one for Moses, and one for Elijah,” not knowing what he said.
verses.Luke.9.34: While he said these things, a cloud came and overshadowed them, and they were afraid as they entered into the cloud.
verses.Luke.9.35: A voice came out of the cloud, saying, “This is my beloved Son. Listen to him!”
verses.Luke.9.36: When the voice came, Jesus was found alone. They were silent, and told no one in those days any of the things which they had seen.
verses.Luke.9.37: On the next day, when they had come down from the mountain, a great multitude met him.
verses.Luke.9.38: Behold, a man from the crowd called out, saying, “Teacher, I beg you to look at my son, for he is my only born child.
verses.Luke.9.39: Behold, a spirit takes him, he suddenly cries out, and it convulses him so that he foams; and it hardly departs from him, bruising him severely.
verses.Luke.9.40: I begged your disciples to cast it out, and they couldn’t.”
verses.Luke.9.41: Jesus answered, “Faithless and perverse generation, how long shall I be with you and bear with you? Bring your son here.”
verses.Luke.9.42: While he was still coming, the demon threw him down and convulsed him violently. But Jesus rebuked the unclean spirit, healed the boy, and gave him back to his father.
verses.Luke.9.43: They were all astonished at the majesty of God. But while all were marveling at all the things which Jesus did, he said to his disciples,
verses.Luke.9.44: “Let these words sink into your ears, for the Son of Man will be delivered up into the hands of men.”
verses.Luke.9.45: But they didn’t understand this saying. It was concealed from them, that they should not perceive it, and they were afraid to ask him about this saying.
verses.Luke.9.46: An argument arose among them about which of them was the greatest.
verses.Luke.9.47: Jesus, perceiving the reasoning of their hearts, took a little child, and set him by his side,
verses.Luke.9.48: and said to them, “Whoever receives this little child in my name receives me. Whoever receives me receives him who sent me. For whoever is least among you all, this one will be great.”
verses.Luke.9.49: John answered, “Master, we saw someone casting out demons in your name, and we forbade him, because he doesn’t follow with us.”
verses.Luke.9.50: Jesus said to him, “Don’t forbid him, for he who is not against us is for us.”
verses.Luke.9.51: It came to pass, when the days were near that he should be taken up, he intently set his face to go to Jerusalem
verses.Luke.9.52: and sent messengers before his face. They went and entered into a village of the Samaritans, so as to prepare for him.
verses.Luke.9.53: They didn’t receive him, because he was traveling with his face set toward Jerusalem.
verses.Luke.9.54: When his disciples, James and John, saw this, they said, “Lord, do you want us to command fire to come down from the sky and destroy them, just as Elijah did?”
verses.Luke.9.55: But he turned and rebuked them, “You don’t know of what kind of spirit you are.
verses.Luke.9.56: For the Son of Man didn’t come to destroy men’s lives, but to save them.” They went to another village.
verses.Luke.9.57: As they went on the way, a certain man said to him, “I want to follow you wherever you go, Lord.”
verses.Luke.9.58: Jesus said to him, “The foxes have holes and the birds of the sky have nests, but the Son of Man has no place to lay his head.”
verses.Luke.9.59: He said to another, “Follow me!” But he said, “Lord, allow me first to go and bury my father.”
verses.Luke.9.60: But Jesus said to him, “Leave the dead to bury their own dead, but you go and announce God’s Kingdom.”
verses.Luke.9.61: Another also said, “I want to follow you, Lord, but first allow me to say good-bye to those who are at my house.”
verses.Luke.9.62: But Jesus said to him, “No one, having put his hand to the plow and looking back, is fit for God’s Kingdom.”
verses.Luke.14.1: When he went into the house of one of the rulers of the Pharisees on a Sabbath to eat bread, they were watching him.
verses.Luke.14.2: Behold, a certain man who had dropsy was in front of him.
verses.Luke.14.3: Jesus, answering, spoke to the lawyers and Pharisees, saying, “Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath?”
verses.Luke.14.4: But they were silent. He took him, and healed him, and let him go.
verses.Luke.14.5: He answered them, “Which of you, if your son or an ox fell into a well, wouldn’t immediately pull him out on a Sabbath day?”
verses.Luke.14.6: They couldn’t answer him regarding these things.
verses.Luke.14.7: He spoke a parable to those who were invited, when he noticed how they chose the best seats, and said to them,
verses.Luke.14.8: “When you are invited by anyone to a wedding feast, don’t sit in the best seat, since perhaps someone more honorable than you might be invited by him,
verses.Luke.14.9: and he who invited both of you would come and tell you, ‘Make room for this person.’ Then you would begin, with shame, to take the lowest place.
verses.Luke.14.10: But when you are invited, go and sit in the lowest place, so that when he who invited you comes, he may tell you, ‘Friend, move up higher.’ Then you will be honored in the presence of all who sit at the table with you.
verses.Luke.14.11: For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted.”
verses.Luke.14.12: He also said to the one who had invited him, “When you make a dinner or a supper, don’t call your friends, nor your brothers, nor your kinsmen, nor rich neighbors, or perhaps they might also return the favor, and pay you back.
verses.Luke.14.13: But when you make a feast, ask the poor, the maimed, the lame, or the blind;
verses.Luke.14.14: and you will be blessed, because they don’t have the resources to repay you. For you will be repaid in the resurrection of the righteous.”
verses.Luke.14.15: When one of those who sat at the table with him heard these things, he said to him, “Blessed is he who will feast in God’s Kingdom!”
verses.Luke.14.16: But he said to him, “A certain man made a great supper, and he invited many people.
verses.Luke.14.17: He sent out his servant at supper time to tell those who were invited, ‘Come, for everything is ready now.’
verses.Luke.14.18: They all as one began to make excuses. “The first said to him, ‘I have bought a field, and I must go and see it. Please have me excused.’
verses.Luke.14.19: “Another said, ‘I have bought five yoke of oxen, and I must go try them out. Please have me excused.’
verses.Luke.14.20: “Another said, ‘I have married a wife, and therefore I can’t come.’
verses.Luke.14.21: “That servant came, and told his lord these things. Then the master of the house, being angry, said to his servant, ‘Go out quickly into the streets and lanes of the city, and bring in the poor, maimed, blind, and lame.’
verses.Luke.14.22: “The servant said, ‘Lord, it is done as you commanded, and there is still room.’
verses.Luke.14.23: “The lord said to the servant, ‘Go out into the highways and hedges, and compel them to come in, that my house may be filled.
verses.Luke.14.24: For I tell you that none of those men who were invited will taste of my supper. For many are called, but few are chosen.’”
verses.Luke.14.25: Now great multitudes were going with him. He turned and said to them,
verses.Luke.14.26: “If anyone comes to me, and doesn’t disregard his own father, mother, wife, children, brothers, and sisters, yes, and his own life also, he can’t be my disciple.
verses.Luke.14.27: Whoever doesn’t bear his own cross and come after me, can’t be my disciple.
verses.Luke.14.28: For which of you, desiring to build a tower, doesn’t first sit down and count the cost, to see if he has enough to complete it?
verses.Luke.14.29: Or perhaps, when he has laid a foundation and isn’t able to finish, everyone who sees begins to mock him,
verses.Luke.14.30: saying, ‘This man began to build and wasn’t able to finish.’
verses.Luke.14.31: Or what king, as he goes to encounter another king in war, will not sit down first and consider whether he is able with ten thousand to meet him who comes against him with twenty thousand?
verses.Luke.14.32: Or else, while the other is yet a great way off, he sends an envoy and asks for conditions of peace.
verses.Luke.14.33: So therefore, whoever of you who doesn’t renounce all that he has, he can’t be my disciple.
verses.Luke.14.34: “Salt is good, but if the salt becomes flat and tasteless, with what do you season it?
verses.Luke.14.35: It is fit neither for the soil nor for the manure pile. It is thrown out. He who has ears to hear, let him hear.”
verses.Luke.8.1: Soon afterwards, he went about through cities and villages, preaching and bringing the good news of God’s Kingdom. With him were the twelve,
verses.Luke.8.2: and certain women who had been healed of evil spirits and infirmities: Mary who was called Magdalene, from whom seven demons had gone out;
verses.Luke.8.3: and Joanna, the wife of Chuzas, Herod’s steward; Susanna; and many others who served them from their possessions.
verses.Luke.8.4: When a great multitude came together and people from every city were coming to him, he spoke by a parable:
verses.Luke.8.5: “The farmer went out to sow his seed. As he sowed, some fell along the road, and it was trampled under foot, and the birds of the sky devoured it.
verses.Luke.8.6: Some seed fell on the rock, and as soon as it grew, it withered away, because it had no moisture.
verses.Luke.8.7: Some fell amid the thorns, and the thorns grew with it and choked it.
verses.Luke.8.8: Some fell into the good ground and grew and produced one hundred times as much fruit.” As he said these things, he called out, “He who has ears to hear, let him hear!”
verses.Luke.8.9: Then his disciples asked him, “What does this parable mean?”
verses.Luke.8.10: He said, “To you it is given to know the mysteries of God’s Kingdom, but to the rest it is given in parables, that ‘seeing they may not see, and hearing they may not understand.’
verses.Luke.8.11: “Now the parable is this: The seed is the word of God.
verses.Luke.8.12: Those along the road are those who hear; then the devil comes and takes away the word from their heart, that they may not believe and be saved.
verses.Luke.8.13: Those on the rock are they who, when they hear, receive the word with joy; but these have no root. They believe for a while, then fall away in time of temptation.
verses.Luke.8.14: What fell among the thorns, these are those who have heard, and as they go on their way they are choked with cares, riches, and pleasures of life; and they bring no fruit to maturity.
verses.Luke.8.15: Those in the good ground, these are those who with an honest and good heart, having heard the word, hold it tightly, and produce fruit with perseverance.
verses.Luke.8.16: “No one, when he has lit a lamp, covers it with a container or puts it under a bed; but puts it on a stand, that those who enter in may see the light.
verses.Luke.8.17: For nothing is hidden that will not be revealed, nor anything secret that will not be known and come to light.
verses.Luke.8.18: Be careful therefore how you hear. For whoever has, to him will be given; and whoever doesn’t have, from him will be taken away even that which he thinks he has.”
verses.Luke.8.19: His mother and brothers came to him, and they could not come near him for the crowd.
verses.Luke.8.20: Some people told him, “Your mother and your brothers stand outside, desiring to see you.”
verses.Luke.8.21: But he answered them, “My mother and my brothers are these who hear the word of God and do it.”
verses.Luke.8.22: Now on one of those days, he entered into a boat, himself and his disciples, and he said to them, “Let’s go over to the other side of the lake.” So they launched out.
verses.Luke.8.23: But as they sailed, he fell asleep. A wind storm came down on the lake, and they were taking on dangerous amounts of water.
verses.Luke.8.24: They came to him and awoke him, saying, “Master, Master, we are dying!” He awoke and rebuked the wind and the raging of the water; then they ceased, and it was calm.
verses.Luke.8.25: He said to them, “Where is your faith?” Being afraid, they marveled, saying to one another, “Who is this then, that he commands even the winds and the water, and they obey him?”
verses.Luke.8.26: Then they arrived at the country of the Gadarenes, which is opposite Galilee.
verses.Luke.8.27: When Jesus stepped ashore, a certain man out of the city who had demons for a long time met him. He wore no clothes, and didn’t live in a house, but in the tombs.
verses.Luke.8.28: When he saw Jesus, he cried out and fell down before him, and with a loud voice said, “What do I have to do with you, Jesus, you Son of the Most High God? I beg you, don’t torment me!”
verses.Luke.8.29: For Jesus was commanding the unclean spirit to come out of the man. For the unclean spirit had often seized the man. He was kept under guard and bound with chains and fetters. Breaking the bonds apart, he was driven by the demon into the desert.
verses.Luke.8.30: Jesus asked him, “What is your name?” He said, “Legion,” for many demons had entered into him.
verses.Luke.8.31: They begged him that he would not command them to go into the abyss.
verses.Luke.8.32: Now there was there a herd of many pigs feeding on the mountain, and they begged him that he would allow them to enter into those. Then he allowed them.
verses.Luke.8.33: The demons came out of the man and entered into the pigs, and the herd rushed down the steep bank into the lake and were drowned.
verses.Luke.8.34: When those who fed them saw what had happened, they fled and told it in the city and in the country.
verses.Luke.8.35: People went out to see what had happened. They came to Jesus and found the man from whom the demons had gone out, sitting at Jesus’ feet, clothed and in his right mind; and they were afraid.
verses.Luke.8.36: Those who saw it told them how he who had been possessed by demons was healed.
verses.Luke.8.37: All the people of the surrounding country of the Gadarenes asked him to depart from them, for they were very much afraid. Then he entered into the boat and returned.
verses.Luke.8.38: But the man from whom the demons had gone out begged him that he might go with him, but Jesus sent him away, saying,
verses.Luke.8.39: “Return to your house, and declare what great things God has done for you.” He went his way, proclaiming throughout the whole city what great things Jesus had done for him.
verses.Luke.8.40: When Jesus returned, the multitude welcomed him, for they were all waiting for him.
verses.Luke.8.41: Behold, a man named Jairus came. He was a ruler of the synagogue. He fell down at Jesus’ feet and begged him to come into his house,
verses.Luke.8.42: for he had an only born daughter, about twelve years of age, and she was dying. But as he went, the multitudes pressed against him.
verses.Luke.8.43: A woman who had a flow of blood for twelve years, who had spent all her living on physicians and could not be healed by any,
verses.Luke.8.44: came behind him and touched the fringe of his cloak. Immediately the flow of her blood stopped.
verses.Luke.8.45: Jesus said, “Who touched me?” When all denied it, Peter and those with him said, “Master, the multitudes press and jostle you, and you say, ‘Who touched me?’”
verses.Luke.8.46: But Jesus said, “Someone did touch me, for I perceived that power has gone out of me.”
verses.Luke.8.47: When the woman saw that she was not hidden, she came trembling; and falling down before him declared to him in the presence of all the people the reason why she had touched him, and how she was healed immediately.
verses.Luke.8.48: He said to her, “Daughter, cheer up. Your faith has made you well. Go in peace.”
verses.Luke.8.49: While he still spoke, one from the ruler of the synagogue’s house came, saying to him, “Your daughter is dead. Don’t trouble the Teacher.”
verses.Luke.8.50: But Jesus hearing it, answered him, “Don’t be afraid. Only believe, and she will be healed.”
verses.Luke.8.51: When he came to the house, he didn’t allow anyone to enter in, except Peter, John, James, the father of the child, and her mother.
verses.Luke.8.52: All were weeping and mourning her, but he said, “Don’t weep. She isn’t dead, but sleeping.”
verses.Luke.8.53: They were ridiculing him, knowing that she was dead.
verses.Luke.8.54: But he put them all outside, and taking her by the hand, he called, saying, “Child, arise!”
verses.Luke.8.55: Her spirit returned, and she rose up immediately. He commanded that something be given to her to eat.
verses.Luke.8.56: Her parents were amazed, but he commanded them to tell no one what had been done.
verses.Luke.7.1: After he had finished speaking in the hearing of the people, he entered into Capernaum.
verses.Luke.7.2: A certain centurion’s servant, who was dear to him, was sick and at the point of death.
verses.Luke.7.3: When he heard about Jesus, he sent to him elders of the Jews, asking him to come and save his servant.
verses.Luke.7.4: When they came to Jesus, they begged him earnestly, saying, “He is worthy for you to do this for him,
verses.Luke.7.5: for he loves our nation, and he built our synagogue for us.”
verses.Luke.7.6: Jesus went with them. When he was now not far from the house, the centurion sent friends to him, saying to him, “Lord, don’t trouble yourself, for I am not worthy for you to come under my roof.
verses.Luke.7.7: Therefore I didn’t even think myself worthy to come to you; but say the word, and my servant will be healed.
verses.Luke.7.8: For I also am a man placed under authority, having under myself soldiers. I tell this one, ‘Go!’ and he goes; and to another, ‘Come!’ and he comes; and to my servant, ‘Do this,’ and he does it.”
verses.Luke.7.9: When Jesus heard these things, he marveled at him, and turned and said to the multitude who followed him, “I tell you, I have not found such great faith, no, not in Israel.”
verses.Luke.7.10: Those who were sent, returning to the house, found that the servant who had been sick was well.
verses.Luke.7.11: Soon afterwards, he went to a city called Nain. Many of his disciples, along with a great multitude, went with him.
verses.Luke.7.12: Now when he came near to the gate of the city, behold, one who was dead was carried out, the only born son of his mother, and she was a widow. Many people of the city were with her.
verses.Luke.7.13: When the Lord saw her, he had compassion on her and said to her, “Don’t cry.”
verses.Luke.7.14: He came near and touched the coffin, and the bearers stood still. He said, “Young man, I tell you, arise!”
verses.Luke.7.15: He who was dead sat up and began to speak. Then he gave him to his mother.
verses.Luke.7.16: Fear took hold of all, and they glorified God, saying, “A great prophet has arisen among us!” and, “God has visited his people!”
verses.Luke.7.17: This report went out concerning him in the whole of Judea and in all the surrounding region.
verses.Luke.7.18: The disciples of John told him about all these things.
verses.Luke.7.19: John, calling to himself two of his disciples, sent them to Jesus, saying, “Are you the one who is coming, or should we look for another?”
verses.Luke.7.20: When the men had come to him, they said, “John the Baptizer has sent us to you, saying, ‘Are you he who comes, or should we look for another?’”
verses.Luke.7.21: In that hour he cured many of diseases and plagues and evil spirits; and to many who were blind he gave sight.
verses.Luke.7.22: Jesus answered them, “Go and tell John the things which you have seen and heard: that the blind receive their sight, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised up, and the poor have good news preached to them.
verses.Luke.7.23: Blessed is he who finds no occasion for stumbling in me.”
verses.Luke.7.24: When John’s messengers had departed, he began to tell the multitudes about John, “What did you go out into the wilderness to see? A reed shaken by the wind?
verses.Luke.7.25: But what did you go out to see? A man clothed in soft clothing? Behold, those who are gorgeously dressed and live delicately are in kings’ courts.
verses.Luke.7.26: But what did you go out to see? A prophet? Yes, I tell you, and much more than a prophet.
verses.Luke.7.27:
This is he of whom it is written,
‘Behold, I send my messenger before your face,
who will prepare your way before you.’
verses.Luke.7.28: “For I tell you, among those who are born of women there is not a greater prophet than John the Baptizer; yet he who is least in God’s Kingdom is greater than he.”
verses.Luke.7.29: When all the people and the tax collectors heard this, they declared God to be just, having been baptized with John’s baptism.
verses.Luke.7.30: But the Pharisees and the lawyers rejected the counsel of God, not being baptized by him themselves.
verses.Luke.7.31: “To what then should I compare the people of this generation? What are they like?
verses.Luke.7.32: They are like children who sit in the marketplace and call to one another, saying, ‘We piped to you, and you didn’t dance. We mourned, and you didn’t weep.’
verses.Luke.7.33: For John the Baptizer came neither eating bread nor drinking wine, and you say, ‘He has a demon.’
verses.Luke.7.34: The Son of Man has come eating and drinking, and you say, ‘Behold, a glutton and a drunkard, a friend of tax collectors and sinners!’
verses.Luke.7.35: Wisdom is justified by all her children.”
verses.Luke.7.36: One of the Pharisees invited him to eat with him. He entered into the Pharisee’s house and sat at the table.
verses.Luke.7.37: Behold, a woman in the city who was a sinner, when she knew that he was reclining in the Pharisee’s house, brought an alabaster jar of ointment.
verses.Luke.7.38: Standing behind at his feet weeping, she began to wet his feet with her tears, and she wiped them with the hair of her head, kissed his feet, and anointed them with the ointment.
verses.Luke.7.39: Now when the Pharisee who had invited him saw it, he said to himself, “This man, if he were a prophet, would have perceived who and what kind of woman this is who touches him, that she is a sinner.”
verses.Luke.7.40: Jesus answered him, “Simon, I have something to tell you.” He said, “Teacher, say on.”
verses.Luke.7.41: “A certain lender had two debtors. The one owed five hundred denarii, and the other fifty.
verses.Luke.7.42: When they couldn’t pay, he forgave them both. Which of them therefore will love him most?”
verses.Luke.7.43: Simon answered, “He, I suppose, to whom he forgave the most.” He said to him, “You have judged correctly.”
verses.Luke.7.44: Turning to the woman, he said to Simon, “Do you see this woman? I entered into your house, and you gave me no water for my feet, but she has wet my feet with her tears, and wiped them with the hair of her head.
verses.Luke.7.45: You gave me no kiss, but she, since the time I came in, has not ceased to kiss my feet.
verses.Luke.7.46: You didn’t anoint my head with oil, but she has anointed my feet with ointment.
verses.Luke.7.47: Therefore I tell you, her sins, which are many, are forgiven, for she loved much. But one to whom little is forgiven, loves little.”
verses.Luke.7.48: He said to her, “Your sins are forgiven.”
verses.Luke.7.49: Those who sat at the table with him began to say to themselves, “Who is this who even forgives sins?”
verses.Luke.7.50: He said to the woman, “Your faith has saved you. Go in peace.”
verses.Luke.13.1: Now there were some present at the same time who told him about the Galileans whose blood Pilate had mixed with their sacrifices.
verses.Luke.13.2: Jesus answered them, “Do you think that these Galileans were worse sinners than all the other Galileans, because they suffered such things?
verses.Luke.13.3: I tell you, no, but unless you repent, you will all perish in the same way.
verses.Luke.13.4: Or those eighteen on whom the tower in Siloam fell and killed them—do you think that they were worse offenders than all the men who dwell in Jerusalem?
verses.Luke.13.5: I tell you, no, but, unless you repent, you will all perish in the same way.”
verses.Luke.13.6: He spoke this parable. “A certain man had a fig tree planted in his vineyard, and he came seeking fruit on it and found none.
verses.Luke.13.7: He said to the vine dresser, ‘Behold, these three years I have come looking for fruit on this fig tree, and found none. Cut it down! Why does it waste the soil?’
verses.Luke.13.8: He answered, ‘Lord, leave it alone this year also, until I dig around it and fertilize it.
verses.Luke.13.9: If it bears fruit, fine; but if not, after that, you can cut it down.’”
verses.Luke.13.10: He was teaching in one of the synagogues on the Sabbath day.
verses.Luke.13.11: Behold, there was a woman who had a spirit of infirmity eighteen years. She was bent over and could in no way straighten herself up.
verses.Luke.13.12: When Jesus saw her, he called her and said to her, “Woman, you are freed from your infirmity.”
verses.Luke.13.13: He laid his hands on her, and immediately she stood up straight and glorified God.
verses.Luke.13.14: The ruler of the synagogue, being indignant because Jesus had healed on the Sabbath, said to the multitude, “There are six days in which men ought to work. Therefore come on those days and be healed, and not on the Sabbath day!”
verses.Luke.13.15: Therefore the Lord answered him, “You hypocrites! Doesn’t each one of you free his ox or his donkey from the stall on the Sabbath and lead him away to water?
verses.Luke.13.16: Ought not this woman, being a daughter of Abraham whom Satan had bound eighteen long years, be freed from this bondage on the Sabbath day?”
verses.Luke.13.17: As he said these things, all his adversaries were disappointed; and all the multitude rejoiced for all the glorious things that were done by him.
verses.Luke.13.18: He said, “What is God’s Kingdom like? To what shall I compare it?
verses.Luke.13.19: It is like a grain of mustard seed which a man took and put in his own garden. It grew and became a large tree, and the birds of the sky live in its branches.”
verses.Luke.13.20: Again he said, “To what shall I compare God’s Kingdom?
verses.Luke.13.21: It is like yeast, which a woman took and hid in three measures of flour, until it was all leavened.”
verses.Luke.13.22: He went on his way through cities and villages, teaching, and traveling on to Jerusalem.
verses.Luke.13.23: One said to him, “Lord, are they few who are saved?” He said to them,
verses.Luke.13.24: “Strive to enter in by the narrow door, for many, I tell you, will seek to enter in and will not be able.
verses.Luke.13.25: When once the master of the house has risen up and has shut the door, and you begin to stand outside and to knock at the door, saying, ‘Lord, Lord, open to us!’ then he will answer and tell you, ‘I don’t know you or where you come from.’
verses.Luke.13.26: Then you will begin to say, ‘We ate and drank in your presence, and you taught in our streets.’
verses.Luke.13.27: He will say, ‘I tell you, I don’t know where you come from. Depart from me, all you workers of iniquity.’
verses.Luke.13.28: There will be weeping and gnashing of teeth when you see Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and all the prophets in God’s Kingdom, and yourselves being thrown outside.
verses.Luke.13.29: They will come from the east, west, north, and south, and will sit down in God’s Kingdom.
verses.Luke.13.30: Behold, there are some who are last who will be first, and there are some who are first who will be last.”
verses.Luke.13.31: On that same day, some Pharisees came, saying to him, “Get out of here and go away, for Herod wants to kill you.”
verses.Luke.13.32: He said to them, “Go and tell that fox, ‘Behold, I cast out demons and perform cures today and tomorrow, and the third day I complete my mission.
verses.Luke.13.33: Nevertheless I must go on my way today and tomorrow and the next day, for it can’t be that a prophet would perish outside of Jerusalem.’
verses.Luke.13.34: “Jerusalem, Jerusalem, you who kills the prophets and stones those who are sent to her! How often I wanted to gather your children together, like a hen gathers her own brood under her wings, and you refused!
verses.Luke.13.35: Behold, your house is left to you desolate. I tell you, you will not see me until you say, ‘Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord!’”
verses.Luke.12.1: Meanwhile, when a multitude of many thousands had gathered together, so much so that they trampled on each other, he began to tell his disciples first of all, “Beware of the yeast of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy.
verses.Luke.12.2: But there is nothing covered up that will not be revealed, nor hidden that will not be known.
verses.Luke.12.3: Therefore whatever you have said in the darkness will be heard in the light. What you have spoken in the ear in the inner rooms will be proclaimed on the housetops.
verses.Luke.12.4: “I tell you, my friends, don’t be afraid of those who kill the body, and after that have no more that they can do.
verses.Luke.12.5: But I will warn you whom you should fear. Fear him who after he has killed, has power to cast into Gehenna. Yes, I tell you, fear him.
verses.Luke.12.6: “Aren’t five sparrows sold for two assaria coins? Not one of them is forgotten by God.
verses.Luke.12.7: But the very hairs of your head are all counted. Therefore don’t be afraid. You are of more value than many sparrows.
verses.Luke.12.8: “I tell you, everyone who confesses me before men, the Son of Man will also confess before the angels of God;
verses.Luke.12.9: but he who denies me in the presence of men will be denied in the presence of God’s angels.
verses.Luke.12.10: Everyone who speaks a word against the Son of Man will be forgiven, but those who blaspheme against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven.
verses.Luke.12.11: When they bring you before the synagogues, the rulers, and the authorities, don’t be anxious how or what you will answer or what you will say;
verses.Luke.12.12: for the Holy Spirit will teach you in that same hour what you must say.”
verses.Luke.12.13: One of the multitude said to him, “Teacher, tell my brother to divide the inheritance with me.”
verses.Luke.12.14: But he said to him, “Man, who made me a judge or an arbitrator over you?”
verses.Luke.12.15: He said to them, “Beware! Keep yourselves from covetousness, for a man’s life doesn’t consist of the abundance of the things which he possesses.”
verses.Luke.12.16: He spoke a parable to them, saying, “The ground of a certain rich man produced abundantly.
verses.Luke.12.17: He reasoned within himself, saying, ‘What will I do, because I don’t have room to store my crops?’
verses.Luke.12.18: He said, ‘This is what I will do. I will pull down my barns, build bigger ones, and there I will store all my grain and my goods.
verses.Luke.12.19: I will tell my soul, “Soul, you have many goods laid up for many years. Take your ease, eat, drink, and be merry.”’
verses.Luke.12.20: “But God said to him, ‘You foolish one, tonight your soul is required of you. The things which you have prepared—whose will they be?’
verses.Luke.12.21: So is he who lays up treasure for himself, and is not rich toward God.”
verses.Luke.12.22: He said to his disciples, “Therefore I tell you, don’t be anxious for your life, what you will eat, nor yet for your body, what you will wear.
verses.Luke.12.23: Life is more than food, and the body is more than clothing.
verses.Luke.12.24: Consider the ravens: they don’t sow, they don’t reap, they have no warehouse or barn, and God feeds them. How much more valuable are you than birds!
verses.Luke.12.25: Which of you by being anxious can add a cubit to his height?
verses.Luke.12.26: If then you aren’t able to do even the least things, why are you anxious about the rest?
verses.Luke.12.27: Consider the lilies, how they grow. They don’t toil, neither do they spin; yet I tell you, even Solomon in all his glory was not arrayed like one of these.
verses.Luke.12.28: But if this is how God clothes the grass in the field, which today exists and tomorrow is cast into the oven, how much more will he clothe you, O you of little faith?
verses.Luke.12.29: “Don’t seek what you will eat or what you will drink; neither be anxious.
verses.Luke.12.30: For the nations of the world seek after all of these things, but your Father knows that you need these things.
verses.Luke.12.31: But seek God’s Kingdom, and all these things will be added to you.
verses.Luke.12.32: “Don’t be afraid, little flock, for it is your Father’s good pleasure to give you the Kingdom.
verses.Luke.12.33: Sell what you have and give gifts to the needy. Make for yourselves purses which don’t grow old, a treasure in the heavens that doesn’t fail, where no thief approaches and no moth destroys.
verses.Luke.12.34: For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.
verses.Luke.12.35: “Let your waist be dressed and your lamps burning.
verses.Luke.12.36: Be like men watching for their lord when he returns from the wedding feast, that when he comes and knocks, they may immediately open to him.
verses.Luke.12.37: Blessed are those servants whom the lord will find watching when he comes. Most certainly I tell you that he will dress himself, make them recline, and will come and serve them.
verses.Luke.12.38: They will be blessed if he comes in the second or third watch and finds them so.
verses.Luke.12.39: But know this, that if the master of the house had known in what hour the thief was coming, he would have watched and not allowed his house to be broken into.
verses.Luke.12.40: Therefore be ready also, for the Son of Man is coming in an hour that you don’t expect him.”
verses.Luke.12.41: Peter said to him, “Lord, are you telling this parable to us, or to everybody?”
verses.Luke.12.42: The Lord said, “Who then is the faithful and wise steward, whom his lord will set over his household, to give them their portion of food at the right times?
verses.Luke.12.43: Blessed is that servant whom his lord will find doing so when he comes.
verses.Luke.12.44: Truly I tell you that he will set him over all that he has.
verses.Luke.12.45: But if that servant says in his heart, ‘My lord delays his coming,’ and begins to beat the menservants and the maidservants, and to eat and drink and to be drunken,
verses.Luke.12.46: then the lord of that servant will come in a day when he isn’t expecting him and in an hour that he doesn’t know, and will cut him in two, and place his portion with the unfaithful.
verses.Luke.12.47: That servant who knew his lord’s will, and didn’t prepare nor do what he wanted, will be beaten with many stripes,
verses.Luke.12.48: but he who didn’t know, and did things worthy of stripes, will be beaten with few stripes. To whomever much is given, of him will much be required; and to whom much was entrusted, of him more will be asked.
verses.Luke.12.49: “I came to throw fire on the earth. I wish it were already kindled.
verses.Luke.12.50: But I have a baptism to be baptized with, and how distressed I am until it is accomplished!
verses.Luke.12.51: Do you think that I have come to give peace on the earth? I tell you, no, but rather division.
verses.Luke.12.52: For from now on, there will be five in one house divided, three against two, and two against three.
verses.Luke.12.53: They will be divided, father against son, and son against father; mother against daughter, and daughter against her mother; mother-in-law against her daughter-in-law, and daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law.”
verses.Luke.12.54: He said to the multitudes also, “When you see a cloud rising from the west, immediately you say, ‘A shower is coming,’ and so it happens.
verses.Luke.12.55: When a south wind blows, you say, ‘There will be a scorching heat,’ and it happens.
verses.Luke.12.56: You hypocrites! You know how to interpret the appearance of the earth and the sky, but how is it that you don’t interpret this time?
verses.Luke.12.57: “Why don’t you judge for yourselves what is right?
verses.Luke.12.58: For when you are going with your adversary before the magistrate, try diligently on the way to be released from him, lest perhaps he drag you to the judge, and the judge deliver you to the officer, and the officer throw you into prison.
verses.Luke.12.59: I tell you, you will by no means get out of there until you have paid the very last penny.”
verses.John.2.1: The third day, there was a wedding in Cana of Galilee. Jesus’ mother was there.
verses.John.2.2: Jesus also was invited, with his disciples, to the wedding.
verses.John.2.3: When the wine ran out, Jesus’ mother said to him, “They have no wine.”
verses.John.2.4: Jesus said to her, “Woman, what does that have to do with you and me? My hour has not yet come.”
verses.John.2.5: His mother said to the servants, “Whatever he says to you, do it.”
verses.John.2.6: Now there were six water pots of stone set there after the Jews’ way of purifying, containing two or three metretes apiece.
verses.John.2.7: Jesus said to them, “Fill the water pots with water.” So they filled them up to the brim.
verses.John.2.8: He said to them, “Now draw some out, and take it to the ruler of the feast.” So they took it.
verses.John.2.9: When the ruler of the feast tasted the water now become wine, and didn’t know where it came from (but the servants who had drawn the water knew), the ruler of the feast called the bridegroom
verses.John.2.10: and said to him, “Everyone serves the good wine first, and when the guests have drunk freely, then that which is worse. You have kept the good wine until now!”
verses.John.2.11: This beginning of his signs Jesus did in Cana of Galilee, and revealed his glory; and his disciples believed in him.
verses.John.2.12: After this, he went down to Capernaum, he, and his mother, his brothers, and his disciples; and they stayed there a few days.
verses.John.2.13: The Passover of the Jews was at hand, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem.
verses.John.2.14: He found in the temple those who sold oxen, sheep, and doves, and the changers of money sitting.
verses.John.2.15: He made a whip of cords and drove all out of the temple, both the sheep and the oxen; and he poured out the changers’ money and overthrew their tables.
verses.John.2.16: To those who sold the doves, he said, “Take these things out of here! Don’t make my Father’s house a marketplace!”
verses.John.2.17: His disciples remembered that it was written, “Zeal for your house will eat me up.”
verses.John.2.18: The Jews therefore answered him, “What sign do you show us, seeing that you do these things?”
verses.John.2.19: Jesus answered them, “Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up.”
verses.John.2.20: The Jews therefore said, “It took forty-six years to build this temple! Will you raise it up in three days?”
verses.John.2.21: But he spoke of the temple of his body.
verses.John.2.22: When therefore he was raised from the dead, his disciples remembered that he said this, and they believed the Scripture and the word which Jesus had said.
verses.John.2.23: Now when he was in Jerusalem at the Passover, during the feast, many believed in his name, observing his signs which he did.
verses.John.2.24: But Jesus didn’t entrust himself to them, because he knew everyone,
verses.John.2.25: and because he didn’t need for anyone to testify concerning man; for he himself knew what was in man.
verses.Luke.19.1: He entered and was passing through Jericho.
verses.Luke.19.2: There was a man named Zacchaeus. He was a chief tax collector, and he was rich.
verses.Luke.19.3: He was trying to see who Jesus was, and couldn’t because of the crowd, because he was short.
verses.Luke.19.4: He ran on ahead and climbed up into a sycamore tree to see him, for he was going to pass that way.
verses.Luke.19.5: When Jesus came to the place, he looked up and saw him, and said to him, “Zacchaeus, hurry and come down, for today I must stay at your house.”
verses.Luke.19.6: He hurried, came down, and received him joyfully.
verses.Luke.19.7: When they saw it, they all murmured, saying, “He has gone in to lodge with a man who is a sinner.”
verses.Luke.19.8: Zacchaeus stood and said to the Lord, “Behold, Lord, half of my goods I give to the poor. If I have wrongfully exacted anything of anyone, I restore four times as much.”
verses.Luke.19.9: Jesus said to him, “Today, salvation has come to this house, because he also is a son of Abraham.
verses.Luke.19.10: For the Son of Man came to seek and to save that which was lost.”
verses.Luke.19.11: As they heard these things, he went on and told a parable, because he was near Jerusalem, and they supposed that God’s Kingdom would be revealed immediately.
verses.Luke.19.12: He said therefore, “A certain nobleman went into a far country to receive for himself a kingdom and to return.
verses.Luke.19.13: He called ten servants of his and gave them ten mina coins, and told them, ‘Conduct business until I come.’
verses.Luke.19.14: But his citizens hated him, and sent an envoy after him, saying, ‘We don’t want this man to reign over us.’
verses.Luke.19.15: “When he had come back again, having received the kingdom, he commanded these servants, to whom he had given the money, to be called to him, that he might know what they had gained by conducting business.
verses.Luke.19.16: The first came before him, saying, ‘Lord, your mina has made ten more minas.’
verses.Luke.19.17: “He said to him, ‘Well done, you good servant! Because you were found faithful with very little, you shall have authority over ten cities.’
verses.Luke.19.18: “The second came, saying, ‘Your mina, Lord, has made five minas.’
verses.Luke.19.19: “So he said to him, ‘And you are to be over five cities.’
verses.Luke.19.20: Another came, saying, ‘Lord, behold, your mina, which I kept laid away in a handkerchief,
verses.Luke.19.21: for I feared you, because you are an exacting man. You take up that which you didn’t lay down, and reap that which you didn’t sow.’
verses.Luke.19.22: “He said to him, ‘Out of your own mouth I will judge you, you wicked servant! You knew that I am an exacting man, taking up that which I didn’t lay down and reaping that which I didn’t sow.
verses.Luke.19.23: Then why didn’t you deposit my money in the bank, and at my coming, I might have earned interest on it?’
verses.Luke.19.24: He said to those who stood by, ‘Take the mina away from him and give it to him who has the ten minas.’
verses.Luke.19.25: “They said to him, ‘Lord, he has ten minas!’
verses.Luke.19.26: ‘For I tell you that to everyone who has, will more be given; but from him who doesn’t have, even that which he has will be taken away from him.
verses.Luke.19.27: But bring those enemies of mine who didn’t want me to reign over them here, and kill them before me.’”
verses.Luke.19.28: Having said these things, he went on ahead, going up to Jerusalem.
verses.Luke.19.29: When he came near to Bethsphage and Bethany, at the mountain that is called Olivet, he sent two of his disciples,
verses.Luke.19.30: saying, “Go your way into the village on the other side, in which, as you enter, you will find a colt tied, which no man has ever sat upon. Untie it and bring it.
verses.Luke.19.31: If anyone asks you, ‘Why are you untying it?’ say to him: ‘The Lord needs it.’”
verses.Luke.19.32: Those who were sent went away and found things just as he had told them.
verses.Luke.19.33: As they were untying the colt, its owners said to them, “Why are you untying the colt?”
verses.Luke.19.35: Then they brought it to Jesus. They threw their cloaks on the colt and sat Jesus on them.
verses.Luke.19.36: As he went, they spread their cloaks on the road.
verses.Luke.19.37: As he was now getting near, at the descent of the Mount of Olives, the whole multitude of the disciples began to rejoice and praise God with a loud voice for all the mighty works which they had seen,
