verses.Luke.19.38: saying, “Blessed is the King who comes in the name of the Lord! Peace in heaven, and glory in the highest!”
verses.Luke.19.39: Some of the Pharisees from the multitude said to him, “Teacher, rebuke your disciples!”
verses.Luke.19.40: He answered them, “I tell you that if these were silent, the stones would cry out.”
verses.Luke.19.41: When he came near, he saw the city and wept over it,
verses.Luke.19.42: saying, “If you, even you, had known today the things which belong to your peace! But now, they are hidden from your eyes.
verses.Luke.19.43: For the days will come on you when your enemies will throw up a barricade against you, surround you, hem you in on every side,
verses.Luke.19.44: and will dash you and your children within you to the ground. They will not leave in you one stone on another, because you didn’t know the time of your visitation.”
verses.Luke.19.45: He entered into the temple and began to drive out those who bought and sold in it,
verses.Luke.19.46: saying to them, “It is written, ‘My house is a house of prayer,’ but you have made it a ‘den of robbers’!”
verses.Luke.19.47: He was teaching daily in the temple, but the chief priests, the scribes, and the leading men among the people sought to destroy him.
verses.Luke.19.48: They couldn’t find what they might do, for all the people hung on to every word that he said.
verses.Luke.20.1: On one of those days, as he was teaching the people in the temple and preaching the Good News, the priests and scribes came to him with the elders.
verses.Luke.20.2: They asked him, “Tell us: by what authority do you do these things? Or who is giving you this authority?”
verses.Luke.20.3: He answered them, “I also will ask you one question. Tell me:
verses.Luke.20.4: the baptism of John, was it from heaven, or from men?”
verses.Luke.20.5: They reasoned with themselves, saying, “If we say, ‘From heaven,’ he will say, ‘Why didn’t you believe him?’
verses.Luke.20.6: But if we say, ‘From men,’ all the people will stone us, for they are persuaded that John was a prophet.”
verses.Luke.20.7: They answered that they didn’t know where it was from.
verses.Luke.20.8: Jesus said to them, “Neither will I tell you by what authority I do these things.”
verses.Luke.20.9: He began to tell the people this parable: “A man planted a vineyard and rented it out to some farmers, and went into another country for a long time.
verses.Luke.20.10: At the proper season, he sent a servant to the farmers to collect his share of the fruit of the vineyard. But the farmers beat him and sent him away empty.
verses.Luke.20.11: He sent yet another servant, and they also beat him and treated him shamefully, and sent him away empty.
verses.Luke.20.12: He sent yet a third, and they also wounded him and threw him out.
verses.Luke.20.13: The lord of the vineyard said, ‘What shall I do? I will send my beloved son. It may be that seeing him, they will respect him.’
verses.Luke.20.14: “But when the farmers saw him, they reasoned among themselves, saying, ‘This is the heir. Come, let’s kill him, that the inheritance may be ours.’
verses.Luke.20.15: Then they threw him out of the vineyard and killed him. What therefore will the lord of the vineyard do to them?
verses.Luke.20.16: He will come and destroy these farmers, and will give the vineyard to others.” When they heard that, they said, “May that never be!”
verses.Luke.20.17:
But he looked at them and said, “Then what is this that is written,
‘The stone which the builders rejected
was made the chief cornerstone’?
verses.Luke.20.18:
Everyone who falls on that stone will be broken to pieces,
but it will crush whomever it falls on to dust.”
verses.Luke.20.19: The chief priests and the scribes sought to lay hands on him that very hour, but they feared the people—for they knew he had spoken this parable against them.
verses.Luke.20.20: They watched him and sent out spies, who pretended to be righteous, that they might trap him in something he said, so as to deliver him up to the power and authority of the governor.
verses.Luke.20.21: They asked him, “Teacher, we know that you say and teach what is right, and aren’t partial to anyone, but truly teach the way of God.
verses.Luke.20.22: Is it lawful for us to pay taxes to Caesar, or not?”
verses.Luke.20.23: But he perceived their craftiness, and said to them, “Why do you test me?
verses.Luke.20.24: Show me a denarius. Whose image and inscription are on it?” They answered, “Caesar’s.”
verses.Luke.20.25: He said to them, “Then give to Caesar the things that are Caesar’s, and to God the things that are God’s.”
verses.Luke.20.26: They weren’t able to trap him in his words before the people. They marveled at his answer and were silent.
verses.Luke.20.27: Some of the Sadducees came to him, those who deny that there is a resurrection.
verses.Luke.20.28: They asked him, “Teacher, Moses wrote to us that if a man’s brother dies having a wife, and he is childless, his brother should take the wife and raise up children for his brother.
verses.Luke.20.29: There were therefore seven brothers. The first took a wife, and died childless.
verses.Luke.20.30: The second took her as wife, and he died childless.
verses.Luke.20.31: The third took her, and likewise the seven all left no children, and died.
verses.Luke.20.33: Therefore in the resurrection whose wife of them will she be? For the seven had her as a wife.”
verses.Luke.20.34: Jesus said to them, “The children of this age marry and are given in marriage.
verses.Luke.20.35: But those who are considered worthy to attain to that age and the resurrection from the dead neither marry nor are given in marriage.
verses.Luke.20.36: For they can’t die any more, for they are like the angels and are children of God, being children of the resurrection.
verses.Luke.20.37: But that the dead are raised, even Moses showed at the bush, when he called the Lord ‘The God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.’
verses.Luke.20.38: Now he is not the God of the dead, but of the living, for all are alive to him.”
verses.Luke.20.39: Some of the scribes answered, “Teacher, you speak well.”
verses.Luke.20.40: They didn’t dare to ask him any more questions.
verses.Luke.20.41: He said to them, “Why do they say that the Christ is David’s son?
verses.Luke.20.42:
David himself says in the book of Psalms,
‘The Lord said to my Lord,
“Sit at my right hand,
verses.Luke.20.43: until I make your enemies the footstool of your feet.”’
verses.Luke.20.44: “David therefore calls him Lord, so how is he his son?”
verses.Luke.20.45: In the hearing of all the people, he said to his disciples,
verses.Luke.20.46: “Beware of those scribes who like to walk in long robes, and love greetings in the marketplaces, the best seats in the synagogues, and the best places at feasts;
verses.Luke.20.47: who devour widows’ houses, and for a pretense make long prayers. These will receive greater condemnation.”
verses.John.1.1: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.
verses.John.1.2: The same was in the beginning with God.
verses.John.1.3: All things were made through him. Without him, nothing was made that has been made.
verses.John.1.4: In him was life, and the life was the light of men.
verses.John.1.5: The light shines in the darkness, and the darkness hasn’t overcome it.
verses.John.1.6: There came a man sent from God, whose name was John.
verses.John.1.7: The same came as a witness, that he might testify about the light, that all might believe through him.
verses.John.1.8: He was not the light, but was sent that he might testify about the light.
verses.John.1.9: The true light that enlightens everyone was coming into the world.
verses.John.1.10: He was in the world, and the world was made through him, and the world didn’t recognize him.
verses.John.1.11: He came to his own, and those who were his own didn’t receive him.
verses.John.1.12: But as many as received him, to them he gave the right to become God’s children, to those who believe in his name:
verses.John.1.13: who were born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God.
verses.John.1.14: The Word became flesh and lived among us. We saw his glory, such glory as of the only born Son of the Father, full of grace and truth.
verses.John.1.15: John testified about him. He cried out, saying, “This was he of whom I said, ‘He who comes after me has surpassed me, for he was before me.’”
verses.John.1.16: From his fullness we all received grace upon grace.
verses.John.1.17: For the law was given through Moses. Grace and truth were realized through Jesus Christ.
verses.John.1.18: No one has seen God at any time. The only born Son, who is in the bosom of the Father, has declared him.
verses.John.1.19: This is John’s testimony, when the Jews sent priests and Levites from Jerusalem to ask him, “Who are you?”
verses.John.1.20: He declared, and didn’t deny, but he declared, “I am not the Christ.”
verses.John.1.21: They asked him, “What then? Are you Elijah?” He said, “I am not.” “Are you the prophet?” He answered, “No.”
verses.John.1.22: They said therefore to him, “Who are you? Give us an answer to take back to those who sent us. What do you say about yourself?”
verses.John.1.23: He said, “I am the voice of one crying in the wilderness, ‘Make straight the way of the Lord,’ as Isaiah the prophet said.”
verses.John.1.24: The ones who had been sent were from the Pharisees.
verses.John.1.25: They asked him, “Why then do you baptize if you are not the Christ, nor Elijah, nor the prophet?”
verses.John.1.26: John answered them, “I baptize in water, but among you stands one whom you don’t know.
verses.John.1.27: He is the one who comes after me, who is preferred before me, whose sandal strap I’m not worthy to loosen.”
verses.John.1.28: These things were done in Bethany beyond the Jordan, where John was baptizing.
verses.John.1.29: The next day, he saw Jesus coming to him, and said, “Behold, the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world!
verses.John.1.30: This is he of whom I said, ‘After me comes a man who is preferred before me, for he was before me.’
verses.John.1.31: I didn’t know him, but for this reason I came baptizing in water, that he would be revealed to Israel.”
verses.John.1.32: John testified, saying, “I have seen the Spirit descending like a dove out of heaven, and it remained on him.
verses.John.1.33: I didn’t recognize him, but he who sent me to baptize in water said to me, ‘On whomever you will see the Spirit descending and remaining on him is he who baptizes in the Holy Spirit.’
verses.John.1.34: I have seen and have testified that this is the Son of God.”
verses.John.1.35: Again, the next day, John was standing with two of his disciples,
verses.John.1.36: and he looked at Jesus as he walked, and said, “Behold, the Lamb of God!”
verses.John.1.37: The two disciples heard him speak, and they followed Jesus.
verses.John.1.38: Jesus turned and saw them following, and said to them, “What are you looking for?” They said to him, “Rabbi” (which is to say, being interpreted, Teacher), “where are you staying?”
verses.John.1.39: He said to them, “Come and see.” They came and saw where he was staying, and they stayed with him that day. It was about the tenth hour.
verses.John.1.40: One of the two who heard John and followed him was Andrew, Simon Peter’s brother.
verses.John.1.41: He first found his own brother, Simon, and said to him, “We have found the Messiah!” (which is, being interpreted, Christ).
verses.John.1.42: He brought him to Jesus. Jesus looked at him and said, “You are Simon the son of Jonah. You shall be called Cephas” (which is by interpretation, Peter).
verses.John.1.43: On the next day, he was determined to go out into Galilee, and he found Philip. Jesus said to him, “Follow me.”
verses.John.1.44: Now Philip was from Bethsaida, the city of Andrew and Peter.
verses.John.1.45: Philip found Nathanael, and said to him, “We have found him of whom Moses in the law and also the prophets, wrote: Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph.”
verses.John.1.46: Nathanael said to him, “Can any good thing come out of Nazareth?” Philip said to him, “Come and see.”
verses.John.1.47: Jesus saw Nathanael coming to him, and said about him, “Behold, an Israelite indeed, in whom is no deceit!”
verses.John.1.48: Nathanael said to him, “How do you know me?” Jesus answered him, “Before Philip called you, when you were under the fig tree, I saw you.”
verses.John.1.49: Nathanael answered him, “Rabbi, you are the Son of God! You are King of Israel!”
verses.John.1.50: Jesus answered him, “Because I told you, ‘I saw you underneath the fig tree,’ do you believe? You will see greater things than these!”
verses.John.1.51: He said to him, “Most certainly, I tell you all, hereafter you will see heaven opened, and the angels of God ascending and descending on the Son of Man.”
verses.Luke.21.1: He looked up and saw the rich people who were putting their gifts into the treasury.
verses.Luke.21.2: He saw a certain poor widow casting in two small brass coins.
verses.Luke.21.3: He said, “Truly I tell you, this poor widow put in more than all of them,
verses.Luke.21.4: for all these put in gifts for God from their abundance, but she, out of her poverty, put in all that she had to live on.”
verses.Luke.21.5: As some were talking about the temple and how it was decorated with beautiful stones and gifts, he said,
verses.Luke.21.6: “As for these things which you see, the days will come in which there will not be left here one stone on another that will not be thrown down.”
verses.Luke.21.7: They asked him, “Teacher, so when will these things be? What is the sign that these things are about to happen?”
verses.Luke.21.8: He said, “Watch out that you don’t get led astray, for many will come in my name, saying, ‘I am he,’ and, ‘The time is at hand.’ Therefore don’t follow them.
verses.Luke.21.9: When you hear of wars and disturbances, don’t be terrified, for these things must happen first, but the end won’t come immediately.”
verses.Luke.21.10: Then he said to them, “Nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom.
verses.Luke.21.11: There will be great earthquakes, famines, and plagues in various places. There will be terrors and great signs from heaven.
verses.Luke.21.12: But before all these things, they will lay their hands on you and will persecute you, delivering you up to synagogues and prisons, bringing you before kings and governors for my name’s sake.
verses.Luke.21.13: It will turn out as a testimony for you.
verses.Luke.21.14: Settle it therefore in your hearts not to meditate beforehand how to answer,
verses.Luke.21.15: for I will give you a mouth and wisdom which all your adversaries will not be able to withstand or to contradict.
verses.Luke.21.16: You will be handed over even by parents, brothers, relatives, and friends. They will cause some of you to be put to death.
verses.Luke.21.17: You will be hated by all men for my name’s sake.
verses.Luke.21.18: And not a hair of your head will perish.
verses.Luke.21.19: “By your endurance you will win your lives.
verses.Luke.21.20: “But when you see Jerusalem surrounded by armies, then know that its desolation is at hand.
verses.Luke.21.21: Then let those who are in Judea flee to the mountains. Let those who are in the middle of her depart. Let those who are in the country not enter therein.
verses.Luke.21.22: For these are days of vengeance, that all things which are written may be fulfilled.
verses.Luke.21.23: Woe to those who are pregnant and to those who nurse infants in those days! For there will be great distress in the land and wrath to this people.
verses.Luke.21.24: They will fall by the edge of the sword, and will be led captive into all the nations. Jerusalem will be trampled down by the Gentiles until the times of the Gentiles are fulfilled.
verses.Luke.21.25: “There will be signs in the sun, moon, and stars; and on the earth anxiety of nations, in perplexity for the roaring of the sea and the waves;
verses.Luke.21.26: men fainting for fear and for expectation of the things which are coming on the world, for the powers of the heavens will be shaken.
verses.Luke.21.27: Then they will see the Son of Man coming in a cloud with power and great glory.
verses.Luke.21.28: But when these things begin to happen, look up and lift up your heads, because your redemption is near.”
verses.Luke.21.29: He told them a parable. “See the fig tree and all the trees.
verses.Luke.21.30: When they are already budding, you see it and know by your own selves that the summer is already near.
verses.Luke.21.31: Even so you also, when you see these things happening, know that God’s Kingdom is near.
verses.Luke.21.32: Most certainly I tell you, this generation will not pass away until all things are accomplished.
verses.Luke.21.33: Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will by no means pass away.
verses.Luke.21.34: “So be careful, or your hearts will be loaded down with carousing, drunkenness, and cares of this life, and that day will come on you suddenly.
verses.Luke.21.35: For it will come like a snare on all those who dwell on the surface of all the earth.
verses.Luke.21.36: Therefore be watchful all the time, praying that you may be counted worthy to escape all these things that will happen, and to stand before the Son of Man.”
verses.Luke.21.37: Every day Jesus was teaching in the temple, and every night he would go out and spend the night on the mountain that is called Olivet.
verses.Luke.21.38: All the people came early in the morning to him in the temple to hear him.
verses.Luke.17.1: He said to the disciples, “It is impossible that no occasions of stumbling should come, but woe to him through whom they come!
verses.Luke.17.2: It would be better for him if a millstone were hung around his neck, and he were thrown into the sea, rather than that he should cause one of these little ones to stumble.
verses.Luke.17.3: Be careful. If your brother sins against you, rebuke him. If he repents, forgive him.
verses.Luke.17.4: If he sins against you seven times in the day, and seven times returns, saying, ‘I repent,’ you shall forgive him.”
verses.Luke.17.5: The apostles said to the Lord, “Increase our faith.”
verses.Luke.17.6: The Lord said, “If you had faith like a grain of mustard seed, you would tell this sycamore tree, ‘Be uprooted and be planted in the sea,’ and it would obey you.
verses.Luke.17.7: But who is there among you, having a servant plowing or keeping sheep, that will say when he comes in from the field, ‘Come immediately and sit down at the table’?
verses.Luke.17.8: Wouldn’t he rather tell him, ‘Prepare my supper, clothe yourself properly, and serve me while I eat and drink. Afterward you shall eat and drink’?
verses.Luke.17.9: Does he thank that servant because he did the things that were commanded? I think not.
verses.Luke.17.10: Even so you also, when you have done all the things that are commanded you, say, ‘We are unworthy servants. We have done our duty.’”
verses.Luke.17.11: As he was on his way to Jerusalem, he was passing along the borders of Samaria and Galilee.
verses.Luke.17.12: As he entered into a certain village, ten men who were lepers met him, who stood at a distance.
verses.Luke.17.13: They lifted up their voices, saying, “Jesus, Master, have mercy on us!”
verses.Luke.17.14: When he saw them, he said to them, “Go and show yourselves to the priests.” As they went, they were cleansed.
verses.Luke.17.15: One of them, when he saw that he was healed, turned back, glorifying God with a loud voice.
verses.Luke.17.16: He fell on his face at Jesus’ feet, giving him thanks; and he was a Samaritan.
verses.Luke.17.17: Jesus answered, “Weren’t the ten cleansed? But where are the nine?
verses.Luke.17.18: Were there none found who returned to give glory to God, except this foreigner?”
verses.Luke.17.19: Then he said to him, “Get up, and go your way. Your faith has healed you.”
verses.Luke.17.20: Being asked by the Pharisees when God’s Kingdom would come, he answered them, “God’s Kingdom doesn’t come with observation;
verses.Luke.17.21: neither will they say, ‘Look, here!’ or, ‘Look, there!’ for behold, God’s Kingdom is within you.”
verses.Luke.17.22: He said to the disciples, “The days will come when you will desire to see one of the days of the Son of Man, and you will not see it.
verses.Luke.17.23: They will tell you, ‘Look, here!’ or ‘Look, there!’ Don’t go away or follow after them,
verses.Luke.17.24: for as the lightning, when it flashes out of one part under the sky, shines to another part under the sky, so will the Son of Man be in his day.
verses.Luke.17.25: But first, he must suffer many things and be rejected by this generation.
verses.Luke.17.26: As it was in the days of Noah, even so it will also be in the days of the Son of Man.
verses.Luke.17.27: They ate, they drank, they married, and they were given in marriage until the day that Noah entered into the ship, and the flood came and destroyed them all.
verses.Luke.17.28: Likewise, even as it was in the days of Lot: they ate, they drank, they bought, they sold, they planted, they built;
verses.Luke.17.29: but in the day that Lot went out from Sodom, it rained fire and sulfur from the sky and destroyed them all.
verses.Luke.17.30: It will be the same way in the day that the Son of Man is revealed.
verses.Luke.17.31: In that day, he who will be on the housetop and his goods in the house, let him not go down to take them away. Let him who is in the field likewise not turn back.
verses.Luke.17.33: Whoever seeks to save his life loses it, but whoever loses his life preserves it.
verses.Luke.17.34: I tell you, in that night there will be two people in one bed. One will be taken and the other will be left.
verses.Luke.17.35: There will be two grinding grain together. One will be taken and the other will be left.”
verses.Luke.17.37: They, answering, asked him, “Where, Lord?” He said to them, “Where the body is, there the vultures will also be gathered together.”
verses.Luke.18.1: He also spoke a parable to them that they must always pray and not give up,
verses.Luke.18.2: saying, “There was a judge in a certain city who didn’t fear God and didn’t respect man.
verses.Luke.18.3: A widow was in that city, and she often came to him, saying, ‘Defend me from my adversary!’
verses.Luke.18.4: He wouldn’t for a while; but afterward he said to himself, ‘Though I neither fear God nor respect man,
verses.Luke.18.5: yet because this widow bothers me, I will defend her, or else she will wear me out by her continual coming.’”
verses.Luke.18.6: The Lord said, “Listen to what the unrighteous judge says.
verses.Luke.18.7: Won’t God avenge his chosen ones who are crying out to him day and night, and yet he exercises patience with them?
verses.Luke.18.8: I tell you that he will avenge them quickly. Nevertheless, when the Son of Man comes, will he find faith on the earth?”
verses.Luke.18.9: He also spoke this parable to certain people who were convinced of their own righteousness, and who despised all others:
verses.Luke.18.10: “Two men went up into the temple to pray; one was a Pharisee, and the other was a tax collector.
verses.Luke.18.11: The Pharisee stood and prayed by himself like this: ‘God, I thank you that I am not like the rest of men: extortionists, unrighteous, adulterers, or even like this tax collector.
verses.Luke.18.12: I fast twice a week. I give tithes of all that I get.’
verses.Luke.18.13: But the tax collector, standing far away, wouldn’t even lift up his eyes to heaven, but beat his chest, saying, ‘God, be merciful to me, a sinner!’
verses.Luke.18.14: I tell you, this man went down to his house justified rather than the other; for everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, but he who humbles himself will be exalted.”
verses.Luke.18.15: They were also bringing their babies to him, that he might touch them. But when the disciples saw it, they rebuked them.
verses.Luke.18.16: Jesus summoned them, saying, “Allow the little children to come to me, and don’t hinder them, for God’s Kingdom belongs to such as these.
verses.Luke.18.17: Most certainly, I tell you, whoever doesn’t receive God’s Kingdom like a little child, he will in no way enter into it.”
verses.Luke.18.18: A certain ruler asked him, saying, “Good Teacher, what shall I do to inherit eternal life?”
verses.Luke.18.19: Jesus asked him, “Why do you call me good? No one is good, except one: God.
verses.Luke.18.20: You know the commandments: ‘Don’t commit adultery,’ ‘Don’t murder,’ ‘Don’t steal,’ ‘Don’t give false testimony,’ ‘Honor your father and your mother.’”
verses.Luke.18.21: He said, “I have observed all these things from my youth up.”
verses.Luke.18.22: When Jesus heard these things, he said to him, “You still lack one thing. Sell all that you have and distribute it to the poor. Then you will have treasure in heaven; then come, follow me.”
verses.Luke.18.23: But when he heard these things, he became very sad, for he was very rich.
verses.Luke.18.24: Jesus, seeing that he became very sad, said, “How hard it is for those who have riches to enter into God’s Kingdom!
verses.Luke.18.25: For it is easier for a camel to enter in through a needle’s eye than for a rich man to enter into God’s Kingdom.”
verses.Luke.18.26: Those who heard it said, “Then who can be saved?”
verses.Luke.18.27: But he said, “The things which are impossible with men are possible with God.”
verses.Luke.18.28: Peter said, “Look, we have left everything and followed you.”
verses.Luke.18.29: He said to them, “Most certainly I tell you, there is no one who has left house, or wife, or brothers, or parents, or children, for God’s Kingdom’s sake,
verses.Luke.18.30: who will not receive many times more in this time, and in the world to come, eternal life.”
verses.Luke.18.31: He took the twelve aside and said to them, “Behold, we are going up to Jerusalem, and all the things that are written through the prophets concerning the Son of Man will be completed.
verses.Luke.18.32: For he will be delivered up to the Gentiles, will be mocked, treated shamefully, and spit on.
verses.Luke.18.33: They will scourge and kill him. On the third day, he will rise again.”
verses.Luke.18.34: They understood none of these things. This saying was hidden from them, and they didn’t understand the things that were said.
verses.Luke.18.35: As he came near Jericho, a certain blind man sat by the road, begging.
verses.Luke.18.36: Hearing a multitude going by, he asked what this meant.
verses.Luke.18.37: They told him that Jesus of Nazareth was passing by.
verses.Luke.18.38: He cried out, “Jesus, you son of David, have mercy on me!”
verses.Luke.18.39: Those who led the way rebuked him, that he should be quiet; but he cried out all the more, “You son of David, have mercy on me!”
verses.Luke.18.40: Standing still, Jesus commanded him to be brought to him. When he had come near, he asked him,
verses.Luke.18.41: “What do you want me to do?” He said, “Lord, that I may see again.”
verses.Luke.18.42: Jesus said to him, “Receive your sight. Your faith has healed you.”
verses.Luke.18.43: Immediately he received his sight and followed him, glorifying God. All the people, when they saw it, praised God.
verses.Luke.22.1: Now the feast of unleavened bread, which is called the Passover, was approaching.
verses.Luke.22.2: The chief priests and the scribes sought how they might put him to death, for they feared the people.
verses.Luke.22.3: Satan entered into Judas, who was also called Iscariot, who was counted with the twelve.
verses.Luke.22.4: He went away and talked with the chief priests and captains about how he might deliver him to them.
verses.Luke.22.5: They were glad, and agreed to give him money.
verses.Luke.22.6: He consented and sought an opportunity to deliver him to them in the absence of the multitude.
verses.Luke.22.7: The day of unleavened bread came, on which the Passover must be sacrificed.
verses.Luke.22.8: Jesus sent Peter and John, saying, “Go and prepare the Passover for us, that we may eat.”
verses.Luke.22.9: They said to him, “Where do you want us to prepare?”
verses.Luke.22.10: He said to them, “Behold, when you have entered into the city, a man carrying a pitcher of water will meet you. Follow him into the house which he enters.
verses.Luke.22.11: Tell the master of the house, ‘The Teacher says to you, “Where is the guest room, where I may eat the Passover with my disciples?”’
verses.Luke.22.12: He will show you a large, furnished upper room. Make preparations there.”
verses.Luke.22.13: They went, found things as Jesus had told them, and they prepared the Passover.
verses.Luke.22.14: When the hour had come, he sat down with the twelve apostles.
verses.Luke.22.15: He said to them, “I have earnestly desired to eat this Passover with you before I suffer,
verses.Luke.22.16: for I tell you, I will no longer by any means eat of it until it is fulfilled in God’s Kingdom.”
verses.Luke.22.17: He received a cup, and when he had given thanks, he said, “Take this and share it among yourselves,
verses.Luke.22.18: for I tell you, I will not drink at all again from the fruit of the vine, until God’s Kingdom comes.”
verses.Luke.22.19: He took bread, and when he had given thanks, he broke and gave it to them, saying, “This is my body which is given for you. Do this in memory of me.”
verses.Luke.22.20: Likewise, he took the cup after supper, saying, “This cup is the new covenant in my blood, which is poured out for you.
verses.Luke.22.21: But behold, the hand of him who betrays me is with me on the table.
verses.Luke.22.22: The Son of Man indeed goes as it has been determined, but woe to that man through whom he is betrayed!”
verses.Luke.22.23: They began to question among themselves which of them it was who would do this thing.
verses.Luke.22.24: A dispute also arose among them, which of them was considered to be greatest.
verses.Luke.22.25: He said to them, “The kings of the nations lord it over them, and those who have authority over them are called ‘benefactors.’
verses.Luke.22.26: But not so with you. Rather, the one who is greater among you, let him become as the younger, and one who is governing, as one who serves.
verses.Luke.22.27: For who is greater, one who sits at the table, or one who serves? Isn’t it he who sits at the table? But I am among you as one who serves.
verses.Luke.22.28: “But you are those who have continued with me in my trials.
verses.Luke.22.29: I confer on you a kingdom, even as my Father conferred on me,
verses.Luke.22.30: that you may eat and drink at my table in my Kingdom. You will sit on thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.”
verses.Luke.22.31: The Lord said, “Simon, Simon, behold, Satan asked to have all of you, that he might sift you as wheat,
verses.Luke.22.32: but I prayed for you, that your faith wouldn’t fail. You, when once you have turned again, establish your brothers.”
verses.Luke.22.33: He said to him, “Lord, I am ready to go with you both to prison and to death!”
verses.Luke.22.34: He said, “I tell you, Peter, the rooster will by no means crow today until you deny that you know me three times.”
verses.Luke.22.35: He said to them, “When I sent you out without purse, bag, and sandals, did you lack anything?” They said, “Nothing.”
verses.Luke.22.36: Then he said to them, “But now, whoever has a purse, let him take it, and likewise a bag. Whoever has none, let him sell his cloak, and buy a sword.
verses.Luke.22.37: For I tell you that this which is written must still be fulfilled in me: ‘He was counted with transgressors.’ For that which concerns me is being fulfilled.”
verses.Luke.22.38: They said, “Lord, behold, here are two swords.” He said to them, “That is enough.”
verses.Luke.22.39: He came out and went, as his custom was, to the Mount of Olives. His disciples also followed him.
verses.Luke.22.40: When he was at the place, he said to them, “Pray that you don’t enter into temptation.”
verses.Luke.22.41: He was withdrawn from them about a stone’s throw, and he knelt down and prayed,
verses.Luke.22.42: saying, “Father, if you are willing, remove this cup from me. Nevertheless, not my will, but yours, be done.”
verses.Luke.22.43: An angel from heaven appeared to him, strengthening him.
verses.Luke.22.44: Being in agony, he prayed more earnestly. His sweat became like great drops of blood falling down on the ground.
verses.Luke.22.45: When he rose up from his prayer, he came to the disciples and found them sleeping because of grief,
verses.Luke.22.46: and said to them, “Why do you sleep? Rise and pray that you may not enter into temptation.”
verses.Luke.22.47: While he was still speaking, a crowd appeared. He who was called Judas, one of the twelve, was leading them. He came near to Jesus to kiss him.
verses.Luke.22.48: But Jesus said to him, “Judas, do you betray the Son of Man with a kiss?”
verses.Luke.22.49: When those who were around him saw what was about to happen, they said to him, “Lord, shall we strike with the sword?”
verses.Luke.22.50: A certain one of them struck the servant of the high priest, and cut off his right ear.
verses.Luke.22.51: But Jesus answered, “Let me at least do this”—and he touched his ear and healed him.
verses.Luke.22.52: Jesus said to the chief priests, captains of the temple, and elders, who had come against him, “Have you come out as against a robber, with swords and clubs?
verses.Luke.22.53: When I was with you in the temple daily, you didn’t stretch out your hands against me. But this is your hour, and the power of darkness.”
verses.Luke.22.54: They seized him and led him away, and brought him into the high priest’s house. But Peter followed from a distance.
verses.Luke.22.55: When they had kindled a fire in the middle of the courtyard and had sat down together, Peter sat among them.
verses.Luke.22.56: A certain servant girl saw him as he sat in the light, and looking intently at him, said, “This man also was with him.”
verses.Luke.22.57: He denied Jesus, saying, “Woman, I don’t know him.”
verses.Luke.22.58: After a little while someone else saw him and said, “You also are one of them!” But Peter answered, “Man, I am not!”
verses.Luke.22.59: After about one hour passed, another confidently affirmed, saying, “Truly this man also was with him, for he is a Galilean!”
verses.Luke.22.60: But Peter said, “Man, I don’t know what you are talking about!” Immediately, while he was still speaking, a rooster crowed.
verses.Luke.22.61: The Lord turned and looked at Peter. Then Peter remembered the Lord’s word, how he said to him, “Before the rooster crows you will deny me three times.”
verses.Luke.22.62: He went out, and wept bitterly.
verses.Luke.22.63: The men who held Jesus mocked him and beat him.
verses.Luke.22.64: Having blindfolded him, they struck him on the face and asked him, “Prophesy! Who is the one who struck you?”
verses.Luke.22.65: They spoke many other things against him, insulting him.
verses.Luke.22.66: As soon as it was day, the assembly of the elders of the people were gathered together, both chief priests and scribes, and they led him away into their council, saying,
verses.Luke.22.67: “If you are the Christ, tell us.” But he said to them, “If I tell you, you won’t believe,
verses.Luke.22.68: and if I ask, you will in no way answer me or let me go.
verses.Luke.22.69: From now on, the Son of Man will be seated at the right hand of the power of God.”
verses.Luke.22.70: They all said, “Are you then the Son of God?” He said to them, “You say it, because I am.”
verses.Luke.22.71: They said, “Why do we need any more witness? For we ourselves have heard from his own mouth!”
verses.Luke.23.1: The whole company of them rose up and brought him before Pilate.
verses.Luke.23.2: They began to accuse him, saying, “We found this man perverting the nation, forbidding paying taxes to Caesar, and saying that he himself is Christ, a king.”
verses.Luke.23.3: Pilate asked him, “Are you the King of the Jews?” He answered him, “So you say.”
verses.Luke.23.4: Pilate said to the chief priests and the multitudes, “I find no basis for a charge against this man.”
verses.Luke.23.5: But they insisted, saying, “He stirs up the people, teaching throughout all Judea, beginning from Galilee even to this place.”
verses.Luke.23.6: But when Pilate heard Galilee mentioned, he asked if the man was a Galilean.
verses.Luke.23.7: When he found out that he was in Herod’s jurisdiction, he sent him to Herod, who was also in Jerusalem during those days.
verses.Luke.23.8: Now when Herod saw Jesus, he was exceedingly glad, for he had wanted to see him for a long time, because he had heard many things about him. He hoped to see some miracle done by him.
verses.Luke.23.9: He questioned him with many words, but he gave no answers.
verses.Luke.23.10: The chief priests and the scribes stood, vehemently accusing him.
verses.Luke.23.11: Herod with his soldiers humiliated him and mocked him. Dressing him in luxurious clothing, they sent him back to Pilate.
verses.Luke.23.12: Herod and Pilate became friends with each other that very day, for before that they were enemies with each other.
verses.Luke.23.13: Pilate called together the chief priests, the rulers, and the people,
verses.Luke.23.14: and said to them, “You brought this man to me as one that perverts the people, and behold, having examined him before you, I found no basis for a charge against this man concerning those things of which you accuse him.
verses.Luke.23.15: Neither has Herod, for I sent you to him, and see, nothing worthy of death has been done by him.
verses.Luke.23.16: I will therefore chastise him and release him.”
verses.Luke.23.17: Now he had to release one prisoner to them at the feast.
verses.Luke.23.18: But they all cried out together, saying, “Away with this man! Release to us Barabbas!”—
verses.Luke.23.19: one who was thrown into prison for a certain revolt in the city, and for murder.
verses.Luke.23.20: Then Pilate spoke to them again, wanting to release Jesus,
verses.Luke.23.21: but they shouted, saying, “Crucify! Crucify him!”
verses.Luke.23.22: He said to them the third time, “Why? What evil has this man done? I have found no capital crime in him. I will therefore chastise him and release him.”
verses.Luke.23.23: But they were urgent with loud voices, asking that he might be crucified. Their voices and the voices of the chief priests prevailed.
verses.Luke.23.24: Pilate decreed that what they asked for should be done.
verses.Luke.23.25: He released him who had been thrown into prison for insurrection and murder, for whom they asked, but he delivered Jesus up to their will.
verses.Luke.23.26: When they led him away, they grabbed one Simon of Cyrene, coming from the country, and laid the cross on him to carry it after Jesus.
verses.Luke.23.27: A great multitude of the people followed him, including women who also mourned and lamented him.
verses.Luke.23.28: But Jesus, turning to them, said, “Daughters of Jerusalem, don’t weep for me, but weep for yourselves and for your children.
verses.Luke.23.29: For behold, the days are coming in which they will say, ‘Blessed are the barren, the wombs that never bore, and the breasts that never nursed.’
verses.Luke.23.30: Then they will begin to tell the mountains, ‘Fall on us!’ and tell the hills, ‘Cover us.’
verses.Luke.23.31: For if they do these things in the green tree, what will be done in the dry?”
verses.Luke.23.32: There were also others, two criminals, led with him to be put to death.
verses.Luke.23.33: When they came to the place that is called “The Skull”, they crucified him there with the criminals, one on the right and the other on the left.
verses.Luke.23.34: Jesus said, “Father, forgive them, for they don’t know what they are doing.” Dividing his garments among them, they cast lots.
verses.Luke.23.35: The people stood watching. The rulers with them also scoffed at him, saying, “He saved others. Let him save himself, if this is the Christ of God, his chosen one!”
verses.Luke.23.36: The soldiers also mocked him, coming to him and offering him vinegar,
verses.Luke.23.37: and saying, “If you are the King of the Jews, save yourself!”
verses.Luke.23.38: An inscription was also written over him in letters of Greek, Latin, and Hebrew: “THIS IS THE KING OF THE JEWS.”
verses.Luke.23.39: One of the criminals who was hanged insulted him, saying, “If you are the Christ, save yourself and us!”
verses.Luke.23.40: But the other answered, and rebuking him said, “Don’t you even fear God, seeing you are under the same condemnation?
verses.Luke.23.41: And we indeed justly, for we receive the due reward for our deeds, but this man has done nothing wrong.”
verses.Luke.23.42: He said to Jesus, “Lord, remember me when you come into your Kingdom.”
verses.Luke.23.43: Jesus said to him, “Assuredly I tell you, today you will be with me in Paradise.”
verses.Luke.23.44: It was now about the sixth hour, and darkness came over the whole land until the ninth hour.
verses.Luke.23.45: The sun was darkened, and the veil of the temple was torn in two.
verses.Luke.23.46: Jesus, crying with a loud voice, said, “Father, into your hands I commit my spirit!” Having said this, he breathed his last.
verses.Luke.23.47: When the centurion saw what was done, he glorified God, saying, “Certainly this was a righteous man.”
verses.Luke.23.48: All the multitudes that came together to see this, when they saw the things that were done, returned home beating their chests.
verses.Luke.23.49: All his acquaintances and the women who followed with him from Galilee stood at a distance, watching these things.
verses.Luke.23.50: Behold, there was a man named Joseph, who was a member of the council, a good and righteous man
verses.Luke.23.51: (he had not consented to their counsel and deed), from Arimathaea, a city of the Jews, who was also waiting for God’s Kingdom.
verses.Luke.23.52: This man went to Pilate, and asked for Jesus’ body.
verses.Luke.23.53: He took it down and wrapped it in a linen cloth, and laid him in a tomb that was cut in stone, where no one had ever been laid.
verses.Luke.23.54: It was the day of the Preparation, and the Sabbath was drawing near.
verses.Luke.23.55: The women who had come with him out of Galilee followed after, and saw the tomb and how his body was laid.
verses.Luke.23.56: They returned and prepared spices and ointments. On the Sabbath they rested according to the commandment.
verses.Luke.24.1: But on the first day of the week, at early dawn, they and some others came to the tomb, bringing the spices which they had prepared.
verses.Luke.24.2: They found the stone rolled away from the tomb.
verses.Luke.24.3: They entered in, and didn’t find the Lord Jesus’ body.
verses.Luke.24.4: While they were greatly perplexed about this, behold, two men stood by them in dazzling clothing.
verses.Luke.24.5: Becoming terrified, they bowed their faces down to the earth. The men said to them, “Why do you seek the living among the dead?
verses.Luke.24.6: He isn’t here, but is risen. Remember what he told you when he was still in Galilee,
verses.Luke.24.7: saying that the Son of Man must be delivered up into the hands of sinful men and be crucified, and the third day rise again?”
verses.Luke.24.9: returned from the tomb, and told all these things to the eleven and to all the rest.
verses.Luke.24.10: Now they were Mary Magdalene, Joanna, and Mary the mother of James. The other women with them told these things to the apostles.
verses.Luke.24.11: These words seemed to them to be nonsense, and they didn’t believe them.
verses.Luke.24.12: But Peter got up and ran to the tomb. Stooping and looking in, he saw the strips of linen lying by themselves, and he departed to his home, wondering what had happened.
verses.Luke.24.13: Behold, two of them were going that very day to a village named Emmaus, which was sixty stadia from Jerusalem.
verses.Luke.24.14: They talked with each other about all of these things which had happened.
verses.Luke.24.15: While they talked and questioned together, Jesus himself came near, and went with them.
verses.Luke.24.16: But their eyes were kept from recognizing him.
verses.Luke.24.17: He said to them, “What are you talking about as you walk, and are sad?”
verses.Luke.24.18: One of them, named Cleopas, answered him, “Are you the only stranger in Jerusalem who doesn’t know the things which have happened there in these days?”
verses.Luke.24.19: He said to them, “What things?” They said to him, “The things concerning Jesus the Nazarene, who was a prophet mighty in deed and word before God and all the people;
verses.Luke.24.20: and how the chief priests and our rulers delivered him up to be condemned to death, and crucified him.
verses.Luke.24.21: But we were hoping that it was he who would redeem Israel. Yes, and besides all this, it is now the third day since these things happened.
verses.Luke.24.22: Also, certain women of our company amazed us, having arrived early at the tomb;
verses.Luke.24.23: and when they didn’t find his body, they came saying that they had also seen a vision of angels, who said that he was alive.
verses.Luke.24.24: Some of us went to the tomb and found it just like the women had said, but they didn’t see him.”
verses.Luke.24.25: He said to them, “Foolish people, and slow of heart to believe in all that the prophets have spoken!
verses.Luke.24.26: Didn’t the Christ have to suffer these things and to enter into his glory?”
verses.Luke.24.27: Beginning from Moses and from all the prophets, he explained to them in all the Scriptures the things concerning himself.
verses.Luke.24.28: They came near to the village where they were going, and he acted like he would go further.
verses.Luke.24.29: They urged him, saying, “Stay with us, for it is almost evening, and the day is almost over.” He went in to stay with them.
verses.Luke.24.30: When he had sat down at the table with them, he took the bread and gave thanks. Breaking it, he gave it to them.
verses.Luke.24.31: Their eyes were opened and they recognized him; then he vanished out of their sight.
verses.Luke.24.32: They said to one another, “Weren’t our hearts burning within us while he spoke to us along the way, and while he opened the Scriptures to us?”
verses.Luke.24.33: They rose up that very hour, returned to Jerusalem, and found the eleven gathered together, and those who were with them,
verses.Luke.24.34: saying, “The Lord is risen indeed, and has appeared to Simon!”
verses.Luke.24.35: They related the things that happened along the way, and how he was recognized by them in the breaking of the bread.
verses.Luke.24.36: As they said these things, Jesus himself stood among them, and said to them, “Peace be to you.”
verses.Luke.24.37: But they were terrified and filled with fear, and supposed that they had seen a spirit.
verses.Luke.24.38: He said to them, “Why are you troubled? Why do doubts arise in your hearts?
verses.Luke.24.39: See my hands and my feet, that it is truly me. Touch me and see, for a spirit doesn’t have flesh and bones, as you see that I have.”
verses.Luke.24.40: When he had said this, he showed them his hands and his feet.
verses.Luke.24.41: While they still didn’t believe for joy, and wondered, he said to them, “Do you have anything here to eat?”
verses.Luke.24.42: They gave him a piece of a broiled fish and some honeycomb.
verses.Luke.24.43: He took them, and ate in front of them.
verses.Luke.24.44: He said to them, “This is what I told you while I was still with you, that all things which are written in the law of Moses, the prophets, and the psalms concerning me must be fulfilled.”
verses.Luke.24.45: Then he opened their minds, that they might understand the Scriptures.
verses.Luke.24.46: He said to them, “Thus it is written, and thus it was necessary for the Christ to suffer and to rise from the dead the third day,
verses.Luke.24.47: and that repentance and remission of sins should be preached in his name to all the nations, beginning at Jerusalem.
verses.Luke.24.48: You are witnesses of these things.
verses.Luke.24.49: Behold, I send out the promise of my Father on you. But wait in the city of Jerusalem until you are clothed with power from on high.”
verses.Luke.24.50: He led them out as far as Bethany, and he lifted up his hands and blessed them.
verses.Luke.24.51: While he blessed them, he withdrew from them and was carried up into heaven.
verses.Luke.24.52: They worshiped him and returned to Jerusalem with great joy,
verses.Luke.24.53: and were continually in the temple, praising and blessing God. Amen.
verses.John.8.1: but Jesus went to the Mount of Olives.
verses.John.8.2: Now very early in the morning, he came again into the temple, and all the people came to him. He sat down and taught them.
verses.John.8.3: The scribes and the Pharisees brought a woman taken in adultery. Having set her in the middle,
verses.John.8.4: they told him, “Teacher, we found this woman in adultery, in the very act.
verses.John.8.5: Now in our law, Moses commanded us to stone such women. What then do you say about her?”
verses.John.8.6: They said this testing him, that they might have something to accuse him of. But Jesus stooped down and wrote on the ground with his finger.
verses.John.8.7: But when they continued asking him, he looked up and said to them, “He who is without sin among you, let him throw the first stone at her.”
verses.John.8.8: Again he stooped down and wrote on the ground with his finger.
verses.John.8.9: They, when they heard it, being convicted by their conscience, went out one by one, beginning from the oldest, even to the last. Jesus was left alone with the woman where she was, in the middle.
verses.John.8.10: Jesus, standing up, saw her and said, “Woman, where are your accusers? Did no one condemn you?”
verses.John.8.11: She said, “No one, Lord.” Jesus said, “Neither do I condemn you. Go your way. From now on, sin no more.”
verses.John.8.12: Again, therefore, Jesus spoke to them, saying, “I am the light of the world. He who follows me will not walk in the darkness, but will have the light of life.”
verses.John.8.13: The Pharisees therefore said to him, “You testify about yourself. Your testimony is not valid.”
verses.John.8.14: Jesus answered them, “Even if I testify about myself, my testimony is true, for I know where I came from, and where I am going; but you don’t know where I came from, or where I am going.
verses.John.8.15: You judge according to the flesh. I judge no one.
verses.John.8.16: Even if I do judge, my judgment is true, for I am not alone, but I am with the Father who sent me.
verses.John.8.17: It’s also written in your law that the testimony of two people is valid.
verses.John.8.18: I am one who testifies about myself, and the Father who sent me testifies about me.”
verses.John.8.19: They said therefore to him, “Where is your Father?” Jesus answered, “You know neither me nor my Father. If you knew me, you would know my Father also.”
verses.John.8.20: Jesus spoke these words in the treasury, as he taught in the temple. Yet no one arrested him, because his hour had not yet come.
verses.John.8.21: Jesus said therefore again to them, “I am going away, and you will seek me, and you will die in your sins. Where I go, you can’t come.”
verses.John.8.22: The Jews therefore said, “Will he kill himself, because he says, ‘Where I am going, you can’t come’?”
verses.John.8.23: He said to them, “You are from beneath. I am from above. You are of this world. I am not of this world.
verses.John.8.24: I said therefore to you that you will die in your sins; for unless you believe that I am he, you will die in your sins.”
verses.John.8.25: They said therefore to him, “Who are you?” Jesus said to them, “Just what I have been saying to you from the beginning.
verses.John.8.26: I have many things to speak and to judge concerning you. However, he who sent me is true; and the things which I heard from him, these I say to the world.”
verses.John.8.27: They didn’t understand that he spoke to them about the Father.
verses.John.8.28: Jesus therefore said to them, “When you have lifted up the Son of Man, then you will know that I am he, and I do nothing of myself, but as my Father taught me, I say these things.
verses.John.8.29: He who sent me is with me. The Father hasn’t left me alone, for I always do the things that are pleasing to him.”
verses.John.8.30: As he spoke these things, many believed in him.
verses.John.8.31: Jesus therefore said to those Jews who had believed him, “If you remain in my word, then you are truly my disciples.
verses.John.8.32: You will know the truth, and the truth will make you free.”
verses.John.8.33: They answered him, “We are Abraham’s offspring, and have never been in bondage to anyone. How do you say, ‘You will be made free’?”
verses.John.8.34: Jesus answered them, “Most certainly I tell you, everyone who commits sin is the bondservant of sin.
verses.John.8.35: A bondservant doesn’t live in the house forever. A son remains forever.
verses.John.8.36: If therefore the Son makes you free, you will be free indeed.
verses.John.8.37: I know that you are Abraham’s offspring, yet you seek to kill me, because my word finds no place in you.
verses.John.8.38: I say the things which I have seen with my Father; and you also do the things which you have seen with your father.”
verses.John.8.39: They answered him, “Our father is Abraham.” Jesus said to them, “If you were Abraham’s children, you would do the works of Abraham.
verses.John.8.40: But now you seek to kill me, a man who has told you the truth which I heard from God. Abraham didn’t do this.
verses.John.8.41: You do the works of your father.” They said to him, “We were not born of sexual immorality. We have one Father, God.”
verses.John.8.42: Therefore Jesus said to them, “If God were your father, you would love me, for I came out and have come from God. For I haven’t come of myself, but he sent me.
verses.John.8.43: Why don’t you understand my speech? Because you can’t hear my word.
verses.John.8.44: You are of your father the devil, and you want to do the desires of your father. He was a murderer from the beginning, and doesn’t stand in the truth, because there is no truth in him. When he speaks a lie, he speaks on his own; for he is a liar, and the father of lies.
verses.John.8.45: But because I tell the truth, you don’t believe me.
verses.John.8.46: Which of you convicts me of sin? If I tell the truth, why do you not believe me?
verses.John.8.47: He who is of God hears the words of God. For this cause you don’t hear, because you are not of God.”
verses.John.8.48: Then the Jews answered him, “Don’t we say well that you are a Samaritan, and have a demon?”
verses.John.8.49: Jesus answered, “I don’t have a demon, but I honor my Father and you dishonor me.
verses.John.8.50: But I don’t seek my own glory. There is one who seeks and judges.
verses.John.8.51: Most certainly, I tell you, if a person keeps my word, he will never see death.”
verses.John.8.52: Then the Jews said to him, “Now we know that you have a demon. Abraham died, as did the prophets; and you say, ‘If a man keeps my word, he will never taste of death.’
verses.John.8.53: Are you greater than our father Abraham, who died? The prophets died. Who do you make yourself out to be?”
verses.John.8.54: Jesus answered, “If I glorify myself, my glory is nothing. It is my Father who glorifies me, of whom you say that he is our God.
verses.John.8.55: You have not known him, but I know him. If I said, ‘I don’t know him,’ I would be like you, a liar. But I know him and keep his word.
verses.John.8.56: Your father Abraham rejoiced to see my day. He saw it and was glad.”
verses.John.8.57: The Jews therefore said to him, “You are not yet fifty years old! Have you seen Abraham?”
verses.John.8.58: Jesus said to them, “Most certainly, I tell you, before Abraham came into existence, I AM.”
verses.John.8.59: Therefore they took up stones to throw at him, but Jesus hid himself and went out of the temple, having gone through the middle of them, and so passed by.
verses.John.5.1: After these things, there was a feast of the Jews, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem.
verses.John.5.2: Now in Jerusalem by the sheep gate, there is a pool, which is called in Hebrew, “Bethesda”, having five porches.
verses.John.5.3: In these lay a great multitude of those who were sick, blind, lame, or paralyzed, waiting for the moving of the water;
verses.John.5.4: for an angel went down at certain times into the pool and stirred up the water. Whoever stepped in first after the stirring of the water was healed of whatever disease he had.
verses.John.5.5: A certain man was there who had been sick for thirty-eight years.
verses.John.5.6: When Jesus saw him lying there, and knew that he had been sick for a long time, he asked him, “Do you want to be made well?”
verses.John.5.7: The sick man answered him, “Sir, I have no one to put me into the pool when the water is stirred up, but while I’m coming, another steps down before me.”
verses.John.5.8: Jesus said to him, “Arise, take up your mat, and walk.”
verses.John.5.9: Immediately, the man was made well, and took up his mat and walked. Now that day was a Sabbath.
verses.John.5.10: So the Jews said to him who was cured, “It is the Sabbath. It is not lawful for you to carry the mat.”
verses.John.5.11: He answered them, “He who made me well said to me, ‘Take up your mat and walk.’ ”
verses.John.5.12: Then they asked him, “Who is the man who said to you, ‘Take up your mat and walk’?”
verses.John.5.13: But he who was healed didn’t know who it was, for Jesus had withdrawn, a crowd being in the place.
verses.John.5.14: Afterward Jesus found him in the temple and said to him, “Behold, you are made well. Sin no more, so that nothing worse happens to you.”
verses.John.5.15: The man went away, and told the Jews that it was Jesus who had made him well.
verses.John.5.16: For this cause the Jews persecuted Jesus and sought to kill him, because he did these things on the Sabbath.
verses.John.5.17: But Jesus answered them, “My Father is still working, so I am working, too.”
verses.John.5.18: For this cause therefore the Jews sought all the more to kill him, because he not only broke the Sabbath, but also called God his own Father, making himself equal with God.
verses.John.5.19: Jesus therefore answered them, “Most certainly, I tell you, the Son can do nothing of himself, but what he sees the Father doing. For whatever things he does, these the Son also does likewise.
verses.John.5.20: For the Father has affection for the Son, and shows him all things that he himself does. He will show him greater works than these, that you may marvel.
verses.John.5.21: For as the Father raises the dead and gives them life, even so the Son also gives life to whom he desires.
verses.John.5.22: For the Father judges no one, but he has given all judgment to the Son,
verses.John.5.23: that all may honor the Son, even as they honor the Father. He who doesn’t honor the Son doesn’t honor the Father who sent him.
verses.John.5.24: “Most certainly I tell you, he who hears my word and believes him who sent me has eternal life, and doesn’t come into judgment, but has passed out of death into life.
verses.John.5.25: Most certainly I tell you, the hour comes, and now is, when the dead will hear the Son of God’s voice; and those who hear will live.
verses.John.5.26: For as the Father has life in himself, even so he gave to the Son also to have life in himself.
verses.John.5.27: He also gave him authority to execute judgment, because he is a son of man.
verses.John.5.28: Don’t marvel at this, for the hour comes in which all who are in the tombs will hear his voice
verses.John.5.29: and will come out; those who have done good, to the resurrection of life; and those who have done evil, to the resurrection of judgment.
verses.John.5.30: I can of myself do nothing. As I hear, I judge; and my judgment is righteous, because I don’t seek my own will, but the will of my Father who sent me.
verses.John.5.31: “If I testify about myself, my witness is not valid.
verses.John.5.32: It is another who testifies about me. I know that the testimony which he testifies about me is true.
verses.John.5.33: You have sent to John, and he has testified to the truth.
verses.John.5.34: But the testimony which I receive is not from man. However, I say these things that you may be saved.
verses.John.5.35: He was the burning and shining lamp, and you were willing to rejoice for a while in his light.
verses.John.5.36: But the testimony which I have is greater than that of John; for the works which the Father gave me to accomplish, the very works that I do, testify about me, that the Father has sent me.
verses.John.5.37: The Father himself, who sent me, has testified about me. You have neither heard his voice at any time, nor seen his form.
verses.John.5.38: You don’t have his word living in you, because you don’t believe him whom he sent.
verses.John.5.39: “You search the Scriptures, because you think that in them you have eternal life; and these are they which testify about me.
verses.John.5.40: Yet you will not come to me, that you may have life.
verses.John.5.41: I don’t receive glory from men.
verses.John.5.42: But I know you, that you don’t have God’s love in yourselves.
verses.John.5.43: I have come in my Father’s name, and you don’t receive me. If another comes in his own name, you will receive him.
verses.John.5.44: How can you believe, who receive glory from one another, and you don’t seek the glory that comes from the only God?
verses.John.5.45: “Don’t think that I will accuse you to the Father. There is one who accuses you, even Moses, on whom you have set your hope.
verses.John.5.46: For if you believed Moses, you would believe me; for he wrote about me.
verses.John.5.47: But if you don’t believe his writings, how will you believe my words?”
verses.John.10.1: “Most certainly, I tell you, one who doesn’t enter by the door into the sheep fold, but climbs up some other way, is a thief and a robber.
verses.John.10.2: But one who enters in by the door is the shepherd of the sheep.
verses.John.10.3: The gatekeeper opens the gate for him, and the sheep listen to his voice. He calls his own sheep by name and leads them out.
verses.John.10.4: Whenever he brings out his own sheep, he goes before them; and the sheep follow him, for they know his voice.
verses.John.10.5: They will by no means follow a stranger, but will flee from him; for they don’t know the voice of strangers.”
verses.John.10.6: Jesus spoke this parable to them, but they didn’t understand what he was telling them.
verses.John.10.7: Jesus therefore said to them again, “Most certainly, I tell you, I am the sheep’s door.
verses.John.10.8: All who came before me are thieves and robbers, but the sheep didn’t listen to them.
verses.John.10.9: I am the door. If anyone enters in by me, he will be saved, and will go in and go out and will find pasture.
verses.John.10.10: The thief only comes to steal, kill, and destroy. I came that they may have life, and may have it abundantly.
verses.John.10.11: “I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep.
verses.John.10.12: He who is a hired hand, and not a shepherd, who doesn’t own the sheep, sees the wolf coming, leaves the sheep, and flees. The wolf snatches the sheep and scatters them.
verses.John.10.13: The hired hand flees because he is a hired hand and doesn’t care for the sheep.
verses.John.10.14: I am the good shepherd. I know my own, and I’m known by my own;
verses.John.10.15: even as the Father knows me, and I know the Father. I lay down my life for the sheep.
verses.John.10.16: I have other sheep which are not of this fold. I must bring them also, and they will hear my voice. They will become one flock with one shepherd.
verses.John.10.17: Therefore the Father loves me, because I lay down my life, that I may take it again.
verses.John.10.18: No one takes it away from me, but I lay it down by myself. I have power to lay it down, and I have power to take it again. I received this commandment from my Father.”
verses.John.10.19: Therefore a division arose again among the Jews because of these words.
verses.John.10.20: Many of them said, “He has a demon and is insane! Why do you listen to him?”
verses.John.10.21: Others said, “These are not the sayings of one possessed by a demon. It isn’t possible for a demon to open the eyes of the blind, is it?”
verses.John.10.22: It was the Feast of the Dedication at Jerusalem.
verses.John.10.23: It was winter, and Jesus was walking in the temple, in Solomon’s porch.
verses.John.10.24: The Jews therefore came around him and said to him, “How long will you hold us in suspense? If you are the Christ, tell us plainly.”
verses.John.10.25: Jesus answered them, “I told you, and you don’t believe. The works that I do in my Father’s name, these testify about me.
verses.John.10.26: But you don’t believe, because you are not of my sheep, as I told you.
verses.John.10.27: My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me.
verses.John.10.28: I give eternal life to them. They will never perish, and no one will snatch them out of my hand.
verses.John.10.29: My Father who has given them to me is greater than all. No one is able to snatch them out of my Father’s hand.
verses.John.10.30: I and the Father are one.”
verses.John.10.31: Therefore the Jews took up stones again to stone him.
verses.John.10.32: Jesus answered them, “I have shown you many good works from my Father. For which of those works do you stone me?”
verses.John.10.33: The Jews answered him, “We don’t stone you for a good work, but for blasphemy, because you, being a man, make yourself God.”
verses.John.10.34: Jesus answered them, “Isn’t it written in your law, ‘I said, you are gods’?
verses.John.10.35: If he called them gods, to whom the word of God came (and the Scripture can’t be broken),
verses.John.10.36: do you say of him whom the Father sanctified and sent into the world, ‘You blaspheme,’ because I said, ‘I am the Son of God’?
verses.John.10.37: If I don’t do the works of my Father, don’t believe me.
verses.John.10.38: But if I do them, though you don’t believe me, believe the works, that you may know and believe that the Father is in me, and I in the Father.”
verses.John.10.39: They sought again to seize him, and he went out of their hand.
verses.John.10.40: He went away again beyond the Jordan into the place where John was baptizing at first, and he stayed there.
verses.John.10.41: Many came to him. They said, “John indeed did no sign, but everything that John said about this man is true.”
verses.John.9.1: As he passed by, he saw a man blind from birth.
verses.John.9.2: His disciples asked him, “Rabbi, who sinned, this man or his parents, that he was born blind?”
verses.John.9.3: Jesus answered, “This man didn’t sin, nor did his parents, but that the works of God might be revealed in him.
verses.John.9.4: I must work the works of him who sent me while it is day. The night is coming, when no one can work.
verses.John.9.5: While I am in the world, I am the light of the world.”
verses.John.9.6: When he had said this, he spat on the ground, made mud with the saliva, anointed the blind man’s eyes with the mud,
verses.John.9.7: and said to him, “Go, wash in the pool of Siloam” (which means “Sent”). So he went away, washed, and came back seeing.
verses.John.9.8: Therefore the neighbors and those who saw that he was blind before said, “Isn’t this he who sat and begged?”
verses.John.9.9: Others were saying, “It is he.” Still others were saying, “He looks like him.” He said, “I am he.”
verses.John.9.10: They therefore were asking him, “How were your eyes opened?”
verses.John.9.11: He answered, “A man called Jesus made mud, anointed my eyes, and said to me, ‘Go to the pool of Siloam and wash.’ So I went away and washed, and I received sight.”
verses.John.9.12: Then they asked him, “Where is he?” He said, “I don’t know.”
verses.John.9.13: They brought him who had been blind to the Pharisees.
verses.John.9.14: It was a Sabbath when Jesus made the mud and opened his eyes.
verses.John.9.15: Again therefore the Pharisees also asked him how he received his sight. He said to them, “He put mud on my eyes, I washed, and I see.”
verses.John.9.16: Some therefore of the Pharisees said, “This man is not from God, because he doesn’t keep the Sabbath.” Others said, “How can a man who is a sinner do such signs?” So there was division among them.
verses.John.9.17: Therefore they asked the blind man again, “What do you say about him, because he opened your eyes?” He said, “He is a prophet.”
verses.John.9.18: The Jews therefore didn’t believe concerning him, that he had been blind and had received his sight, until they called the parents of him who had received his sight,
verses.John.9.19: and asked them, “Is this your son, whom you say was born blind? How then does he now see?”
verses.John.9.20: His parents answered them, “We know that this is our son, and that he was born blind;
verses.John.9.21: but how he now sees, we don’t know; or who opened his eyes, we don’t know. He is of age. Ask him. He will speak for himself.”
verses.John.9.22: His parents said these things because they feared the Jews; for the Jews had already agreed that if any man would confess him as Christ, he would be put out of the synagogue.
verses.John.9.23: Therefore his parents said, “He is of age. Ask him.”
verses.John.9.24: So they called the man who was blind a second time, and said to him, “Give glory to God. We know that this man is a sinner.”
verses.John.9.25: He therefore answered, “I don’t know if he is a sinner. One thing I do know: that though I was blind, now I see.”
verses.John.9.26: They said to him again, “What did he do to you? How did he open your eyes?”
verses.John.9.27: He answered them, “I told you already, and you didn’t listen. Why do you want to hear it again? You don’t also want to become his disciples, do you?”
verses.John.9.28: They insulted him and said, “You are his disciple, but we are disciples of Moses.
verses.John.9.29: We know that God has spoken to Moses. But as for this man, we don’t know where he comes from.”
verses.John.9.30: The man answered them, “How amazing! You don’t know where he comes from, yet he opened my eyes.
verses.John.9.31: We know that God doesn’t listen to sinners, but if anyone is a worshiper of God and does his will, he listens to him.
verses.John.9.32: Since the world began it has never been heard of that anyone opened the eyes of someone born blind.
verses.John.9.33: If this man were not from God, he could do nothing.”
verses.John.9.34: They answered him, “You were altogether born in sins, and do you teach us?” Then they threw him out.
verses.John.9.35: Jesus heard that they had thrown him out, and finding him, he said, “Do you believe in the Son of God?”
verses.John.9.36: He answered, “Who is he, Lord, that I may believe in him?”
verses.John.9.37: Jesus said to him, “You have both seen him, and it is he who speaks with you.”
verses.John.9.38: He said, “Lord, I believe!” and he worshiped him.
verses.John.9.39: Jesus said, “I came into this world for judgment, that those who don’t see may see; and that those who see may become blind.”
verses.John.9.40: Those of the Pharisees who were with him heard these things, and said to him, “Are we also blind?”
verses.John.9.41: Jesus said to them, “If you were blind, you would have no sin; but now you say, ‘We see.’ Therefore your sin remains.
verses.John.11.1: Now a certain man was sick, Lazarus from Bethany, of the village of Mary and her sister, Martha.
verses.John.11.2: It was that Mary who had anointed the Lord with ointment and wiped his feet with her hair, whose brother Lazarus was sick.
verses.John.11.3: The sisters therefore sent to him, saying, “Lord, behold, he for whom you have great affection is sick.”
verses.John.11.4: But when Jesus heard it, he said, “This sickness is not to death, but for the glory of God, that God’s Son may be glorified by it.”
verses.John.11.5: Now Jesus loved Martha, and her sister, and Lazarus.
verses.John.11.6: When therefore he heard that he was sick, he stayed two days in the place where he was.
verses.John.11.7: Then after this he said to the disciples, “Let’s go into Judea again.”
verses.John.11.8: The disciples asked him, “Rabbi, the Jews were just trying to stone you. Are you going there again?”
verses.John.11.9: Jesus answered, “Aren’t there twelve hours of daylight? If a man walks in the day, he doesn’t stumble, because he sees the light of this world.
verses.John.11.10: But if a man walks in the night, he stumbles, because the light isn’t in him.”
verses.John.11.11: He said these things, and after that, he said to them, “Our friend Lazarus has fallen asleep, but I am going so that I may awake him out of sleep.”
verses.John.11.12: The disciples therefore said, “Lord, if he has fallen asleep, he will recover.”
verses.John.11.13: Now Jesus had spoken of his death, but they thought that he spoke of taking rest in sleep.
verses.John.11.14: So Jesus said to them plainly then, “Lazarus is dead.
verses.John.11.15: I am glad for your sakes that I was not there, so that you may believe. Nevertheless, let’s go to him.”
verses.John.11.16: Thomas therefore, who is called Didymus, said to his fellow disciples, “Let’s also go, that we may die with him.”
verses.John.11.17: So when Jesus came, he found that he had been in the tomb four days already.
verses.John.11.18: Now Bethany was near Jerusalem, about fifteen stadia away.
verses.John.11.19: Many of the Jews had joined the women around Martha and Mary, to console them concerning their brother.
verses.John.11.20: Then when Martha heard that Jesus was coming, she went and met him, but Mary stayed in the house.
verses.John.11.21: Therefore Martha said to Jesus, “Lord, if you would have been here, my brother wouldn’t have died.
verses.John.11.22: Even now I know that whatever you ask of God, God will give you.”
verses.John.11.23: Jesus said to her, “Your brother will rise again.”
verses.John.11.24: Martha said to him, “I know that he will rise again in the resurrection at the last day.”
verses.John.11.25: Jesus said to her, “I am the resurrection and the life. He who believes in me will still live, even if he dies.
verses.John.11.26: Whoever lives and believes in me will never die. Do you believe this?”
verses.John.11.27: She said to him, “Yes, Lord. I have come to believe that you are the Christ, God’s Son, he who comes into the world.”
verses.John.11.28: When she had said this, she went away and called Mary, her sister, secretly, saying, “The Teacher is here and is calling you.”
verses.John.11.29: When she heard this, she arose quickly and went to him.
verses.John.11.30: Now Jesus had not yet come into the village, but was in the place where Martha met him.
verses.John.11.31: Then the Jews who were with her in the house and were consoling her, when they saw Mary, that she rose up quickly and went out, followed her, saying, “She is going to the tomb to weep there.”
verses.John.11.32: Therefore when Mary came to where Jesus was and saw him, she fell down at his feet, saying to him, “Lord, if you would have been here, my brother wouldn’t have died.”
verses.John.11.33: When Jesus therefore saw her weeping, and the Jews weeping who came with her, he groaned in the spirit and was troubled,
verses.John.11.34: and said, “Where have you laid him?” They told him, “Lord, come and see.”
verses.John.11.36: The Jews therefore said, “See how much affection he had for him!”
verses.John.11.37: Some of them said, “Couldn’t this man, who opened the eyes of him who was blind, have also kept this man from dying?”
verses.John.11.38: Jesus therefore, again groaning in himself, came to the tomb. Now it was a cave, and a stone lay against it.
verses.John.11.39: Jesus said, “Take away the stone.” Martha, the sister of him who was dead, said to him, “Lord, by this time there is a stench, for he has been dead four days.”
verses.John.11.40: Jesus said to her, “Didn’t I tell you that if you believed, you would see God’s glory?”
verses.John.11.41: So they took away the stone from the place where the dead man was lying. Jesus lifted up his eyes and said, “Father, I thank you that you listened to me.
verses.John.11.42: I know that you always listen to me, but because of the multitude standing around I said this, that they may believe that you sent me.”
verses.John.11.43: When he had said this, he cried with a loud voice, “Lazarus, come out!”
verses.John.11.44: He who was dead came out, bound hand and foot with wrappings, and his face was wrapped around with a cloth. Jesus said to them, “Free him, and let him go.”
verses.John.11.45: Therefore many of the Jews who came to Mary and saw what Jesus did believed in him.
verses.John.11.46: But some of them went away to the Pharisees and told them the things which Jesus had done.
verses.John.11.47: The chief priests therefore and the Pharisees gathered a council, and said, “What are we doing? For this man does many signs.
verses.John.11.48: If we leave him alone like this, everyone will believe in him, and the Romans will come and take away both our place and our nation.”
verses.John.11.49: But a certain one of them, Caiaphas, being high priest that year, said to them, “You know nothing at all,
verses.John.11.50: nor do you consider that it is advantageous for us that one man should die for the people, and that the whole nation not perish.”
verses.John.11.51: Now he didn’t say this of himself, but being high priest that year, he prophesied that Jesus would die for the nation,
verses.John.11.52: and not for the nation only, but that he might also gather together into one the children of God who are scattered abroad.
verses.John.11.53: So from that day forward they took counsel that they might put him to death.
verses.John.11.54: Jesus therefore walked no more openly among the Jews, but departed from there into the country near the wilderness, to a city called Ephraim. He stayed there with his disciples.
verses.John.11.55: Now the Passover of the Jews was at hand. Many went up from the country to Jerusalem before the Passover, to purify themselves.
verses.John.11.56: Then they sought for Jesus and spoke with one another as they stood in the temple, “What do you think—that he isn’t coming to the feast at all?”
verses.John.11.57: Now the chief priests and the Pharisees had commanded that if anyone knew where he was, he should report it, that they might seize him.
verses.John.6.1: After these things, Jesus went away to the other side of the sea of Galilee, which is also called the Sea of Tiberias.
verses.John.6.2: A great multitude followed him, because they saw his signs which he did on those who were sick.
verses.John.6.3: Jesus went up into the mountain, and he sat there with his disciples.
verses.John.6.4: Now the Passover, the feast of the Jews, was at hand.
verses.John.6.5: Jesus therefore, lifting up his eyes and seeing that a great multitude was coming to him, said to Philip, “Where are we to buy bread, that these may eat?”
verses.John.6.6: He said this to test him, for he himself knew what he would do.
verses.John.6.7: Philip answered him, “Two hundred denarii worth of bread is not sufficient for them, that every one of them may receive a little.”
verses.John.6.8: One of his disciples, Andrew, Simon Peter’s brother, said to him,
verses.John.6.9: “There is a boy here who has five barley loaves and two fish, but what are these among so many?”
verses.John.6.10: Jesus said, “Have the people sit down.” Now there was much grass in that place. So the men sat down, in number about five thousand.
